IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r4.claim: إذ may be extra in the cited clauses from 2:30 and 31:13, where the sense is simply “and He said.”
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r4.anchor: و (إذ) قد تزاد، كقوله: وإذ قال ربك للملائكة [البقرة: 30] .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r5.claim: He also cites Ibn Mayyada's line beginning إذ لا يزال as poetic evidence for the extra use of إذ.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p157/r5.anchor: وقال ابن ميادة : إذ لا يزال قائل: أبن أبن

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r1.claim: Adam’s story appears as the first Quranic story in al-Baqara; al-Araf later starts from creation and formation, as a continuation of the earlier account.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r1.anchor: وردت أوليات القصة عند أول ذكر لها في أول سورة من سور القرآن

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r2.claim: The preceding verse begins by honoring humanity through creation of the earth’s contents for people and ends by affirming God’s knowledge; Adam’s story develops both themes.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r2.anchor: بدأت بتكريم الإنسان: {خَلَقَ لَكُمْ مَّا فِي الأرض جَمِيعاً} وختمت بالعلم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r3.claim: The story honors Adam through his appointment as earth’s vicegerent, his being taught all the names beyond the angels’ knowledge, and the angels’ prostration to him.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r3.anchor: ذكر استخلاف آدم في الأرض: {إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الأرض خَلِيفَةً} فهذا تكريم، إذا المستخلف ذو منزلة رفيعة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r4.claim: Knowledge is central: God has comprehensive knowledge, angels know only what God teaches them, and Adam is taught what enables him to fulfill the vicegerency.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r4.anchor: إثبات العلم الشامل لله. 2- نفي العلم عن الملائكة إلا ما عَلَّمهم إياه ربُّ العزة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r5.claim: Successful vicegerency requires authority to manage the entrusted domain and the capacity and knowledge to do so; the preceding verse summarizes both through creation of the earth for people and God's knowledge.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r5.anchor: الاستخلاف الناجح لا بد أن يتم له أمران: الأول: أن يكون للخليفة حَقُّ التصرف والتدبير

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r6.claim: Al-Baqara’s account centers on Adam’s honor, with knowledge and vicegerency serving that theme; al-Araf has another purpose, and Adam’s honor there is secondary.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r6.anchor: القصة في هذا الموطن في كل حلقاتها ومجالاتها مبنية في الحقيقة على تكريم آدم

BURHAN:v3p194/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p194/r9.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v3p194/r9.claim: One explanation supplies a description of the appointed successor's future conduct; otherwise the angels would have had no basis to predict corruption, and the remaining text confirms the omission.
BURHAN:v3p194/r9.anchor: قيل المعنى جاعل في الأرض خليفة يفعل كذا وكذا وإلا فمن أين علم الملائكة أنهم يفسدون

ITQAN:v2p430/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p430/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ITQAN:v2p430/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda and Ibn Qutayba treat some Qur'anic instances of إذ as emphatic, equivalent to qad, including وإذ قال ربك للملائكة.
ITQAN:v2p430/r6.anchor: قاله أبو عبيدة وتبعه ابن قتيبة وحملا عليه آيات منها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.claim: The phrase about being dead, then made alive, dying, and being revived can be attached to an implied command to remember these events; the beginning already lets the thoughtful infer the return.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.anchor: إذ من البدءة تعلم العودة لمن تدبر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.claim: Humanity was made for lasting life, not extinction: God created the cosmos for people, as provision, means, and support for their preservation and development.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.anchor: لم يخلق هذا النوع البشري للفناء بل للبقاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r3.claim: The story of Adam is a manifest example that humanity is the intended purpose of this existence and that wisdom requires resurrection to a realm without disorder, where divine wisdom is fully evident.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r3.anchor: النوع الآدمي هو المقصود بالذات من هذا الوجود

BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r1.claim: The account displays Adam's distinction through knowledge, the angels' prostration, his residence in Paradise, and God's provision of repentance after his lapse.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r1.anchor: ثم بإسجاد الملائكة له , ثم بإسكانه الجنة , ثم بتلقي أسباب التوبة عند صدور الهفوة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r2.claim: A report says Muhammad is God's most honored creature; when asked about the angels, Ibn Salam says they are obedient creatures like the earth, sky, clouds, mountains, and winds, whereas Muhammad is most honored.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r2.anchor: عن بشر بن شغاف عن عبد الله بن سلام رضي الله عنه قال : ( إن أكرم خليقة الله على الله أبو القاسم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r3.speaker: البيهقي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r3.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says Ibn Salam's statement is not merely a Companion report but has the ruling of a report raised to the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r3.anchor: وقال البيهقي : إنه ليس بموقوف بل حكمه الرفع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r8.claim: The return of direct address to Muhammad reveals the unseen past of God's conversation with the angels about Adam, encouraging the guided toward higher ranks and calling the heedless back; revelation leads the rationally guided from faith to certainty.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p84/r8.anchor: عاد وجه الخطاب إليه صلى الله عليه وسلم بما هو إعلام بغائب الماضي عن كائن الوقت

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r1.claim: The angels trusted their many acts of obedience and presumed sinlessness, so they magnified themselves and belittled Adam when questioning his appointment as vicegerent.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r1.anchor: لما نظروا إلى كثرة طاعتهم واستعداد عصمتهم ونظروا إلى نتائج الصفات النفسانية استعظموا أنفسهم واستصغروا آدم وذريته

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r2.claim: Israelites made the same entitlement argument against Talut; God answered that kingship rests on divine choice and superiority in knowledge and physique, not wealth.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r2.anchor: قالوا أنى يكون له الملك علينا ونحن أحق بالملك منه

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r3.claim: God's answer to the angels is expanded by Adam's election, teaching him the names, and creating him with His hands: succession is bestowed by God, not earned through abundant worship.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r3.anchor: ليعلموا أن استعداد ملك الخلافة واستحقاقها ليس بكثرة الطاعات

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r4.claim: After the angels boasted, God favored Adam with knowledge of the names; their prostration showed that God needs no service and that grace belongs to Him.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r4.anchor: فبتفاخرهم على آدم صاروا ساجدين له ليعلموا أن الحق تعالى مستغن عن طاعتهم

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r5.claim: God's knowledge of Adam also includes hidden faults unknown to angels: bodily dispositions shared with animals and vices produced by the commanding self when the spirit follows it without the discipline of sacred law.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r5.anchor: له رذائل وأوصاف مذمومة لا يعلمها الملائكة لأنهم لا يعلمون منه أوصافا مذمومة هي من نتائج قالبه

BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r6.claim: Those soul-born faults include vanity, ostentation, seeking reputation, envy, preferring worldly life, innovation, deviation, and holding evil opinions.
BURSEVI:v1p76#3/r6.anchor: من العجب والرياء والسمعة والحسد واشتراء الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة والابتداع

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r1.claim: Modern non-Islamic theories reducing matter to force and force to spirit reproduce the philosophers’ doctrine of immaterial substances; treating such entities as conceptual aligns with theologians.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r1.anchor: Zamanımızda gayr-i İslâmî felsefelerin maddeyi kuvvete, kuvveti rûha ircâ‘eden nazariyeleri de esasında hukemânın sâlifu’z-zikr cevâhir-i mücerrede nazariyesidir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r2.claim: If the material cosmos is one heaven and other heavens exist beyond it, the reality and stations of angels extend to inconceivable heights and depths.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r2.anchor: Bâlâda beyan olunan kavl-i muhtâr vechile bütün kâinât-ı mâddiye bir semâ olduğuna ve bunlardan mâ‘adâ semâlar bulunduğuna göre, hakīkat-i melâikenin ve bunların makamlarının ne kadar yüksekliklere ve derinliklere varacağını tasavvur etmelidir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r3.claim: A prophetic report says heaven groans rightly because every space the size of a footstep contains an angel prostrating or bowing.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r3.anchor: Semâ gıcırdamaktadır. Ve gıcırdamak hakkıdır. Onda bir kadem mevzi‘i yoktur ki bunda bir melek-i sâcid veya râki‘bulunmasın.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r4.claim: A report gives successively immense ratios among humans, jinn, land and sea animals, angels of earth, and angels of successive heavens.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r4.anchor: Benî Âdem cinnin öşrü, bunlar hayvânât-ı berriyenin öşrü, hepsi tuyûrun öşrü

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r5.claim: The narration says all these angels are tiny beside those circling the Throne; the hosts of the Preserved Tablet and Gabriel are countless, and only God knows their kinds, lifetimes, and worship.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r5.anchor: Sonra bunların mecmû‘u Arş etrafında dönen melâikeye karşı denizden bir katre kalır.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r6.claim: A prophetic ascent report describes battlement-like angels; Gabriel has seen them since his creation but never the same one twice, and one angel says God created 400,000 stars in its lifetime.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r6.anchor: “Bunlar nereye gidiyorlar?” diye Resûlullah Cebrâil’e sordu, Cebrâil “bilmiyorum, ancak yaratıldığımdan beri ben bunları görürüm

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r7.claim: These accounts exceed contemporary astronomy; subtle ether bodies cannot explain all angels, at most earthly and lowest-heaven angels unless the lowest heaven is narrowly construed, unlike theologians’ preferred view.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r7.anchor: Şüphe yok ki bu tenvîrât asr-ı hâzırdaki hey’et fikrinden de çok yüksektir ve bunların hepsini ecsâm-ı lâtîfe-i esîriye ile tahdid etmek de pek muvâfık olmasa gerektir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r8.claim: One view restricts the angels addressed here to angels of earth, transmitted by al-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r8.anchor: Bundan murad melâike-i arzdır diyenler olmuştur ki bu da Dahhâk’in İbn Abbas radıyallahu ‘anhümâ’dan bir rivayetine müntehî olmaktadır.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r9.claim: Most Companions and Successors understand all angels, since the wording is general and has no qualifier.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r9.anchor: Lâkin ekser sahâbe ve tâbiîn rıdvânullahi ‘aleyhim ecmaîn hazarâtı lafzın umûmuna ve muhassıs bulunmadığına mebnî bütün melâike olduğunu söylemişlerdir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r10.claim: The angels’ question follows their being told the primordial decree concerning succession on earth; God answers that He knows what they do not.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r10.anchor: İşte bütün melâike arzda hilâfete müte‘allik böyle bir takdîr-i ezelînin kendilerine teblîği üzerine hitâb-ı ilâhî karşısında

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r11.claim: Although angels know generally that God’s knowledge surpasses theirs, His emphatic ‘I indeed’ signals a specific hidden matter: the wisdom and fitness of succession that prompted their wonder at evil.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r11.anchor: makām-ı inkârda tekid ifade eden إِنِّى ile takviye ederek Cenâb-ı Allah’ın bunu tekrar ihbar etmesi gösterir ki murâd-ı ilâhî bu umum içinde bir husûsu

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r12.claim: The answer says angels do not know the wisdom, motives, and fitness of caliphate; it also implies angelic qualities alone are insufficient and that requesting office is improper.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r12.anchor: hilâfetin hikmet ve devâ‘îsi ve ona liyâkat meselesi hakkında bilmediğiniz cihetler var.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r13.claim: He invokes the maxim that a person seeking judicial office should not be appointed to it.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#4/r13.anchor: ‘adem-i kifayetine ve talebin ‘adem-i cevâzına da zımnen işaret buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r3.claim: The detailed reply explains the earlier summary that God knows what the angels do not; a genuine summary and its detail have the same meaning.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r3.anchor: evvelki إِنِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ kavl-i celîlinin mânasını tafsil ve tefsir etti.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r4.claim: Angelic speech is truly a matter of meaning, not verbal or nominal forms; otherwise a statement made in summary would not amount to its detailed version.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r4.anchor: melâikeye olan kelâmın hakikati ancak mânadan ibarettir, suver-i lafziye ve ismiye değildir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r5.claim: The immediate purpose is specifically to establish and manifest the wisdom and causes of Adam's fitness for vicegerency, which the angels had not grasped.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r5.anchor: bilhassa [317] Âdem aleyhisselâm’da tahakkuk eden devâ‘î-i hilâfeti takrir ve izhâr-ı hikmet ü kudrettir

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r6.claim: God connects His acts to hidden causes and wisdom, yet no creature can claim entitlement through a cause: He creates causes and grants outcomes, and His will is the true original cause.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r6.anchor: Sebeb-i aslî ve hakīkī ancak O’nun iradesidir. Hikmet de O’nun lâzımıdır.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r7.claim: God announced Adam's vicegerency to the angels summarily, as if consulting them, then trained Adam through teaching the names.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r7.anchor: melâikesine istişare eder gibi icmâlen tebliğ etmiş

ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.claim: The story clearly and subtly reveals how divine lordship manifests, recalls inward blessings embedded in human nature, and leads into the later direct-address warning.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#7/r9.anchor: rubûbiyyet-i ilâhiyenin tarz-ı tecellîsi büyük bir vuzuh ve pek ince bir üslup ile ifham edilerek

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.claim: Idh is a built temporal noun for past time, built because it resembles a particle in form or need.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.anchor: اسم ثنائي الوضع مبني لشبهه بالحرف وضعا أو افتقارا، وهو ظرف زمان للماضي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.claim: After idh comes a nominal or verbal clause; with a verbal clause, fronting its subject and annexing idh to a present-initial clause are poor usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.anchor: وما بعده جملة اسمية أو فعلية، وإذا كانت فعلية قبح تقديم الاسم على الفعل وإضافته إلى المصدرة بالمضارع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.claim: A present verb governed by idh is made past in meaning; idh remains adverbial unless another time noun is annexed to it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.anchor: وعمل المضارع فيه مما يجعل المضارع ماضيا، وهو ملازم للظرفية إلا أن يضاف إليه زمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.claim: Idh cannot be an object, causal or sudden particle, locative adverb, or redundant word, contrary to claims that it has those uses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.anchor: ولا يكون مفعولا به، ولا حرفا للتعليل أو المفاجأة، ولا ظرف مكان، ولا زائدة، خلافا لزاعمي ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda treats the mīm in malak as original, derives it from strength, and calls its plural malāʾika on faʿāʾila anomalous.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.anchor: ميمه أصلية وهو فعل من الملك، وهو القوة، ولا حذف فيه، وجمع على فعائلة شذوذا، قاله أبو عبيدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.claim: A competing account supposes malak came from malāk on faʿʿāl, although masculine and feminine faʿʿāl plurals on faʿāʾil are uncommon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.anchor: وكأنهم توهموا أنه ملاك على وزن فعال، وقد جمعوا فعالا المذكر، والمؤنث على فعائل قليلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.claim: One analysis reconstructs the original form as faʿʾal like shamʾal, then transfers the vowel and deletes letters; malʾak is also attested.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.anchor: وقيل وزنه في الأصل فعأل نحو شمأل ثم نقلوا الحركة وحذفوا، وقد جاء فيه ملأك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.claim: One derivation connects malak to lāka, to send: the original was malʾak, reduced by moving the vowel and deleting, with malāʾika on mufāʿala.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.anchor: فمنهم من قال: الفاء لام، والعين همزة، من لاك إذا أرسل، وهي لغة محكية، فملك أصله ملأك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r9.claim: Abu Ubayda gives the malʾak derivation, which Abū al-Fatḥ also selects; on this account malāʾika is mufāʿala.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r9.anchor: وهذا قول أبي عبيدة، واختاره أبو الفتح، وملائكة على هذا القول مفاعلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r10.claim: Another derivation makes the first radical hamza and the second lām from al-ʾalūka, message; māʾlak was inverted into malʾak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r10.anchor: ومنهم من قال الفاء همزة، والعين لام من الألوكة، وهي الرسالة، فيكون على هذا أصله مألكا، ويكون ملأك مقلوبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r11.claim: A third derivation links malak to lāka, to roll something in the mouth; the messenger carries a message in the mouth, with the middle radical deleted for ease.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r11.anchor: ومنهم من قال: الفاء لام، والعين واو، من لاك الشيء: أداره في فيه، وصاحب الرسالة يديرها في فيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r12.claim: On the third derivation, malāʾika is mufāʿala and its hamza replaces wāw, as in maṣāʾib.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r12.anchor: وملائكة على القول مفاعلة، والهمزة أبدلت من واو كما أبدلت في مصائب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r13.speaker: النضر بن شميل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r13.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl says Arabs neither derive nor inflect malak, whose etymology has escaped knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r13.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: الملك لا تشتق العرب فعله ولا تصرفه، وهو مما فات علمه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r14.claim: The tāʾ in malāʾika marks a feminine plural, or, according to another view, intensification; poetry uses the form without tāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221#2/r14.anchor: والتاء في الملائكة لتأنيث الجمع، وقيل: للمبالغة، وقد ورد بغير تاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r1.claim: An unnamed poet uses malāʾik without the tāʾ found in the ordinary plural malāʾika.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r1.anchor: أنا خالد صلت عليك الملائك خليفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r2.claim: Khalīfa is on faʿīla, which can be an intensive active form like al-ʿalīm or a passive form like al-naṭīḥa; its tāʾ can intensify.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r2.anchor: خليفة: فعيلة، وفعيلة تأتي بمعنى الفاعل للمبالغة، كالعليم، أو بمعنى المفعول كالنطيحة، والهاء للمبالغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r3.claim: Safk means pouring or spilling and is used only of blood; safaka, safika, and asfaka share the same meaning, with two present-tense patterns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r3.anchor: السفك: الصب والإراقة، لا يستعمل إلا في الدم، ويقال: سفك وسفك وأسفك بمعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r4.claim: Damāʾ is the plural of dam; its omitted final weak radical may be yāʾ or wāw, as shown by damiyān and damwān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r4.anchor: الدماء: جمع دم، ولامه ياء أو واو محذوفة لقولهم: دميان ودموان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r5.claim: The language also attests shortening and consonant doubling for dam, while grammarians differ over the deleted radical's original vowel pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r5.anchor: وقصره وتضعيفه مسموعان من لسان العرب. والمحذوف اللام، قيل: أصله فعل، وقيل: فعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r6.claim: Tasbīḥ means declaring God free of evil, is used only for God, and derives from sabḥ, running; the one who glorifies runs in that declaration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p222/r6.anchor: التسبح: تنزيه الله وتبرئته عن السوء، ولا يستعمل إلا لله تعالى، وأصله من السبح، وهو الجري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r15.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r15.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and Ibn Qutayba take idh as redundant; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this and criticizes their grammatical competence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r15.anchor: فذهب أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة إلى زيادتها، وهذا ليس بشيء، وكان أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة ضعيفين في علم النحو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r16.claim: An alternative reads idh as qad, yielding wa-qad qāla rabbuka, but Abū Ḥayyān rejects it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r16.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أنها بمعنى قد، التقدير: وقد قال ربك، وهذا ليس بشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r17.claim: Some parse idh as an object of an unspoken udhkur, but this wrongly removes it from its temporal-adverbial function.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p223/r17.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أنه منصوب نصب المفعول به باذكر، أي واذكر: إذ قال ربك، وهذا ليس بشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿAṭiyya, and others permit construing idh as an object of udhkur, though Abū Ḥayyān rejects that analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r1.anchor: وأجاز ذلك الزمخشري وابن عطية وناس قبلهما وبعدهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r2.claim: Some make idh nominative as the beginning of creation; others make it accusative as the beginning of creation occurred when God spoke.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r2.anchor: فقال بعضهم: هي في موضع رفع، التقدير: ابتداء خلقكم. وقال بعضهم في موضع نصب، التقدير: وابتداء خلقكم، إذ قال ربك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects both parses because human creation did not begin when God spoke to the angels, while a temporal predicate must occur within its time adverb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r3.anchor: وكلا هذين القولين لا تحرير فيه، لأن ابتداء خلقنا لم يكن وقت قول الله للملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r4.claim: Idh cannot be governed by the following qāla because idh is annexed to that clause, and an annexed complement cannot govern its annexer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r4.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أن إذ منصوب يقال بعدها، وليس بشيء، لأن إذ مضافة إلى الجملة بعدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r5.claim: Parsing idh under aḥyākum requires unsupported deletion; revival did not occur at that time, and it deletes a relative clause while retaining its complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r5.anchor: وهذا ليس بشيء لأنه حذف بغير دليل، وفيه أن الإحياء ليس واقعا في وقت قول الله للملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r6.claim: Making idh depend on khalaqakum from the earlier command requires a redundant wāw and separates the governor from it with long, syntactically independent verses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r6.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أنه معمول لخلقكم من قوله تعالى: اعبدوا ربكم الذي خلقكم إذ قال ربك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān counts eight such analyses and says the Qurʾān should be kept clear of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r7.anchor: فهذه ثمانية أقوال ينبغي أن ينزه كتاب الله عنها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r8.claim: He prefers governing idh with qālū: when God says He will place a khalifa, the angels respond, Would You place one there who corrupts? This is clear temporal usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r8.anchor: أي وقت قول الله للملائكة: إني جاعل في الأرض، قالوا أتجعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r9.claim: Attributing the speech to the Lord fits the prior mention of provision on earth and honors the Messenger through a special address that introduces humanity's origin and destiny.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r9.anchor: وإسناد القول إلى الرب في غاية من المناسبة والبيان، لأنه لما ذكر أنه خلق لهم ما في الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r10.claim: The shift from general address to the Prophet's particular address hints that he receives the greatest share of what follows; Abū Ḥayyān recalls his universal mission and precedence among prophets.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r10.anchor: وهذا تنويع في الخطاب، وخروج من الخطاب العام إلى الخطاب الخاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r11.claim: The lām in lil-malāʾika marks conveying speech, one of the lām's functions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r11.anchor: واللام في للملائكة: للتبليغ، وهو أحد المعاني التي جاءت لها اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r12.claim: The apparent reading makes the angels general; another group takes them specifically as earthly angels after the jinn or as those who fought with Iblis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r12.anchor: فظاهر لفظ الملائكة العموم. وقال بذلك قوم، وقال قوم هو عام المراد به الخصوص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r13.claim: The predicate after qāla is introduced by anna to stress that the reported statement is certain to occur.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p224/r13.anchor: ومعمول القول إني جاعل، وكان ذلك مصدرا بأن، لأن المقصود تأكيد الجملة المخبر بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r1.claim: Most Arabs open the hamza in anna after qāla only under stated conditions, while Banū Sulaym do so without conditions; an unnamed poet illustrates their usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r1.anchor: وبنو سليم يفتحونها بعده من غير شرط، وقال شاعرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r2.claim: Jāʿil is an active participle with future force; if it governs its object, that is better than annexation for Sibawayh, while al-Kisāʾī considers both equal and Abū Ḥayyān prefers annexation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r2.anchor: جاعل: اسم فاعل بمعنى الاستقبال، ويجوز إضافته للمفعول إلا إذا فصل بينهما كهذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r3.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r3.claim: Sībawayh says that when the active participle operates, using it as an operative form is better than annexing it to its object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r3.anchor: وإذا جاز إعماله، فهو أحسن من الإضافة، نص على ذلك سيبويه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r4.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī regards the operative and annexed constructions as equal; Abū Ḥayyān chooses annexation as better.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r4.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هما سواء، والذي أختاره أن الإضافة أحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r5.speaker: أبو روق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r5.claim: One view makes jaʿala mean create, taking one object; Abū Rawq holds this, close to reports from al-Ḥasan and Qatāda.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r5.anchor: أحدهما: أنه بمعنى الخلق، فيتعدى إلى واحد، قاله أبو روق، وقريب منه ما روي عن الحسن وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r6.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r6.claim: A second view, held by al-Farrāʾ, makes jaʿala mean turn into, taking two objects, with fī al-arḍ supplying the second; al-Zamakhsharī gives only this view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r6.anchor: والثاني: أنه بمعنى التصيير، فيتعدى إلى اثنين. والثاني هو في الأرض، أي: مصير في الأرض خليفة، قاله الفراء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r7.claim: Both meanings are possible, but creation is stronger: if the first jaʿala meant appointment, the angels' reply would have explicitly called its object a khalifa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r7.anchor: وكلا القولين سائغ، إلا أن الأول عندي أجود، لأنهم قالوا: أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r8.claim: There is no need to supply an omitted khalifa, since wording without ellipsis is better; the active participle conveys a settled state rather than gradual renewal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r8.anchor: ولا احتياج إلى تقدير خليفة لدلالة ما قبله عليه، لأنه إضمار، وكلام بغير إضمار أحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r9.claim: Whether jaʿala means create or appoint, Adam became khalifa only once, so the act was not repeated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r9.anchor: لم يكن إلا مرة واحدة، فلا تكرر فيه، إذ لم يخلقه أو لم يصيره خليفة إلا مرة واحدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r10.claim: The apparent sense of fī al-arḍ is the whole earth, as the majority hold; another view identifies the land as Mecca.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r10.anchor: وقوله: في الأرض: ظاهره الأرض كلها، وهو قول الجمهور. وقيل: أرض مكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r11.speaker: ابن سابط
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r11.claim: Ibn Sābiṭ transmits the Mecca interpretation as a report traced to the Prophet; Abū Ḥayyān says it should be followed if authentic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p226/r11.anchor: وروى ابن سابط هذا التفسير بأنها أرض مكة مرفوعا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فإن صح ذلك لم يعدل عنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r1.claim: An unnamed poem responds to claims that the Hijaz land is recent by saying the speaker seeks nothing beyond the earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r1.anchor: يقولون لي أرض الحجاز حديثة ... فقلت وما لي في سوى الأرض مطلب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r2.claim: The majority read khalīfa with fāʾ; it can mean an active successor or one replaced, and in the active sense one entrusted to act in another's place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: خليفة، بالفاء، ويحتمل أن يكون بمعنى الخالف، ويحتمل أن يكون بمعنى المخلوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r3.claim: One view identifies the khalifa as Adam, succeeding earthly angels, the jinn, Iblis in earthly rule, or God; Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās are cited for the last view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r3.anchor: أو عن الله تعالى، وهو قول ابن مسعود وابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r4.claim: The prophets are God's successors on earth, and Adam alone is named because he is the forefather of all successors, as tribal names can stand for the whole tribe.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r4.anchor: والأنبياء هم خلائف الله في أرضه، واقتصر على آدم لأنه أبو الخلائف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r5.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the khalifa is Adam's progeny, each generation replacing another; the singular can represent a collective, as in other Qurʾanic passages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r5.anchor: وقيل: ولد آدم لأنه يخلف بعضهم بعضا: إذا هلكت أمة خلفتها أخرى، قاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r6.claim: Another view treats khalifa as the title of anyone entrusted with governing earth's people and overseeing their interests, as Caesar, Kisrā, and Tubbaʿ are royal titles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r6.anchor: وقيل: الخليفة اسم لكل من انتقل إليه تدبير أهل الأرض والنظر في مصالحهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r7.claim: Views differ on Adam's delegated task: judging with truth and justice, or cultivating the earth through farming, construction, and canals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r7.anchor: وفي المستخلف فيه آدم قولان: أحدهما: الحكم بالحق والعدل. الثاني: عمارة الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r8.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Abū al-Barahsim ʿImrān read khalīqa with qāf, a variant whose meaning is clear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r8.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي وأبو البرهسم عمران: خليقة، بالقاف ومعناه واضح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r9.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says God first placed angels in heaven and jinn on earth; after the jinn corrupted and fought, Iblis led angels who expelled them and took earthly rule.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r9.anchor: وروي ما يدل على ذلك عن ابن عباس، وهو ما ملخصه: أن الله أسكن الملائكة السماء، والجن الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r10.claim: In Ibn ʿAbbās's account, God gave Iblis earthly and lower-heaven sovereignty and Paradise's treasury; pride led him to think he was God's most honored angel, so the announced successor would replace him and his host.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227/r10.anchor: وأعطى الله إبليس ملك الأرض وملك سماء الدنيا وخزانة الجنة، فكان يعبد تارة في الأرض وتارة في الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r1.claim: If the angels addressed are all angels, the statement exposes Iblis's pride and reveals what God already knew; reports are cited from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī through his teachers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r1.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس، وعن السدي، عن أشياخه: وأن يبلو طاعة الملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the announcement tests the angels' obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r2.anchor: وأن يبلو طاعة الملائكة، قاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r3.claim: Other proposed purposes are to expose angels' inability to encompass God's knowledge and to honor Adam in advance so they welcome him when created.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r3.anchor: أو أن يظهر عجزهم عن الإحاطة بعلمه، أو أن يعظم آدم بذكر الخلافة قبل وجوده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r4.claim: The announcement could teach that Adam was created to inhabit earth although his creation began in heaven, and model consulting learned people despite already knowing the answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r4.anchor: أو أن يعلمهم بخلقه ليسكن الأرض وإن كان ابتداء خلقه في السماء، وأن يعلمنا أن نشاور ذوي الأحلام منا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r5.claim: It could also lead angels to admit and revise assumptions about complete knowledge, show Adam's learning by asking him to name things, or teach obedience without requiring full understanding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r5.anchor: أو أن يتجاوز الخطاب بما ذكر فيحصل منهم الاعتراف والرجوع عما كانوا يظنون من كمال العلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the announcement reassured angels who feared the Fire and believed no creatures existed besides themselves; God said it was for those who disobey Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r6.anchor: قاله ابن زيد. وقال بعض أهل الإشارة في قوله: إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r7.speaker: أهل الإشارة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r7.claim: Some mystically inclined interpreters see divine care as preceding Adam's sin and surviving it: although disobedience caused expulsion, God did not strip Adam of honor or succession and later accepted him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r7.anchor: سابق العناية، لا يؤثر فيه حدوث الجناية، ولا يحط عن رتبة الولاية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r8.claim: An unnamed poem illustrates how a beloved's many virtues outweigh one fault; another poem likewise says a single lapse should not provoke blame.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r8.anchor: وإذا الحبيب أتى بذنب واحد ... جاءت محاسنه بألف شفيع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says God singled Adam out by announcing a khalifa, unlike the creation of the heavens, throne, or Paradise, thereby honoring and distinguishing him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r9.anchor: ويقال إن الله سبحانه خلق ما خلق ولم يقل في شيء منها ما قال في حديث آدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r10.claim: He reiterates that the preferred governor of idh is qālū, with the following clause أتجعل as its governed complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r10.anchor: قالوا تقدم أن الاختيار في العامل إذ هو، قالوا: ومعموله الجملة من قوله: أتجعل؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r11.claim: Because angels neither know the unseen nor speak first, their question must rest on prior information or a premise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p227#2/r11.anchor: ولما كانت الملائكة لا تعلم الغيب ولا تسبق بالقول، لم يكن قولهم: أتجعل فيها الآية، إلا عن نبأ ومقدمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r1.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r1.claim: The interrogative hamza also conveys astonishment, according to Makkī and others, at God's appointing a successor who would disobey or be disobeyed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r1.anchor: فهو قد صحبه معنى التعجب، قاله مكي وغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the question as magnifying and honoring the appointment and the resulting disobedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو استفهام على طريق الاستعظام، والإكبار للاستخلاف والعصيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reads the question as a request for confirmation, illustrated by an unnamed poet's rhetorical question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو استفهام معناه التقرير، قاله أبو عبيدة، قال الشاعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r4.claim: Under the first three readings, angels' prior knowledge may come from God, the Preserved Tablet, observation of other created beings, analogy with earlier earthly inhabitants, or inference from the word khalifa and its association with injustice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r4.anchor: وعلى هذه الأقوال يكون علمهم بذلك قد سبق، إما بإخبار من الله، أو بمشاهدة في اللوح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r5.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r5.claim: A fourth view from Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā takes the question plainly: will this successor be like the earlier jinn who inhabited the earth?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو استفهام محض، قاله أحمد بن يحيى، وقدره: أتجعل هذا الخليفة على طريقة من تقدم من الجن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r6.speaker: أبو الفضل التجلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r6.claim: Abū al-Faḍl al-Tajallī paraphrases the question as asking whether God will instead appoint one who does not cause corruption.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r6.anchor: وفسره أبو الفضل التجلي: أي أم تجعل من لا يفسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r7.claim: Another proposed complement contrasts the question with the angels' state: will You change us, though we glorify You?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r7.anchor: وقدره غيرهما، ونحن نسبح بحمدك، أم تتغير؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r8.claim: For surprise, magnification, or confirmation, the question has no complement; for the plain-question view it is من يفسد, while the other view makes the circumstantial clause its complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r8.anchor: فعلى الأقوال الثلاثة الأول لا معادل للاستفهام، لأنه مذهوب به مذهب التعجب أو الاستعظام أو التقرير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r9.claim: The majority read yasfiku with kasra on fāʾ and a nominative kāf; other transmitted readings use ḍamma, the forms from asfaka or doubled safaka, or an accusative kāf from Ibn Hurmuz.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p228/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ويسفك بكسر الفاء ورفع الكاف. وقرأ أبو حياة وابن أبي عبلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r1.claim: The cited poem pairs being bright-eyed with spending a night as if stung, illustrating that the two actions can occur together.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r1.anchor: معناه: أيكون منك مبيت ريان مع مبيتي منك بكذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the accusative a waṣr wāw: the conjunction redirects a verb from its expected mood to accusative, as in other Qurʾanic readings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r2.anchor: وقال أبو محمد بن عطية: النصب بواو الصرف قال: كأنه قال من يجمع أن يفسد وأن يسفك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya's waṣr-wāw analysis because Basran grammarians do not recognize it; they posit an implicit an after wāw, and he criticizes Ibn ʿAṭiyya's preference.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r3.anchor: والنصب بواو الصرف ليس من مذاهب البصريين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r4.claim: Because yufsid is affirmative and does not imply every kind of corruption, the angels name bloodshed as the gravest form, which destroys God's created bodies.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r4.anchor: ولما كانت الصلة يفسد، وهو فعل في سياق الإثبات، فلا يدل على التعميم في الفساد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r5.claim: Repeating fīhā after corruption highlights the reversal of a place of worship into one of wrongdoing; the parallel is 2:11, while omission after bloodshed avoids three repetitions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r5.anchor: وكرر فيها لأن في ذلك تنبيها على أن ما كان محلا للعبادة وطاعة الله كيف يصير محلا للفساد؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r6.claim: The circumstantial clause wa-naḥnu nusabbiḥu has several reported senses: divine transcendence (Qatāda), remembrance aloud (al-Mufaḍḍal), humility (Ibn al-Anbārī), or prayer (Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās).
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r6.anchor: ونحن نسبح: جملة حالية، والتسبيح التنزيه، قاله قتادة: أو رفع الصوت بذكر الله تعالى، قاله المفضل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p229/r7.claim: Mujāhid interprets tasbīḥ as magnifying God; other views make it a special angelic liturgy or the formula subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r1.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r1.claim: In a report from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit through Abū Dharr, the Prophet says the best words are what God chose for angels or servants: subḥān Allāh wa-bi-ḥamdih.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r1.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت، عن أبي ذر، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل: أي الكلام أفضل قال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r2.claim: In bi-ḥamdika, the bāʾ can mark accompaniment: the angels glorify while joined by praise, a circumstantial phrase within another circumstantial phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r2.anchor: بحمدك: في موضع الحال، والباء فيه للحال، أي نسبح ملتبسين بحمدك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r3.claim: Alternatively, bāʾ marks cause: praise arises from enabling and beneficence, so the angels glorify because God grants them good; ḥamd is annexed to its object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r3.anchor: وقيل: الباء للسبب، أي بسبب حمدك، والحمد هو الثناء، والثناء ناشيء عن التوفيق للخير والإنعام على المثنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r4.claim: The Basrans allow omission of the subject in a verbal noun construction; unlike some grammarians, Abū Ḥayyān says this is not forbidden because generic nouns do not take pronouns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r4.anchor: والفاعل عند البصريين محذوف في باب المصدر، وإن كان من قواعدهم أن الفاعل لا يحذف وليس ممنوع في المصدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r5.claim: There is no need to reorder the phrase as though bi-ḥamdika interrupts wa-nuqaddisu; word order inversion is limited to poetic necessity, and praise naturally accompanies tasbīḥ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r5.anchor: ولا حاجة تدعو إلى أن في الكلام تقديما وتأخيرا، كما ذهب إليه بعضهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r6.claim: Wa-nuqaddisu laka reinforces wa-nusabbiḥu because purification and declaring God free of evil are close in meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r6.anchor: وجاء قوله بعد: ونقدس لك كالتوكيد، لأن التقديس هو: التطهير، والتسبيح هو: التنزيه والتبرئة من السوء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r7.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others interpret taqdīs as purifying themselves for God from impurities; Abū Muslim instead makes its object their deeds, purified from sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r7.anchor: ومفعوله أنفسنا لك من الأدناس، قاله الضحاك وغيره، أو أفعالنا من المعاصي، قاله أبو مسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r8.speaker: مجاهد وأبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r8.claim: Mujāhid and Abū Ṣāliḥ understand taqdīs as magnifying and glorifying God; other reports interpret it as prayer or purification from human deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r8.anchor: أو المعنى: نكبرك ونعظمك. قاله مجاهد وأبو صالح، أو نصلي لك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r9.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās says the angels mean that they purify themselves from the deeds of Adam's descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r9.anchor: أو نتطهر من أعمالهم يعنون بني آدم. حكي ذلك عن ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r10.claim: Another spiritual interpretation takes taqdīs as cleansing hearts from attention to anything besides God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r10.anchor: أو نطهر قلوبنا عن الالتفات إلى غيرك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r11.claim: The lām in laka may be extra, purposive, attached to nuqaddisu or nusabbiḥu, transitive, or explanatory with an omitted taqdīsuna laka; Abū Ḥayyān prefers the transitive function.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p230/r11.anchor: والأحسن أن تكون معدية للفعل، كهي في قوله: يسبح لله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r1.claim: He rejects reading the angels’ glorification as a question with an omitted interrogative and an omitted alternative, since the syntax gives no evidence for either deletion.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r2.claim: Islamic doctrine holds angels immune from sin and objection; this premise led exegetes to interpret their words in a linguistically plausible way, against a minority of Hashwiyya.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r2.anchor: وكان من القواعد الشرعية والعقائد الإسلامية عصمة الملائكة من المعاصي والاعتراض، لم يخالف في ذلك إلا طائفة من الحشوية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r3.speaker: بعض أهل الإشارات
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r3.claim: Some allusive interpreters say the angels thought God had consulted them about keeping the vicegerency with worshippers, so they advised against appointing those who would corrupt and kill; God decides.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r3.anchor: وقال بعض أهل الإشارات: الملائكة لما توهموا أن الله تعالى أقامهم في مقام المشورة بأن لهم وجه المصلحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r4.speaker: صفي الدين أبو عبد الله الحسين ابن الوزير أبي الحسن علي بن أبي المنصور الخزرجي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r4.claim: The author of Fakk al-Azrar assigns the apparent objection to Iblis and the glorification and obedience to the angels, who had first spoken in a collective answer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r4.anchor: صاحب (كتاب فك الأزرار) ، وهو الشيخ صفي الدين أبو عبد الله الحسين ابن الوزير أبي الحسن علي بن أبي المنصور الخزرجي، قال: في ذلك الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan calls that division a good interpretation, analogous to a collective quotation whose different statements belong to different groups.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r5.anchor: وهو تأويل حسن، وصار شبيها بقوله تعالى: وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى تهتدوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r6.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r6.claim: One view takes the angels’ self-description as permission to praise one’s qualifications before an appointing authority when seeking office, if one can avoid injustice and sees a benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p231/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى جواز التمدح إلى من له الحكم في التولية ممن يقصد الولاية، إذا أمن على نفسه الجور والحيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r1.claim: The angels’ example permits Joseph to seek office and describe his own qualifications, as he did when asking to oversee Egypt’s storehouses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r1.anchor: ولذلك جاز ليوسف، على نبينا وعليه السلام، طلبه الولاية، ومدح نفسه بما فيها فقال: اجعلني على خزائن الأرض إني حفيظ عليم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r2.claim: He prefers parsing ما after أعلم as a relative pronoun and rejects treating it as an indefinite adjective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r2.anchor: وما مفعولة بها موصولة، قيل: أو نكرة موصوفة، وقد تقدم: أنا لا نختار، كونها نكرة موصوفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r3.speaker: مكي بن أبي طالب والمهدوي وغيرهما
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r3.claim: Makkī, al-Mahdawī, and others allow أعلم as an active participle; on that parse ما may be genitive by annexation or accusative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r3.anchor: وأجاز مكي بن أبي طالب والمهدوي وغيرهما أن تكون أعلم هنا اسما بمعنى فاعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r4.claim: Others parse أعلم as a comparative meaning more knowing than you, with ما governed as the object of an implied verb meaning I know.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p232/r4.anchor: وأجاز بعضهم أن تكون أفعل التفضيل. والتقدير: أعلم منكم، وما منصوبة بفعل محذوف يدل عليه أعلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r1.claim: He rejects the proposed comparative parse because it requires omitting both the comparison phrase meaning than you and the verb governing the relative pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r1.anchor: وهذا القول فيه خروج عن الظاهر وادعاء حذفين: أحدهما: حذف المفضل عليه وهو منكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda allows أفعل to mean an active participle, but the grammarians reject that analysis; Abu Hayyan sides with the grammarians.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r2.anchor: ادعاء أن أفعل تأتي بمعنى فاعل، وهذا قال به أبو عبيدة من المتقدمين، وخالفه النحويون وردوا عليه قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r3.speaker: النحويون المتقدمون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r3.claim: The earlier grammarians maintain that أفعل always carries a comparative sense, and Abu Hayyan endorses their position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r3.anchor: والصحيح ما ذهب إليه النحويون المتقدمون من كون أفعل لا يخلو من التفضيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r4.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r4.claim: Some later grammarians allow أفعل to occur without comparison, treating it as an active participle or an adjective of inherent quality.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r4.anchor: وإن كان يوجد في كلام بعض المتأخرين أن أفعل قد يخلو من التفضيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r5.speaker: أبو العباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r5.claim: Abu al-Abbas regards comparative-free use of أفعل as productive, while the cited grammarian says the sounder rule is to limit it to attested usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r5.anchor: مؤولا باسم فاعل أو صفة مشبهة، مطرد عند أبي العباس، والأصح قصره على السماع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r6.claim: Even grammarians who allow comparative-free أفعل do not all let it govern like an active participle; Abu Hayyan rejects inventing such unattested constructions by analogy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r6.anchor: والقائلون بوجود ذلك لا يقولون بإعماله عمل اسم الفاعل إلا بعضهم، فأجاز ذلك، والصحيح ما ذهب إليه النحويون المتقدمون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r7.claim: He insists that the apparent reading is the present-tense verb أعلم and warns against imposing unattested grammatical patterns on Quranic wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r7.anchor: وكيف يعدل في كتاب الله عن الشيء الظاهر الواضح من كون أعلم فعلا مضارعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي عن أشياخه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī from his teachers say God knew what was in Iblis’s mind despite his rebellion and disobedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r8.anchor: علمه ما في نفس إبليس مع البغي والمعصية، قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي عن أشياخه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r9.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r9.claim: Qatāda says God knew that prophets and righteous people would descend from the vicegerent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r9.anchor: أو علمه بأنه سيكون من ذلك الخليفة أنبياء وصالحون، قاله قتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says God knew which jinn and humans would fill Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p233/r10.anchor: أو علمه بمن يملأ جهنم من الجنة والناس، قاله ابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r1.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God knows outcomes: trials may lead someone thought obedient into sin, or someone thought sinful into obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r1.anchor: ومن تظنون أنه عاص فيؤديه الابتلاء إلى الطاعة فيطيع، قاله الزجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r2.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r2.claim: Another explanation is God’s complete knowledge of outward and inward matters, subtle and evident, near and distant, good and bad, across changing conditions and times.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r2.anchor: علمه بظواهر الأمور وباطنها، جليها ودقيقها، عاجلها وآجلها، صالحها وفاسدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r3.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r3.claim: Another explanation contrasts God’s knowledge, gained without acquisition, inquiry, reflection, or thought, with human knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r3.anchor: أو علمه بغير اكتساب ولا نظر ولا تدبر ولا فكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r4.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r4.claim: One proposed explanation is that God knew Iblis was among the angels addressed.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r5.speaker: قول غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r5.claim: One proposed explanation is that God knew the angels were magnifying themselves through their glorification and sanctification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r5.anchor: أو علمه باستعظامكم أنفسكم بالتسبيح والتقديس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r6.claim: The wording leaves unspecified what God knows beyond the angels’ knowledge; that claim requires their submission and acceptance of his decision because his knowledge encompasses what no scholar can encompass.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r6.anchor: وأبهم في إخباره الأشياء التي يعلمها دونهم، فإذا كان كذلك، فإخباره بأنه يجعل في الأرض خليفة يقتضي التسليم له والرجوع إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r7.claim: He says the best explanation of the unspecified knowledge is God’s statement that he knows the unseen of the heavens and earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p234/r7.anchor: والأحسن أن يفسر هذا المبهم بما أخبر به تعالى عنه من قوله، قال: ألم أقل لكم إني أعلم غيب السماوات والأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.claim: In Arabic, successive quoted statements normally need no conjunction marking sequence because their semantic order is clear; he cites the dialogue about the angels and Adam and many Quranic examples.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240/r2.anchor: والجملة المفتتحة بالقول إذا كانت مرتبا بعضها على بعض في المعنى، فالأصح في لسان العرب أنها لا يؤتى فيها بحرف ترتب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r5.claim: The angels’ questioning lacked the pure submission appropriate to them; obedience without understanding the wisdom or asking in surprise would better suit their purity and complete qualities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p240#2/r5.anchor: وكان الامتثال والتسليم، بغير تعجب ولا استفهام، أليق بمقامهم لطهارة ذواتهم وكمال صفاتهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r1.claim: God drew out the angels’ concealed self-admiration in their worship, making them disclose their hidden thoughts by citing their glorification.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r1.anchor: استخرج الحق سبحانه منهم ما استكن في قلوبهم من استعظام طاعاتهم والملاحظة إلى أفعالهم بهذا الخطاب

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r2.claim: Knowledge is a greater merit than action: the angels had more and earlier worship, while Adam had more knowledge, which established his rank.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r2.anchor: الفضيلة بالعلم أتم من الفضيلة بالفعل

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r3.claim: God’s answer that He knows what the angels do not know refers to His forgiveness of Adam’s descendants.

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r4.claim: The angels’ glorification displays their deeds and merit, while forgiveness of human sins displays the Creator’s generosity and mercy.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r4.anchor: في تسبيحهم إظهار فعلهم واشتهار خصائصهم وفضلهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r5.claim: God needs no worship; their glorification establishes their own praise, while His forgiveness establishes the Creator’s praise.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r5.anchor: والحق سبحانه غني عن طاعات كل مطيع

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r6.claim: God knows the believers’ pure beliefs and keen inward protection of their covenantal love, even when disobedience stains their outward state.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r6.anchor: من صفاء عقائد المؤمنين منهم في محبتنا

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r7.claim: God knows His love for them and the inward secrets He hides in them, unlike angels who openly display their states.

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r8.claim: God knows humans’ humbled, broken hearts despite their bad deeds, whereas angels’ hearts become proud when they display glorification.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r8.anchor: من انكسار قلوبهم وإن ارتكبوا قبيح أفعالهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r9.claim: The brokenness of servants’ hearts carries powerful standing with God, despite their outwardly disobedient condition.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r9.anchor: وإن لانكسار قلوب العباد عندنا لذماما قويا

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r10.claim: Angelic glorification has no significance without God’s favor, and human sins cause no harm when met by His pardon.

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r11.claim: God clothed the angels in obedience and purification, but clothed humans in pardon, mercy, generosity, and forgiveness.

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r12.claim: If God’s protection made the angels fortunate, His mercy has also reached human beings.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r12.anchor: إن أسعدتكم عصمتي فلقد أدركتهم رحمتي

QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r13.claim: The angels’ goodness is secured by infallibility, while human wrongdoers are immersed in mercy.
QUSHAYRI:v1p34/r13.anchor: لئن كان محسنكم عتيق العصمة فإن مجرمهم غريق الرحمة

DURR-FULL:v1p121/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r6.claim: The angels' disclosed speech was their question about placing someone in the earth who would cause corruption there.
DURR-FULL:v1p121/r6.anchor: وفي قوله {وأعلم ما تبدون} قال: قولهم {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها}

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r1.speaker: معمر بن المثنى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r1.claim: Maʿmar ibn al-Muthannā says the particle idh is redundant, yielding the sense “and your Lord said.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj calls Abū ʿUbayda’s claim that idh is redundant an audacious interpretation; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says all exegetes rejected it.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r3.claim: The majority reject redundancy and connect idh to an implied command: “remember when your Lord said.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r3.anchor: ليست بزائدة وإنما هي معلقة بفعل مقدر تقديره واذكر إذ قال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r4.claim: They also relate the passage to the prior statement that God created everything on earth for humanity, with creation beginning when He addressed the angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r4.anchor: خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا الآية، يقتضي أن يكون التقدير وابتداء خلقكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r5.claim: God’s possessive address to Muḥammad, “your Lord,” and the second-person suffix honor him and display special favor toward him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r5.anchor: إضافة رب إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ومخاطبته بالكاف تشريف منه له

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r6.claim: The singular malak is derived from malāk on the pattern mafʿal, from lāka, “to send”; malāʾika is its plural on the pattern mafāʿila.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r6.anchor: والملائكة واحدها ملك أصله ملاك على وزن مفعل من لاك إذا أرسل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r7.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r7.claim: Another etymology derives malak from maʾlak, from alaka, “to send,” and parses malāʾika as its plural.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r7.anchor: أصل ملك مألك، من ألك إذا أرسل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r8.speaker: عدي بن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r8.claim: The poet ʿAdī ibn Zayd uses maʾlakan as evidence for the alternative derivation of malak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r8.anchor: أبلغ النعمان عني مألكا ... أنه قد طال حبسي وانتظاري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r9.claim: Both laʾaka and alaka are attested; the hamza shifts after the lām, producing the form maʿfal and plural maʿāfila.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r9.anchor: اللغتان مسموعتان لأك وألك، قلبت فيه الهمزة بعد اللام فجاء وزنه معفل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r10.speaker: ابن كيسان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r10.claim: Ibn Kaysān derives malak from malaka, treating the hamza as extra as in shamʾal from shamal, and gives the plural pattern faʿāʾila.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r10.anchor: هو من ملك يملك، والهمزة فيه زائدة كما زيدت في شمأل من شمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r11.claim: A poetic line preserves the word malʾak in its original form, supporting the underlying hamza analysis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r11.anchor: فلست لأنسي ولكن لملأك ... تنزل من جو السماء يصوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r12.speaker: ابن كيسان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r12.claim: In ordinary speech the hamza is eased and its vowel transferred to the lām or ʿayn; the tāʾ in malāʾika marks a nonliteral feminine plural or intensification, with the first account clearer to Ibn ʿAṭiyya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r12.anchor: والهاء في ملائكة لتأنيث الجموع غير حقيقي، وقيل هي للمبالغة كعلامة ونسابة، والأول أبين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r13.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r13.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the hamza in malāʾika is inserted because its singular is malak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r13.anchor: الهمزة في ملائكة مجتلبة لأن واحدها ملك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Abū ʿUbayda’s explanation is the direction toward which Ibn Kaysān inclined.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116/r14.anchor: فهذا الذي نحا إليه ابن كيسان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r1.claim: Mujāhid, Abū Ṣāliḥ, and others explain “we sanctify You” as magnifying God and declaring His remembrance free of anything unworthy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r1.anchor: ونقدس لك معناه ونقدسك أي نعظمك ونطهر ذكرك عما لا يليق به. قاله مجاهد وأبو صالح وغيرهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r2.claim: Some interpret “we sanctify You” as “we pray to You”; Ibn ʿAṭiyya judges this weak.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r3.claim: For “I know what you do not know,” the more apparent parsing makes aʿlam a future verb and mā its direct object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r3.anchor: الأظهر أن أعلم فعل مستقبل، وما في موضع نصب به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r4.claim: An alternative parses aʿlam as a noun with mā in the genitive as its complement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r4.anchor: وقيل أعلم اسم، وما في موضع خفض بالإضافة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r5.speaker: سيبويه والخليل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r5.claim: Sībawayh and al-Khalīl say an afʿal form used as an indefinite proper name does not take nunation; al-Akhfash allows it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r5.anchor: فسيبويه والخليل لا يصرفانه، والأخفش يصرفه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Iblīs became proud after God appointed him keeper of the lowest heaven, taking the honor as a special merit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r6.anchor: كان إبليس- لعنه الله- قد أعجب ودخله الكبر لما جعله الله خازن السماء الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r7.claim: A second report from Ibn ʿAbbās says Iblīs’s pride arose after God sent him to defeat and kill the corrupt jinn with his army.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r7.anchor: لما بعثه الله إلى قتل الجن الذين كانوا أفسدوا في الأرض فهزمهم وقتلهم بجنده

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r8.claim: Iblīs took his success as proof of superiority and, in relation to Adam, incurred unbelief and disobedience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r8.anchor: واعتقد أن ذلك لمزية له واستحقب الكفر والمعصية في جانب آدم عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r9.claim: On Ibn ʿAbbās’s account, God’s “I know what you do not know” refers to the discordant pride hidden within Iblīs, unknown to the angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r9.anchor: وهي لا تعلم أن في نفس إبليس خلاف ذلك. قال الله لهم إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون يعني ما في نفس إبليس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r10.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r10.claim: Qatāda says God meant the future virtuous deeds of prophets, excellent people, and obedient descendants of Adam, which the angels did not know.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p118/r10.anchor: يعني أفعال الفضلاء من بني آدم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r10.claim: God’s announcement that He would place a successor on earth tests the angels, brings about their response, and instructs them through Adam’s teaching and honor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p121/r10.anchor: هذا منه امتحان لهم واختبار ليقع منهم ما وقع ويؤدبهم تعالى من تعليم آدم وتكريمه

NAHHAS:v1p208/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p208/r1.claim: An unattributed poetic line occurs in the preceding discussion of ما; the excerpt gives no poet or explicit gloss for the line.

NAHHAS:v1p208/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p208/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p208/r2.claim: Mīm may assimilate into mīm. ما is accusative with أعلم if verbal; if nominal, it may be genitive by annexation or accusative, with tanwīn dropped because the form is diptote.
NAHHAS:v1p208/r2.anchor: ويجوز إدغام الميم في الميم و ما في موضع نصب بأعلم إذا جعلته فعلا

RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r6.claim: In the exchange with the angels, God answers their concern about human corruption by saying He knows what they do not, setting knowledge itself as the relevant answer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p182#2/r6.anchor: لما قال : { إني جاعل فى الارض خليفة } ( البقرة : 30 ) قالت الملائكة : { أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها }

RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r1.claim: God answers the angels through knowledge rather than power, will, hearing, sight, or other attributes, showing knowledge’s superior rank among divine perfections.
RAZI-FULL:v2p183/r1.anchor: وإنما جعل صفة العلم جوابا لهم وذلك يدل على أن صفات الجلال والكمال

RAZI-FULL:v25p73#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p73#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p73#2/r5.claim: Being God’s servant is a greater honor than earthly caliphate: Adam’s caliph title did not deter Satan, but Satan has no power over those God calls His servants.
RAZI-FULL:v25p73#2/r5.anchor: الخطاب بعبادي أشرف منازل المكلف ، وذلك لأن الله تعالى لما خلق آدم آتاه اسما عظيما وهو اسم الخلافة كما قال تعالى : { إني جاعل فى الارض خليفة }

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.claim: Eve enters without an account of her origin; although primordial Adam represents all humanity, male and female, the Quran does not explain how this Adam becomes the first couple.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r47.anchor: the Quran does not explicitly discuss the process by which this primordial Adam is differentiated into the first male and female

TABATABAI:2:30-32/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r1.claim: The angels infer that an earthly successor must be numerous and socially organized, while embodied life and competition make corruption and bloodshed unavoidable.
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r1.anchor: ففهموا من هناك أن الخلافة المرادة لا تقع في الأرض إلا بكثرة من الأفراد ونظام اجتماعي بينهم يفضي بالآخرة إلى الفساد والسفك،

TABATABAI:2:30-32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r2.claim: A vicegerent must represent God in all existential affairs, effects, laws, and governance; the flawed earthly being appears unfit to represent the perfectly pure God.
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r2.anchor: والخلافة وهي قيام شيء مقام آخر لا تتم إلا بكون الخليفة حاكيا للمستخلف في جميع شؤونه الوجودية وآثاره وأحكامه وتدابيره بما هو مستخلف،

TABATABAI:2:30-32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
