TABATABAI:2:30-32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r3.claim: The angels ask to understand what they do not know; this is clarification rather than objection, as their acknowledgment that God is All-knowing and Wise accepts His wisdom.
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r3.anchor: وهذا الكلام من الملائكة في مقام تعرف ما جهلوه واستيضاح ما أشكل عليهم من أمر هذا الخليفة، وليس من الاعتراض والخصومة في شيء،

TABATABAI:2:30-32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r4.claim: They reason that the successor's purpose is to glorify and sanctify God, but earthly life draws the human toward evil; they claim angels already fulfill that purpose and ask why appoint a human.
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r4.anchor: فملخص قولهم يعود إلى أن جعل الخلافة إنما هو لأجل أن يحكي الخليفة مستخلفه بتسبيحه بحمده وتقديسه له بوجوده،

TABATABAI:2:30-32/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r5.claim: The angels offer themselves as God's successors, or ask Him to appoint them, questioning the benefit of an earthly successor.
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r5.anchor: فنحن خلفائك أو فاجعلنا خلفاء لك، فما فائدة جعل هذه الخلافة الأرضية لك؟

TABATABAI:2:30-32/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r7.claim: Divine vicegerency is shared by Adam's descendants; teaching the names deposits knowledge in humanity so its effects can unfold gradually and become actual through guidance.
TABATABAI:2:30-32/r7.anchor: فالخلافة غير مقصورة على شخص آدم عليه السلام بل بنوه يشاركونه فيها من غير اختصاص، ويكون معنى تعليم الأسماء إيداع هذا العلم في الإنسان بحيث يظهر منه آثاره تدريجا دائما

TABATABAI:2:30-33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r1.claim: Qur'anic references to peoples succeeding earlier peoples support the view that earthly vicegerency is general to humanity, not exclusive to Adam.
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r1.anchor: إذ جعلكم خلفاء من بعد قوم نوح الأعراف 69، وقوله تعالى ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض يونس 14،

TABATABAI:2:30-33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r2.claim: God does not deny that the earthly successor will cause corruption and bloodshed, nor does He dispute the angels' own glorification and sanctification.
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r2.anchor: لم ينف عن خليفة الأرض الفساد وسفك الدماء، ولا كذب الملائكة في دعواهم التسبيح والتقديس،

TABATABAI:2:30-33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r3.claim: Instead, God reveals a divine secret that angels cannot bear but the earthly successor can; this capacity makes up for the successor's corruption and bloodshed.
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r3.anchor: بل إنما أبدى شيئا آخر وهو أن هناك أمرا لا يقدر الملائكة على حمله ولا تتحمله، ويتحمله هذا الخليفة الأرضي

TABATABAI:2:30-33/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r6.claim: The setting implies the angels claimed the vicegerency and assumed Adam lacked it; testing their knowledge shows Adam's fitness and their lack of it.
TABATABAI:2:30-33/r6.anchor: فإن هذا السياق يعطي أنهم ادعوا الخلافة وأذعنوا بانتفائها عن آدم وكان اللازم أن يعلم الخليفة بالأسماء

TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r1.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r1.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet's account of the first creation: the Prophet's light produces all good, is divided into stages creating the Throne, Kursi, pen, Tablet, Paradise, angels, sun, moon, and virtues; its drops create 124,000 prophetic spirits, whose breaths create the spirits of friends, martyrs, and righteous people.
TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r1.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال قلت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أول شيء خلق الله ما هو؟ فقال نور نبيك يا جابر

TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says many mutually reinforcing reports witness to the thesis already presented and warns against dismissing these traditions as Sufi fabrications.
TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r2.anchor: والأخبار في هذه المعاني كثيرة، متظافرة، وأنت إذا أجلت نظرة التأمل والإمعان فيها وجدتها شواهد على ما قدمناه،

TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r3.claim: He argues that creation contains hidden realities: even the natural world, its narrowest and lowest domain, continually yields new unknowns as scientific inquiry uncovers facts.
TABATABAI:2:30-33#2/r3.anchor: وكلما لاح لهم معلوم واحد بان لهم مجاهيل كثيرة، وهي عالم الطبيعة أضيق العوالم وأخسها فما ظنك بما ورائها،

THALABI:v1p174/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p174/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p174/r1.claim: Thalabi reads the opening as ‘And your Lord said’ in the past tense.
THALABI:v1p174/r1.anchor: وإذ قال ربك يعني: وقد قال

THALABI:v1p174/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p174/r2.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v1p174/r2.claim: An alternative takes the phrase as an instruction to remember when the Lord spoke.
THALABI:v1p174/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه: واذكر إذ قال ربك

THALABI:v1p174/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p174/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p174/r3.claim: Idh and idha mark time: idh normally refers to the past and idha to the future, though they can exchange places.
THALABI:v1p174/r3.anchor: و (إذ) و (إذا) حرفا توقيت، إلا أن (إذ) للماضي و (إذا) للمستقبل، وقد يوضع أحدهما موضع الآخر

THALABI:v1p174/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p174/r4.speaker: المبرد
THALABI:v1p174/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad says future-form verbs after idh refer to past events, citing ‘when they plotted against you’ and ‘when he says.’
THALABI:v1p174/r4.anchor: قال المبرد: إذا جاء (إذ) مع المستقبل كان معناه ماضيا نحو قوله: وإذ يمكر بك وإذ يقول

THALABI:v1p174/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p174/r5.speaker: المبرد
THALABI:v1p174/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad says idha with a past-form verb can refer to the future, citing Qur’anic examples and a poem whose idh means ‘will reward.’
THALABI:v1p174/r5.anchor: وإذا إذ جاء مع الماضي كان معناه مستقبلا كقوله: فإذا جاءت الطامة الكبرى

THALABI:v1p174/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p174/r6.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v1p174/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses past idh for a future reward; Thalabi glosses the line as ‘he will reward him.’
THALABI:v1p174/r6.anchor: وقال الشاعر: ثم جزاه الله عنا إذ جزا … جنات عدن والعلا إلى العلا أي يجزيه

THALABI:v1p174/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p174/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p174/r7.claim: The angels addressed here were those who had been on earth.

THALABI:v1p174/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p174/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p174/r8.claim: Malak means messenger; the singular is malak, from malik, and the plural is malaika, from terms for message or messenger.
THALABI:v1p174/r8.anchor: والملائكة: الرسل، واحدها ملك، وأصله: مالك، وجمعه: ملائكة

THALABI:v1p177/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p177/r1.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v1p177/r1.claim: Mujahid says God knew Iblis would disobey and created him for that disobedience.
THALABI:v1p177/r1.anchor: ابن نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله: إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون قال: علم من إبليس المعصية وخلقه لها

THALABI:v1p177#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p177#2/r1.speaker: سلمان
THALABI:v1p177#2/r1.claim: Salman defines a caliph as one who rules justly, distributes equally, cares for subjects like family, and judges by God’s Book.
THALABI:v1p177#2/r1.anchor: فقال سلمان: الخليفة الذي يعدل في الرعية ويقسم بينهم بالسوية ويشفق عليهم شفقة الرجل على أهله

THALABI:v1p177#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p177#2/r2.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v1p177#2/r2.claim: Ka‘b says he thought no one present besides himself knew the difference between caliph and king, then praises Salman for wisdom, knowledge, and justice.
THALABI:v1p177#2/r2.anchor: فقال كعب: ما كنت أحسب أن في المجلس أحدا يعرف الخليفة من الملك غيري

THALABI:v1p177#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p177#2/r3.speaker: سلمان
THALABI:v1p177#2/r3.claim: Salman tells Umar that a ruler who collects even a little Muslim tax and spends it wrongly is a king; Umar weeps at the answer.
THALABI:v1p177#2/r3.anchor: وروى زاذان عن سلمان: إن عمر قال له: أملك أنا أم خليفة؟ فقال سلمان: إن أنت جبيت من أرض المسلمين

THALABI:v1p177#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p177#2/r4.speaker: معاوية
THALABI:v1p177#2/r4.claim: Mu‘awiya says caliphate means upholding truth, ruling justly, and directing people to God’s command, rather than accumulating or distributing wealth.
THALABI:v1p177#2/r4.anchor: وعن يونس: إن معاوية كان يقول إذا جلس على المنبر: أيها الناس إن الخلافة ليست لجمع المال ولا تفريقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj transmits an unnamed explanation: God told angels humanity would corrupt and shed blood; they asked why, expecting creatures to glorify and purify God like them, and the disclosure confirmed divine knowledge of the unseen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r1.anchor: وقال الزجاج حكاية عن غيره: المعنى في هذا هو (¬1): أن الله أعلم الملائكة أنه جاعل في الأرض خليفة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r2.claim: The missing divine announcement is inferred from the angels' answer: the text omits it for concision, as al-Shanfara's poetry also omits an understood phrase.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r2.anchor: فإن قيل: فأين إخبار الله بذلك للملائكة فإنا لا نراه في القرآن؟ قيل: هو محذوف مكتفى بدلالة الكلام عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r3.claim: The angels may have asked to learn the wisdom, not objected: after the jinn were removed, they occupied earth and asked why corrupting humans would replace them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون هذا القول من الملائكة على وجه استعلام وجه الحكمة، لا على الإنكار.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and most commentators say angels compared Adam's descendants with corrupting jinn; God knew Iblis's pride and delusion, and angels later admitted ignorance when unable to name things.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين: إن الله تعالى لما اطلع على كبر إبليس قال للملائكة الذين كانوا معه:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r5.claim: The apparent address suggests the creation troubled angels: their worship had lightened while they lived on earth, and they feared returning to heaven, where worship would burden them again.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p326/r5.anchor: ومع وضوح هذه الأقوال فإن ظاهر الخطاب يدل على أنه شق على الملائكة خلق الخليفة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r1.claim: Tasbih means declaring God free of every evil, and it can also mean prayer; to glorify God is to pray to Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r1.anchor: معنى التسبيح: تنزيه الله من كل سوء، وقد يكون بمعنى الصلاة، ويقال: سبح لله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r2.claim: Al-Hasan explains the angels' phrase as saying, Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: معناه: يقول سبحان الله وبحمده

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r3.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r3.claim: Al-Azhari says exegetes and linguists agree that tasbih means declaring God transcendent and free of evil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r3.anchor: قال الأزهري (¬4): أجمع المفسرون وأهل المعاني: أن معنى (¬5) تسبيح الله، تنزيه الله وتبرئته عن السوء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r4.claim: The word's root means distancing; anyone praising God and distancing Him from evil has glorified and purified Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r4.anchor: وأصل التسبيح (¬6) في اللغة، التبعيد من قولك: سبحت في الأرض، إذا تباعدت فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r5.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r5.claim: Some linguists explain tasbih with praise as speaking God's praise: praise and gratitude themselves honor Him and acknowledge His worthiness to be purified and exalted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r5.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني: معنى قوله: {نسبح بحمدك} نتكلم بالحمد لك، والنطق بالحمد لله تسبيح له،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r6.claim: Subhan Allah means God's freedom from evil and became an exclamation of wonder; al-A'sha's verse uses it to express astonishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r6.anchor: ومعنى قول القائل (سبحان الله): براءة الله من السوء (¬3) وتنزيهه، وكثر لفظ (سبحان الله) في كلامهم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives the concise sense of the angels' words as declaring God free of evil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p329/r7.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الزجاج في معنى: {نسبح بحمدك} قال: نبرئك من السوء

ELMALILI:2:30-33/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r17.claim: God's making a vicegerent means granting him some divine powers and attributes so that he may exercise delegated authority over creation in God's name.
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r17.anchor: Kendi irâdemden kudret ve sıfâtımdan ona bazı salâhiyetler vereceğim; o Bana izâfeten, Bana niyâbeten mahlukātım üzerinde birtakım tasarrufâta sâhip olacak

ELMALILI:2:30-33/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r18.claim: The vicegerent has no authority in his own right: he is a deputy charged to apply God's will, commands, and laws.
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r18.anchor: o bu hususta asîl olmayacak, kendi zâtı ve şahsı nâmına bi’l-asâle icrâ-yı ahkâm edecek değil, ancak Benim bir nâibim, bir kalfam olacak

ELMALILI:2:30-33/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r19.claim: Successors will carry out the same assigned duty, as expressed in the statement that God made people successors on earth.
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r19.anchor: sonra onun arkasından gelenler ve ona halef olarak aynı vazifeyi icrâ edecek olanlar bulunacak هُوَ ٱلَّذِى جَعَلَكُمْ خَلَٰٓئِفَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ

ELMALILI:2:30-33/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r20.speaker: ashâb-ı kirâm ve tâbiîn
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r20.claim: The account's meaning is the distilled substance of extensive interpretations transmitted from the Companions and Successors.
ELMALILI:2:30-33/r20.anchor: Bu mâna ashâb-ı kirâmdan ve tâbiînden uzun uzadıya nakledilegelen tefsirlerin hulâsası ve hâsılıdır.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r1.claim: The word jaʿil may mean create: when jaʿl takes one object it means creation, and here it is broader and more general than khalq while allowing both senses.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r1.anchor: جعل (ca‘l) bir mef‘ûle müte‘addî olursa halk demek olur. Burada da “ca‘l”, “halk”dan e‘am ve daha mutlaktır.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r2.claim: The creation of the human is specified later in the verses about making a human from clay; the announcement of jaʿil follows the conception of khalq, distinguishing the determination of essence from attributes.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r2.anchor: işbu جَاعِلٌۭ tebliği إِنِّي خَالِقٌ takdîrinden sonra görünüyor.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r3.claim: Khalifa is an intensive nominal adjective from khalif, on the faʿīl pattern with the meaning of fāʿil; French représentant conveys the sense, with khalāʾif and khulafāʾ as plurals and khilāfa as the verbal noun.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r4.claim: Khilāfa, like agency, is deputation in place of principal authority: taking another's place to some extent and representing that principal.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r4.anchor: Hilâfet, “vekâlet” gibi, “asâlet”in mukabili olarak başkasına niyâbet etmek, yani az veya çok onun yerini tutarak onu temsil etmek demektir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r5.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r5.claim: Deputyship may arise from the principal's absence, need, or incapacity, or simply from the principal honoring a deputy despite none of those causes.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r5.anchor: Râgıb’ın Müfredât’ında beyânı vechile bu niyâbet de

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r6.claim: God's appointing His chosen servants as successors is a form of deputation bestowed purely to honor them.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r6.anchor: mahza asîlin nâibine bir şeref bahşederek tekrim etmesinden neş’et eder. Ve işte Cenâb-ı Allah’ın arzda evliyâsını istihlâfı bu kabîldendir.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r7.claim: A deputy's worth and honor are proportionate to the principal's honor and the degree of representation.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r7.anchor: Demek ki her nâibin, halifenin kıymet ve şerefi

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r8.claim: The angels understood the honor of vicegerency but feared the possible evil of giving a creature on earth such high discretionary authority.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r8.anchor: melâike bir taraftan bundaki şerefi takdir ettiler, diğer taraftan da yerdeki bir mahlûka min-tarafillah böyle yüksek bir salâhiyyet-i irâdiye bahşedilmesinde bir şer ihtimâlinden de korktular.

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r9.claim: Mention of earth implies a human made from clay; the angels wondered whether he would misuse delegated authority as if it were his own and cause corruption.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r9.anchor: “Yerde” deyince إِنِّى خَٰلِقٌۢ بَشَرًۭا مِّن طِينٍۢ takdîri anlaşılıyordu. Acaba bu salâhiyeti alan, hüsn-i isti‘mâl edebilecek mi?

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r10.claim: God had not yet disclosed the degree of authority or its hidden wisdom, so the angels asked about the risk of corruption and bloodshed.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r10.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak henüz bu noktaları ve o [301] salâhiyetin derecesini ve hikem-i hafiyyesini bildirmemiş olmakla melekler

ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r11.claim: The angels' question was an inquiry about wisdom, not an objection, though it implicitly showed their own desire for vicegerency.
ELMALILI:2:30-33#2/r11.anchor: maksadları hâşâ itiraz olmayıp hikmetini bir istifsar olduğunu bildirdiler, ma‘amâfîh bununla hilâfete zımnen bir rağbet de izhar ettiler.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r1.claim: إذ is a past-time adverb that shifts a present verb into the past, is indeclinable because it resembles a particle in form and dependence, and may be followed by clauses; fronting a noun before the verb in a verbal clause is awkward.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r1.anchor: " إذ " ظرف زمان ماض، يخلص المضارع للمضي وبني لشبهه بالحرف في الوضع والافتقار

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r2.claim: إذ is not declinable except when attached to a time noun, is not a direct object despite many grammarians' analysis, and is not a place adverb, redundant, causal particle or suddenness particle.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r2.anchor: ولا يتصرف إلا بإضافة الزمن إليه نحو: يومئذ وحينئذ، ولا يكون مفعولا به

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r3.claim: When the clause governed by إذ is omitted and understood, tanwin compensates for it and kasra avoids two sukuns rather than marking inflection; the author rejects al-Akhfash's alternative.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r3.anchor: وقد تحذف الجملة المضاف هو إليها للعلم ويعوض منها تنوين كقوله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r4.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash says the original was وأنت حينئذ, with حين omitted while its genitive remains; the author calls this weak.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r4.anchor: وللأخفش أن يقول: أصله " وأنت حينئذ " فلما حذف المضاف بقي المضاف إليه

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r5.claim: قال ربك is a verbal clause in the genitive because it is annexed to the temporal adverb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r5.anchor: و { قال ربك } جملة فعلية في محل خفض بإضافة الظرف إليها

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r6.claim: Of nine analyses of إذ, the best and simplest makes it governed by قالوا أتجعل فيها: the angels said this at the time God said إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r6.anchor: أحسنها أنه منصوب ب { قالوا أتجعل فيها } أي: قالوا ذلك القول وقت قول الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r7.claim: One proposal governs إذ by an implied اذكر; the author has already rejected making إذ itself a direct object.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r7.anchor: الثاني: أنه منصوب ب " اذكر " مقدرا وقد تقدم أنه لا يتصرف فلا يقع مفعولا

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r8.claim: A proposal links إذ to خلقكم in 4:1 and calls the wāw redundant, but the author dismisses it because of the long distance.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r8.anchor: الثالث: أنه منصوب ب " خلقكم " المتقدم في قوله: اتقوا ربكم الذي خلقكم

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r9.claim: A proposal makes the later قال govern إذ, but this fails because a mudaf ilayh cannot govern its mudaf.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r9.anchor: الرابع: أنه منصوب ب " قال " بعده. وهو فاسد لأن المضاف إليه لا يعمل في المضاف

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r10.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r10.claim: A fifth analysis treats إذ as redundant, attributed to Abu Ubayd.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r10.anchor: الخامس: أنه زائد ويعزى لأبي عبيد

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r11.claim: A sixth analysis gives إذ the meaning قد.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r12.claim: A seventh makes إذ predicate to an omitted subject; an eighth governs it by an implied ابتدأ خلقكم. The author rejects both since creation's beginning was not the time of the statement, and إذ is indeclinable.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r13.claim: A ninth proposal governs إذ with an implied أحياكم; it is rejected because the two events occurred at different times.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30/r13.anchor: التاسع: أنه منصوب ب " أحياكم " مقدرا، وهذا مردود باختلاف الوقتين

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r1.claim: للملائكة attaches to قال, and ل is the particle of communication.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r1.anchor: و " للملائكة " متعلق ب " قال " واللام للتبليغ

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r2.claim: One etymology makes ملك a form فعَل from الملك with original mīm; on this account only its plural فعائلة is irregular.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r2.anchor: فقال بعضهم: ملك ووزنه فعل من الملك، وشذ جمعه على فعائلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r3.claim: Another original-mīm derivation starts from ملأك with an extra hamza like شمأل; its vowel shifts to the lām and the hamza drops, while the plural preserves the original addition.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: بل أصله ملأك، والهمزة فيه زائدة كشمأل ثم نقلت حركة الهمزة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r4.claim: A third derivation makes mīm extra and derives the word from ألك, to send. Poems with مألكة, بألوك and مألك attest the message sense; the derivation involves metathesis and hamza deletion, with the plural restoring hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r4.anchor: فمنهم من قال: هو مشتق من " ألك " أي: أرسل ففاؤه همزة وعينه لام

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r5.claim: A fourth analysis derives it from لأك, also meaning to send; the poem فلست لإنسي ولكن لملأك witnesses the form, and the plural restores hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r5.anchor: ومنهم من قال: هو مشتق من لأك أي أرسل أيضا، ففاؤه لام وعينه همزة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r6.claim: A fifth derivation connects ملك to لاكه يلوكه, to turn something over, since an angel turns a message in the mouth; it derives singular ملوك and plural ملاوكة with vowel change, deletion and hamza formation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو مشتق من: لاكه يلوكه أي: أداره يديره، لأن الملك يدير الرسالة في فيه

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r7.speaker: النضر بن شميل
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r7.claim: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl says ملك has no derivation in Arab usage.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#2/r7.anchor: قال النضر بن شميل: " لا اشتقاق للملك عند العرب "

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r1.claim: The ة in ملائكة marks a feminine plural as in صلادمة, or could be an intensifier as in علامة and نسابة; the author rejects that latter view. Poetry attests rare deletion of the suffix in الملائك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r1.anchor: والهاء في ملائكة لتأنيث الجمع نحو: صلادمة. وقيل للمبالغة كعلامة ونسابة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r2.claim: إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة is the quoted content and direct object of قال; إن is closed because it follows قال without a meaning of supposition.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r2.anchor: هذه الجملة معمول القول، فهي في محل نصب به، وكسرت " إن " هنا لوقوعها بعد القول

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r3.claim: When قول means supposition, إن may be opened or closed; a poem closes it despite its sense, apparently following the surface form of قول.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r3.anchor: فإن كان بمعنى الظن جرى فيها وجهان: الفتح والكسر

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r4.claim: General rule: open إن when its clause can replace a verbal noun; close it when it cannot, such as after قول, initially, in a relative clause or circumstantial clause. Both are possible when substitution is ambiguous, such as after فاء الجزاء or إذا الفجائية.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r4.anchor: كل موضع لم يسد مسدها وجب فيه كسرها كوقوعها بعد القول ومبتدأة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r5.claim: If جاعل means خالق, خليفة is its object and في الأرض either attaches to جاعل or is an omitted phrase circumstantially modifying the following indefinite noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r5.anchor: و " في الأرض " فيه حينئذ قولان، أحدهما وهو الواضح أنه متعلق بجاعل. الثاني: أنه متعلق بمحذوف لأنه حال من النكرة بعده

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes جاعل to mean صير, making خليفة the first object and في الأرض the fronted second object.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r6.anchor: القول الثاني: أنه بمعنى مصير، ولم يذكر الزمخشري غيره

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r7.claim: خليفة can mean an active successor, succeeding the people addressed or the jinn who preceded them; this is stronger because its feminine suffix is regular for the active sense.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r7.anchor: و " خليفة " يجوز أن يكون بمعنى فاعل أي: يخلفكم أو يخلف من كان قبله من الجن، وهذا أصح

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r8.claim: Alternatively, خليفة means one succeeded by each later generation; the feminine suffix is not regular for this passive sense unless the word has become noun-like, as in النطيحة and الذبيحة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r8.anchor: وقيل: بمعنى مفعول أي: يخلف كل جيل من تقدمه، وليس دخول التاء حينئذ قياسا

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r9.claim: The singular خليفة can intend Adam and his descendants collectively, using the ancestor as with tribal names Mudar and Rabi'a; another view understands خليفة as a generic.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#3/r9.anchor: وإنما وحد " خليفة " وإن كان المراد الجمع لأنه أريد به آدم وذريته

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r1.claim: A reading substitutes خليقة with qāf for the verse’s خليفة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r2.claim: خليفة is accusative as the object of جاعل; active participles govern like their verbs and may be annexed to their object for lightness if nothing intervenes.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r2.anchor: و " خليفة " منصوب ب " جاعل " كما تقدم، لأنه اسم فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r3.claim: قالوا governs إذ قال ربك, which al-Samīn identifies as the preferred parsing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r3.anchor: تقدم أن " قالوا " عامل في " إذ قال ربك " وأنه المختار

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the hamza in أتجعل as astonishment.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r5.speaker: unspecified
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r5.claim: Another view treats the hamza as confirmation, supported by the poetic question ألستم خير من ركب المطايا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r5.anchor: وقيل: للتقرير كقوله: 334 ألستم خير من ركب المطايا

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r6.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls the question استشهاد: would God place one who corrupts there like those before? Al-Samīn calls this phrasing unusual.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r6.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " للاستشهاد " ، أي: أتجعل فيها من يفسد كمن كان قبل

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r7.claim: If تجعل means create, the first فيها is attached to it and من يفسد is its object.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r7.anchor: إن قيل: إنها بمعنى الخلق، و " من يفسد " مفعول به

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r8.claim: If تجعل means make into, the first فيها is its second object, advanced before من يفسد.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r8.anchor: إنها بمعنى التصيير فيكون " فيها " مفعولا ثانيا قدم على الأول

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r9.claim: من may be a relative pronoun, leaving the following clause without an independent syntactic position; as an indefinite it makes the clause accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r9.anchor: من " تحتمل أن تكون موصولة أو نكرة موصوفة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r10.claim: The second فيها is governed by يفسد, and يسفك coordinates with يفسد under either parsing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r10.anchor: و " فيها " الثانية متعلقة ب " يفسد ". و " يسفك " عطف على " يفسد "

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r11.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r11.claim: The majority read يسفك in the indicative; another reading makes it subjunctive as an answer to the question with أن understood after wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r11.anchor: والجمهور على رفعه، وقرئ منصوبا على جواب الاستفهام

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r12.claim: An anonymous poem beginning أتبيت ريان illustrates the subjunctive after an understood أن.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the subjunctive governed by واو الصرف, a Kufan term for wāw redirecting inflection to the subjunctive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " منصوب بواو الصرف " وهذه عبارة الكوفيين

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r14.claim: Readings vary between kasra and ḍamma on fāʾ, a ḍamma on the imperfect prefix from أسفك, and a doubled form for intensity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r14.anchor: والمشهور " يسفك " بكسر الفاء، وقرئ بضمها

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r15.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r15.claim: سفك means pouring and is normally used only of blood; Ibn Fāris and al-Jawharī also allow tears, while al-Mahdawī adds scattered speech.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#4/r15.anchor: والسفك: هو الصب، ولا يستعمل إلا في الدم، وقال ابن فارس، والجوهري

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r1.claim: دماء is the plural of دم; a declinable noun cannot consist of two letters, so the third radical, its final letter, is omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r1.anchor: والدماء: جمع دم، ولا يكون اسم معرب على حرفين

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r2.claim: The omitted radical may be wāw or yāʾ as in the duals دموان and دميان; the poem uses الدميان.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r3.claim: Grammarians disagree whether دم follows فَعْل with a quiescent middle radical or فَعَل with it open.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r3.anchor: وهل وزن دم " فعل " بسكون العين أو فعل بفتحها قولان

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r4.claim: The deleted radical may disappear and دم be used as shortened دما, as in the cited poem.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r4.anchor: 337 كأطوم فقدت برغزها أعقبتها الغبس منه عدما

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r5.claim: The mīm of دم may also be geminated; an anonymous poem uses دمك in that form.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r5.anchor: 338 أهان دمك فرغا بعد عزته يا عمرو

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r6.claim: The underlying plural is الدماو or الدماي; its final weak letter becomes hamza after an extra final alif, as in كساء and رداء.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r6.anchor: وأصل: الدماء: الدماو أو الدماي، فقلب حرف العلة همزة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r7.claim: The wāw is circumstantial; ونحن نسبح is a nominal clause in the accusative as a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r7.anchor: الواو للحال، و { ونحن نسبح } جملة من مبتدأ وخبر

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r8.claim: بحمدك attaches to an omitted circumstantial phrase: they glorify accompanied by praise, two nested circumstantial states.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r8.anchor: و " بحمدك " متعلق بمحذوف، لأنه حال أيضا، والباء فيه للمصاحبة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r9.claim: An alternative makes the bāʾ causal and attaches it to تسبيح; Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats the phrase as an interpolated acknowledgment of God's guidance.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r10.claim: Al-Samīn takes Ibn ʿAṭiyya to aim at a causal bāʾ with an omitted verb: praise of God occasioned their glorification and sanctification.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r10.anchor: كأنه يحاول أن تكون الباء للسببية، ولكن يكون ما تعلقت به الباء فعلا محذوفا

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r11.claim: الحمد is a verbal noun annexed to its object, with subject omitted as بحمدنا إياك; the claim that the noun itself contains a subject is mistaken.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r11.anchor: والحمد هنا: مصدر مضاف لمفعوله، وفاعله محذوف تقديره: بحمدنا إياك

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r12.claim: Grammarians disagree whether a verbal noun used in place of a verb can contain an implicit pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r12.anchor: على أنه قد حكي خلاف في المصدر الواقع موقع الفعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r13.claim: نقدس coordinates with نسبح and is a predicate of نحن; its omitted object is ourselves and our actions.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r13.anchor: و " نقدس " عطف على " نسبح " فهو خبر أيضا عن " نحن "

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r14.claim: لك may attach to نقدس or نسبح with a causal sense; it may also be redundant (a weak view), transitive, or explanatory as in سقيا لك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#5/r14.anchor: و " لكم " متعلق به أو ب " نسبح " ، ومعناها العلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r1.claim: The estimate تقديسنا لك suits the context better than estimating أعني.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r1.anchor: وهذا التقدير أحسن من تقدير قولهم: " أعني " لأنه أليق بالموضع

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya accepts placing ونحن نسبح inside an implied question: وأنحن نسبح أم نتغير.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r2.anchor: وأبعد من زعم أن جملة قوله " ونحن نسبح " داخلة في حيز استفهام مقدر

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r3.claim: Al-Samīn rejects omitting an interrogative hamza without أم; most grammarians reject it, though al-Akhfash allows it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r3.anchor: وهذا يأباه الجمهور، أعني حذف همزة الاستفهام من غير ذكر " أم " المعادلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r4.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash allows an omitted interrogative hamza, including in وتلك نعمة تمنها علي.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r5.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r5.claim: A poem’s طربت وما شوقا إلى البيض أطرب is also analyzed with an omitted hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r5.anchor: 339 طربت وما شوقا إلى البيض أطرب

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r6.claim: When أم follows it signals the omitted hamza; a poem’s بسبع رمين الجمر أم بثمان implies أبسبع.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r6.anchor: 341 فوالله ما أدري وإن كنت داريا بسبع

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r7.claim: تسبيح means declaring transcendence and disavowal; its root سبْح denotes distance, as in swimming.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r7.anchor: والتسبيح: التنزيه والبراءة، وأصله من السبح وهو البعد

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r8.claim: سبحان الله declares God transcendent and free of what does not befit Him; the poem uses سبحان من علقمة for تنزيها.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r8.anchor: 342 أقول لما جاءني فخره سبحان من علقمة الفاخر

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r9.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r9.claim: Al-Rāghib reads سبحان من علقمة sarcastically as سبحان علقمة with من added; another explanation supplies الله من أجل علقمة, which al-Samīn questions as applying the formula to other than God.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r9.anchor: قال الراغب في قوله سبحان من علقمة: " إن أصله سبحان علقمة

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r10.claim: تقديس means purification, as in الأرض المقدسة, بيت المقدس, and روح القدس.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r10.anchor: والتقديس: التطهير، ومنه الأرض المقدسة، وبيت المقدس، وروح القدس

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r11.claim: An anonymous poem uses ثوب المقدس for a garment purified for its wearers.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r11.anchor: 343 فأدركنه يأخذن بالساق والنسا كما شبرق الولدان ثوب المقدس

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives تقديس from traveling far in the land, making its sense close to تسبيح.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#6/r12.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " هو من قدس في الأرض إذا ذهب فيها وأبعد

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r1.claim: إني contracts إنني by dropping one of three adjacent nūns; the correct view deletes the middle nūn rather than the nūn of protection.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r1.anchor: أصل إني: إنني فاجتمع ثلاثة أمثال، فحذفنا أحدها، وهل هو نون الوقاية أو النون الوسطى؟ قولان الصحيح الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r2.claim: The clause إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون occupies the accusative position as content of قال.

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r3.claim: أعلم is apparently an imperfect verb governing ما as object; ما may be relative or indefinite with the resumptive pronoun omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r3.anchor: " أعلم " يجوز فيه أن يكون فعلا مضارعا وهو الظاهر، و " ما " مفعول به

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r4.speaker: المهدوي
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r4.claim: Al-Mahdawī, Makkī, and Abū al-Baqāʾ treat أعلم as the noun عالم; ما may be genitive or accusative and أعلم is diptote.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r4.anchor: وقال المهدوي، ومكي وتبعهما أبو البقاء: " إن " أعلم " اسم بمعنى عالم

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r5.claim: Al-Samīn rejects the noun analysis as resting on weak premises: أفعل meaning فاعل without comparison and governing like an active participle.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r5.anchor: وهذا مبني على أصلين ضعيفين، أحدهما: جعل أفعل بمعنى فاعل من غير تفضيل

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r6.claim: Another analysis takes أعلم as comparative with منكم omitted and ما as object of implied علمت, since the comparative does not govern it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r6.anchor: وقيل: " أعلم " على بابها من كونها للتفضيل، والمفضل عليه محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r7.claim: An anonymous poem is analyzed with القوانس governed by an implied ضرب, not by أضرب.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r7.anchor: 345 فلم أر مثل الحي حيا مصبحا ولا مثلنا يوم التقينا فوارسا

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r8.claim: Applying that analysis here requires deleting both the comparison phrase and the verb governing ما, making the ellipsis remote.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r8.anchor: بعد لحذف شيئين: المفضل عليه والناصب ل " ما "

SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r9.claim: The contraction is compared with إنا معكم earlier in the sūra.
SAMIN-DURR:2:30#7/r9.anchor: الصحيح الثاني، وهذا شبيه بما تقدم في

ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda calls idh redundant; al-Zajjāj rejects this as reckless because idh is a noun meaning ‘time.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة " إذ " ههنا زائدة، وهذا إقدام من أبي عبيدة

ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r2.claim: After mentioning the creation of people and others, the passage links their creation to the time God told the angels He would place a successor on earth.
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r2.anchor: والحجة في (إذ) أن الله تعالى ذكر خلق الناس وغيرهم، فكأنه قال ابتدأ خلقكم

ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r3.claim: The report about Adam and the angels’ prostration proves Muhammad’s prophethood to scriptural communities: Arabs did not know it, while scripture readers or revelation did.
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r3.anchor: ففي إخبار النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - دليل على تثبيت رسالته إذ آتاهم بما ليس من علم العرب

ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r4.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r4.claim: A people called jinn lived on earth, corrupted it and shed blood; God sent angels to drive them away, and the angels then inhabited earth.
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r4.anchor: روي أن خلقا يقال لهم الجان كانوا في الأرض فأفسدوا وسفكوا الدماء

ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r5.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r5.claim: Another account says God told the angels some descendants of Adam would shed blood and allowed their question to affirm that He knows the unseen.
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r5.anchor: وقال قوم: المعنى فيه غير هذا وهو أن الله عز وجل أعلم الملائكة أنه جاعل في الأرض خليفة

ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r6.claim: The angels ask to learn the wisdom, not to object: they seek clarification of the truth if their expectation is correct.
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r6.anchor: وتأويل استخبارهم هذا على جهة الاستعلام وجهة الحكمة، لا على الإنكار

ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r7.claim: In the reported account, God gave the angels leave to ask about the matter.
ZAJJAJ:v1p108/r7.anchor: وأذن الله عز وجل للملائكة أن يسألوه عن ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r1.claim: God will test those the angels expect to obey, and through the test guide them.
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r1.anchor: أي أبتلي من تظنون أنه يطيع فيهديه الابتلاء،

ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the hamza affirms making here and cites Jarīr’s ألستم as evidence for the form’s affirmative force.
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r2.anchor: الألف ههنا إنما هي على إيجاب الجعل

ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r3.claim: Safaka means to pour or spill something.
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r3.anchor: ومعنى (يسفك) يصب، يقال سفك الشيء إذا صبه

ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r4.claim: To glorify God with praise means to declare Him free of evil.

ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r5.claim: Any act intended for God may be called tasbīḥ; completing prayer is one Arabic use of tasbīḥ.
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r5.anchor: وكل من عمل عملا قصد به الله فقد سبح، يقال فرغت من تسبيحي أي من صلاتي

ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r6.speaker: سيبويه وغيره من النحويين
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r6.claim: Sībawayh and other grammarians gloss subḥān Allāh as declaring God free of evil and exalting Him above it.
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r6.anchor: وقال سيبويه وغيره من النحويين: إن معنى سبحان الله: براءة الله من السوء

ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r7.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s line uses the word سبحان to mean disavowal of ʿAlqama and his boasting.

ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r8.claim: Nuqaddisu laka means purifying ourselves for God; the obedient person is purified, and Bayt al-Maqdis is the purified house or place of purification from sins.
ZAJJAJ:v1p109/r8.anchor: ومعنى (نقدس لك) أي نطهر أنفسنا لك، وكذلك من أطاعك نقدسه أي نطهره

ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n21/r1.claim: Asad renders idh as “lo” here because it can mark a sudden or unexpected event or a turn in discourse, rather than simply “when.”
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n21/r1.anchor: idh is also used to indicate "the sudden, or unexpected, occurrence of a thing" (cf. Lane 1, 39), or a sudden turn in the discourse

ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n21/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n21/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n21/r2.claim: The ensuing allegory about reason implanted in human beings connects logically with the preceding passages.
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n21/r2.anchor: The subsequent allegory, relating as it does to the faculty of reason implanted in man, is logically connected with the preceding passages.

ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n22/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n22/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n22/r1.claim: Khalifah derives from khalafa, “he succeeded”; in this allegory it denotes humanity’s rightful supremacy on earth, which Asad renders as inheriting the earth.
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n22/r1.anchor: used in this allegory to denote man's rightful supremacy on earth

ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n22/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n22/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n22/r2.claim: Asad connects this reading to verses that call human beings khalaʾif al-arḍ, successors on earth.
ASAD-NOTES:2:30#n22/r2.anchor: where all human beings are - spoken of as khala'if al-ard

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r1.speaker: الخطابي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r1.claim: Al-Khattabi says Qur'anic rhetoric is miraculous because it combines three levels of eloquence, excluding the disapproved hybrid, to achieve both grandeur and sweetness.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r1.anchor: ثم إن الخطابي في شرح فكرته في النظم المعجز، يرى من الإعجاز أن تأتي بلاغات القرآن جامعة لطبقات ثلاث متفاوتة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r2.claim: Bint al-Shati rejects the implication that Qur'anic passages occupy lower eloquence levels: inimitability reaches the highest level, and one sura need not combine all three because the challenge concerns a single sura.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r2.anchor: أولاهما: أن فهمنا للإعجاز البياني، فوت لأعلى درجات البلاغة دون أوسطها وأدناها. والأخرى، أن هذه الدرجات الثلاث لا تجتمع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r3.speaker: الخطابي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r3.claim: Al-Khattabi was an early observer of fine semantic distinctions among Qur'anic terms often treated as synonyms, including knowledge and knowing, praise and thanks, and emancipation and manumission.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p102/r3.anchor: وسبق "الخطابي" أيضاً إلى لمح فروق دقيقة في الدلالة، لألفاظ قرآنية جرت معاجمنا وكتب المفسرين على القول بترادفها

IBNMAJAH:981/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:981/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNMAJAH:981/r1.claim: Sahl reports that the Prophet tied an imam’s leadership to accountability, complementing the verse’s appointment of a khalifa: good conduct benefits him and worshippers, while wrongdoing falls on him.
IBNMAJAH:981/r1.anchor: إِنِّي سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ يَقُولُ

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr opens the attached yāʾ after a kasra before an open or kasra hamza; this rule includes إني أعلم.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r1.anchor: مثل قوله: إني أعلم [البقرة/ 30] وعهدي الظالمين

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r2.claim: He does not open the yāʾ before a hamza with ḍamma, as in the cited examples; his opening rule is restricted to the open and kasra hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r2.anchor: ولا يحرك الياء التي ذكرت لك عند الألف المضمومة

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr does not follow one consistent rule for these attached yāʾ vowels; his individual cases are listed separately by sūra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p411#2/r4.anchor: وكان ابن كثير لا يستمر على قياس واحد كما فعل أبو عمرو

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r2.claim: The case for opening the attached yāʾ is that its original vowel is fatḥa, parallel to the addressee kāf, which is also opened.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r2.anchor: أن أصل هذه الياء الحركة، لأنها بإزاء الكاف للمخاطب فكما فتحت الكاف كذلك تفتح الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r3.claim: Although vowels on weak letters are often avoided, fatḥa is acceptable: yāʾ in al-qāḍī is inflected with fatḥa, and accusative غَوَاشٍ retains its yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r3.anchor: الفتحة من بينها لا تكره فيها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r4.claim: When a consonant precedes the suffix yāʾ, speakers agree on fatḥa in examples such as بشراي and غلاماي, supporting that as its underlying vowel after a vowel too.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r4.anchor: ومما يدل على استحقاقها التحرك بالفتح أنها إذا سكن ما قبلها اتفقوا على تحريكها بالفتح

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r5.claim: The moving feminine/plural nūn in فعلن and يفعلن is another pronominal parallel; despite an objection that it moves only to avoid adjacent sukūns, its likeness to kāf and tāʾ supports movement.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p413/r5.anchor: ويدل على لزوم تحركها بالفتح تحريكهم النون في فعلن، ويفعلن، وهو حرف ضمير كالياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r1.speaker: مُسْكِنُو الياء
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r1.claim: Those who leave the yāʾ still argue that even fatḥa is avoided on yāʾ; Arabic compounds can preserve it still, and poetry extends that practice.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r1.anchor: وحجة من أسكن أن الفتحة مع الياء قد كرهت في الكلام، كما كرهت الحركتان الأخريان فيها

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r2.claim: Sukūn is reinforced by yāʾ’s similarity to alif: they are close in articulation, can substitute for each other, and the long vowel supplies what movement would otherwise provide.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r2.anchor: ومما يؤكد الإسكان فيها أنها مشابهة للألف، والألف تسكن، في الأحوال الثلاث

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr’s reason for opening yāʾ before a light hamza is that hamza can induce fatḥa in otherwise unopen forms such as يقرأ and يبرأ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p415/r3.anchor: فأما حجة أبي عمرو في فتحه الياء مما رآه خفيفا مع الهمزة، فهي أن الهمزة قد فتح لها ما لم يكن يفتح

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r1.claim: Hamza with fatḥa or kasra can draw fatḥa onto the preceding yāʾ, but a ḍamma hamza does not; the cited word examples show the distinction.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r1.anchor: والمفتوحة والمكسورة سيان في إتباع الياء لها في التحريك بالفتح

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r2.claim: The separate-word hamza in these readings is analogized to a hamza inside one word, as Arabic often extends connected-word patterns across word boundaries.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r2.anchor: قيل: يشبه المنفصل بالمتصل هنا، كما شبهه به في

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r3.claim: The explanation that fatḥa merely clarifies the faint yāʾ is rejected: if that were the cause, Abū ʿAmr would also open it before ḍamma hamza and other gutturals.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p417/r3.anchor: فإنا لا نرى أن أبا عمرو اعتبر هذا الذي سلكه هذا القائل

FARISI-HUJJA:v1p418/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p418/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p418/r1.claim: The passage raises an objection that hamza may open the preceding letter even when hamza itself has ḍamma, but provides no answer in this fragment.
FARISI-HUJJA:v1p418/r1.anchor: فإن قلت: فإن الهمزة قد تفتح لها ما قبلها وإن كانت مضمومة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r1.claim: Opening the possessive yāʾ treats it as a built pronoun like hāʾ or kāf; the vowel is fitting after the preceding kasra.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن فتحها أنها ها هنا كالهاء والكاف في قولك إنه وانك وهي اسم مكنى

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r2.claim: Sukūn avoids the heaviness of a vowel on yāʾ and restores the pronoun's underlying built form.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن أسكن أن يقول الحركة على الياء ثقيلة وأصل البناء السكون فأسكنتها تخفيفا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r3.speaker: القراء
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r3.claim: One group opens yāʾ before a hamza with fatḥa but uses sukūn before ḍamma or kasra, avoiding those heavier vowel combinations.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r3.anchor: منهم من يفتحها مع المفتوحة ويسكنها مع المضمومة والمكسورة استثقالا للحركة معهما

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r4.speaker: القراء
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r4.claim: Another group uses sukūn before ḍamma, the heaviest vowel, but opens yāʾ before the other hamzas.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r4.anchor: ومنهم من يسكنها مع المضمومة ويفتحها مع ما سواها لأن الضمة أثقل الحركات

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r5.speaker: القراء
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r5.claim: A third group deletes the possessive yāʾ entirely and relies on the remaining vowel.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r5.anchor: ومنهم من يحذفها أصلا ويجتزي بالحركة منها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r6.claim: When attached to a one-letter word, opening yāʾ is preferable so elision at two adjacent sukūns does not leave a one-letter word; sukūn remains permissible.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r6.anchor: فان اتصلت بحرف واحد فالوجه فتحها لئلا تسقط لالتقاء الساكنين فتبقى الكلمة على حرف واحد واسكانها جائز

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r7.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r7.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r7.claim: Arabic permits four possessive-yāʾ forms: opening, sukūn, adding an alif to soften the vowel, or deleting the yāʾ for brevity.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p74/r7.anchor: وللعرب في ياءات الاضافة أربعة أوجه فتحها على الأصل واسكانها تخفيفا وإثبات الألف بعدها تليينا للحركة وحذفها اختصارا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr opens the first-person yāʾ after a kasra before an open or kasra hamza attached to a noun or verb, unless the letter is lengthened.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r7.anchor: فكان أبو عمرو يفتح ياء الإضافة المكسور ما قبلها عند الألف المهموزة المفتوحة والمكسورة إذا كانت متصلة باسم أو بفعل

NASHR:v1p282/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p282/r1.speaker: ابن مجاهد
NASHR:v1p282/r1.claim: The al-Yazīdī transmission assimilates the discussed sequence, while the remaining group articulates it; Ibn Mujāhid preferred articulation.
NASHR:v1p282/r1.anchor: كلهم عن اليزيدي وهي رواية أبي زيد وابن وافد عن ابن عباس كلاهما، عن أبي عمرو، وروى إظهاره سائر الجماعة، وهو اختيار ابن مجاهد

NASHR:v1p282/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p282/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v1p282/r2.claim: Via ʿIṣma b. ʿUrwa, Abū ʿAmr is reported to avoid assimilation because the word has few letters.
NASHR:v1p282/r2.anchor: عن أبي عمرو: لا أدغمها لقلة حروفها

NASHR:v1p282/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p282/r3.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p282/r3.claim: Al-Dānī rejects the few-letters objection: consensus assimilates لك كيدا, which is shorter in pronunciation than آل.
NASHR:v1p282/r3.anchor: ورد الداني هذا المانع بإدغام لك كيدا إجماعا، إذ هو أقل حروفا من " آل "

NASHR:v1p282/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p282/r4.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v1p282/r4.claim: Al-Dānī explains the attested articulation as caused by an irregular middle consonant: the Basrans derive it from أهل, the Kufans from أول, with substitutions changing the word.
NASHR:v1p282/r4.anchor: اعتلال عينه بالبدل إذا كانت هاء على قول البصريين والأصل " أهل "

NASHR:v1p282/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p282/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p282/r5.claim: The author suggests Abū ʿAmr meant low frequency in the Qurʾān by few letters; recurrence matters, and Abū ʿAmr may also have weighed defectiveness and the received transmission.
NASHR:v1p282/r5.anchor: أي: لقلة دورها في القرآن، فإن قلة الدور وكثرته معتبر كما سيأتي في المتقاربين

NASHR:v1p282/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p282/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p282/r6.claim: The catalogue gives 139 instances for mīm, 70 for nūn, and 18 for wāw, split into 13 after a ḍamma and five after sukūn.
NASHR:v1p282/r6.anchor: نحو ونحن نسبح، ويستحيون نساءكم وجملته سبعون حرفا

NASHR:v1p282/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p282/r7.speaker: ابن فرح
NASHR:v1p282/r7.claim: For wāw preceded by ḍamma, Ibn Farḥ and several other routes transmit assimilation, with named route exceptions; Egyptian and Maghribi authorities also preferred it.
NASHR:v1p282/r7.anchor: فروى إدغامه ابن فرح من جميع طرقه إلا العطار وابن شيطا عن الحمامي

NASHR:v1p293/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p293/r1.speaker: اليزيدي وشجاع
NASHR:v1p293/r1.claim: The continuation reports assimilation through al-Yazīdī and Shujāʿ, while other transmitters of Abū ʿAmr articulate; Abū Ṭāhir preferred articulation because of the shīn’s spreading quality.
NASHR:v1p293/r1.anchor: اليزيدي وشجاع، وروى إظهاره سائر أصحاب الإدغام، عن أبي عمرو، وبه قرأ الشذائي

NASHR:v1p293/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p293/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p293/r2.claim: The author says sīn’s hiss does not prevent assimilation, so the two reported faces are balanced and both are sound; he read and accepts both.
NASHR:v1p293/r2.anchor: ولا يمنع الإدغام من أجل صفير السين، فحصل التكافؤ، والوجهان صحيحان

NASHR:v1p293/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p293/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p293/r6.claim: Qāf assimilates into kāf in the listed contexts; the source gives examples both with a vowel before qāf and after a preceding sukūn.
NASHR:v1p293/r6.anchor: تدغم في الكاف إذا تحرك ما قبلها نحو " ينفق كيف " وجملته أحد عشر حرفا

NASHR:v1p293/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p293/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p293/r7.claim: Kāf assimilates into qāf when preceded by a vowel; when preceded by sukūn, the source says it is not assimilated and lists examples.
NASHR:v1p293/r7.anchor: تدغم إذا تحرك ما قبلها في القاف نحو ونقدس لك. قال: وجملته اثنان وثلاثون حرفا

NASHR:v1p293/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p293/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p293/r8.claim: Lām assimilates into rā when preceded by a vowel; the passage begins listing examples of this rule.
NASHR:v1p293/r8.anchor: تدغم إذا تحرك ما قبلها في الراء بأي حركة تحركت هي، نحو رسل ربك، كمثل ريح

QIRAAT-ER:2:30:30#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:30:30#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:30:30#1/r1.claim: The canonical innīya with fatḥa and innī with sukūn differ phonologically in pause or connection, with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:2:30:30#1/r1.anchor: Fatḥa on yāʾ (inniya) vs. sukūn (innī) — canonical variant

AZRAQI:v1p32/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p32/r1.speaker: الملائكة
AZRAQI:v1p32/r1.claim: In al-Husayn's account, the angels ask why God appoints a successor other than themselves, since they would not corrupt, shed blood, or rival one another.
AZRAQI:v1p32/r1.anchor: فقالت الملائكة أي رب أخليفة من غيرنا ممن يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ويتحاسدون ويتباغضون

AZRAQI:v1p32/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p32/r2.speaker: علي بن الحسين
AZRAQI:v1p32/r2.claim: The angels take God's answer as a rebuke, flee to the Throne, bow their heads, plead and weep, and circle it for three hours.
AZRAQI:v1p32/r2.anchor: فظنت الملائكة إن ما قالوا ردا على ربهم عز وجل وأنه قد غضب من قولهم فلاذوا بالعرش

AZRAQI:v1p32/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p32/r3.speaker: علي بن الحسين
AZRAQI:v1p32/r3.claim: God sends mercy down and places the house called al-Ḍirāḥ beneath the Throne, on four emerald pillars and covered by a red ruby.
AZRAQI:v1p32/r3.anchor: فنزلت الرحمن عليهم فوضع الله تعالى تحت العرش بيتا على أربع أساطين من زبرجد وغشاهن بياقوتة حمراء

AZRAQI:v1p32/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p32/r4.speaker: علي بن الحسين
AZRAQI:v1p32/r4.claim: The angels are told to circle al-Ḍirāḥ instead of the Throne; the report identifies it as the heavenly Frequented House.
AZRAQI:v1p32/r4.anchor: فطافت الملائكة بالبيت وتركوا العرش وصار أهون عليهم من العرش وهو البيت المعمور

AZRAQI:v1p32/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p32/r5.speaker: علي بن الحسين
AZRAQI:v1p32/r5.claim: Seventy thousand angels enter the Frequented House each day and night and never return to it.
AZRAQI:v1p32/r5.anchor: يدخله في كل يوم وليلة سبعون ألف ملك لا يعودون فيه أبدا

AZRAQI:v1p32/r6.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p32/r6.speaker: علي بن الحسين
AZRAQI:v1p32/r6.claim: God then sends angels to build an earthly house matching the heavenly one and orders earth's inhabitants to circle it as heaven's angels circle the Frequented House.
AZRAQI:v1p32/r6.anchor: بعث ملائكة فقال لهم أبنوا لي بيتا في الأرض بمثاله وقدره فأمر الله سبحانه من في الأرض من خلقه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r1.claim: Qatada says God had informed the angels that an earlier earthly creation would cause corruption and bloodshed, which explains their question.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ﴾ قال كان الله أعلمهم إذا كان في الأرض خلق أفسدوا فيها وسفكوا الدماء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the angels’ tasbih as glorification: “tasbih.”
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ونحن نسبح بحمدك ﴾ قال التسبيح التسبيح

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r3.claim: Qatada explains the angels’ taqdis as prayer.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p42/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ونقدس لك ﴾ قال التقديس الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r1.claim: After recounting favors to earlier people, God follows with a universal blessing and complete honor; beneficence to the ancestor also benefits the descendant.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r1.anchor: لما أمتن سبحانه على من تقدم بما تقدم أتبع ذلك بنعمة عامة وكرامة تامة والإحسان إلى الأصل إحسان إلى الفرع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r2.claim: Idh is a past-time adverb, indeclinable because of its particle-like form and dependence; its clause is verbal or nominal, with time inferred from its predicate or context.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r2.anchor: ظرف زمان للماضي مبني لشبهه بالحرف وضعا وافتقارا ويكون ما بعدها جملة فعلية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r3.claim: Idh generally remains adverbial, though grammarians dispute whether it can be an object, causal particle, suddenness marker, place adverb, or redundant; al-Baḥr denies those uses outside contextual implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r3.anchor: وفي وقوعها مفعولا به أو حرف تعليل أو مفاجأة أو ظرف مكان أو زائدة خلاف وفي البحر إنها لا تقع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r4.speaker: المعربون
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r4.claim: Grammarians variously call idh redundant or equivalent to qad, place it as a subject or an object of an omitted verb, attach it to earlier wording, or connect it to dhikr.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r4.anchor: وأختلف المعربون فيها هنا فقيل : زائدة وبمعنى قد وفي موضع رفع أي ابتداء خلقكم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī judges several proposed parses false or strained and favors making idh accusative through the following qālū, whose relation to it is clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r5.anchor: وهذه عدة أقوال بعضها غير صحيح والبعض فيه تكلف فاللائق أن تجعل منصوبة بقالوا الآتي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r6.claim: The story is joined to what precedes as one narrative episode following another.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r6.anchor: والجملة بما فيها عطف على ما قبلها عطف القصة على القصة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r7.claim: The direct address to Muhammad signals his greatest share in the announced affair: he is the greatest vicegerent and foremost imam in creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r7.anchor: وكان في تنويعه والخروج من عامه إلى خاصه رمزا إلى أن المقبل عليه بالخطاب له الحظ الأعظم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r8.speaker: ابن الفارض
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r8.claim: Ibn al-Fāriḍ's verse voices the Muhammadan Reality: although outwardly a son of Adam, Muhammad bears an inner meaning that witnesses to his fatherhood.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r8.anchor: ولله تعالى در سيدي إبن الفارض حيث يقول عن لسان الحقيقة المحمدية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r9.claim: The prefixed lām marks transmission to the angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r9.anchor: واللام الجارة للتبليغ و ( الملائكة ) جمع ملئك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r10.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r10.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, whose account the majority favor, derives malāʾika from malʾak by metathesis and connects it to al-ūlūka, meaning the message; angels are messengers to people.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r10.anchor: مقلوب مالك صفة مشبهة عند الكسائي وهو مختار الجمهور من الألوكة وهي الرسالة فهم رسل إلى الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r11.speaker: ابن كيسان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r11.claim: Ibn Kaysān rejects metathesis and derives the word as faʿāl from al-mulk, with an added hamza, meaning one who rules what God entrusts or has strength; al-Ālūsī calls the derivation remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r11.anchor: وقيل : لا قلب فابن كيسان إلى أنه فعال من الملك بزيادة الهمزة لأنه مالك ما جعله الله تعالى إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r12.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r12.claim: Abū ʿUbayda derives the term from lāka, “to send,” as a passive verbal noun or intensive place noun; al-Ālūsī calls this remote because lāka is uncommon.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r12.anchor: وأبو عبيدة إلى أنه مفعل من لاك إذا أرسل مصدر ميمي بمعنى المفعول أو اسم مكان على المبالغة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r13.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r13.claim: Some treat the word as hollow from lāka yalūku; the feminine ending is explained either as feminine plural or as an intensifier.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r13.anchor: وبعض جعله أجوف من لاك يلوك والتاء لتأنيث الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r14.claim: The plural's feminine agreement reflects the semantic feminine of a group, as grammarians say every collective is feminine by construing it as a community.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r14.anchor: ولم يجعل لتأنيث اللفظ كالظلمة لإعتبارهم التأنيث المعنوي في كل جمع حيث قالوا : كل جمع مؤنث بتأويل الجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r15.claim: A line of poetry shows malāʾik without the feminine tāʾ; the poet is not identified in this passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218/r15.anchor: وقد ورد بغير تاء في قوله + أبا خالد صلت عليك الملائك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r1.speaker: أكثر المسلمين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r1.claim: Most Muslims hold that angels are luminous bodies; another view calls them airy beings able, by God's permission, to assume different forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r1.anchor: أكثر المسلمين إلى أنها أجسام نورانية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r2.speaker: النصارى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r2.claim: Christians identify angels with separate rational souls; their pure souls are good angels, while the wicked are demons.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r2.anchor: وقالت النصارى : إنها الأنفس الناطقة المفارقة لا بد أنها الصافية الخيرة والخبيثة عندهم شياطين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r3.speaker: عبدة الأوثان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r3.claim: Idolaters identify angels with stars, regarding auspicious stars as angels of mercy and unlucky ones as angels of punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r3.anchor: وقال عبدة الأوثان : إنها هذه الكواكب السعد منها ملائكة الرحمة والنحس ملائكة العذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r4.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r4.claim: Philosophers describe angels as immaterial substances distinct in essence from rational souls; some identify them with ten intellects and celestial souls.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r4.anchor: والفلاسفة يقولون : إنها جواهر مجردة مخالفة للنفوس الناطقة في الحقيقة وصرح بعضهم بأنها العقول العشرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī's own account divides angels into two groups: those absorbed in knowing God and those charged with managing affairs by divine decree.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r5.anchor: وهي عندنا منقسمة إلى قسمين قسم شأنهم الاستغراق في معرفة الحق والتنزه عن الاشتغال بغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r6.claim: The first group are the exalted and proximate angels, constantly glorifying God without fatigue.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r6.anchor: يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون وهم العليون والملائكة المقربون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r7.claim: The second group manages affairs from heaven to earth according to the prior decree; they obey commands and include heavenly and earthly angels, whose number only God knows.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r7.anchor: قسم يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض على ما سبق به القضاء وجرى به القلم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r8.claim: A report says heaven groans, for every span in it contains an angel prostrating or bowing; no grading is supplied here.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r8.anchor: وفي الخبر أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط ما فيها موضع قدم إلا وفيه ملك ساجد أو راكع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r9.claim: Angels vary in form and size; only people with sanctified souls see them in their true forms, though they may appear in bodies visible to all.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r9.anchor: وهم مختلفون في الهيآت متفاوتون في العظم لا يراهم على ما هم عليه إلا أرباب النفوس القدسية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r10.claim: The author says Gabriel, appearing before the Prophet as Diḥya al-Kalbī, did not leave the Lote Tree; he says similar manifestations occur for perfected saints.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r10.anchor: صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لم يفارق سدرة المنتهى ومثله يقع للكمل من الأولياء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī acknowledges that this account exceeds rational demonstration but professes belief in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r11.anchor: وهذا ما وراء طور العقل وأنا به من المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r12.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r12.claim: The people of God describe the first manifestation as al-ʿamāʾ; its light disclosed the entranced angels, who preceded the natural bodily world and all other creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r12.anchor: أن أول مظهر للحق جل شأنه العما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r13.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r13.claim: In this account, God selected one of those angels as the first intellect and pen, taught it the intended creation and divine names, then derived the Tablet and commanded the Pen to record events through Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r13.anchor: عين واحدا من هؤلاء وهو أول ملك ظهر عن ملائكة ذلك النور سماه العقل والقلم وتجلى له في مجلى التعليم الوهبي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r14.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r14.claim: The Pen has 360 teeth and the Intellect 360 manifestations; each yields 360 classes of general knowledge unfolded on the Tablet, beginning with nature beneath the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r14.anchor: فجعل لهذا العلم ثلثمائة وستين سنا من كونه قلما ومن كونه عقلا ثلثمائة وستين تجليا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r15.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r15.claim: Their cosmology next describes absolute darkness receiving light, the Throne appearing with the Merciful's manifest Name, and surrounding angels whose sole occupation is glorification.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r15.anchor: فأفاض عليها النور إفاضة ذاتية بمساعدة الطبيعة فلآم شعثها ذلك النور فظهر العرش فأستوى عليه أسم الرحمن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r16.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r16.claim: The account places the Kursī inside the Throne, creates nested heavens and their inhabitants, and develops generated forms, spirits, bodies, and fitting sustenance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r16.anchor: ثم أوجد الكرسي في جوف هذا العرش وجعل فيه ملائكة من جنس طبيعته فكل فلك أصل لما خلق فيه من عماره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r17.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r17.claim: The account says God continually creates angels from the world's breaths for as long as its inhabitants breathe.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p218#2/r17.anchor: ولا يزال الحق سبحانه يخلق منأنفاس العالم ملائكة ماداموا متنفسين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r1.claim: One view takes the address to include all angels, since the wording is general and has no qualifier restricting it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r1.anchor: في الملائكة المقول لهم فقيل : كلهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r2.claim: Another view limits the address to earthly angels because the discussion concerns vicegerency on earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r2.anchor: وقيل : ملائكة الأرض بقرينة أن الكلام في خلافة الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r3.claim: A further view says the addressees were Iblīs and angels who had fought rebellious jinn inhabiting the earth, driving them to mountain passes and islands.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r3.anchor: وقيل : إبليس ومن كان معه في محاربة الجن الذين أسكنوا الأرض دهرا طويلا ففسدوا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r4.speaker: السادة الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r4.claim: The Sufi masters exclude the two world-dwelling angels from the address: other angels bearing divine names and attributes are addressed, while the absorbed ones neither perceive nor prostrate.
