ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r4.anchor: والذي عليه السادة الصوفية قدس الله تعالى أسرارهم أنهم ما عدا العالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r5.speaker: السادة الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r5.claim: They identify one addressed angel as al-Rūḥ, the highest Pen, or First Intellect, a mirror of the divine Essence and the axis of the worlds and their inhabitants.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r5.anchor: وجعلوا من أولئك الملك المسمى بالروح وبالقلم الأعلى وبالعقل الأول وهو المرآة لذاته تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r6.speaker: السادة الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r6.claim: This angel knew Adam's creation and rank because it inscribed all that would be on the Tablet, which experientially knew what the Pen wrote.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r6.anchor: فإنه الذي سطر في اللوح ما كان وما يكون واللوح قد علم علم ذوق ما خطه القلم فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r7.speaker: السادة الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r7.claim: They say the angel appeared fully in the Muhammadan Reality, as indicated by the revelation of a spirit from God's command; hence Muhammad is creation's supreme and true vicegerent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r7.anchor: وقد ظهر هذا الملك بكماله في الحقيقة المحمدية كما يشير إليه قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r8.claim: Jāʿil can mean “making into,” taking khalīfa and “in the earth” as two objects; or “creating,” with one object and “in the earth” modifying khalīfa.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r8.anchor: أسم فاعل من الجعل بمعنى التصيير فيتعدى لإثنين والأول هنا خليفة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r9.claim: On the creation reading, “in the earth” modifies khalīfa and is fronted to create anticipation; the active participle works with future sense and dependence on a subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r9.anchor: متعلق بخليفة وقدم للتشويق وعمل الوصف لأنه بمعنى الإستقبال ومعتمد على مسند إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r10.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r10.claim: Al-Baḥr prefers “creating,” given the contrast; the transformative sense would require an explicit or implied khalīfa.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p219/r10.anchor: ورجح في البحر كونه بمعنى الخلق لما في المقابل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r1.claim: The majority take “the earth” to mean the whole earth; another view identifies it as Mecca, based on a report attributed to the Prophet that the author considers probably unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r1.anchor: قال الجمهور أو أرض مكة وروى هذا مرفوعا والظاهر أنه لم يصح وإلا لم يعدل عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r2.claim: Earth is specified because it is the realm of change and transformation, where the effects of all divine names sought by God become manifest, unlike the higher realm.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r2.anchor: وخص سبحانه الأرض لأنها من عالم التغيير والاستحالات فيظهر بحكم الخلافة فيها حكم جميع الأسماء الإلهية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r3.claim: A khalīfa succeeds another and acts in their place; its feminine ending is intensive, so the term can designate a man.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r3.anchor: والخليفة من يخلف غيره وينوب عنه والهاء للمبالغة ولهذا يطلق على المذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r4.speaker: المشهور
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r4.claim: The best-known interpretation identifies the khalīfa as Adam, matching the report, singular wording, and context; corruption and bloodshed are attributed to him causally or as potential in those succeeding him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r4.anchor: والمشهور أن المراد به آدم عليه السلام وهو الموافق للرواية ولإفراد اللفظ ولما في السياق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r5.claim: Adam is God's vicegerent in the earth; prophets likewise succeed him in cultivating earth, governing people, perfecting souls, and carrying out God's command, not from divine need.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r5.anchor: أنه خليفة الله تعالى في أرضه وكذا كل نبي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r6.claim: The author explains the need for a vicegerent by the recipient's dense bodily nature and God's transcendence; under the divine order, an intermediary with both transcendent and attached aspects receives and transmits emanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r6.anchor: ولكن لقصور المستخلف عليه لما أنه في غاية الكدورة والظلمة الجسمانية وذاته تعالى في غاية التقدس

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r7.claim: One view takes the khalīfa as Adam and his descendants, supported by the angels' wording; their exchange would then disclose Adam's superiority as the origin of those who follow him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r7.anchor: وقيل : هو وذريته عليه السلام ويؤيده ظاهر قول الملائكة فإلزامهم حينئذ بإظهار فضل آدم عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r8.claim: On this descendants interpretation, humans succeed earlier earth-dwellers, whether the jinn, Iblīs and his companions, or they succeed one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r8.anchor: ومعنى كونهم خلفاء أنهم يخلفون من قبلهم من الجن بني الجان أو من إبليس ومن معه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r9.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r9.claim: The people of God identify Adam as God's vicegerent, father of later vicegerents, and comprehensive locus of divine beauty and majesty; both of God's hands are thereby described as right hands.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r9.anchor: وعند أهل الله تعالى المراد بالخليفة آدم وهو عليه السلام خليفة الله تعالى وأبو الخلفاء والمجلي له سبحانه وتعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r10.speaker: الخليفة الأعظم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r10.claim: The report from the supreme vicegerent says God created Adam in His image, or in the image of the Merciful; the author uses it to explain Adam's comprehensiveness.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r10.anchor: قال الخليفة الأعظم صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : إن الله تعالى خلق آدم على صورته أو على صورة الرحمن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r11.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r11.claim: They say the Perfect Human's vicegerency continues until and beyond Resurrection; if this cosmic spirit departed, the world would die, since humanity is its inward support.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r11.anchor: ولم تزل تلك الخلافة في الإنسان الكامل إلى قيام الساعة وساعة القيام بل متى فارق هذا الإنسان العالم مات العالم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r12.claim: The comprehensive divine Name makes vicegerency and cosmic governance possible, while God alone truly acts; the author notes the difficulty of this doctrine and its many deniers.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r12.anchor: ولما كان هذا الاسم الجامع قابل الحضرتين بذاته صحت له الخلافة وتدبير العالم والله سبحانه الفعال لما يريد ولا فاعل على الحقيقة سواه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r13.claim: Announcing the plan to the angels may teach consultation in a matter resembling it, honor the appointed creature, or display his merit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r13.anchor: وفائدة قوله تعالى هذا للملائكة تعليم المشاورة لأن هذه المعاملة تشبهها أو تعظيم شأن المجعول وإظهار فضله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r14.claim: Alternatively, God may have introduced Adam to the angels so they could recognize his rank, since his divine image concealed his inward reality from the upper host except the Tablet and Pen.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أنه سبحانه أراد بذلك تعريف آدم عليه السلام لهم ليعرفوا قدره لأنه باطن عن الصورة الكونية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r15.speaker: الشيخ الأكبر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r15.claim: The Shaykh al-Akbar dates this announcement to Virgo after 17,000 years of the world's age; he gives 8,000 years for the endless afterlife and 71,000 conventional years for the bounded natural world.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r15.anchor: وكان هذا القول على ماذكره الشيخ الأكبر قدس سره في دولة السنبلة بعد مضي سبعة عشر ألف سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r16.speaker: زيد بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r16.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads khalīfa with qāf as khalīqa; the meaning remains clear.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p220/r16.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي خليقة بالقاف والمعنى واضح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r1.claim: The angels ask about the hidden wisdom and removal of their doubt, not whether the appointment itself will occur, which they already knew.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r1.anchor: استكشاف عن الحكمة الخفية وعما يزيل الشبهة وليس استفهاما عن نفس الجعل والاستخلاف لأنهم قد علموه قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r2.claim: Another reading hears astonishment that an earth-reformer should be appointed from among those who corrupt, or that disobedient people replace obedient inhabitants.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r2.anchor: أو تعجب من أن يستخلف لعمارة الأرض وإصلاحها من يفسد فيها أو يستخلف مكان أهل الفساد مثلهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r3.claim: A purely interrogative reading supplies an omitted alternative: will God appoint one who corrupts or one who does not? Another makes the clause circumstantial, asking whether the angels will change while glorifying.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r3.anchor: وقيل : استفهام محض حذف فيه المعاد لأي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r4.speaker: علاء الدين الموصلي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r4.claim: ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn al-Mawṣilī chose the circumstantial reading; al-Ālūsī says respect restrains him from commenting on that choice and ultimately upholds the explanation he has set out.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r4.anchor: وأختار ذلك شيخنا علاء الدين الموصلي روح الله تعالى روحه والأدب يسكتني عنه وعلى كل تقدير

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r5.speaker: الحشوية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that the interrogative is denial; the Ḥashwiyya use it to argue that angels are not infallible because they objected to God and disparaged humanity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r5.anchor: وعلى كل تقدير ليست الهمزة للإنكار كما زعمته الحشوية مستدلين بالآية على عدم عصمة الملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r6.speaker: الخواص
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r6.claim: Al-Shaʿrānī transmits from al-Khawwāṣ that only heavenly angels are infallible, as pure intellects without an opposing desire.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r6.anchor: نقل عن شيخه الخواص أنه خص العصمة بملائكة السماء معلالا له بأنهم عقول مجردة بلا منازع ولا شهوة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r7.speaker: الخواص
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r7.claim: Al-Khawwāṣ's account says earthly angels can err and places Iblīs among them at the Emerald Mountain near the eastern equator; al-Ālūsī says this would make earthly objection conceivable, God forbid.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r7.anchor: إن الملائكة الأرضية غير معصومين ولذلك وقع إبليس فيما وقع إذ كان من ملائكة الأرض الساكنين بجبل الياقوت

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r8.claim: Some reports say ten thousand angels who asked were consumed by fire; al-Ālūsī judges this report incorrect.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r8.anchor: ويستأنس له بما ورد في بعض الأخبار أن القائلين كانوا عشرة آلاف نزلت عليهم نار فأحرقتهم وعندي أن ذلك غير صحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r9.claim: Another view makes Iblīs the sole speaker, with the plural attribution like saying a clan killed someone when only one member did; al-Ālūsī favors his prior account.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r9.anchor: وقيل : إن القائل إبليس وقد كان إذ ذاك معدودا في عداد الملائكة ويكون نسبة القول إليهم على حد بنو فلان قتلوا فلانا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r10.claim: Repeating “therein” stresses the extent of corruption; its omission after the mention of bloodshed is sufficient and rhetorically apt.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r10.anchor: وتكرار الظرف للدلالة على الإفراط في الفساد ولم يكرره بعد للاكتفاء مع ما في التكرار مما لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r11.claim: Safk means pouring or spilling and is used only of blood, or of blood and tears; the blood intended is unlawful by contextual indication, though another view makes the term comprehensive.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r12.claim: Dam has a weak final root consonant, either yāʾ or wāw; short and doubled forms are attested, and its original pattern is faʿl or fuʿl.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r12.anchor: جمع دم لامه ياء أو واو وقصره وتضعيفه مسموعان وأصله فعل أو فعل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r13.claim: Another view takes the bloodshed comprehensively, including lawful and unlawful blood, with the point that the angels could not distinguish among its kinds.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r13.anchor: وقيل : الاستغراق فيتضمن جميع أنواعها من المحظور وغيره والمقصود عدم تمييزه بينها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r14.speaker: إبن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r14.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads the verb with ḍamma on the fāʾ and also reports forms from asfaka and the doubled form of safaka.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r14.anchor: وقرأ إبن أبي عبلة يسفكبضم الفاء ويسفك من أسفك وبالتضعيف من سفك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r15.speaker: إبن هرمز
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r15.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads the final kāf with fatḥa, parsed as a subjunctive answering the interrogative; a passive reading is also transmitted, with an understood “among them” referring back to man.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r16.claim: The angels' judgment that humans would corrupt and shed blood need not claim knowledge of the unseen or conjecture: God informed them, as the divine reply implies, and the Qur'an omits the explicit explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p221/r16.anchor: ولكن بإخبار من الله تعالى ولم يقص علينا فيما حكى عنهم اكتفاء بدلالة الجواب عليه للإيجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r1.claim: The angels first asked what the appointed vicegerent would do; told that his descendants would corrupt and kill one another, they raised their question.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r1.anchor: قالوا : وما يكون من ذلك الخليفة قال : تكون له ذرية يفسدون في الأرض ويقتل بعضهم بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r2.claim: One view says the angels learned of human corruption from the Preserved Tablet; al-Alusi objects that this leaves their question unanswered and needs a strained reply.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r2.anchor: وقيل : عرفوا ذلك من اللوح ويبعده عدم علم الجواب ويحتاج الجواب إلى تكلف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r3.claim: Another view says they inferred corruption from the non-infallibility of other creatures, which entails sin, conflict, and bloodshed.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r3.anchor: وقيل : عرفوه إستنباطا عما ركز في عقولهم من عدم عصمة غيرهم المفضي إلى العلم بصدور المعصية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r4.claim: A further view says they analogized one of the two morally accountable species to the other because both lack infallibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r4.anchor: وقيل : قياسا لأحد الثقلين على الآخر بجامع إشتراكهما في عدم العصمة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r5.claim: Al-Alusi signals flaws in the two explanations that infer the angels' knowledge from non-infallibility and analogy.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r6.claim: The angels may have inferred the possibility of corruption from the title khalifa: vicegerency entails reform and control of those under the vicegerent, but also the possibility of wrongdoing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أنهم علموا ذلك من تسميته خليفة لأن الخلافة تقتضي الإصلاح وقهر المستخلف عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r7.claim: As a locus of divine majesty and beauty, the vicegerent can manifest both; corruption and bloodshed are effects of majesty, while the angels left the unremarkable effects of beauty unmentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r7.anchor: أو لأنها مجلى الجلال كما أنها مجلى الجمال ولكل آثار والإفساد والسفكمن آثار الجلال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r8.claim: The clause is circumstantial, attached to the subject of “Will You place”; it states the point of difficulty: appointing one who may corrupt while the angels are infallible.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r8.anchor: ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك حال من ضمير الفاعل في ( أتجعل ) وفيها تقرير لجهة الإشكال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r9.claim: The angels seek the reason that would favor appointing the vicegerent; their question is inquiry, not astonishment or boasting that would compromise their infallibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r9.anchor: وليس المقصود إلا الإستفسار عن المرجح لا العجب والتفاخر حتى يضر بعصمتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r10.speaker: الحشوية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r10.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the Hashwiyya claim that the angels' comparison expresses pride and thereby harms their infallibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r10.anchor: حتى يضر بعصمتهم كما زعمت الحشوية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r11.claim: It is not established that a nominal clause used as an emphatic circumstantial clause must omit its pronoun and conjunction; al-Alusi cites Sharh al-Tashil.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r11.anchor: ولزوم الضمير وترك الواو في الجملة الأسمية إذا وقعت حالا مؤكدة غير مسلم كما في شرح التسهيل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r12.claim: The imperfect verbs indicate continuous action.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r13.claim: Putting the subject before the verbal predicate conveys restriction: the angels, in contrast to the proposed vicegerent, glorify God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r13.anchor: وتقديم المسند إليه على المسند الفعلي للإختصاص

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r14.claim: Al-Alusi calls far-fetched the parsing of the clause as an interrogative with both the interrogative particle and its counterpart omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r14.anchor: ومن الغريب جعل الجملة إستفهامية حذف منها الأداة وكذا المعادل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r15.claim: Tasbih literally means declaring God far removed; here it means declaring Him free of whatever is unbefitting, and it takes a direct object or a lām-marked object.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r15.anchor: والتسبيح في الأصل مطلق التبعيد والمراد به تبعيد الله تعالى عن السوء وهو متعد بنفسه ويعدى باللام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r16.claim: The lām in “for You” can mark devotion: the act is done for God and sincerely for His sake.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r16.anchor: إشعارا بأن إيقاع الفعل لأجل الله تعالى وخالصا لوجهه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r17.claim: The omitted object of tasbih may be construed with the lām, following the parallel construction, or without it, following the verb's basic transitivity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r17.anchor: فالمفعول المقدر ههنا يمكن أن يكون باللام على وفق قرينة وأن يكون بدونه كما هو أصله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r18.claim: The phrase “with Your praise” is circumstantial; the bāʾ denotes continued companionship and accompaniment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r18.anchor: و ( بحمدك ) في موضع الحال والباء لإستدامة الصحبة والمعية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r19.claim: If “Your praise” is construed as an active genitive, it figuratively means God's enabling and guidance, denying any implication of angelic self-congratulation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r19.anchor: وإضافة الحمد إما إلى الفاعل والمراد لازمه مجازا من التوفيق والهداية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r20.claim: If “Your praise” is construed as an objective genitive, the angels mean that they praise God because He enabled them to glorify Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222/r20.anchor: أو إلى المفعول أي متلبسين بحمدنا لك على ما وفقتنا لتسبيحك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r1.claim: Tasbih may denote the specific formula “Glory to the Possessor of sovereignty and dominion, glory to the Possessor of might and power, glory to the Living who never dies.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r1.anchor: المراد به تسبيح خاص وهو سبحان ذي الملك والملكوت سبحان ذي العظمة والجبروت سبحان الحي الذي لا يموت

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the angels mean “Glory be to God and praise be to Him.”

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r3.speaker: أبو ذر عن النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r3.claim: In a report transmitted from Ubadah ibn al-Samit from Abu Dharr, the Prophet calls “Glory be to God and praise be to Him” the best utterance God chose for His angels or servants; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r3.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت عن أبي ذر أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم سئل أي الكلام أفضل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r4.claim: Taqdis is commonly treated as synonymous with tasbih.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r4.anchor: والتقديسفي المشهور كالتسبيح معنى وأحتاجوا لدفع التكرار إلى أن أحدهما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r5.claim: To avoid redundancy, one view assigns tasbih to deeds and taqdis to beliefs.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r5.anchor: وأحتاجوا لدفع التكرار إلى أن أحدهما بإعتبار الطاعات والآخر الإعتقادات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r6.claim: Another view makes tasbih transcendence from what is unbefitting and taqdis a stronger transcendence of God's essence from what He does not deem fitting; the pairing “سبوح قدوس” supports this.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : التسبيح تنزيهه تعالى عما لا يليق به والتقديس تنزيهه في ذاته عما لا يراه لائقا بنفسه فهو أبلغ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r7.claim: Taqdis may also mean purification: the angels purify themselves from impurities, their acts from sins, or their hearts from attending to anything besides God.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون بمعنى التطهير والمراد نسبحك ونطهر أنفسنا من الأدناس أو أفعالنا من المعاصي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r8.claim: The lām in “for You” may mark purpose with nuqaddisu, be a transitive marker as in “I prostrated to God,” indicate clarification, or be extra with the object understood as the prepositional phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r8.anchor: ولام ( لك ) إما للعلة متعلق بنقدس والحمل على التنازع مما فيه تنازع أو معدية للفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r9.claim: The apparent reading is that the same angels utter both clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r9.anchor: ثم الظاهر أن قائل هذه الجملة هو قائل الجملة الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r10.speaker: صفي الدين الخزرجي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r10.claim: Al-Khazraji says the speakers differ: Iblis, included among the angels, voiced the objection, while the other angels voiced glorification after his refusal separated him from them; al-Alusi calls this an interpretive gloss, not tafsir.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r10.anchor: وأغرب الشيخ صفي الدين الخزرجي في كتابه فك الأزرار فجعل القائل مختلفا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r11.claim: Al-Khazraji compares the two-part response to the divided alternative “Be Jews or Christians and you will be guided.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r11.anchor: فالكلام شبيه بقوله تعالى : ( وقالوا كونوا هودا أو نصارى تهتدوا )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r12.claim: God means that He knows the wisdom in appointing the vicegerent, of which the angels know nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r12.anchor: أي اعلم من الحكم في ذلك ما أنتم بمعزل عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r13.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r13.claim: One explanation is that God knows Iblis's coming disobedience and Adam's obedience.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : أراد بذلك علمه بمعصية إبليس وطاعة آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r14.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r14.claim: Another explanation is that prophets and righteous people will descend from the vicegerent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r14.anchor: وقيل : بأنه سيكون من ذلك الخليفة أنبياء وصالحون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r15.claim: Al-Alusi prefers explaining the unspecified knowledge by God's statement that He knows the unseen of the heavens and earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r15.anchor: وقيل : الأحسن أن يفسر هذا المبهم بما أخبر به تعالى عنه بقوله سبحانه : ( إني أعلم غيب السموات والأرض )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r16.speaker: قوم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r16.claim: The mystical reading sees the verse as explaining the complete wisdom of vicegerency: God manifests His names and attributes through a fully prepared human mirror, since the angels' limited readiness cannot manifest them all.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r16.anchor: أن المراد من الآية بيان الحكمة في الخلافة على دق وجه وأكمله فكأنه قال جل شأنه أريد الظهور بأسمائي وصفاتي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r17.claim: أعلم is an imperfect verb here; construing it as the elative adjective “more knowing” is not an acceptable reading of the Qur'an.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p222#2/r17.anchor: و ( أعلم ) فعل مضارع وإحتمال أنه أفعل تفضيل مما لا ينبغي أن يخرج عليه كتاب الله سبحانه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r1.claim: The phrase may mean And your Lord said, with idh redundant, or may mean Remember when your Lord said; this explains similar Quranic constructions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r1.anchor: أي وقال ربك وإذ زائدة وقيل معناه واذكر إذ قال ربك وكذلك كل ما ورد في القرآن من هذا النحو

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r2.speaker: المبرد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad says idh is past and idha future, though either can stand in place of the other; idh with a future form means a past event, as in 8:30.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r2.anchor: قال المبرد: إذا جاء {إذ} مع المستقبل كان معناه ماضيا كقوله تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r3.claim: Malak derives from ma'lak, from words meaning message; the hamza shifted after the lam, then was dropped for ease of frequent use and its vowel moved to the lam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r3.anchor: وأصله مألك من المألكة والألوكة والألوك، وهي: الرسالة فقلبت فقيل ملأك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r4.claim: The angels addressed were those who had lived on earth after God settled angels in heaven and jinn on earth; the jinn later became envious, rebellious, corrupt, and murderous.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r4.anchor: وذلك أن الله تعالى خلق السماء والأرض وخلق الملائكة والجن فأسكن الملائكة السماء وأسكن الجن الأرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r5.claim: A force of angels called jinn, the keepers of the gardens, led by Iblis, drove the earthly jinn into mountains, valleys, and islands, then occupied earth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r5.anchor: فبعث الله إليهم جندا من الملائكة يقال لهم: الجن، وهم خزان الجنان اشتق لهم من الجنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r6.claim: God gave Iblis rule over earth, the lowest heaven, and the Garden treasury; his worship across these places led him to pride and the belief that he was God's most honored angel.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r7.anchor: خالق. {في الأرض خليفة} أي بدلا منكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r8.claim: The announced khalifa is a replacement for the angels, whom God will raise up to Him; they disliked this because they had been the least worshipful angels.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p78/r8.anchor: أي بدلا منكم ورافعكم إلي، فكرهوا ذلك لأنهم كانوا أهون الملائكة عبادة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r1.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r1.claim: One view identifies the khalifa as Adam because he came after the jinn; another says he is called khalifa because others will succeed him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r1.anchor: والمراد بالخليفة هاهنا آدم سماه خليفة لأنه خلف الجن أي جاء بعدهم وقيل لأنه يخلفه غيره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r2.claim: Baghawi prefers that Adam is God's deputy on earth, charged with establishing His rulings and carrying out His commands.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r2.anchor: والصحيح أنه خليفة الله في أرضه لإقامة أحكامه وتنفيذ وصاياه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r3.claim: The angels mean disobedience and unlawful bloodshed, as the jinn had done; they inferred the unseen from what they had witnessed, though they did not know it directly.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r3.anchor: {ويسفك الدماء} بغير حق أي كما فعل بنو الجان فقاسوا الشاهد على الغائب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r4.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the angels say Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi; this is the prayer of creation, beasts, and other creatures besides humans, by which they receive provision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: نقول سبحان الله وبحمده

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r5.speaker: أبو ذر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r5.claim: Abu Dharr reports that the Prophet named Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi as the best speech chosen by God for His angels or servants; Baghawi gives no grading.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r5.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت عن أبي ذر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل أي الكلام أفضل قال:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r6.claim: Another explanation is that the angels mean they pray in accordance with God's command; Ibn Abbas says tasbih throughout the Quran means prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r6.anchor: وقيل: ونحن نصلي بأمرك، قال ابن عباس: كل ما في القرآن من التسبيح فالمراد منه الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r7.claim: Qaddas means to praise God as holy and pure; other explanations are to purify themselves for obedience or to declare Him transcendent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r7.anchor: أي نثني عليك بالقدس والطهارة وقيل: ونطهر أنفسنا لطاعتك وقيل: وننزهك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r8.claim: The lām is an added connective particle.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r8.anchor: واللام صلة وقيل: لم يكن هذا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r9.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r9.claim: One view says the angels were not objecting or boasting of their deeds; they were expressing wonder and seeking the wisdom behind the decision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r9.anchor: وقيل: لم يكن هذا من الملائكة على طريق الاعتراض والعجب بالعمل بل على سبيل التعجب وطلب وجه الحكمة فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r10.claim: God's answer points to the wisdom and benefit in His decision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r10.anchor: الله {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} المصلحة فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r11.claim: One explanation is that Adam's descendants will include obedient prophets, saints, and scholars.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r11.anchor: وقيل: إني أعلم أن في ذريته من يطيعني ويعبدني من الأنبياء والأولياء والعلماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r12.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r12.claim: Another explanation is that an angel among them, Iblis, will disobey God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r12.anchor: وقيل: إني أعلم أن فيكم من يعصيني وهو إبليس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r13.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r13.claim: A further explanation is that humans will sin and God will forgive them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r13.anchor: وقيل إني أعلم أنهم يذنبون وأنا أغفر لهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r14.speaker: أهل الحجاز والبصرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r14.claim: The Hijaz and Basra readers open the ya in inni a'lam and in most possessive ya forms before an alif with fatḥa; readers differ on the detailed exceptions.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p79/r14.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة إني أعلم بفتح الياء وكذلك كل ياء إضافة استقبلها ألف مفتوحة إلا في مواضع معدودة

BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r1.claim: Wa-idh is the object of an omitted imperative, 'remember'; commanding recollection of the time also requires remembering its events and details.
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r1.anchor: {وإذ} مفعول اذكر مقدرة أي : اذكر لهم وأخبر وقت

BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r2.claim: The recipient phrase routinely comes first in this construction because the quoted speech is often long, while its placement adds emphasis and anticipation.
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r2.anchor: {للملائكة} اللام للتبليغ وتقديم الجار والمجرور في هذا الباب

BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r3.claim: Malāʾika is the plural of malak, with tāʾ marking a feminine collective; angels are named as intermediaries and messengers between God and people, from alūka, message.
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r3.anchor: والملائكة جمع ملك والتاء لتأكيد تأنيث الجماعة وسموا بها

BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r4.speaker: أكثر المسلمين
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r4.claim: Most Muslims hold that angels are subtle bodies able to assume different forms; the prophets' sightings are evidence.
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r4.anchor: والملائكة عند أكثر المسلمين أجسام لطيفة قادرة على التشكل بأشكال مختلفة

BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r5.claim: A report scales angelic populations by successive tenfold ratios from humans, jinn, and animal kinds through the seven heavens, then describes six hundred thousand vast throne pavilions.
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r5.anchor: وروي في شرح كثرتهم أن بني آدم عشر الجن وهما عشر حيوانات البر والكل عشر الطيور

BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r6.claim: The same report says each span of the throne pavilions contains angels prostrating, bowing, or standing and glorifying God.
BURSEVI:v1p72#3/r6.anchor: وما منه من مقدار شبر إلا وفيه ملك ساجد أو راكع أو قائم لهم زجل بالتسبيح والتقديس

BURSEVI:v1p73/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73/r1.claim: The report says angels around the Throne are like a drop in the sea, with further countless ranks serving the Tablet and Gabriel; only God knows their kinds and worship.
BURSEVI:v1p73/r1.anchor: الذين يحومون حول العرش كالقطرة في البحر

BURSEVI:v1p73/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v1p73/r2.claim: During the Ascension the Prophet saw angels continually walking past a station; Gabriel did not know where they went and had never seen one return.
BURSEVI:v1p73/r2.anchor: وروي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم حين عرج به إلى السماء رأى ملائكة في موضع بمنزلة شرف

BURSEVI:v1p73/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73/r3.claim: In the same report, an angel says he cannot date his creation, but God has made a star every four thousand years and four hundred thousand since his creation.
BURSEVI:v1p73/r3.anchor: فقال : لا أدري غير أن الله تعالى يخلق في كل أربعة آلاف سنة كوكبا

BURSEVI:v1p73/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73/r4.claim: The account says jinn, children of al-Jānn, were created from smokeless flame between heaven and earth and inhabited earth long before Adam.
BURSEVI:v1p73/r4.anchor: وخلق الله الجان من لهب من نار لا دخان لها بين السماء والأرض

BURSEVI:v1p73/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73/r5.claim: After a long period, the jinn grew envious and oppressive, corrupted the earth, and killed; God sent the lowest-heaven angels under Iblis to defeat and expel them.
BURSEVI:v1p73/r5.anchor: فعمروا دهرا طويلا في الأرض مقدار سبعة آلاف سنة ثم ظهر فيهم الحسد والبغي فأفسدوا وقتلوا

BURSEVI:v1p73/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73/r6.claim: The narrative gives Iblis the name ʿAzāzīl and describes his rule over earth, the lowest heaven, and Paradise's treasury; he became proud of God's favors and imagined himself most honored.
BURSEVI:v1p73/r6.anchor: وكان اسمه عزازيل وكان أكثرهم علما فهبطوا إلى الأرض حتى هزموا الجن

BURSEVI:v1p73/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73/r7.claim: Jāʿil means making or appointing; the khalīfa is Adam, succeeding the jinn on earth, where the prior corruption and oppression occurred.
BURSEVI:v1p73/r7.anchor: {إني جاعل} أي : مصير {في الأرض} دون السماء لأن التباغي والتظالم

BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r1.claim: God preserves the world through a single pole-like khalīfa in each age: Adam began the succession and Jesus will end it.
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r1.anchor: واعلم أن الله تعالى يحفظ العالم بالخليفة كما يحفظ الخزائن بالختم

BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r2.claim: A vicegerent mediates divine influx because God is utterly transcendent while recipients are entangled in bodily needs and blameworthy traits; the mediator has both transcendence and attachment.
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r2.anchor: والحكمة في الاستخلاف قصور المستخلف عليه عن قبول فيضه وتلقى أمره بغير واسطة

BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r3.claim: Bursevī illustrates mediation with cartilage between bone and flesh, a minister between ruler and subjects, and dry wood between fire and wet wood.
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r3.anchor: ألا يرى أن العظم لما عجز عن أخذ الغذاء من اللحم لما بينهما من التباعد جعل الله تعالى بحكمته بينهما الغضروف

BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r4.claim: The first purpose of telling the angels is to teach consultation with trustworthy advisers before acting, despite God's complete knowledge and wisdom.
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r4.anchor: الأول : تعليم المشاورة في أمورهم قبل أن يقدموا عليها وعرضها على ثقاتهم

BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r5.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r5.claim: The cited Mathnawī verses say consultation brings insight and wisdom, as minds assist one another.
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r5.anchor: مشورت إدراك وهشياري دهد عقلها مر عقل را يارى دهد

BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r6.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r6.claim: Bursevī cites the Prophet's instruction to consult, since the person consulted is entrusted with confidence.
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r6.anchor: كفت يغمبر بكم أي : رأى زن

BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r7.claim: Bursevī also says even the wisest man, finest mount, and most devout woman need a counselor, a whip, and a spouse respectively.
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r7.anchor: ويقال : أعقل الرجال لا يستغني عن مشاورة أولي الألباب

BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r8.claim: The second purpose is to honor Adam by announcing his coming to the inhabitants of the divine realm and naming him khalīfa before his creation.
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r8.anchor: والثاني : تعظيم شأن المجعول بأن بشر بوجوده سكان ملكوته ولقبه بالخليفة قبل خلقه

BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r9.claim: The third purpose is to disclose Adam's outweighing merit despite the corruption angels anticipate, through their question and God's answer.
BURSEVI:v1p73#2/r9.anchor: والثالث : إظهار فضله الراجح على ما فيه من المفاسد بسؤالهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r1.claim: The announcement of Adam’s creation and honor, including God’s command that the angels prostrate, is a third favor extending to all his descendants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r1.anchor: تعداد لنعمة ثالثة تعم الناس كلهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r2.claim: إذ marks a past time in which another event occurred, while إذا marks a future time; both are annexed to clauses, built like relative forms, used causally or conditionally, and always adverbial because they are nondeclinable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r2.anchor: وإذا: ظرف وضع لزمان نسبة ماضية وقع فيه أخرى

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r3.claim: In 46:21, ‘remember the brother of ʿĀd when he warned his people’ means remember the event at that time: the event is omitted and its ظرف stands in its place.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r3.anchor: فعلى تأويل: اذكر الحادث إذا كان كذا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r4.claim: The عامل for إذ may be قالوا, اذكر understood as in its many explicit Qur’anic uses, or an implicit phrase from the preceding verse; on the last analysis this clause coordinates with خلق لكم within its relative clause.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r4.anchor: أو أذكر على التأويل المذكور لأنه جاء معمولا له صريحا في القرآن كثيرا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r5.speaker: معمر
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r5.anchor: في حكم الصلة. وعن معمر أنه مزيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r6.claim: الملائكة is the plural of ملأك in its original form, like الشمائل from شمأل; مألك is inverted from مألكة, a message, since angels convey God’s messages to people or are messengers to them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r6.anchor: والملائكة جمع ملأك على الأصل كالشمائل جمع شمأل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r7.speaker: أكثر المسلمين
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r7.claim: Most Muslims hold that angels are subtle bodies able to assume different forms, reasoning that messengers saw them in such forms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r7.anchor: فذهب أكثر المسلمين إلى أنها أجسام لطيفة قادرة على التشكل بأشكال مختلفة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r8.speaker: طائفة من النصارى
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r8.claim: A group of Christians holds that angels are virtuous human souls separated from their bodies.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r8.anchor: وقالت طائفة من النصارى: هي النفوس الفاضلة البشرية المفارقة للأبدان

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r9.speaker: الحكماء
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r9.claim: The philosophers describe angels as immaterial substances distinct from rational souls; one class is absorbed in knowing God and free of other occupation, the exalted, close angels, who glorify without tiring.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r9.anchor: وزعم الحكماء أنهم جواهر مجردة مخالفة للنفوس الناطقة في الحقيقة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r10.speaker: الحكماء
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r10.claim: In the philosophers’ account, the second class manages affairs from heaven to earth as divinely decreed; they include celestial and earthly angels.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30/r10.anchor: وقسم يدبر الأمر من السماء إلى الأرض على ما سبق به القضاء وجرى به القلم الإلهي

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r1.claim: The unqualified address includes all angels; alternatives limit it to angels of earth or to Iblis and his angelic company, who were sent to defeat corrupting jinn that had first inhabited earth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r1.anchor: والمقول لهم: الملائكة كلهم لعموم اللفظ وعدم المخصص

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r2.claim: جاعل from جعل takes two objects, here في الأرض and خليفة, because it is future and depends on a subject; it can also mean ‘creator.’
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r2.anchor: وجاعل: من جعل الذي له مفعولان

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r3.claim: خليفة is one who succeeds or represents another, with its feminine ending marking intensification.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r3.anchor: والخليفة من يخلف غيره وينوب منابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r4.claim: The primary referent is Adam, and more generally every prophet God appoints to cultivate the earth, govern people, perfect their souls, and execute His command; this appointment answers human inability to receive divine command without an intermediary, not any need in God for a deputy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r4.anchor: والمراد به آدم عليه الصلاة والسلام لأنه كان خليفة الله في أرضه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r5.claim: God does not appoint an angel as prophet because people cannot receive His effusion and command directly; perfected prophets receive angels, while the highest may speak to God without an intermediary, as Moses and Muhammad did.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r5.anchor: ولذلك لم يستنبىء ملكا كما قال

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r6.claim: Other interpretations take خليفة as a successor to earth’s previous inhabitants, or as Adam together with his descendants succeeding predecessors or one another; the singular may stand for his descendants, ‘one who succeeds you,’ or a collective succession.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r6.anchor: أو خليفة من سكن الأرض قبله

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#2/r7.claim: God’s announcement teaches consultation, honors the future inhabitant by naming him before creation, and displays his preponderant virtue through the angels’ question and answer; wisdom requires abundant good even when accompanied by lesser evil.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r1.claim: The angels express surprise that a corruptor be appointed to cultivate and repair the earth, or that sinful people replace its obedient inhabitants; they seek the hidden wisdom like learners seeking clarification, not objecting to God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r1.anchor: تعجب من أن يستخلف لعمارة الأرض وإصلاحها من يفسد فيها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r2.claim: Their question is neither objection nor backbiting against humanity: angels are too honored for that, as 21:26–27 says they do not precede God in speech and obey Him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r2.anchor: وليس باعتراض على الله تعالى جلت قدرته

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r3.claim: The angels may have known of future corruption from God’s report, the Preserved Tablet, reasoned that infallibility belongs to angels, or inferred it by analogy between the two kinds of beings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r3.anchor: وإنما عرفوا ذلك بإخبار من الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r4.claim: The related verbs all mean pouring: سفك is used of blood and tears, سبك of molten jewels, سفح for pouring from above, and شن (also سن) for pouring from a waterskin’s mouth.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r4.anchor: والسفك والسبك والسفح والشن أنواع من الصب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#3/r5.claim: An unnamed reading makes يسفك passive; the omitted agent referring to من, whether relative or adjective, is understood as ‘blood is shed among them.’

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r1.claim: This circumstantial clause explains the question as a friend asking why a trusted stranger is favored: why appoint sinners when we are sinless and more entitled? Its purpose is to ask what favors humans, not to boast.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r2.claim: The angels understood humans to combine appetite and anger, which could cause corruption and bloodshed, with intellect, which prompts knowledge and obedience. Considering the powers separately, they thought angels could realize intellect’s benefits without those harms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r2.anchor: وكأنهم علموا أن المجعول خليفة ذو ثلاث قوى عليها مدار أمره

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r3.claim: They overlooked that appetite and anger, disciplined by reason, yield chastity, courage, resisting desire, and justice; the human composite also enables grasping particulars, inventing crafts, and bringing nature’s potential benefits into actuality, the purpose of succession.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#4/r3.anchor: وغفلوا عن فضيلة كل واحدة من القوتين إذا صارت مهذبة مطواعة للعقل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r1.claim: God’s reply asserts knowledge of the wisdom the angels had not grasped, including the good achieved through the human composite and its disciplined powers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r1.anchor: قال إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r2.claim: Both tasbīḥ and taqdīs declare God far removed from imperfection; the terms evoke traveling far through land or water. Taqdīs also means purification, since cleansing removes impurity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r2.anchor: والتسبيح تبعيد الله تعالى عن السوء وكذلك التقديس

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r3.claim: بحمدك is circumstantial: ‘while praising You for teaching us to know You and enabling our glorification’; this qualification prevents the angels’ self-attribution of praise from implying conceit.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r3.anchor: في موضع الحال، أي: متلبسين بحمدك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r4.claim: We purify our souls from sins for Your sake; the angels set glorification against the corruption (understood by some as idolatry) and purification against the grave vice of bloodshed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r4.anchor: ونقدس لك نطهر نفوسنا عن الذنوب لأجلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r5.claim: Some hold that the lām in لك is extra.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:30#5/r5.anchor: عن الآثام وقيل: نقدسك واللام مزيدة

BURSEVI:v1p74/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74/r1.claim: Wisdom permits a small evil when it prevents a much greater evil, as removing a diseased limb can save the whole body.
BURSEVI:v1p74/r1.anchor: بيان أن الحكمة تقتضي ما يغلب خيره فإن ترك الخير الكثير لأجل الشر القليل شر كثير

BURSEVI:v1p74/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74/r2.claim: Repeating the locative phrase emphasizes how implausible the angels find the prospect of corruption on earth.

BURSEVI:v1p74/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74/r3.claim: The angels mean unjustly spilling blood, and the wording names bloodshed because it is the ugliest kind of killing.
BURSEVI:v1p74/r3.anchor: أي : يصبها ظلما كما يسفك بنو الجان والتعبير عن القتل بسفك الدماء لما أنه أقبح أنواع القتل

BURSEVI:v1p74/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74/r4.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v1p74/r4.claim: Some gnostics identify the disputers as earth angels, jinn, and devils dominated by darkness, rather than heavenly angels who recognize the Perfect Human’s rank.
BURSEVI:v1p74/r4.anchor: قال بعض العارفين الملائكة الذين نازعوا في آدم ليسوا من أهل الجبروت ولا من أهل الملكوت السماوية

BURSEVI:v1p74/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74/r5.claim: Mentioning earth signals that earth angels challenged Adam; heavenly angels administer the upper world, while earth angels envied the caliphate and their own dominion.
BURSEVI:v1p74/r5.anchor: بتخصيص الأرض بالذكر وإن كان خليفة في العالم كله في الحقيقة هو إيماء أيضا بأن ملائكة الأرض هم الطاعنون

BURSEVI:v1p74/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74/r6.claim: The angels’ objection and dispute before the wise Creator is excused because of His perfect wisdom and workmanship.
BURSEVI:v1p74/r6.anchor: وأما الاعتراض على فعل الحكيم والنزاع في صنعه عند حضرته فمعفو عنه لكمال حكمته وإتقان صنعته

BURSEVI:v1p74/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74/r7.speaker: المثنوي
BURSEVI:v1p74/r7.claim: The Mathnawi says divine mercy precedes wrath and that God’s disclosure of this precedence places the impulse to question in the listener.
BURSEVI:v1p74/r7.anchor: قال في "المثنوي" : زانكه أين دمها اكر نالا يقست رحمت من بر غضب هم سابقست

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r1.claim: The continuation of the Mathnawi image compares the angels’ forbearance to foam on a sea of divine forbearance: foam passes, while the sea remains.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r1.anchor: حلم ايشان كف بحر حلم ماست كف رود آيد ولى دريا بجاست

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r2.speaker: الفتوحات
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r2.claim: The Futuhat says Harut and Marut were among the angels who disputed Adam and were tested by God through manifesting corruption and bloodshed.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r2.anchor: وفي "الفتوحات" أن هاروت وماروت من الملائكة الدين نازعوا آدم ولأجل هذا ابتلاهما الله تعالى بإظهار الفساد وسفك الدماء

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r3.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r3.claim: The Prophet warns against gloating over a brother’s misfortune, since God may relieve him and test the one who gloats.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r3.anchor: فافهم سر قوله عليه السلام : "دع الشماتة عن أخيك فيعافيه الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r4.claim: Some angels sent to aid the fighters also shed blood, but do so zealously in defense of God’s religion and law.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r4.anchor: وأيضا من تلك الملائكة الطاعنين بسفك الدماء الملائكة التي أرسلها الله تعالى نصرة للمجاهدين

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r5.claim: Tasbih declares God free of what is unfitting; praise recalls His blessings; taqdis describes Him with fitting exaltation and denies what is unfitting.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r5.anchor: فالتسبيح لإظهار صفات الجلال والحمد لتذكير صفات الأنعام

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r6.claim: The lām in “for You” may explain the act, as in a supplication formula, or be an added particle; the implied object is sanctifying God.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r6.anchor: فاللام للبيان كما في سقيا لك متعلقة بمصدر محذوف ويجوز أن تكون مزيدة

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r7.speaker: التيسير
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r7.claim: Al-Taysir distinguishes tasbih as negating what is unfitting for God and taqdis as affirming what is fitting for Him.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r7.anchor: قال في "التيسير" التسبيح نفي ما لا يليق به والتقديس إثبات ما يليق به

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r8.speaker: داود القيصري
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r8.claim: Dawud al-Qaysari says tasbih is broader: taqdis also negates perfections ascribed to created things, since their attachment to creation restricts them.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r8.anchor: وقال الشيخ داود القيصري قدس سره التسبيح أعم من التقديس لأنه تنزيه الحق عن نقائص الإمكان والحدوث

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r9.claim: The angels’ question expresses their claim to greater entitlement to the caliphate and asks why humans were preferred despite their expected corruption.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r9.anchor: والمقصود عرض أحقيتهم منهم بالخلافة والاستفسار عما رجح بني آدم عليهم مع ما هو متوقع منهم من الفساد

BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r10.claim: God knows the wisdom of appointing Adam: his descendants include obedient and disobedient people, through whom merit and justice become manifest; creatures cannot know the Creator’s hidden governance.
BURSEVI:v1p74#2/r10.anchor: من الحكمة والمصلحة باستخلاف آدم عليه السلام وإن من ذريته الطائع والعاصي فيظهر الفضل والعدل

BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r1.claim: The seeker should show humility before God, His caliphs, shaykhs, and scholars, avoiding ego and displays of knowledge; one pursuing annihilation should not admire the self.
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r1.anchor: وفي الآية تنبيه للسالك بأن يتأدب بين يدي الحق تعالى وخلفائه والمشايخ والعلماء لئلا يظهر بالأنانية

BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r2.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r2.claim: Saʿdi’s poem warns against approaching a temptation after seeing another caught by it, and against learning from others’ misfortunes only when they befall oneself.
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r2.anchor: قال السعدي : نرود مرغ سوى دانه فراز ون دكر مرغ بيند اندربند

BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r3.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation says jaʿl is broader than creation: it includes creating Adam and additionally endowing him with the special attribute of caliphate, as with David.
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r3.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل فى الارض خليفة} إنما قال جاعل وما قال خالق لمعنيين

BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r4.claim: It also assigns jaʿl to the world of Command and malakut, in contrast with creation of the sensory world; the Qur’an calls heavens and earth created but darkness and light made.
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r4.anchor: أن للجعلية اختصاصا بعالم الأمور وهو للملكوت وهو ضد عالم الخلق لأنه هو عالم الأجسام والمحسوسات

BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r5.claim: This reading treats darkness and light as malakuti rather than sensory realities, since sensory darkness and light are already contained in the heavens and earth.
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r5.anchor: وإنما قلنا الظلمات والنور من الملكوتيات

BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r6.claim: Adam is called created from clay in reference to his body, but made a caliph in reference to his spirit; this marks his distinction and dignity.
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r6.anchor: فكذلك لما أخبر الله تعالى عن آدم بما يتعلق بجسمانيته ذكره بالخلقية

BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r7.claim: God’s announcement of Adam’s caliphate displays his honor to the angels, so they should revere him rather than reject the human traits shown by him and his descendants.
BURSEVI:v1p74#3/r7.anchor: وفي إني جاعل إشارة أخرى وهو إظهار عزة آدم عليه السلام على الملائكة لينظروا إليه بنظر التعظيم

BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r1.claim: One purpose of calling Adam caliph is to show that God graciously accepted humanity for servanthood and caliphate, encouraging people not to despair but to continue serving.
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r1.anchor: ومنها لنعلم أن الله تعالى من كمال فضله وكرمه قد قبلنا بالعبودية والخلافة

BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r2.claim: Caliphate depends on spiritual preparedness and capacity, which angels lack; the seeker must value and work to attain this great capacity.
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r2.anchor: ومنها لنعلم أن فساد الاستعداد أمر عظيم وبناء جسيم ومبنى الخلافة على الاستعداد والقابلية وليس للملائكة

BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r3.claim: Angels saw Adam’s body before the spirit was breathed into it and perceived its elemental mixture and human, animal, and predatory traits, reasoning by analogy with animals already created.
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r3.anchor: لأنهم نظروا إلى جسد آدم قبل نفخ الروح فشاهدوا بالنظر الملكي في ملكوت جسده المخلوق من العناصر الأربعة المتضادة

BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r4.claim: What is unseen depends on the observer: the malakut is hidden from sensory humans but visible to angels and to people granted spiritual sight.
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r4.anchor: وهذا لا يكون غيبا في حقهم وإنما يكون غيبا لنا لأنا ننظر بالحس والملكوت يكون لأهل الحس غيبا

BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r5.claim: The malakut is witnessed by angels, while the divine presence remains hidden from them; they cannot ascend to that presence.
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r5.anchor: فالغيب ما غاب عنك وما شاهدته فهو شهادة فالملكوت للملائكة شهادة والحضرة الإلهية لهم غيب

BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r6.claim: Humans unite a sensory body, a spirit from the unseen malakut, and a secret prepared to receive divine illumination; spiritual training raises them from the witnessed world to malakut.
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r6.anchor: وإن في الإنسان صورة من عالم الشهادة المحسوسة وروحا من عالم الغيب الملكوتي غير المحسوس وسرا مستعدا لقبول فيض الأنوار الإلهية

BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r7.claim: Through following the Prophet, the human secret rises from malakut to jabarut and the hidden of the hidden, witnessing the lights of divine beauty and majesty and becoming a caliph of the seen and unseen.
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r7.anchor: وبسر المتابعة وخصوصيتها يترقى من عالم الملكوت إلى عالم الجبروت والعظموت وهو غيب الغيب

BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r8.claim: The human capacity for the hidden of the hidden is the concealed secret in human preparedness that God knows and the angels do not.
BURSEVI:v1p76#2/r8.anchor: فهذا هو السر المكنون المركوز في استعداد الإنسان الذي كان الله يعلم منه والملائكة لا يعلمونه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r5.claim: The account of humanity’s beginning continues the command to worship the Lord and explains the description of God as Lord of the worlds.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r5.anchor: عطفا على قوله : { اعبدوا ربكم } وبيانا لقوله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r1.claim: Biqai outlines four aims of the surah’s discourse: show divine names, awaken hope and fear about the unseen end, recount God’s past acts to spur worship, and reveal the inward reality of the present.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r1.anchor: أحدها التنبيه على الآيات بمقتضى أسماء الله من اسمه الملك إلى اسمه الرحمن الرحيم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r2.claim: Al-Harali links the Adam account to the preceding stages of the surah: after categorizing people and issuing a general call beneath the veil of predestination, revelation now discloses the beginning of human creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r2.anchor: ثم أنزل الخطاب إلى آية الدعوة من وراء حجاب الستر بسابق التقدير فعم به الناس ونبههم على آيات ربوبيته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r3.claim: Biqai reads Adam’s public creation story as a manifest sign concealing the more elevated, privately understood account of Muhammad’s creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r3.anchor: فذكر خلق آدم ظاهر خبء ما عطف عليه وهو والله أعلم ذكر خلق محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r4.claim: “Your Lord” is the benefactor who showed mercy to humanity through Muhammad and kept him concealed within the disclosure of Adam’s creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r4.anchor: أي المحسن إليك برحمة العباد بك الذي خبأك في إظهار خلق آدم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r5.claim: The conjunction wāw joins what follows to something stated or understood before it; idh is an ambiguous noun for a past event or time.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r5.anchor: فإن الواو حرف يجمع ما بعده مع شيء قبله إفصاحا في اللفظ أو إفهاما في المعنى , وإنما يقع ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r6.claim: Qawl is the outward arrangement of verbal forms, like the joining of visible forms; the heart apprehends speech through the ear as it apprehends visible things through sight.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r6.anchor: { قال } من القول وهو إبداء صور الكلم نظما بمنزلة ائتلاف الصور المحسوسة جمعا , فالقول مشهود القلب بواسطة الأذن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r7.speaker: أهل العربية
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r7.claim: The grammarians derive malāʾika from the inverted form malāʾik, itself from maʾlak and the root of sending a message; on this account the mīm is extra.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r7.anchor: وتأويل الملائكة عند أهل العربية أنه جمع ملاك مقلوب من مألك من الألك وهي الرسالة ,

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r8.speaker: أهل العربية
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r8.claim: A second derivation connects malak to dominion and control, as in kneading dough, with an original mīm and the sense of shaping or ordering.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r8.anchor: ويكون الملك من الملك وهو إحكام ما منه التصوير , من ملكت العجين , وجمعه أملاك , تكون فيه الميم أصلية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r9.claim: Biqai proposes that malāʾika gathers both senses, messenger and ordering power, as a coined word can unite meanings from two roots.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r9.anchor: فليكن اسم ملائكة جامعا للمعنيين منحوتا من الأصلين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r10.claim: Biqai compares the blended derivation to insān, which he says carries both the senses of sociability and forgetfulness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p85/r10.anchor: كثيرا ما يوجد ذلك في أسماء الذوات الجامعة كلفظ إنسان بما ظهر فيه من أنه من الأنس والنسيان معا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r1.claim: Biqai describes two levels of discourse, a general one and a higher, more particular one that yields increasingly elevated meanings.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r1.anchor: رتبة عامة ورتبة خاصة أفصح وأعلى كلما وكلاما . قال : وفيه أي هذا الخطاب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r2.claim: The disclosure isolates discerning hearts in attachment to God alone: God gave Adam life without the angels, so hearts should not depend on any created favorite, preparing for the warning about following Satan.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r2.anchor: قال : وفيه أي هذا الخطاب مع ذلك استخلاص لبواطن أهل الفطانة من أن تعلق بواطنهم بأحد من دونه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r3.claim: Biqai says every verse connects with what precedes and prepares for what follows; this coherence is part of the Qur’an’s inimitability.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r3.anchor: وبذلك كان انتظام الآي داخلا في معنى الإعجاز الذي لا يأتي الخلق بمثله ولو كان بعضهم لبعض ظهيرا .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r4.claim: Inna conveys emphasis grounded in the speaker’s own self and knowledge, while the first-person suffix marks attribution to oneself.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r4.anchor: { إني } إن حرف يفهم توكيدا من ذات نفس المؤكد وعلمه . والياء اسم علي يخص المضيف إلى نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r5.claim: Adam’s succession extends across the earth through himself and his descendants; the singular khalīfa suits the completeness of this role, though it can also be generic.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r5.anchor: ولما كانت خلافة آدم عليه السلام كاملة في جميع الأرض بنفسه وبذريته وحد لذلك مع أنه يصح أن يراد به الجنس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r6.claim: A khalīfa is one who carries out the predecessor’s work according to that deputy’s rank; humans succeed one another, while Adam is God’s deputy in the realm of dominion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r6.anchor: الخليفة ذات قائم بما يقوم به المستخلف على حسب رتبة ذلك الخليفة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r7.claim: The reminder invites worship and love by recounting God’s favors before humanity existed: His defense of them before angels, Adam’s knowledge and honor, and His forgiveness of Adam despite expelling Iblis after his worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p86/r7.anchor: فذكر لهم ما حاج به ملائكته عنهم , وما شرف به أباهم آدم من العلم وأمر الملائكة المقربين بالسجود له

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r11.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r11.claim: Abu Malik says every Qur'anic statement introduced by “when” refers to something that has occurred.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r11.anchor: عن أبي مالك قال: ما كان في القرآن {إذ} فقد كان

DURR-FULL:v1p110/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r1.claim: Al-Hasan glosses “I am placing” as “I am making.”
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {إني جاعل} قال: فاعل

DURR-FULL:v1p110/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r2.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says every occurrence of “made” in the Qur'an means “created.”
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: كل شيء في القرآن {جعل} فهو خلق

DURR-FULL:v1p110/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says God brought Adam out of Paradise before creating him, then cites this verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن الله أخرج آدم من الجنة قبل أن يخلقه ثم قرأ {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة}

DURR-FULL:v1p110/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r4.claim: A report authenticated by al-Hakim says jinn inhabited earth for two thousand years before Adam, corrupted it and shed blood; angels drove them away, prompting their question about a successor.
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: لقد أخرج الله آدم من الجنة قبل أن يدخلها قال الله

DURR-FULL:v1p110/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r5.claim: Ibn Umar is reported as giving the same account as Ibn Abbas about the earlier jinn and the angels' question.
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عمر مثله

DURR-FULL:v1p110/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Iblis belonged to a group called jinn among the angels, was made from scorching fire, and was named al-Harith; other angels were from light and jinn from flame.
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان إبليس من حي من أحياء الملائكة يقال لهم الجن خلقوا من نار السموم

DURR-FULL:v1p110/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r7.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account, jinn first inhabited earth and fought, shed blood, and were defeated by Iblis and an angel army, who drove them to islands and mountain edges.
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r7.anchor: فأول من سكن الأرض الجن فأفسدوا فيها وسفكوا الدماء وقتلوا بعضهم بعضا فبعث الله اليهم إبليس في جند من الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v1p110/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says Iblis became proud after defeating the jinn, while God knew the arrogance in his heart that the angels could not see.
DURR-FULL:v1p110/r8.anchor: فلما فعل إبليس ذلك اغتر بنفسه وقال: قد صنعت شيئا لم يصنعه أحد فاطلع الله على ذلك من قلبه ولم يطلع عليه الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v1p113/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r1.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r1.claim: The angels first submitted, then objected that a successor would corrupt earth; after God turned from them, they circled the Throne six years seeking forgiveness and repenting.
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r1.anchor: عن أنس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن أول من لبى الملائكة قال الله {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة قالوا أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء}

DURR-FULL:v1p113/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r2.speaker: ابن سابط
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r2.claim: Ibn Sabit attributes to the Prophet a report that earth was spread from Mecca, angels first circumambulated its House, and prophets and righteous survivors worshipped there; graves of Noah, Hud, Shuayb, and Salih lie near Zamzam and the sanctuary.
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r2.anchor: عن ابن سابط أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: دحيت الأرض من مكة وكانت الملائكة تطوف بالبيت فهي أول من طاف به

DURR-FULL:v1p113/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r3.claim: Qatada explains the angels' tasbih as glorification and their taqdis as prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} قال التسبيح التسبيح والتقديس الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v1p113/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r4.claim: Abu Dharr reports the Prophet saying God's most beloved words are those He chose for His angels: “Glory to my Lord and praise,” also phrased “Glory be to God and praise.”
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r4.anchor: عن أبي ذر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أحب الكلام إلى الله ما اصطفاه الله لملائكته سبحان ربي وبحمده

DURR-FULL:v1p113/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports Gabriel's account: the lowest heaven prostrates, the second bows, and the third stands until Judgment, reciting “Glory to the Lord of dominion,” “Glory to the Lord of might,” and “Glory to the Ever-Living.”
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير إن عمر بن الخطاب سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن صلاة الملائكة فلم يرد عليه شيئا

DURR-FULL:v1p113/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r6.claim: Ibn Masud and some Companions gloss the angels' “we sanctify You” as “we pray to You.”
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r6.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة في قوله {ونقدس لك} قال: نصلي لك

DURR-FULL:v1p113/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says taqdis means purification.
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال التقديس التطهير

DURR-FULL:v1p113/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r8.claim: Mujahid says the angels mean that they magnify and exalt God.
DURR-FULL:v1p113/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ونقدس لك} قال: نعظمك ونكبرك

DURR-FULL:v1p114/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r1.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r1.claim: Abu Salih glosses the angels' words as magnifying and glorifying God.
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r1.anchor: عن أبي صالح في قوله {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} قال: نعظمك ونمجدك

DURR-FULL:v1p114/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r2.claim: An unattributed gloss says God's undisclosed knowledge concerned Iblis and the purpose for which the successor was created.
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r2.anchor: في قوله {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} قال علم من إبليس وخلقه لها

DURR-FULL:v1p114/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r3.claim: Qatada says God knew that this creation would include prophets, messengers, righteous people, and inhabitants of Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} قال: كان في علم الله أنه سيكون من تلك الخليقة أنبياء ورسل وقوم صالحون وساكنو الجنة

DURR-FULL:v1p114/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r4.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says angels worried earth could not hold Adam and his descendants; God answered that He would appoint death, then hope.
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r4.anchor: عن الحسن قال: لما خلق الله آدم وذريته قالت الملائكة: ربنا إن الأرض لم تسعهم

DURR-FULL:v1p114/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r5.claim: Ibn Umar reports angels' challenge and God sending Harut and Marut to earth; they refused idolatry and killing a child, but wine led to intercourse and murder, after which they chose worldly punishment.
DURR-FULL:v1p114/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر أنه سمع رسول الله صلى اله عليه وسلم يقول: إن آدم لما أهبطه إلى الأرض

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r1.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r1.claim: An isolated gloss attributed to Abu Malik renders the opening as “and when—it had been”; the excerpt gives no fuller explanation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r1.anchor: عن السدى عن أبي مالك : قوله : واذ فقد كان

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says God consulted the angels about creating Adam; Qatadah is also reported to hold this account.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r2.anchor: عن السدى : واذ قال ربك للملائكة اني جاعل في الأرض خليفة فاستشار الملائكة في خلق ادم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r3.claim: Hasan glosses “I am appointing” as “I am doing.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r3.anchor: ثنا الحسن ، قال : قال الله للملائكة : اني جاعل في الأرض خليفة قال لهم : اني فاعل

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
