IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the khalifa is a being created apart from the angels to dwell in and cultivate the earth.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r4.anchor: حدثنا محمد بن اسحاق : قوله : اني جاعل في الأرض خليفة يقول : ساكنا وعامرا يسكنها ويعمرها خلقا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r5.speaker: ابن سابط
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r5.claim: Ibn Sabit reports that the earth spread from Mecca and angels first circumambulated the House; he glosses the location of the khalifa as Mecca.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن سابط ان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال : دحيت الأرض من مكة ، واول من طاف بالبيت الملائكة فقال : اني جاعل في الأرض خليفة يعني مكة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r6.claim: When asked whether Adam was created for heaven or earth, Hasan answers that he was created for earth, citing this verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r6.anchor: عن خالد الحذاء قال : سالت الحسن فقلت : يا أبا سعيد ، ادم للسماء خلق أم الأرض ؟ قال : اما تقرا القران :

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says God brought Adam out of the Garden before he had lived in it, and cites the announcement of an earthly khalifa.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r7.anchor: عن رجل عن ابن عباس قال : اخرج الله ادم من الجنة قبل ان يسكنها اياه ، ثم قرا : اني جاعل في الأرض خليفة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r8.speaker: ابن سابط
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r8.claim: Ibn Sabit says the angels mean people will engage in what is forbidden.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن سابط في قول الله : اتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء قال : يعنون الحرام

IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r1.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says jinn inhabited earth two thousand years before Adam, spread corruption and bloodshed, and were driven to sea islands by an angelic force; this explains the angels' question.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال : كان الجن بنو الجان في الأرض قبل ان يخلق ادم بالفي سنة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya says angels were created Wednesday, jinn Thursday, and Adam Friday; rebellious jinn fought angels, so the angels compared humans' coming corruption and bloodshed to the jinn's.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r2.anchor: عن الربيع عن أبي العالية في قول : اني جاعل في الأرض خليفة إلى قوله : واعلم ما تبدون

IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r3.claim: Hasan says God told the angels He would act; they offered their opinion based on knowledge He had given them, while He withheld other knowledge.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r3.anchor: ثنا الحسن قال : قال الله تعالى للملائكة : اني جاعل في الأرض خليفة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r4.claim: Hasan says God put in the angels' hearts that humans would repeat the jinn's corruption and bloodshed, so they asked what they did.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r4.anchor: قال الحسن : ان الجن كانوا في الأرض يفسدون ويسفكون الدماء ولكن جعل الله في قلوبهم ان ذلك سيكون

IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r5.claim: In a report from Ibn Abbas, God says He is creating humans who will envy and kill one another and corrupt the earth, explaining the angels' question.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p77/r5.anchor: عن السدى عمن حدثه عن ابن عباس قوله : اني جاعل في الأرض خليفة قالوا اتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء

IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r1.claim: Qatadah says God knew earthly creatures would corrupt and shed blood; the angels meant humans.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : اتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء قال : كان الله اعلم انه اذا كان في الأرض خلق

IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r2.speaker: ابن سابط
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r2.claim: Ibn Sabit likewise identifies those who corrupt and shed blood as humans.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r2.anchor: عن ابن سابط في قوله : اتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء يعنون الناس

IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r3.speaker: محمد بن علي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r3.claim: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali reports that the angel al-Sijill saw Adam's creation and affairs in the Preserved Tablet and told Harut and Marut; they then spoke from a sense of superiority over the angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r3.anchor: عن معروف - يعني ابن خربؤ المكي عمن سمع أبا جعفر محمد بن علي يقول : السجل ملك

IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r4.speaker: أبي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r4.claim: The narrator's father says the angels who asked this question numbered ten thousand, and a fire from God burned them.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p78/r4.anchor: قال : سمعت أبي يقول : ان الملائكة الذين قالوا : اتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء

IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r1.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says Iblis led the angels of the lowest heaven, then became proud and rebellious; God knew the rebelliousness within Iblis. Al-Suddi is also reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r1.anchor: عن السدى ، عمن عن ابن عباس قال : كان ابليس على ملائكة سماء الدنيا فاستكبر وهم بالمعصية

IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r2.claim: Mujahid says God knew Iblis's disobedience and created him for it.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد : اني اعلم مالا تعلمون قال : علم من ابليس المعصية ، وخلقه لها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r3.claim: Qatadah says God knew this khalifa's line would include messengers, prophets, righteous people, and people who would dwell in the Garden.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p79/r3.anchor: عن قتادة : قوله : اني اعلم ما لا تعلمون قال : كان من علم الله انه سيكون من ذلك الخليفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r1.claim: The waw moves from the creation of heaven and earth to the creation of the first human, combining proofs of oneness and the falsehood of shirk while shifting to earth's human ruler.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r1.anchor: عطفت الواو قصة خلق أول البشر على قصة خلق السماوات والأرض انتقالا بهم في الاستدلال على أن الله واحد وعلى بطلان شركهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r2.claim: Mention of creation for humanity prepared listeners for the account of humanity's origin, which displays God's power, favor in creating and privileging humans, and appointing them as stewards.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r2.anchor: تهيأت أنفسهم لسماع قصة إيجاد منشأ الناس الذين خلقت الأرض لأجلهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r3.claim: Humanity's first creation is the striking beginning of the life that underlies God's creation of earthly things for people, making this transition apt and independently momentous.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r3.anchor: فكان خلق أصلنا هو أبدع مظاهر إحيائنا الذي هو الأصل في خلق ما في الأرض لنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r4.claim: Idh is a time noun for a past relation concurrent with another past relation; because its time is vague, it is always annexed to a clarifying clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r4.anchor: من أسماء الزمان المبهمة تدل على زمان نسبة ماضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r5.claim: Idh usually functions as an adverbial accusative governed by the verb, but al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn Hishām allow it to function as an object, contrary to the apparent majority view.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r6.claim: In expressions such as yawmaʾidh, idh is added to another time noun in a formal construction, signaling that its normally required clause has been omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p395/r6.anchor: وقد يضاف إليها اسم زمان نحو يومئذ وساعتئذ فتجر بإضافة صورية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r1.claim: One proposed implication of the angels' words is that they claim a stronger title to stewardship: their constant obedience contrasts with the expected corruption of the human appointee.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r1.anchor: الاحتمال الثاني : أن يكون الغرض من قولهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r2.claim: On this reading, the angels' statement is a circumstantial clause governed by tajʿalu, while the implied astonishment and challenge also let the interrogative act as its governing element.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r3.claim: Tasbīḥ is speech, or speech with action, that magnifies and declares God free of deficiency; hence remembrance and prayer can be called tasbīḥ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r3.anchor: والتسبيح قول أو مجموع قول مع عمل يدل على تعظيم الله تعالى وتنزيهه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r4.speaker: قوم من أهل اللغة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r4.claim: Some derive tasbīḥ from rapid swimming, extended to the courses of stars and a running horse, and suggest it evokes swift passage in worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r4.anchor: وقد ذكروا أن التسبيح مشتق من السبح وهو الذهاب السريع في الماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r5.claim: The author considers derivation from swimming by metaphor remote; he prefers derivation from subḥān, with the doubled verb pattern, and notes no un-doubled form meaning glorify is attested.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r5.anchor: وعندي أن كون التسبيح مأخوذا من السبح على وجه المجاز بعيد والوجه أنه مأخوذ من كلمة سبحان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r6.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment: the angels glorify God with praise, since their utterance includes praise and exaltation, avoiding strained analyses of the phrase.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405/r6.anchor: فالباء للملابسة أي نسبح تسبيحا مصحوبا بالحمد لك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r1.claim: Taqdīs means declaring free of deficiency and purifying; it can be enacted in practice, as the word muqaddas in Imruʾ al-Qays's verse suggests.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r1.anchor: والتقديس التنزيه والتطهير وهو إما بالفعل كما أطلق المقدس على الراهب في قول امرىء القيس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r2.claim: Taqdīs may also be an act of belief; the hadith lā quddisat umma means God has not purified a community from satanic impurities when its weak cannot claim rights.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r3.claim: Although qaddasa is transitive directly, the lām with its object intensifies the action, as in shakarta laka and naṣaḥtu laka; Arabic usage treats this as eloquent emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r3.anchor: وفعل قدس يتعدى بنفسه فالإتيان باللام مع مفعوله في الآية لإفادة تأكيد حصول الفعل نحو شكرت لك ونصحت لك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r4.claim: The author rejects analyses that attach laka to an omitted word or make it mean for your sake with an omitted object, calling these departures from eloquent usage; an explanatory lām remains possible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r4.anchor: لا تذهب مع الذين جعلوا قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r5.claim: The angels mean that they exalt God through speech and action and declare Him pure through belief in the perfections fitting the divine essence, so the verbs are not redundant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r5.anchor: نحن نعظمك وننزهك والأول بالقول والعمل والثاني باعتقاد صفات الكمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p405#2/r6.claim: The nominal sentence marks the angels' enduring disposition; fronting we may suggest exclusive constancy, but the author considers simple emphasis more likely.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r1.claim: God's reply answers the angels' question in the dialogue: He knows the human qualities of both virtue and corruption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r1.anchor: أي أعلم ما في البشر من صفات الصلاح ومن صفات الفساد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r2.claim: Human virtue fulfills the purpose of cultivating earth, while corruption does not erase that purpose; the whole includes major benefits and displays human differences and divine knowledge, will, and power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r2.anchor: واعلم أن صلاحه يحصل منه المقصد من تعمير الأرض وأن فساده لا يأتي على المقصد بالإبطال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r3.claim: Human virtues may emerge from paired defects: courage, for example, lies between recklessness and cowardice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r3.anchor: ومن أبدع ذلك أن تركب الصفتين الذميمتين يأتي بصفات الفضائل كحدوث الشجاعة من بين طرفي التهور والجبن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r4.claim: The wording need not add what the angels do know after what they do not know, since that is obvious; the emphasis is on the reach of God's knowledge beyond theirs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r4.anchor: لا حاجة هنا لتقدير وما تعلمون بعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r5.claim: The statement closes the exchange and summarizes the proof: God's knowledge exceeds the angels' and He chose Adam as steward knowing his fitness; inna treats their questioning as doubt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p406/r5.anchor: وتأكيد الجملة بأن لتنزيل الملائكة في مراجعتهم وغفلتهم عن الحكمة منزلة المترددين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p407/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p407/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p407/r7.claim: The following verse's teaching of Adam and demonstration of his distinction give detailed evidence for his fitness as steward, explaining what the angels did not know.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p407/r7.anchor: جعله الله حجة على قوله لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p731/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p731/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p731/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur invokes the angels' dialogue as an earlier example of reported speech in dialogue while explaining the unobserved scene in 2:133.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p731/r4.anchor: فقوله : { قالوا أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها } ( البقرة : 30 ) فيكون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r1.claim: Following al-Kashshaf and Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, the author identifies a Qur’anic pattern: warnings are followed by promises and threats by glad tidings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r1.anchor: بوعيد إلا أعقبه بوعد ، وما جاء بنذارة إلا أعقبها ببشارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r2.claim: The author finds this contrastive pattern only rarely in Arab poetry and cites Labid as an example.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r2.anchor: ورأيت منه قليلا في شعر العرب كقول لبيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r6.claim: In Qur’anic dialogue, replies normally begin with uncoordinated “he said”; a conjunction appears when the narrative shifts to another conversation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r6.anchor: إذا حكى المحاورات والمجاوبات حكاها بلفظ قال دون حروف عطف ، إلا إذا انتقل من محاورة إلى أخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r7.claim: A third aspect of the Qur’an’s miracle is its wisdom-rich meanings and scientific indications, subjects largely absent from eloquent Arab speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r7.anchor: وأما الجهة الثالثة من جهات الإعجاز وهي ما أودعه من المعاني الحكمية والإشارات العلمية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r8.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r8.claim: ʿUmar says poetry was the people’s knowledge and the soundest knowledge they had.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r8.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب كان الشعر علم القوم ولم يكن لهم علم أصح منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r9.claim: He distinguishes conventional knowledge, defined by society and era, from true knowledge that perfects people and reveals beneficial realities; both can confer mastery and partly overlap.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r9.anchor: إن العلم نوعان علم اصطلاحي وعلم حقيقي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r10.claim: Arab poetry focused on observed or imagined scenes rather than truths and virtues central to the Qur’an; al-Razi notes the Qur’an speaks only truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p125/r10.anchor: لأن أغراض شعرهم كانت لا تعدو وصف المشاهدات والمتخيلات والافتراضات المختلفة ولا تحوم حول تقرير الحقائق وفضائل الأخلاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r1.speaker: أبو روق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r1.claim: Abu Rawq, as reported by al-Tabari, takes jaʿil to mean “creator”; its taking one object supports the sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r1.anchor: وجاعل في هذه الآية بمعنى خالق، ذكره الطبري عن أبي روق، ويقضي بذلك تعديها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada take jaʿil in its sense of “doing” or “making.”

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r3.claim: A report from the Prophet says “the earth” here means Mecca, from beneath which earth was spread; it was where prophets’ peoples were destroyed, and Noah’s, Hud’s, and Salih’s graves lie between the Station and the Corner.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن سابط عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «إن الأرض هنا يعني بها مكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r4.claim: Khalīfa means one who succeeds another.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r4.anchor: وخليفة معناه من يخلف. قال ابن عباس:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says jinn preceded Adam, corrupted the earth and shed blood; God sent angels who killed them and drove survivors to sea islands and mountain tops, then made Adam and his descendants successors.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: «كانت الجن قبل بني آدم في الأرض فأفسدوا وسفكوا الدماء فبعث الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says Adam’s children are called successors because each generation follows the preceding one; Ibn Atiyya says this can mean a succeeding or succeeded generation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r6.anchor: وقال الحسن: «إنما سمى الله بني آدم خليفة لأن كل قرن منهم يخلف الذي قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masud says Adam is God’s deputy for judging servants by truth and His commands, a role continued by his descendants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: «إنما معناه خليفة مني في الحكم بين عبادي بالحق وبأوامري»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r8.speaker: زيد بن علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r8.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads khalīqa with qāf.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r9.claim: Angels do not know the unseen or speak ahead of God; the statement that they do not precede Him in speech praises all angels and indicates this is universal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r9.anchor: وقد علمنا قطعا أن الملائكة لا تعلم الغيب ولا تسبق بالقول، وذلك عام في جميع الملائكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r10.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r10.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib infers that angels must have had prior information or an indication about the successor’s corruption.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r10.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر بن الطيب: «فهذه قرينة العموم، فلا يصح مع هذين الشرطين إلا أن يكون عندهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd and others say God had told the angels that the successor’s descendants would corrupt and shed blood, prompting their question.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن زيد وغيره: إن الله تعالى أعلمهم أن الخليفة سيكون من ذريته قوم يفسدون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r12.claim: Their question may express wonder at God appointing a disobedient creature, at the appointee disobeying despite divine favor, or at both appointment and disobedience.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r12.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: فهذا إما على طريق التعجب من استخلاف الله من يعصيه، أو من عصيان من يستخلفه الله في أرضه وينعم عليه بذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r13.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r13.claim: Thaʿlab and others say angels had witnessed the jinn’s corruption and bloodshed, so they asked whether the new successor would follow the jinn’s way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p116#2/r13.anchor: وقال أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب وغيره: إنما كانت الملائكة قد رأت وعلمت ما كان من إفساد الجن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r1.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r1.claim: Others say God told the angels before this announcement that creatures would corrupt and shed blood; they then asked whether this successor was the one foretold or someone else.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r1.anchor: وقال آخرون: كان الله تعالى قد أعلم الملائكة أنه يخلق في الأرض خلقا يفسدون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r2.claim: Safk ordinarily means spilling blood, but can also describe speaking at length.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r2.anchor: والسفك صب الدم، هذا عرفه، وقد يقال سفك كلامه في كذا إذا سرده.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r3.speaker: جمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r3.claim: The majority read yasfiku with kasra on the fāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r3.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور بكسر الفاء. وقرأ أبو حيوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r4.claim: Abu Haywa and Ibn Abi Abla read yasfuku with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r5.speaker: ابن هرمز
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r5.claim: Ibn Hurmuz reads yasfaka in the accusative with wa al-sarf, coordinating one who combines to corrupt and shed blood; al-Mahdawi parses it as an answer to the question, while Ibn Atiyya prefers the first analysis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن هرمز «ويسفك» بالنصب بواو الصرف كأنه قال: من يجمع أن يفسد وأن يسفك.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r6.speaker: المهدوي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r6.claim: Al-Mahdawi parses the accusative as an answer to the question; Ibn Atiyya prefers the wa al-sarf analysis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r6.anchor: وقال المهدوي: هو نصب في جواب الاستفهام. قال القاضي أبو محمد: والأول أحسن.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r7.speaker: بعض المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r7.claim: Some read “while we glorify You” as a question about whether angels should continue in that state or change from it; Ibn Atiyya says this suits a strictly interrogative reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r7.anchor: قال بعض المتأولين: هو على جهة الاستفهام، كأنهم أرادوا ونحن نسبح بحمدك الآية، أم نتغير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r8.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r8.claim: Others take the words as self-praise and a description of their state, as in Joseph’s “I am a careful keeper, knowledgeable”; Ibn Atiyya says this suits their astonishment at God appointing a disobedient successor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: معناه التمدح ووصف حالهم، وذلك جائز لهم كما قال يوسف عليه السلام: إني حفيظ عليم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r9.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r9.claim: Some understand the angels to mean that if God had appointed them to succession on earth, they would glorify Him; this suits the astonishment reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: معنى الآية ونحن لو جعلتنا في الأرض واستخلفتنا نسبح بحمدك.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r10.claim: Glorifying God with praise means declaring Him free of what is unfitting to His essence and attributes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r10.anchor: ومعنى نسبح بحمدك ننزهك عما لا يليق بك وبصفاتك.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud say the angels’ glorification is their prayer to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن مسعود: «تسبيح الملائكة صلاتهم لله»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r12.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r12.claim: Qatada takes tasbih in its ordinary linguistic sense: saying “subhan Allah.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r12.anchor: وقال قتادة: «تسبيح الملائكة قولهم سبحان الله على عرفه في اللغة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r13.claim: Bi-hamdika can mean joining praise to glorification; alternatively, it is an interjection: “we glorify and sanctify,” then a submission that God is praised for guiding them to this.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r13.anchor: وبحمدك معناه: نخلط التسبيح بالحمد ونصله به، ويحتمل أن يكون قوله بحمدك اعتراضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r14.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r14.claim: Al-Dahhak and others explain “we sanctify for You” as purifying themselves to seek God’s approval; sanctification means purification.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r14.anchor: ونقدس لك قال الضحاك وغيره: معناه نطهر أنفسنا لك ابتغاء مرضاتك، والتقديس التطهير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r15.claim: The root means purification, as in “the holy land,” Bayt al-Maqdis, and al-Quds, the thing used to purify.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p117/r15.anchor: والتقديس التطهير بلا خلاف، ومنه الأرض المقدسة أي المطهرة، ومنه بيت المقدس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda, followed by Ibn Qutayba, treats idh as redundant, yielding ‘and your Lord said.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r1.anchor: كان أبوا عبيدة يقول إذ ملغاة وتقدير الكلام وقال ربك وتابعه ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج وابن القاسم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj and Ibn al-Qāsim reject the claim that idh is redundant; al-Zajjāj takes it to mean ‘at the time’ of the beginning of creation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r2.anchor: وعاب ذلك عليهما الزجاج وابن القاسم وقال الزجاج إذ معناها الوقت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r3.claim: Malāʾika derives from al-ūlūk, meaning a message; Labīd’s line about a mother sending a message is evidence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r3.anchor: والملائكة من الألوك وهي الرسالة قال لبيد وغلام أرسلته أمه بألوك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r4.claim: The singular of malāʾika is malak, originally malʾak, as Sibawayh’s verse demonstrates.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r4.anchor: وواحد الملائكة ملك والاصل فيه ملأك وأنشد سيبويه فلست لإنسي ولكن لملأك تنزل من جو السماء يصوب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r5.claim: Abū Isḥāq glosses malʾak as ‘bearer of a message’; related forms include maʾlaka and malʾaka, with maʾālik as a plural, illustrated by a poem to al-Nuʿmān.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق ومعنى ملأك صاحب رسالة يقال مألكة ومألكة وملأكة ومآلك جمع مألكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r6.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r6.claim: One view takes the angels addressed as all the angels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r6.anchor: وفي هؤلاء الملائكة قولان أحدهما أنهمن جميع الملائكة قاله السدي عن أشياخه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r7.claim: The other view identifies them as the angels with Iblīs when he was sent down to earth; Abū Ṣāliḥ transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r7.anchor: والثاني أنهم الذين كانوا مع إبليس حين أهبط إلى الأرض ذكره أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r8.claim: It is related that creatures lived on earth before Adam, caused corruption, and were destroyed by Iblīs and a company of angels sent by God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r8.anchor: ونقل أنه كان في الأرض قبل آدم خلق فأفسدوا فبعث الله إبليس في جماعة من الملائكة فأهلكوهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي عن أشياخه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r9.claim: God knew Iblīs harbored pride and disobedience and wished to reveal it to the angels; this is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and by al-Suddī from his elders.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r9.anchor: علم في نفس إبليس كبرا فأحب أن يطلع الملائكة عليه وأن يظهر ما سبق عليه في علمه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says God announced Adam’s creation to test the angels’ obedience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r10.anchor: أنه أراد أن يبلو طاعة الملائكة قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd says the angels feared after God created fire and told them it was for those who disobeyed; they feared they might disobey, so God announced the earthly khalīfa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r11.anchor: قال لمن عصاني فخافوا وجود المعصية منهم وهم لا يعلمون بوجود خلق سواهم فقال لهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r12.claim: God informed the angels to show that their knowledge could not encompass His wisdom, which they acknowledged in their question.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r12.anchor: أراد إظهار عجزهم عن الإحاطة بعلمه فأخبرهم حتى قالوا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r13.claim: God mentioned Adam’s future vicegerency before his creation to honor him and ensure the angels would revere him if He brought him into being.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r13.anchor: أراد تعظيم آدم بذكره بالخلافة قبل وجوده ليكونوا معظمين له إن أوجده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r14.claim: God meant to tell the angels that Adam would inhabit earth, even though his initial creation took place in heaven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58#2/r14.anchor: أراد إعلامهم بانه خلقه ليسكنه الأرض وإن كانت ابتداء خلقه في السماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r1.claim: Khalīfa means one who succeeds another; Ibn al-Anbārī says its original form was khalīf, with the feminine ending added to intensify praise, like ʿallāma and nasāba.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r1.anchor: والخليفة هو القائم مقام غيره يقال هذا خلف فلان وخليفته قال ابن الانباري والاصل في الخيلفة خليف بغير هاء فدخلت الهاء للمبالغة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r2.claim: One view says Adam is God’s deputy for establishing His law, signs of His oneness, and judgment among His creation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r2.anchor: وهذا قول ابن مسعود و مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r3.claim: The other view says Adam succeeded earlier inhabitants of the earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r3.anchor: والثاني انه خلف من سلف في الأرض قبله وهذا قول ابن عباس والحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r4.claim: One analysis takes the interrogative alif as emphatic confirmation, not a genuine question; Jarīr’s line uses a question to assert that the addressees are best.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r4.anchor: ظاهر الالف الاستفهام دخل على معنى العلم ليقع به تحقيق قال جرير ألستم خير من ركب المطايا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the angels asked to learn the wisdom behind the decision, not as an objection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r5.anchor: لا على وجه الاعتراض ذكره الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r6.claim: A third reading makes the angels ask about their own standing: will God place a corrupting creature there while they glorify Him, or not?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r6.anchor: أنهم سألوا عن حال أنفسهم فتقديره أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ونحن نسبح بحمدك أم لا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد وابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r7.claim: These authorities hold that God had informed the angels the khalīfa’s descendants would corrupt; al-Suddī reports they were told the descendants would envy and kill one another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r7.anchor: أنه بتوقيف من الله تعالى قاله ابن مسعود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وأبي العالية ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r8.claim: The alternative view is that the angels inferred the corruption from the condition of those who had lived before Adam.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p60/r8.anchor: على أحوال من سلف قبل آدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r1.claim: The majority read yasfiku with kasra on the fāʾ; Ibn Miṣraf and Ibrāhīm ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with ḍamma, both being Arabic forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r1.anchor: قرأ الجمهور بكسر الفاء وضمها ابن مصرف وابراهيم بن أبي عبلة وهما لغتان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r2.speaker: طلحة وابن مقسم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r2.claim: Ṭalḥa and Ibn Miqsam read yusaffik with a doubled fāʾ, conveying repeated or intensified action.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r2.anchor: وروي عن طلحة وابن مقسم ويسفك بضم الياء وفتح السين وتشديد الفاء مع كسرها وهي لتكثير الفعل وتكريره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r3.claim: Safk means to pour or spill blood; it is specific to blood, whereas ṣabb, safḥ, and irāqa can describe blood or other things.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r3.anchor: وسفك الدم صبه وإراقته وسفحه وذلك مستعمل في كل مضيع إلا أن السفك يختص الدم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r4.claim: One interpretation takes the angels’ tasbīḥ to mean prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r4.anchor: أحدها أنه الصلاة قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r5.speaker: مقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r5.claim: Muqātil interprets their tasbīḥ as saying ‘subḥāna Allāh.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r5.anchor: والثاني انه قوله سبحان الله قاله مقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r6.speaker: أبو صالح
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r6.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ interprets it as magnification and praise.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r6.anchor: والثالث أنه التعظيم والحمد قاله أبو صالح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r7.speaker: محمد بن القاسم الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Qāsim al-Anbārī interprets it as submission and humility.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r7.anchor: والرابع انه الخضوع والذل قاله محمد بن القاسم الانباري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r8.anchor: القدس الطهارة وفي معنى تقديسهم ثلاثة أقوال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they purify themselves for God from the deeds of the corrupt beings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r9.anchor: أحدها أن معناه نتطهر لك من أعمالهم قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r10.claim: Mujāhid interprets it as honoring and magnifying God.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61/r11.claim: Qatāda interprets it as praying to God.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي عن أشياخه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r1.claim: One interpretation is that God knows the pride and disobedience within Iblīs; this is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī from his elders.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r1.anchor: من البغى والمعصية قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says God knows that prophets and righteous people will emerge from Adam’s descendants.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r2.anchor: أعلم أنه سيكون من ذلك الخليفة أنبياء وصالحون قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the words to mean that God knows He will fill Hell with jinn and humans.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r3.anchor: أعلم أني أملأ جهنم من الجنة والناس قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God knows how events end: testing may lead someone thought obedient, like Iblīs, to sin, while someone thought sinful may obey.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r4.anchor: أعلم عواقب الامور فانا أبتلي من تظنون أنه مطيع فيؤديه الابتلاء إلى المعصية كابليس ومن تظنون به المعصية فيطيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r5.claim: The Prophet said Adam was created from a handful taken from all the earth, so descendants vary in color, temperament, and goodness; al-Tirmidhī graded this report ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r5.anchor: روى أبو موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال إن الله عز وجل خلق آدم من قبضة قبضها من جميع الأرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r6.claim: The Prophet said Adam was sixty cubits tall; the report is in the Ṣaḥīḥs of al-Bukhārī and Muslim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r6.anchor: من حديث أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال خلق الله تعالى آدم طوله ستون ذراعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r7.claim: The Prophet said Adam was created after the afternoon prayer on Friday, in its final hour before night; Muslim alone reports this.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r7.anchor: خلق الله آدم بعد العصر يوم الجمعة آخر الخلق في آخر ساعة من ساعات الجمعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the breath entered Adam through his head, and each part it reached became flesh and blood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p61#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس لما نفخ فيه الروح أتته النفخة من قبل رأسه فجعلت لا تجري منه في شئ إلا صار لحما ودما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r1.claim: God honors Adam's descendants by mentioning them to the highest assembly before creating them; the verse tells Muhammad to recall this and recount it to his people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r1.anchor: يخبر (1) تعالى بامتنانه على بني آدم، بتنويهه بذكرهم في الملأ الأعلى قبل إيجادهم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r2.claim: Abu ʿUbayda claimed idh is extra, making the sense simply “And your Lord said”; Ibn Jarir rejects this, as do all exegetes, and al-Zajjaj calls it rash.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r2.anchor: زعم أن "إذ" هاهنا زائدة، وأن تقدير الكلام: وقال ربك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r3.claim: Khalifa here means people succeeding one another generation after generation, as in the linked verses about successors on earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r3.anchor: أي: قوما يخلف بعضهم بعضا قرنا بعد قرن وجيلا بعد جيل،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r4.speaker: زيد بن علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r4.claim: A noncanonical reading attributed to Zayd ibn ʿAli reads khalifa as khalīqa; al-Zamakhshari and others transmit it, and al-Qurtubi also records it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r4.anchor: [وقرئ في الشاذ: "إني جاعل في الأرض خليقة" حكاه الزمخشري وغيره ونقلها القرطبي عن زيد بن علي]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وجميع أهل التأويل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r5.claim: Some exegetes, whom al-Qurtubi attributes to Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and all interpreters, take the khalifa to mean Adam alone.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r5.anchor: وليس المراد هاهنا بالخليفة آدم، عليه السلام، فقط، كما يقوله طائفة من المفسرين، وعزاه القرطبي إلى ابن مسعود وابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir says the khalifa is apparently not Adam alone: the angels' prediction of corruption and bloodshed concerns a human kind, and he presents possible grounds for their knowledge, including special information, human nature, or analogy with prior inhabitants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r6.anchor: وليس المراد هاهنا بالخليفة آدم، عليه السلام، فقط، كما يقوله طائفة من المفسرين،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r7.speaker: القرطبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi suggests the angels may have understood khalifa as one who judges among people and restrains wrongs and violations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r7.anchor: [أو فهموا من الخليفة أنه الذي يفصل بين الناس ويقع بينهم من المظالم ويرد عنهم المحارم والمآثم، قاله القرطبي]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r8.claim: The angels' question was neither objection nor envy; it sought the wisdom of creating people who may corrupt and kill, when the angels worship without doing so, and why creation was not limited to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r8.anchor: وقول الملائكة هذا ليس على وجه الاعتراض على الله، ولا على وجه الحسد لبني آدم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r9.claim: Qatada says God had already told the angels that the earth-dwellers would corrupt it, prompting their question.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r9.anchor: قال قتادة: وقد تقدم إليهم أنهم يفسدون فيها فقالوا: {أتجعل فيها} الآية]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r10.claim: God answers that He knows the greater good outweighing the harms: humanity will include prophets, messengers, truthful ones, martyrs, righteous people, worshippers, scholars, the humble, and those who love and follow Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p216/r10.anchor: أي: إني أعلم من المصلحة (8) الراجحة في خلق هذا الصنف على المفاسد التي ذكرتموها (9) ما لا تعلمون أنتم؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r1.claim: A sound report says angels alternate in attending people and meet at dawn and afternoon prayers; God asks how they left His servants, and they answer that they were praying both times.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r1.anchor: وقد ثبت في الصحيح (1) : أن الملائكة إذا صعدت إلى الرب تعالى بأعمال عباده سألهم وهو أعلم: كيف تركتم عبادي؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r2.claim: The Prophet says the deeds of night are raised to God before day, and the deeds of day before night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r2.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام: "يرفع إليه عمل الليل قبل النهار، وعمل النهار قبل الليل"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r3.claim: The angels' report that people pray at dawn and afternoon is one explanation of God's statement that He knows what they do not.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r3.anchor: فقولهم: أتيناهم وهم يصلون وتركناهم وهم يصلون من تفسير قوله: {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r4.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r4.claim: One explanation is that God has a detailed wisdom for creating this kind despite the harms the angels mentioned, which they do not know.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r4.anchor: وقيل: معنى قوله جوابا لهم: {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} أن لي حكمة مفصلة في خلق هؤلاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r5.claim: Another explanation takes God's reply as pointing to Iblis's presence among the angels, despite their description of themselves as glorifying and sanctifying God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r5.anchor: وقيل: إنه جواب لقولهم: {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} فقال: {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} أي: من وجود إبليس بينكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r6.claim: A further explanation says the angels were asking to live on earth instead of Adam's descendants; God replied that heaven was more suitable for them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r6.anchor: وقيل: بل تضمن قولهم: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r7.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada, in Ibn Jarir's report, explain God's statement as informing the angels that He was going to create a khalifa.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r7.anchor: قال ابن جرير: حدثني القاسم بن الحسن قال: حدثنا الحسين قال: حدثني الحجاج، عن جرير بن حازم، ومبارك، عن الحسن وأبي بكر، عن الحسن وقتادة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says God consulted the angels about creating Adam; Ibn Kathir says this wording is loose unless it means that God informed them, and prefers al-Hasan and Qatada's wording.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: استشار الملائكة في خلق آدم. رواه ابن أبي حاتم، قال (2) : وروي عن قتادة نحوه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says earth was spread from Mecca, angels first circled the House, and “earth” in the khalifa announcement meant Mecca.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r1.anchor: حدثنا حماد (3) حدثنا عطاء بن السائب، عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط أن رسول الله (4) صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "دحيت الأرض من مكة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir grades that report mursal with a weak chain and an inserted interpretation that “earth” means Mecca; he says the apparent sense is the wider earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r2.anchor: وهذا مرسل، وفي سنده ضعف، وفيه مدرج، وهو أن المراد بالأرض مكة، والله أعلم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi's report says the angels asked what the khalifa would be, and God answered that he would have descendants who corrupt, envy one another, and kill one another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r3.anchor: قال السدي في تفسيره عن أبي مالك وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس -وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir interprets the khalifa as God's deputy in judging among creation: Adam and those who obey God and rule justly; unjust corruption and bloodshed come from others.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن جرير: فكان تأويل الآية على هذا: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} مني، يخلفني في الحكم بين خلقي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir also derives khalifa from one person succeeding another, and says succession here means one generation following another, as in Yunus 14.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن جرير: وإنما [كان تأويل الآية على هذا] (4) معنى الخلافة التي ذكرها الله إنما هي خلافة قرن منهم قرنا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir says a ruler is called khalifa because he succeeds his predecessor and takes charge in his place.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك قيل للسلطان الأعظم: خليفة؛ لأنه خلف الذي كان قبله، فقام بالأمر مقامه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.claim: Ibn Ishaq understands the khalifa as an inhabitant and cultivator who will live on and populate earth, a successor unlike the angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r7.anchor: وكان محمد بن إسحاق يقول في قوله تعالى: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} يقول: ساكنا وعامرا يسكنها ويعمرها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, says jinn first inhabited earth and shed blood; God sent Iblis to defeat and drive them to remote places, then created Adam to succeed them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p217#2/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال: أول من سكن الأرض الجن، فأفسدوا فيها وسفكوا فيها الدماء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r1.speaker: ابن سابط
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r1.claim: The angels’ words about corruption and bloodshed refer to Adam’s descendants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب، عن ابن سابط: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r2.claim: God announced that He would create beings and appoint a successor on an otherwise empty earth where only angels existed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: قال الله للملائكة: إني أريد أن أخلق في الأرض خلقا وأجعل فيها خليفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r3.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وغيرهما من الصحابة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r3.claim: God had informed the angels what Adam’s descendants would do, so they made this statement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r3.anchor: ما رواه السدي، عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وغيرهما من الصحابة: أن الله أعلم الملائكة بما يفعل ذرية آدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r4.claim: Jinn had corrupted the earth before Adam’s descendants, and the angels compared the new beings with them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r4.anchor: ما رواه الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: أن الجن أفسدوا في الأرض قبل بني آدم، فقالت الملائكة ذلك، فقاسوا هؤلاء بأولئك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r5.claim: A report says jinn lived on earth two thousand years before Adam, shed blood and caused corruption; angels drove them to sea islands, after which God announced Adam’s succession.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، قال: كان الجن بنو الجان في الأرض قبل أن يخلق آدم بألفي سنة، فأفسدوا في الأرض، وسفكوا الدماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r6.claim: God created angels on Wednesday, jinn on Thursday and Adam on Friday; some jinn disbelieved, and angels fought them amid corruption and bloodshed, explaining their question.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} إلى قوله: {وأعلم ما تبدون وما كنتم تكتمون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r7.claim: God taught the angels some knowledge and withheld other knowledge; they asked from what they had been taught.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p218/r7.anchor: حدثنا الحسن، قال: قال الله للملائكة: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} قال لهم: إني فاعل. فآمنوا بربهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r1.claim: The jinn had corrupted the earth and shed blood; God placed knowledge of what would happen in the angels’ hearts, prompting their question.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r1.anchor: قال الحسن: إن الجن كانوا في الأرض يفسدون (4) ويسفكون الدماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r2.claim: God told the angels that any creatures placed on earth would cause corruption and shed blood, so they asked this question.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها} كان [الله] (5) أعلمهم أنه إذا كان في الأرض خلق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر محمد بن علي الباقر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r3.claim: A report says the angel al-Sijill saw Adam’s creation and future in the Preserved Book and told Harut and Marut, who spoke out of superiority over the angels.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r3.anchor: عمن سمع أبا جعفر محمد بن علي يقول: السجل ملك، وكان هاروت وماروت من أعوانه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects the al-Baqir report as an objectionable Israelite account; its claim that only two angels spoke also conflicts with the verse’s plural wording.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r4.anchor: وفيه نكارة توجب رده، والله أعلم. ومقتضاه أن الذين قالوا ذلك إنما كانوا اثنين فقط، وهو خلاف السياق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r5.speaker: يحيى بن أبي كثير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r5.claim: A report says ten thousand angels asked the question and a fire from God burned them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r5.anchor: سمعت أبي يقول: إن الملائكة الذين قالوا: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} كانوا عشرة آلاف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the ten-thousand-angels account an objectionable Israelite report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r6.anchor: وهذا -أيضا-إسرائيلي منكر كالذي قبله، والله أعلم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r7.claim: The angels spoke because God had informed them that this would occur among Adam’s creation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r7.anchor: قال ابن جريج: إنما تكلموا بما أعلمهم الله أنه كائن من خلق آدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r8.claim: One explanation is that God permitted the angels to ask after telling them humans would corrupt the earth; their question expressed amazement at how created beings could disobey their Creator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p219/r8.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: وقال بعضهم: إنما قالت الملائكة ما قالت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r1.claim: The angels’ question sought guidance about what they did not know, not denial or objection; Ibn Jarir prefers this explanation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r1.anchor: ذلك من الملائكة على وجه الاسترشاد عما لم يعلموا من ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r2.claim: God’s knowledge included that Adam’s descendants would produce prophets, messengers, righteous people and inhabitants of Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r2.anchor: قال سعيد عن قتادة قوله: {وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r3.claim: A report says the angels thought no creation was more honored or knowledgeable than themselves, then were tested through Adam’s creation, as the heavens and earth were tested by God’s command.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقول: إن الله لما أخذ في خلق آدم قالت الملائكة: ما الله خالق خلقا أكرم عليه منا ولا أعلم منا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r1.claim: Qatada glosses tasbih as tasbih itself and taqdis as prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r1.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق، عن معمر، عن قتادة: التسبيح: التسبيح، والتقديس: الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r2.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وغيرهما من الصحابة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r2.claim: They explain the angels’ words as saying that they pray to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس -وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود-وعن ناس من الصحابة: {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} قال: يقولون: نصلي لك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says the angels mean that they exalt and magnify God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} قال: نعظمك ونكبرك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq interprets the words as a commitment not to disobey God or do anything He dislikes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r5.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسحاق: {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} قال: لا نعصي ولا نأتي شيئا تكرهه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir defines taqdis as glorification and purification: subbuh denotes declaring God free of defect and quddus denotes His purity and exaltedness; the angels disavow what polytheists attribute to Him and affirm His purity from impure qualities.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: التقديس: هو التعظيم والتطهير، ومنه قولهم: سبوح قدوس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أبي ذر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r7.claim: In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet answers that the best speech is what God chose for His angels: Subhan Allah wa bihamdihi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r7.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن أبي ذر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم سئل: أي الكلام أفضل؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r8.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن قرط عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r8.claim: Al-Bayhaqi reports that during the Night Journey the Prophet heard glorification in the highest heavens: Subhan al-Ali al-Ala, subhanahu wa taala.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p220#2/r8.anchor: وروى البيهقي عن عبد الرحمن بن قرط أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة أسري به سمع تسبيحا في السماوات العلا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r1.claim: Qatada says God knew that Adam’s descendants would include prophets, messengers, righteous people and inhabitants of Paradise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: فكان في علم الله أنه سيكون في تلك الخليقة أنبياء ورسل وقوم صالحون وساكنو الجنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r2.speaker: القرطبي وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi and others infer that appointing an imam is obligatory to settle disputes, defend the oppressed, enforce penalties and deter indecencies, since necessary duties require an imam.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r2.anchor: وقد استدل القرطبي وغيره بهذه الآية على وجوب نصب الخليفة ليفصل بين الناس فيما يختلفون فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r3.speaker: طائفة من أهل السنة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r3.claim: One Sunni group holds that the imamate is established by explicit designation, as they say it was for Abu Bakr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r3.anchor: والإمامة تنال بالنص كما يقوله طائفة من أهل السنة في أبي بكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r4.speaker: آخرون من أهل السنة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r4.claim: Another Sunni group holds that the imamate may be established by an indication or allusion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r4.anchor: أو بالإيماء إليه كما يقول آخرون منهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r5.claim: The imamate may be established when a caliph appoints a successor, as Abu Bakr did with Umar ibn al-Khattab.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r5.anchor: أو باستخلاف الخليفة آخر بعده كما فعل الصديق بعمر بن الخطاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r6.claim: A caliph may leave the choice to a council of righteous people, as Umar did.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r6.anchor: أو بتركه شورى في جماعة صالحين كذلك كما فعله عمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r7.claim: The imamate may be established by the people qualified to bind and loose, or by one of them pledging allegiance; the majority requires adherence, and al-Juwayni reports consensus on this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r7.anchor: أو باجتماع أهل الحل والعقد على مبايعته أو بمبايعة واحد منهم له فيجب التزامها عند الجمهور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r8.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r8.claim: An imam who gains power by compelling people to obey must be recognized to prevent division and disagreement; al-Shafi‘i explicitly states this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r8.anchor: أو بقهر واحد الناس على طاعته فتجب لئلا يؤدي ذلك إلى الشقاق والاختلاف، وقد نص عليه الشافعي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r9.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r9.claim: One view says witnesses are not a condition for the imamate contract.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r9.anchor: فمنهم من قال: لا يشترط، وقيل: بلى ويكفي شاهدان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r10.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r10.claim: Another view requires testimony for the imamate contract, with two witnesses sufficient.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r10.anchor: وقيل: بلى ويكفي شاهدان. وقال الجبائي: يجب أربعة وعاقد ومعقود له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r11.speaker: الجبائي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r11.claim: Al-Jubba’i requires four witnesses, a contracting party and the person contracted for; he derives the four witnesses from the remaining members of Umar’s six-person council, while Ibn Kathir finds this reasoning questionable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r11.anchor: وقال الجبائي: يجب أربعة وعاقد ومعقود له، كما ترك عمر رضي الله عنه، الأمر شورى بين ستة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r12.claim: The imam should be male, free, adult, sane, Muslim, just, learned in independent reasoning, perceptive, physically sound, experienced in war and judgment, and Qurayshi according to the correct view; Hashimi descent and infallibility are not required, contrary to extremist Rafidites.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r12.anchor: ويجب أن يكون ذكرا حرا بالغا عاقلا مسلما عدلا مجتهدا بصيرا سليم الأعضاء خبيرا بالحروب والآراء قرشيا على الصحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r13.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r13.claim: A sinful imam is not deposed according to the sounder view, based on the Prophet’s instruction to tolerate him unless manifest unbelief is seen with proof from God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r13.anchor: والصحيح أنه لا ينعزل لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r14.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r14.claim: Whether an imam may resign is disputed; Hasan ibn Ali relinquished authority to Muawiyah for an excuse, and Ibn Kathir says he was praised for it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p221/r14.anchor: وقد عزل الحسن بن علي نفسه وسلم الأمر إلى معاوية لكن هذا لعذر وقد مدح على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r1.claim: The majority forbids appointing two or more imams in one realm, citing a prophetic command to kill anyone who tries to divide a united community; several authorities report consensus.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r1.anchor: فأما نصب إمامين في الأرض أو أكثر فلا يجوز

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r2.speaker: الكرامية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r2.claim: The Karramiyya allow two or more imams, treating Ali and Muawiyah as simultaneously obligatory-to-obey imams and reasoning by analogy from the permissibility of multiple prophets, whose rank is higher.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r2.anchor: وقالت الكرامية: يجوز نصب إمامين فأكثر كما كان علي ومعاوية إمامين واجبي الطاعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق الأستاذ كما حكاه إمام الحرمين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq permits multiple imams when territories are far apart and regions extensive; al-Juwayni hesitates, and Ibn Kathir compares this to Abbasid, Fatimid and Umayyad rival caliphates in Iraq, Egypt and the Maghreb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p222/r3.anchor: وحكى إمام الحرمين عن الأستاذ أبي إسحاق أنه جوز نصب إمامين فأكثر إذا تباعدت الأقطار واتسعت الأقاليم بينهما

JISHUMI:v1p308/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r4.speaker: العامة
JISHUMI:v1p308/r4.claim: The general reading is khalīfa with fāʾ.

JISHUMI:v1p308/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r5.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v1p308/r5.claim: Some are reported to read khalīqa with qāf, meaning a created being; although meaningful, the author rejects it for lacking widely transmitted reading.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r5.anchor: وعن بعضهم: (خليقة) بالقاف يعني خلقا، وهذا وإن كان له معنى صحيح

JISHUMI:v1p308/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p308/r6.claim: Malak derives from the language of sending a message: alīkni means send me, and maʾlaka or alūk means message; the original hamza was dropped for ease.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r6.anchor: الملك: أصله من الرسالة، يقال: ألكني إليه، أي أرسلني، والمألكة الرسالة

JISHUMI:v1p308/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p308/r7.claim: Malak has the pattern mafʿal after deletion of its hamza and became the established name for a class of God’s nonhuman messengers.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r7.anchor: فصار ملك، وهو الرسول، ووزنه مفعل؛ لأن أصله ملأك حذفت الهمزة

JISHUMI:v1p308/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r8.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v1p308/r8.claim: A poet preserves the original hamza in malāʾak; the author says this form is otherwise used only under poetic necessity.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر: فلست لإنسي ولكن لملأك

JISHUMI:v1p308/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p308/r9.claim: Jaʿl changes something from its prior state without bringing it into existence, unlike fiʿl and iḥdāth.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r9.anchor: إلا أن الجعل يتعلق بالشيء لا على سبيل الإيجاد، بخلاف الفعل، والإحداث

JISHUMI:v1p308/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p308/r10.claim: Khalīfa and imām overlap in use, but khalīfa succeeds another while imām leads a group and is to be obeyed.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r10.anchor: والخليفة والإمام واحد في الاستعمال، وبينهما فرق، والخليفة مأخوذ

JISHUMI:v1p308/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p308/r11.claim: Khalaf with fatḥa on the lām denotes righteous successors, while sukūn denotes bad successors, as illustrated in 7:169.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r11.anchor: والخلف بنصب اللام من الصالحين، وبسكون اللام من الطالحين؛ قال تعالى: (فخلف من بعدهم خلف)

JISHUMI:v1p311/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r1.claim: Idh normally refers to the past and idhā to the future, though either can stand in place of the other.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r1.anchor: ويقال: (إذ) لما مضى، و(إذا) لما يستقبل، فيوضع أحدهما موضع الآخر

JISHUMI:v1p311/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r2.speaker: المبرد
JISHUMI:v1p311/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad says idh with a future verb takes past-time meaning, while idhā with a past verb takes future-time meaning; he cites 8:30, 79:34, and 110:1.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r2.anchor: وقال المبرد: إذا جاء (إذ) مع المستقبل كان معناه على الماضي كقوله تعالى: (وإذ يمكر)

JISHUMI:v1p311/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r3.claim: The governing verb for idh is omitted, with the primary estimate wa-udhkur idh, remember when.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r3.anchor: قلنا: محذوف، تقديره: واذكر إذ قال

JISHUMI:v1p311/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r4.claim: Another estimate ties this to the beginning of creation: God began creating people when He said this.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r4.anchor: وقيل: لما ذكر خلق السماوات دل على ابتداء الخلق، فكأنه قال: وابتدأ خلقكم إذ قال

JISHUMI:v1p311/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r5.claim: A further estimate is that God knew their states when He spoke to the angels.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r5.anchor: وقيل: وهو عليم بأحوالكم إذ قال

JISHUMI:v1p311/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r6.claim: The earlier how-can-you-disbelieve clause itself implies an omitted remember, supporting the estimate remember when God spoke.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r6.anchor: وفي الوجه الأول في الكلام دليل على المحذوف؛ لأن قوله: (كيف تكفرون)

JISHUMI:v1p311/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r7.speaker: الشاعر
JISHUMI:v1p311/r7.claim: An unnamed poet’s line supports ellipsis: after a conditional أينما, the understood verb ذهب is omitted.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r7.anchor: قال الشا عر: فإن المنية من يخشها

JISHUMI:v1p311/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة والزجاج
JISHUMI:v1p311/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Zajjāj parse the hamza as affirmative, citing Jarīr’s ألستم as a parallel.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r8.anchor: ألف إيجاب عن أبي عبيدة والزجاج، كقول جرير: ألستم خير من ركب المطايا

JISHUMI:v1p311/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r9.speaker: غيرهما
JISHUMI:v1p311/r9.claim: Other grammarians take the hamza as interrogative: the angels ask whether they are placed alongside a corrupter despite their glorification.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r9.anchor: وقال غيرهما: هو ألف استفهام كأنهم قالوا: أتجعل فيها من يفسد وهذه حالنا

JISHUMI:v1p311/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r10.claim: The author prefers the interrogative: it asks about the angels’ state relative to the appointment, not whether God will appoint a successor.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r10.anchor: والصواب هو الثاني، وإنما غلط من زعم أنها ألف إيجاب

JISHUMI:v1p311/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r11.claim: The interrogative does not imply doubt that God will appoint a successor; it asks whether the angels’ state and the appointment are equally sound.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r11.anchor: وهذا لا يصح؛ لأن الاستفهام لا يوجب الشك في أنه سيجعل

JISHUMI:v1p311/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r12.claim: One analysis treats the lām as extra and reads the phrase as nuqaddisuka, we sanctify You.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r12.anchor: واللام في قوله: ونقدس لك قيل: صلة، تقديره: نقدسك

JISHUMI:v1p311/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r13.claim: Another analysis treats the lām as expressing purpose: we sanctify for Your sake and pleasure.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r13.anchor: وقيل: لام الإضافة، أي نقدس لأجلك ورضاك

JISHUMI:v1p311/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r14.claim: One account connects the verse to preceding favors: human creation and life, earthly things, heaven, then Adam and blessings to his descendants.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r14.anchor: اتصاله بما قبله أنه عد النعم والحجج، فبدأ بذكر خلق الإنسان وحياته

JISHUMI:v1p311/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p311/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p311/r15.claim: Another account says the passage gathers evidence for divine unity from earth and heaven, then follows with the beginning of creation and Adam.
JISHUMI:v1p311/r15.anchor: وقيل: احتج عليهم بالتوحيد فجمع الأدلة في الأرض والسماوات

JISHUMI:v1p313/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r1.claim: One proposed question is how God could create beings He knows will disbelieve, when all His acts are good and He cannot do wrong.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r1.anchor: الخامس: أشكل عليهم خلق من يعلم أنه يكفر ممن جميع أفعاله حسنة، ولا يجوز عليه القبيح

JISHUMI:v1p313/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r2.claim: Another proposed question is why God would create corrupters and then defer their punishment.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r2.anchor: السادس: أشكل عليهم خلق المفسدين مع الإمهال

JISHUMI:v1p313/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r3.claim: A further proposal is that the angels wondered whether God’s successor could be corrupt and sinful.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r3.anchor: السابع: أشكل عليهم أن خليفة الله هل يجوز أن يكون مفسدا فاسقا أم لا

JISHUMI:v1p313/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r4.claim: Another account says the angels were not puzzled but asked, magnifying God, that He not create anyone who would disobey; another reads the words as astonishment at a creature disobeying its creator.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r4.anchor: أنه لم يشكل عليهم شيء ولكن سؤالهم على وجه للمبالغة في إعظامه تعالى

JISHUMI:v1p313/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r5.claim: The angels asked with God’s permission, which He granted because He knew asking benefited them.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r5.anchor: بل بإذن لهم في السؤال لما علم من مصلحتهم في ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p313/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r6.claim: One interpretation is that the angels declare God transcendent above bodily attributes and purify Him of reprehensible acts.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r6.anchor: قيل: ننزهك عن صفات الأجسام، ونقدسك عن قبائح الأفعال

JISHUMI:v1p313/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r7.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p313/r7.claim: Qatāda interprets the angels’ tasbīḥ as the familiar act of glorification.

JISHUMI:v1p313/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p313/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the angels’ tasbīḥ as prayer.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو الصلاة، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p313/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r9.claim: One account says they glorify God by attributing blessings to Him and praising Him for them.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r9.anchor: ننزهك بإضافة النعم إليك، ونحمدك على ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p313/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r10.claim: Another account says glorification benefits the angels, while their ability to perform it comes from God’s enabling.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r10.anchor: لأن نفع التسبيح عائد إلينا، وهو بتوفيقك

JISHUMI:v1p313/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p313/r11.claim: Abū Muslim takes the angels’ sanctification as purifying themselves from sins for God’s sake and pleasure.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r11.anchor: نطهر أنفسنا عن المعاصي ابتغاء مرضاتك، دليله نقدس لك

JISHUMI:v1p313/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r12.claim: Another account treats the lām as extra and the sanctification as directed to God Himself.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r12.anchor: اللام صلة، والتقديس يرجع إلى الله تعالى، وتقديره: نقدسك

JISHUMI:v1p313/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r13.claim: Some say the angels asked God to make them the earthly inhabitants because earthly duties would be lighter.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r13.anchor: قيل: نعم؛ لأن تكليف أهل الأرض أخف

JISHUMI:v1p313/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r14.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p313/r14.claim: Abū ʿAlī says they asked to be placed on earth because it would benefit them.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r14.anchor: وقيل: سألوا ذلك بأن كان لهم فيه صلاح، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v1p313/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r15.claim: One rejects that they asked to replace people because this implies a divine will without evidence; another rearranges the phrase to mean they glorify by God’s guidance and then praise Him.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r15.anchor: وقيل: لا؛ لأنه حكم بإرادتهم، وذلك لا يصح من غير دليل

JISHUMI:v1p313/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r16.claim: One explanation is that God knows prophets, scholars, and saints will arise among Adam’s descendants and knows their great work in religion and worldly affairs.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r16.anchor: قيل: يعلم أن في ذريته أنبياء وعلماء وأولياء، وقيل: أعلم منهم من عظيم حالهم

JISHUMI:v1p313/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r17.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p313/r17.claim: Abū ʿAlī says God knows the interests involved and which location is best for angels and people.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r17.anchor: وقيل: أعلم من المصالح، وأي موضع أصلح لهم ولكم ما لا تعلمون، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v1p313/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p313/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p313/r18.claim: A proposed meaning is God’s knowledge of Iblīs’s concealed disobedience, but the author rejects it because Iblīs has not yet been mentioned.
JISHUMI:v1p313/r18.anchor: وقيل: أعلم من إضمار إبليس المعصية ما لا تعلمون، وليس بالوجه؛ لأنه لم يجر له ذكر

JISHUMI:v1p315/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315/r1.claim: The author questions how declaring God transcendent can fit the Jabriyya view that all injustice, obscenity, and corruption are created and willed by God.
