JISHUMI:v1p315/r1.anchor: كيف يصح التنزيه. وتدل على أن خلق من يعلم أنه يكفر

JISHUMI:v1p315/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315/r2.claim: Creating people whom God knows will disbelieve can still be wise and right.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن خلق من يعلم أنه يكفر يكون حكمة وصوابا

JISHUMI:v1p315/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315/r3.claim: God’s answer implies He does not do evil; it is meaningful as an appeal to knowledge of governance and interests, leading Him to do what is best.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r3.anchor: ويدل قوله: (أعلم ما لا تعلمون) على أنه لا يفعل القبيح

JISHUMI:v1p315/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315/r4.claim: God’s address to the angels establishes that they are accountable beings.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r4.anchor: وتدل على إثبات المكلف فإنه تعالى خاطبهم

JISHUMI:v1p315/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315/r5.claim: Angels are a distinct kind of living creature, with wings, no eating, drinking, or sexual relations; their subtlety makes them invisible unless God strengthens our vision or gives them density.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r5.anchor: والملك حيوان معروف متميز عن سائر الخلق بالصورة، وبأنهم لا يأكلون ولا يشربون ولا ينكحون

JISHUMI:v1p315/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r6.speaker: أصحابنا
JISHUMI:v1p315/r6.claim: The author’s school holds angels to be accountable and free agents, while another group says they are compelled.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r6.anchor: فقال أصحابنا: هم مكلفون ومختارون، وقال جماعة: مجبورون

JISHUMI:v1p315/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r7.speaker: أصحابنا
JISHUMI:v1p315/r7.claim: The author’s school holds angels sinless, citing 66:6; another view says they are not sinless.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r7.anchor: فقال أصحابنا: هم معصومون لقول الله تعالى: (لا يعصون الله ما أمرهم

JISHUMI:v1p315/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r8.speaker: جماعة
JISHUMI:v1p315/r8.claim: One group says believers are superior to angels; another says angels surpass believers but prophets surpass angels.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r8.anchor: فقيل: المؤمنون أفضل منهم، وهو قول جماعة، وقيل: هم أفضل من المؤمنين، والأنبياء أفضل منهم

JISHUMI:v1p315/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r9.speaker: جماعة من الإمامية
JISHUMI:v1p315/r9.claim: Some Imāmīs hold prophets and Imams superior to angels; other views single out the Prophet or suspend judgment.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r9.anchor: وقيل: الأنبياء والأئمة أفضل منهم وهو قول جماعة من الإمامية

JISHUMI:v1p315/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p315/r10.claim: Other positions say only the Prophet is superior to angels, or that the ranking is unknown and judgment should be suspended.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r10.anchor: وقيل: نبينا أفضل منهم فقط، وقيل: لا يعلم ذلك، ويتوقف فيه

JISHUMI:v1p315/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p315/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p315/r11.claim: The author’s position is that angels are superior to all prophets, citing Qur’anic statements about not being an angel, becoming two angels, and Christ and the nearest angels serving God.
JISHUMI:v1p315/r11.anchor: وعندنا: الملائكة أفضل من جميع الأنبياء؛ ولذلك قال تعالى: (ولا أقول لكم إني ملك)

JISHUMI:v1p844/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p844/r1.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v1p844/r1.claim: Asked why God does not prevent Satan, Abū Hāshim says prevention adds duty deserving greater reward, like increased appetite, and Satan's misleading has an effect.
JISHUMI:v1p844/r1.anchor: قيل: اختلفوا، قال أبو هاشم: لأنه زيادة تكليف يستحق به زيادة ثواب، فهو كزيادة الشهوة.

JISHUMI:v1p844/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p844/r2.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p844/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī says Satan's misleading corrupts nothing; the author prefers Abū Hāshim's view.
JISHUMI:v1p844/r2.anchor: وقال أبو علي: لا يفسد به شيء، والأول الوجه.

JISHUMI:v1p844/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p844/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p844/r3.claim: Repel Satan's harm by examining proofs, dispelling doubts, avoiding innovation and error, restraining desires, performing obedience, and avoiding major sins.
JISHUMI:v1p844/r3.anchor: النظر في الأدلة، ودفع الشبه، واجتناب البدع والضلالات؛ ليحصل على سواء الطريق،

JISHUMI:v1p844/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p844/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p844/r4.claim: The enmity belongs to unbelieving jinn, not believers; unbelievers oppose human believers whether jinn or human. Another view makes it inherited without cause, and the author asks what caused Iblīs to refuse Adam's prostration.
JISHUMI:v1p844/r4.anchor: عداوة من كفار الجن دون مؤمنيهم، والكفار أعداء المؤمنين من الإنس كانوا أم من الجن،

JISHUMI:v1p844/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p844/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p844/r5.claim: The warning against following Satan refutes compulsion: if God created misguidance and Satan's whispering, warning against Satan would be more fitting; on compulsion, neither whisper nor human act can affect outcomes.
JISHUMI:v1p844/r5.anchor: وتدل الآية على فساد القول بالجبر؛ لأنه تعالى حذر من اتباع الشيطان، ولو كان الضلال من خلقه والوسوسة من فعله

JISHUMI:v1p883/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p883/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p883/r1.claim: For a competition contract with an invalid condition, the author's school keeps the contract valid and voids the condition; al-Shāfiʿī invalidates the contract.
JISHUMI:v1p883/r1.anchor: والثاني: أنه عقد لازم كالإجارة إذا شرط في عقد المسابقة شرطا فاسدا عندنا يصح العقد، ويبطل الشرط،

JISHUMI:v1p883/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p883/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p883/r2.claim: One view treats expenditure as voluntary; Mujāhid, al-Aṣamm, and Abū Muslim call it an established obligation, namely zakāt.
JISHUMI:v1p883/r2.anchor: فقيل: إنها في التطوع، وهو ثابت، وقيل: هو فرض ثابت وهو الزكاة، عن مجاهد والأصم وأبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v1p883/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p883/r3.speaker: السدي
JISHUMI:v1p883/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says this was obligatory but abrogated by the zakāt verse.
JISHUMI:v1p883/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو فرض منسوخ بآية الزكاة، عن السدي.

JISHUMI:v1p883/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p883/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p883/r4.claim: Because the passage can mean zakāt, the author rejects its abrogation.
JISHUMI:v1p883/r4.anchor: ولا مانع من حمله على الزكاة، فلا يصح القول بنسخه.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r1.claim: إذ is accusative with an implied اذكر, though it can also be governed by قالوا.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r1.anchor: نصب بإضمار اذكر ويجوز ان ينتصب بقالوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r2.claim: الملائكة follows the original form ملاك in its plural pattern, like شمائل from شمأل; the feminine suffix marks a plural group.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r2.anchor: والملائكة جمع ملاك على الأصل كالشمائل في جمع شمأل وإلحاق التاء لتأنيث الجمع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r3.claim: جاعل is from a verb taking two objects; ‘in the earth’ and ‘a successor’ fill the subject-predicate object positions, meaning to make someone a successor there.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r3.anchor: من جعل الذي له مفعولان دخل على المبتدأ والخبر وهما قوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r4.claim: Khalīfa means someone succeeded by another; here it may denote Adam alone with descendants included, or successors collectively, with the angels as the earlier earth-dwellers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r4.anchor: والخليفة من يخلف غيره والمعنى خليفة منكم لأنهم كانوا سكان الأرض فخلفهم فيها آدم وذريته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r5.claim: A variant reads خليقة, with qāf instead of fāʾ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#3/r5.anchor: بالقاف ويجوز ان يريد خليفة مني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r1.claim: God informed the angels beforehand so they would ask and receive an explanation of the wisdom, preventing doubts when the appointment occurred.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r1.anchor: قلت لأي غرض أخبرهم بذلك قلت ليسألوا ذلك السؤال ويجابوا بما اجيبوا به فيعرفوا حكمته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r2.claim: Another explanation is that God taught servants to consult trusted, sincere advisers before acting, despite needing no consultation Himself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r2.anchor: وقيل ليعلم عباده المشاورة في أمورهم قبل أن يقدموا عليها وعرضها على ثقاتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r3.claim: The angels express astonishment at placing sinners where the obedient had been, since God is wise and wills only what is good.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r3.anchor: تعجب من أن يستخلف مكان اهل الطاعة اهل المعصية وهو الحكيم الذي لا يفعل الا الخير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r4.claim: The angels may have learned of the corruption from God’s disclosure or from the Preserved Tablet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r4.anchor: عرفوه بإخبار من الله أو من جهة اللوح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r5.claim: Alternatively, they knew that angels alone were infallible and other creatures would not share their character.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r5.anchor: أو ثبت في علمهم ان الملائكة وحدهم هم الخلق المعصومون وكل خلق سواهم ليسوا على صفتهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r6.claim: They may instead have inferred from one of the two humanlike communities that had inhabited and corrupted the earth before the angels.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r6.anchor: أو قاسوا أحد الثقلين على الآخر حيث أسكنوا الأرض فأفسدوا فيها قبل سكنى الملائكة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r7.claim: The verb has readings with ḍamma or fatḥ on fāʾ, and forms derived from أسفك and سفك.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153#4/r7.anchor: بضم الفاء ويسفك ويسفك من أسفك وسفك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r1.claim: The wāw is circumstantial: ‘Would You appoint one while we are more deserving of favor?’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r1.anchor: للحال كما تقول أتحسن إلى فلان وانا احق منه بالإحسان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: Tasbīḥ and taqdīs mean declaring God far removed from evil; their roots also convey going far away.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: والتسبيح تبعيد الله عن السوء وكذلك تقديسه من سبح في الأرض والماء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r3.claim: بحمدك is circumstantial: they glorify God while praising Him and joined to His praise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r3.anchor: في موضع الحال أي نسبح حامدين لك وملتبسين بحمدك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r4.claim: Without God’s grace through guidance and kindness, the angels could not worship Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r4.anchor: لأنه لولا انعامك علينا بالتوفيق واللطف لم نتمكن من عبادتك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r5.claim: God knows benefits and wise purposes hidden from the angels.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r5.anchor: أي أعلم من المصالح في ذلك ما هو خفي عليكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r6.claim: Servants need only know that God’s actions are good and wise, even when they cannot see the reason.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r6.anchor: كفي العباد ان يعلموا ان افعال الله كلها حسنة وحكمة وإن خفي عليهم وجه الحسن والحكمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r7.claim: God makes part of the wisdom clear in the following account by teaching Adam the names.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r7.anchor: قد بين لهم بعض ذلك فيما اتبعه من قوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r8.claim: Although Arabic speakers derive Adam from brownness or the earth’s surface, the author says Adam is a foreign name, probably on the فاعل pattern.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p154/r8.anchor: وما آدم الا اسم اعجمي وأقرب امره ان يكون على فاعل كآزر وعازر وعابر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda treats إذ as an extra connective, effectively “and your Lord said,” and adduces a line by al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r1.anchor: وهذا قول أبي عبيدة , واستشهد بقول الأسود بن يعفر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r2.speaker: المفضل
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r2.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal says the verse recalls God’s favor to Adam after the preceding reminder of what He created for people on earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r2.anchor: ذكرهم نعمه على أبيهم آدم { إذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة } , وهذا قول المفضل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r3.claim: Alternatively, إذ is not extra: the omitted sense is “He began your creation when,” with ذهب understood after the poet’s أينما.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r3.anchor: وهذا من المحذوف الذي دل عليه الكلام , كما قال النمر بن تولب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r4.claim: Malāʾika is the plural of malak, connected to message; alaka means “send me.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r4.anchor: فأما الملائكة فجمع ملك , وهو مأخوذ من الرسالة , يقال : ألكني إليها أي أرسلني إليها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r5.claim: The Hudhaylī line using ألكني is cited as evidence for the sense “send me.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r5.anchor: قال الهذلي : ألكني وخير الرسو … ل أعلمهم بنواحي الخبر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r6.claim: Al-Awlukah means a message; Labīd’s verse uses it for a message sent by a boy’s mother.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p93/r6.anchor: والألوك الرسالة , قال لبيد بن ربيعة :

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r1.claim: The name al-ūlūka is linked to a message being moved in the mouth; a horse “chews” its iron bit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r1.anchor: وإنما سميت الرسالة ألوكا لأنها تؤلك في الفم , والفرس يألك اللجام ويعلكه , بمعنى يمضغ الحديد بفمه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r2.claim: The angels are the best of living beings and the most intelligent of creatures.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r3.claim: Angels neither eat nor drink, marry, or reproduce.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r3.anchor: إلا أنهم لا يأكلون , ولا يشربون , ولا ينكحون , ولا يتناسلون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r4.claim: They are God’s messengers and never disobey Him in small or great matters.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r4.anchor: وهم رسل الله , لا يعصونه في صغير ولا كبير

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r5.claim: They have subtle bodies and are unseen unless God strengthens human sight to see them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r5.anchor: ولهم أجسام لطيفة لا يرون إلا إذا قوى الله أبصارنا على رؤيتهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r6.anchor: اختلف في معنى { جاعل } على وجهين : أحدهما : أنه بمعنى خالق

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r7.claim: Alternatively, making is giving something a particular state, while origination is bringing it into existence after nonexistence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r7.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى جاعل , لأن حقيقة الجعل فعل الشيء على صفة , وحقيقة الإحداث إيجاد الشيء بعد العدم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r8.claim: Ibn Sābiṭ reports the Prophet said that the earth was spread out from Mecca.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r8.anchor: وروى ابن سابط , أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( دحيت الأرض من مكة )

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r9.claim: The text says this is why Mecca was called Umm al-Qurā, and locates the graves of Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, and Shuʿayb between Zamzam, the Corner, and the Station.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r9.anchor: ولذلك سميت أم القرى , قال : وقبر نوح , وهود , وصالح , وشعيب بن زمزم , والركن , والمقام

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r10.claim: A khalīfa is one who takes another’s place, from the verb khalafa, “to succeed someone.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r10.anchor: وأما ( الخليفة ) فهو القائم مقام غيره , من قولهم : خلف فلان فلانا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r11.claim: With fatḥa, khalaf denotes righteous successors and with sukūn, wicked successors; the Qur’an and a hadith illustrate the distinction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r11.anchor: والخلف بتحريك اللام من الصالحين , والخلف بتسكينها من الطالحين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Adam and his descendants replaced the jinn, who had corrupted the earth and shed blood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r12.anchor: كان في الأرض الجن , فأفسدوا فيها , سفكوا الدماء , فأهلكوا , فجعل آدم وذريته بدلهم , وهذا قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r13.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī takes it as generations of Adam’s children succeeding one another in upholding right and cultivating earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r13.anchor: في إقامة الحق وعمارة الأرض , وهذا قول الحسن البصري

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r14.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the khalīfa is God’s deputy in judging among creation: Adam and those of his descendants who take his place.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r14.anchor: جاعل في الأرض خليفة يخلفني في الحكم بين خلقي , وهو آدم , ومن قام مقامه من ولده , وهذا قول ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r15.claim: The angels’ question may be a genuine request for information about whether God would place a corrupter in the earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r15.anchor: أنهم قالوه استفهما واستخبارا حين قال لهم : إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r16.claim: Alternatively, the question form expresses an assertion; the angels inferred corruption from the jinn who had inhabited earth before.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p94/r16.anchor: أنه إيجاب , وإن خرجت الألف مخرج الاستفهام , كما قال جرير

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r1.claim: On the assertive reading, they may have inferred that a new vicegerent would corrupt the earth because the jinn before them had done so.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r1.anchor: لأنهم رأوا الجن من قبلهم , قد أفسدوا في الأرض , وسفكوا الدماء , فتصوروا أنه إن استخلف

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r2.claim: One explanation of their remark is dismay that creatures blessed and appointed to earth would corrupt it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r2.anchor: قالوه استعظاما لفعلهم , أي كيف يفسدون فيها , ويسفكون الدماء , وقد أنعمت عليهم واستخلفتهم فيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r3.claim: Another explanation is their astonishment that God would appoint them despite knowing they would corrupt and shed blood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r3.anchor: قالوه تعجبا من استخلافه لهم أي كيف تستخلفهم في الأرض وقد علمت أنهم يفسدون فيها ويسفكون الدماء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r4.claim: Safk means pouring out blood specifically, unlike water and other liquids; safḥ is similar but also applies to any liquid wasted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r4.anchor: السفك صب الدم خاصة دون غيره من الماء والمائع , والسفح مثله , إلا أنه مستعمل في كل مائع على وجه التضييع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r5.claim: The word sifāḥ for fornication reflects the waste of its fluid.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r5.anchor: ولذلك قالوا في الزنى : إنه سفاح لتضييع مائه فيه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r6.claim: Tasbīḥ is declaring God free of evil in a mode of exaltation; al-Aʿshā’s line uses subḥān as disavowal.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r6.anchor: والتسبيح في كلامهم التنزيه من السوء على جهة التعظيم , ومنه قول أعشى بني ثعلبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r7.claim: Though others may be described as pure, tasbīḥ is a religious term for the highest degree of exaltation, due only to God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r7.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يسبح عير الله , وإن كان منزها , لأنه صار علما في الدين على أعلى مراتب التعظيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd interpret the angels’ tasbīḥ as prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r8.anchor: أي من المصلين , وهذا قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r9.claim: Mujāhid understands it as glorifying God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r9.anchor: والثاني : معناه نعظمك , وهذا قول مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r10.speaker: المفضل
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r10.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal takes it as the familiar act of tasbīḥ, citing Jarīr’s verse about pilgrims glorifying God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p96/r10.anchor: والثالث : أنه التسبيح المعروف , وهذا قول المفضل , واستشهد بقول جرير

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r1.claim: Taqdīs derives from purification; “the holy land” means the purified land, as the cited line uses al-muqaddas for “purified.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r1.anchor:
كما شبرق الولدان ثوب المقدس
أي المطهر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r2.claim: One interpretation of the angels’ taqdīs is that they pray.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r3.claim: Another interpretation is that they purify God from impurities.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r4.claim: A third is the familiar meaning of consecration or declaring holiness.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd say God refers to Iblīs’s concealed pride and disobedience when commanded to prostrate to Adam.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r5.anchor: أراد ما أضمره إبليس من الاستكبار والمعصية فيما أمروا به من السجود لآدم , وهذا قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r6.claim: Qatāda says God refers to the prophets and messengers among Adam’s descendants, who will act righteously rather than corrupt the earth.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r6.anchor: والثاني : من في ذرية آدم في الأنبياء والرسل الذين يصلحون في الأرض ولا يفسدون , وهذا قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r7.claim: A third explanation is that God means the benefits whose planning He alone knows.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p98/r7.anchor: ما اختص بعلمه من تدبير المصالح

MUJAHID:v1p72#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p72#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p72#2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the angels' praise as exalting and magnifying God.
MUJAHID:v1p72#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك ﴾ قال نعظمك ونكبرك

MUJAHID:v1p72#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p72#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p72#2/r2.claim: God knew of Iblis's disobedience and created him for it.
MUJAHID:v1p72#2/r2.anchor: قال الله عز وجل ﴿ إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون ﴾ قال علم من إبليس المعصية وخلقه لها

MUQATIL:2:30/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30/r1.claim: Muqatil glosses idh as qad, giving the sense that the Lord had said this to the angels.
MUQATIL:2:30/r1.anchor: { وإذ } ، يعنى وقد { قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة } ،

MUQATIL:2:30/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30/r2.claim: Angels and jinn preceded devils and humans; jinn inhabited earth while angels inhabited heaven. Jinn became envious, fought, and God sent a fiery host from the lowest heaven, called jinn, led by Iblis, to earth.
MUQATIL:2:30/r2.anchor: خلق الملائكة والجن قبل خلق الشياطين والإنس، وهو آدم، عليه السلام، فجعلهم سكان الأرض،

MUQATIL:2:30/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30/r3.claim: The jinn liked life on earth despite having fewer worship obligations there; when God announced a successor would replace them and they would be raised to Him, they resented it as the least-working angels.
MUQATIL:2:30/r3.anchor: فلم يكلفوا من العبادة فى الأرض ما كلفوا فى السماء، فأحبوا القيام فى الأرض، فأوحى الله عز وجل إليهم:

MUQATIL:2:30/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30/r4.claim: The angels' question refers to someone committing sins and shedding blood wrongfully, as the jinn had done.
MUQATIL:2:30/r4.anchor: فكرهوا ذلك؛ لأنهم كانوا أهون الملائكة أعمالا، { قالوا أتجعل فيها } ، يقول: أتجعل فى الأرض

MUQATIL:2:30/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30/r5.claim: The angels say they remember God at His command, pray to Him, and magnify His command; Muqatil connects glorification with the thunder in 13:13 remembering God by His command.
MUQATIL:2:30/r5.anchor: يعنى يذكره بأمره، ونقدس لك ونصلى لك ونعظم أمرك.

MUQATIL:2:30#2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r1.claim: God knows that angels will inhabit heaven while Adam and his descendants inhabit earth, including people who glorify and worship Him.
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r1.anchor: إن فى علمى أنكم سكان السماء، ويكون آدم وذريته سكان الأرض، ويكون منهم من يسبح بحمدى ويعبدنى،

MUQATIL:2:30#2/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r2.claim: Adam was made from red and white clay from salty and fresh soil; therefore his descendants include white, red, and black people, believers and unbelievers.
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r2.anchor: فخلق آدم عليه السلام، من طين أحمر وأبيض من السبخة والعذبة، فمن ثم نسله أبيض وأحمر وأسود مؤمن وكافر،

MUQATIL:2:30#2/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r3.claim: Iblis envied Adam's form and asked the angels what they would do if Adam were favored; they replied that they would hear and obey God. Iblis privately resolved not to obey and to mislead Adam.
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r3.anchor: فحسد إبليس تلك الصورة، فقال للملائكة الذين هم معه: أرأيتم هذا الذى لم تروا

MUQATIL:2:30#2/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r4.claim: Adam's shaped clay was left for forty years. Iblis entered through his rear and exited his mouth, boasting that fire would overcome hollow clay.
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r4.anchor: فترك آدم طينا أربعين سنة مصورا، فجعل إبليس يدخل من دبره ويخرج من فيه، ويقول: أنا نار وهذا طين أجوف،

MUQATIL:2:30#2/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r5.claim: Iblis's boast that he would overcome Adam is linked to 34:20, where his expectation is said to come true except for a group of believers; Muqatil explains his claim to seize Adam's descendants as all but a few.
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r5.anchor: يعنى قوله يومئذ: لأغلبنه، وقوله: لأحتنكن، يعنى لأحتوين على ذريته إلا قليلا،

MUQATIL:2:30#2/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r6.claim: When God ordered the spirit to enter Adam, it objected to the dark body and was told to enter unwillingly; it would leave only unwillingly.
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r6.anchor: فقال للروح: ادخلى هذا الجسد، فقالت: أى رب، أين تدخلنى هذا الجسد المظلم؟

MUQATIL:2:30#2/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r7.claim: The spirit entered from Adam's head and reached his navel, making him sit; it then reached his toes, tried to exit, and returned to leave through his nostrils. Adam sneezed and first said praise be to God.
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r7.anchor: ثم نفخ فيه الروح من قبل رأسه، فترددت الروح فيه حتى بلغت نصف جسده موضع السرة، فجعل للقعود،

MUQATIL:2:30#2/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r8.claim: Adam's early sitting as the spirit moved through him is linked to 17:11, which Muqatil glosses as saying the human is hasty.

MUQATIL:2:30#2/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r9.claim: God answered Adam's first praise with a prayer for mercy and said this was why He created him: to glorify and sanctify God; His mercy preceded Adam.
MUQATIL:2:30#2/r9.anchor: فعطس عند ذلك خروجها من منخريه، فقال: الحمد لله، فكان أول كلامه، فرد ربه عز وجل: يرحمك الله،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r1.claim: Before Adam, jinn inhabited earth and corrupted it; angels expelled them to islands, seas, and mountaintops, then settled there.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r1.anchor: لما خلق الله تعالى الأرض أسكن فيها الجن وأسكن فى السماء الملائكة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r2.claim: إذ is governed by an omitted imperative, اذكر, meaning recall the story.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r2.anchor: إذ نصب باضمار اذكر والملائكة جمع ملاك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r3.claim: ملائكة is the plural of ملاك, like شمائل from شمأل.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r3.anchor: والملائكة جمع ملاك كالشمائل جمع شمأل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r4.claim: جاعل means making or appointing, from a verb taking two objects: خليفة and في الأرض.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r5.claim: A khalifa succeeds another; the feminine-pattern form has a hāʾ added for emphasis.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r5.anchor: وهو من يخلف غيره فعيله بمعنى فاعلة وزيدت الهاء للمبالغة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r6.claim: The khalifa may mean a successor to the angels, who had inhabited earth before Adam and his descendants.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r6.anchor: والمعنى خليفة منكم لأنهم كانوا سكان الأرض

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r7.claim: It may refer specifically to Adam, whose mention stands for his descendants, or generally to one who succeeds the angels.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r7.anchor: ولم يقل خلاف أو خلفاء لأنه أريد بالخليفة آدم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r8.claim: Alternatively Adam is God’s vicegerent on earth, as every prophet is; the author cites God’s address to David in 38:26.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r8.anchor: أو خليفة منى لأن آدم كان خليفة الله فى أرضه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r9.claim: God informed the angels either to elicit a question and reveal the appointment’s wisdom or to teach people to consult before acting, though God needs no counsel.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r9.anchor: فيعرفوا حكمته فى استخلافهم قبل كونهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r10.claim: The angels wondered that obedient inhabitants would be replaced by sinners, while affirming God’s wisdom and knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r10.anchor: تعجب من أن يستخلف مكان أهل الطاعة أهل المعصية

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r11.claim: The angels knew through God’s information, the Preserved Tablet, or analogy between the two kinds of beings.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r11.anchor: أو من جهة اللوح أو قاسوا أحد الثقلين على الآخر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r12.claim: يسفك means to pour or shed blood.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r13.claim: The waw in ونحن is circumstantial, and بحمدك is also circumstantial: the angels glorify while praising God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r13.anchor: فى موضع الحال أى نسبح حامدين لك ومتلبسين بحمدك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r14.claim: The construction is like 5:61, where entering with disbelief means entering while disbelieving.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r14.anchor: كقوله تعالى ﴿ وقد دخلوا بالكفر ﴾ أى دخلوا كافرين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r15.claim: نقدس لك means purifying ourselves for God; alternatively tasbih and taqdis mean declaring God free of evil, with a root sense of going away and distancing.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r15.anchor: ونطهر أنفسنا لك وقيل التسبيح والتقديس تبعيد الله من السوء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r16.claim: God knows hidden wisdom: among humans will be prophets, saints, and scholars, along with matters the angels do not know.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r16.anchor: يعنى يكون فيهم الأنبساء و الأولياء والعلماء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r17.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r17.claim: ما is a relative pronoun and object of أعلم, with its antecedent omitted.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r17.anchor: وما بمعنى الذى وهو مفعول أعلم والعائد محذوف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r18.speaker: الحجازيون وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p36/r18.claim: The segment attributes a reading of إني to the Hijazis and Abu ʿAmr.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r1.claim: Idh normally refers to the past and idha to the future, though each can stand in the other’s place.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r1.anchor: إذ وإذا حرفا توقيت فإذ للماضي، وإذا للمستقبل وقد توضع إحداهما موضع الأخرى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r2.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad says idh with a future verb refers to the past, as in 8:30 and 33:37.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r2.anchor: وقل المبرد: إذا جاء «إذ» مع مستقبل كان معناه ماضيا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r3.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad says idha with a past verb can refer to the future, as in 79:34, 80:33, and 110:1.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r3.anchor: وإذا جاء «إذا» مع الماضي كان معناه مستقبلا كقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r4.claim: Abu ʿUbayda (Maʿmar ibn al-Muthanna) takes idh as redundant; al-Qurtubi rejects this, following the grammarians and exegetes.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r4.anchor: وقال معمر بن المثنى أبو عبيدة: «إذ» زائدة والتقدير: وقال ربك واستشهد بقول الأسود بن يعفر:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r5.speaker: الأسود بن يعفر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r5.claim: Al-Aswad ibn Yaʿfur’s line is cited as evidence for Abu ʿUbayda’s reading of idh.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r5.anchor: قول الأسود بن يعفر: فإذ وذلك لا مهاة لذكره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r6.speaker: الزجاج والنحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj, al-Nahhas, and the exegetes reject Abu ʿUbayda: idh is a temporal noun, not an extra particle.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r6.anchor: وأنكر هذا القول الزجاج والنحاس وجميع المفسرين. قال النحاس: وهذا خطأ لأن «إذ» اسم وهي ظرف زمان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r7.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj supplies an omitted clause about beginning creation; al-Qurtubi also allows an implied command, “Remember when,” or a connection to the command to worship the Creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r7.anchor: فالتقدير وابتدأ خلقكم إذ قال فكان هذا من المحذوف الذي دل عليه الكلام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري وأبو المعالي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r8.claim: Al-Ashʿari holds that God’s address is eternal, conditional on the angels’ existence and understanding; Abu al-Maʿali endorses this.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r8.anchor: وهكذا الباب كله في أوامر الله تعالى ونواهيه ومخاطباته. وهذا مذهب الشيخ أبي الحسن الأشعري، وهو الذي ارتضاه أبو المعالي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r9.claim: Rabb means owner, master, rectifier, and restorer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r9.anchor: والرب: المالك والسيد والمصلح والجابر وقد تقدم بيانه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r10.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r10.claim: Ibn Kaysan and others derive malak from milk, on the pattern faʿal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r10.anchor: قال ابن كيسان وغيره: وزن ملك فعل من الملك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r11.claim: Abu ʿUbayda derives malak from laʾaka, “to send,” and explains al-uluka and related forms as “message.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30/r11.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة هو مفعل من لأك إذا أرسل. والألوكة والمألكة والمألكة: الرسالة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r1.claim: Labid’s poem uses aluk for a message, describing a mother sending her boy with one.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r1.anchor:
وغلام أرسلته أمه
بألوك فبذلنا ما سأل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r2.speaker: آخر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r2.claim: An unnamed poet uses maʾlak for a message to al-Nuʿman.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r2.anchor:
وقال آخر:
أبلغ النعمان عني مألكا
إنني قد طال حبسي وانتظاري

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r3.claim: Alikni means “send me”; the hamza moves from initial to medial position, then the form is eased to malak.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r3.anchor: ويقال: ألكني أي أرسلني فأصله هذا مألك، الهمزة فاء الفعل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r4.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r4.claim: Another derivation makes the original malaʾak from malaka, with an augmentative hamza, like shamʾal from shamila.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r4.anchor: وقيل أصله ملأك من ملك يملك، نحو شمأل من شمل فالهمزة زائدة عن ابن كيسان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r5.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r5.claim: A poetic line preserves malaʾak for a messenger descending from the sky.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r5.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
فلست لإنسي ولكن لملأك
تنزل من جو السماء يصوب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r6.speaker: النضر بن شميل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r6.claim: Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl says Arabs recognize no derivation for malak.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r6.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل: لا اشتقاق للملك عند العرب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r7.claim: The ending in malaʾika can mark the feminine plural, like ṣalādimah.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r7.anchor: والهاء في الملائكة تأكيد لتأنيث الجمع ومثله الصلادمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, the ending intensifies the sense, like ʿallāma and nassāba.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r9.speaker: أرباب المعاني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r9.claim: They say God addressed angels not for counsel but to elicit their view of action, worship, praise, and sanctification, then restored their rank by ordering prostration to Adam.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r9.anchor: خاطب الله الملائكة لا للمشورة ولكن لاستخراج ما فيهم من رؤية الحركات والعبادة والتسبيح والتقديس،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r10.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r10.claim: Al-Tabari, citing Abu Rawq, says jaʿil here means “creator”; its single object supports this.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r10.anchor: «جاعل» هنا بمعنى خالق ذكره الطبري عن أبي روق،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r11.claim: Ibn Sabit reports that the earth was spread from Mecca, called Umm al-Qura, and that Noah, Hud, Salih, and Shuʿayb are buried between Zamzam and the Corner and Station.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r11.anchor: والأرض قيل: إنها مكة. روى ابن سابط عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r12.claim: Khalifa as an active noun is a successor to angels or other earlier beings; as a passive noun, it means one made a successor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r12.anchor: و «خليفة» يكون بمعنى فاعل أي يخلف من كان قبله من الملائكة في الأرض، أو من كان قبله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r13.claim: Khalaf with a vowel refers to righteous successors, while the still form refers to wicked ones.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r13.anchor: والخلف بالتحريك من الصالحين، وبتسكينها من الطالحين هذا هو المعروف،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r14.speaker: زيد بن علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r14.claim: The general reading is khalifa with faʾ; Zayd ibn ʿAli reads khalīqa with qaf.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r14.anchor: و «خليفة» بالفاء قراءة الجماعة إلا ما روي عن زيد بن علي فإنه قرأ «خليقة» بالقاف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r15.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r15.claim: Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, and exegetes identify Adam as the khalifa, God’s deputy in carrying out His rulings and commands and the first messenger to earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#2/r15.anchor: والمعنى بالخليفة هنا في قول ابن مسعود وابن عباس وجميع أهل التأويل آدم عليه السلام،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r1.claim: A report from Abu Dharr has the Prophet confirm Adam was a sent prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r1.anchor: حديث أبي ذر، قال: قلت: يا رسول الله أنبيا كان مرسلا؟ قال: «نعم»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r2.claim: Adam was sent to his own forty children, born as twenty pairs of a boy and a girl, whose descendants multiplied.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r2.anchor: وكانوا أربعين ولدا في عشرين بطنا في كل بطن ذكر وأنثى، وتوالدوا حتى كثروا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r3.claim: The account of Adam’s offspring follows the verse about humanity’s single origin and its spouse.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r3.anchor: خلقكم من نفس واحدة وخلق منها زوجها وبث منهما رجالا كثيرا ونساء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r4.claim: Adam’s community was forbidden carrion, blood, and pork.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r4.anchor: وأنزل عليهم تحريم الميتة والدم ولحم الخنزير.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r5.claim: Torah scholars give Adam’s lifespan as 930 years; Wahb ibn Munabbih reports 1,000 years.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r5.anchor: وعاش تسعمائة وثلاثين سنة هكذا ذكر أهل التوراة. وروي عن وهب بن منبه أنه عاش ألف سنة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the verse establishes the duty to appoint an imam or caliph to unify the community and enforce rulings; the community agrees except al-Asamm and followers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r6.anchor: هذه الآية أصل في نصب إمام وخليفة يسمع له ويطاع لتجتمع به الكلمة،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r7.speaker: الأصم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r7.claim: Al-Asamm says appointment is not obligatory if the community performs pilgrimage and jihad, acts fairly, distributes public funds, and applies legal penalties.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r7.anchor: قال: إنها غير واجبة في الدين بل يسوغ ذلك، وأن الأمة متى أقاموا حجهم وجهادهم، وتناصفوا فيما بينهم،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi adduces this verse, David’s caliphate, and the promise to make believers successors as proof of appointment’s obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#3/r8.anchor: ودليلنا قول الله تعالى: { إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة }

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r1.claim: The Companions agreed on Abu Bakr after Saqifa; the Ansar proposed one leader from each group, but were persuaded that Arabs accepted Quraysh.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r1.anchor: وأجمعت الصحابة على تقديم الصديق بعد اختلاف وقع بين المهاجرين والأنصار في سقيفة بني ساعدة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r2.claim: Abu Bakr designated ʿUmar, and no one objected that the office was unnecessary; al-Qurtubi calls the imamate obligatory and a pillar sustaining Muslims.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r2.anchor: ثم إن الصديق رضي الله عنه لما حضرته الوفاة عهد إلى عمر في الإمامة، ولم يقل له أحد هذا أمر غير واجب علينا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r3.speaker: الرافضة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r3.claim: The Rafidites say reason makes appointment obligatory, with revelation only confirming this.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r3.anchor: وقالت الرافضة: يجب نصبه عقلا، وإن السمع إنما ورد على جهة التأكيد لقضية العقل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r4.claim: Reason neither obligates or forbids nor makes things good or bad; appointment is obligatory by revelation, not reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r4.anchor: وهذا فاسد لأن العقل لا يوجب ولا يحظر ولا يقبح ولا يحسن وإذا كان كذلك ثبت أنها واجبة من جهة الشرع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r5.claim: Proposed routes to recognizing an imam are prophetic designation, choice by qualified electors, or possession of the required qualities and self-assertion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r5.anchor: هل يجب من جهة السمع بالنص على الإمام من جهة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، أم من جهة اختيار أهل الحل والعقد له،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r6.speaker: الإمامية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r6.claim: Imamis say the imam is known only through a prophetic text; al-Qurtubi accepts reasoned consideration and qualified consensus as routes.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r6.anchor: فذهبت الإمامية وغيرها إلى أن الطريق الذي يعرف به الإمام هو النص من الرسول عليه السلام ولا مدخل للاختيار فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r7.speaker: الإمامية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r7.claim: Those requiring text alone reject analogy and independent reasoning; factions claim designation for Abu Bakr, al-ʿAbbas, or ʿAli.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r7.anchor: وهؤلاء الذين قالوا لا طريق إليه إلا النص بنوه على أصلهم أن القياس والرأي والاجتهاد باطل لا يعرف به شيء أصلا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r8.claim: A duty to obey one named imam would require the whole community to know him; neither reason nor transmission establishes a particular person.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r8.anchor: لو فرض على الأمة طاعة إمام بعينه بحيث لا يجوز العدول عنه إلى غيره لعلم ذلك لاستحالة تكليف الأمة بأسرها طاعة الله في غير معين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r9.claim: Mass transmission would make a designation as universally evident as prayer, Ramadan fasting, and pilgrimage; solitary reports cannot establish certainty.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#4/r9.anchor: وليس في العقل ما يدل على ثبوت الإمامة لشخص معين، وكذلك ليس في الخبر ما يوجب العلم بثبوت إمام معين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r1.claim: Conflicting groups transmit designation for different imams, so none has priority; without a reliable path to a text, selection and reasoning follow.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r1.anchor: وجب إثبات إمامة أبي بكر والعباس لأن لكل واحد منهما قوما ينقلون النص صريحا في إمامته وإذا بطل إثبات الثلاثة بالنص

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi says reports for Abu Bakr could be assembled against claims of mass designation; the far larger body outside the Imamis denies any designation, so necessary knowledge cannot be denied by a smaller group.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r2.anchor: فإن تعسف متعسف وادعى التواتر والعلم الضروري بالنص فينبغي أن يقابلوا على الفور بنقيض دعواهم في النص على أبي بكر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r3.claim: If a small faction could deny necessary knowledge, established facts about Baghdad and far China could also be denied.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r3.anchor: والعلم الضروري لا يجتمع على نفيه من ينحط عن معشار أعداد مخالفي الإمامية ولو جاز رد الضروري في ذلك لجاز أن ينكر طائفة بغداد والصين الأقصى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r4.claim: The Imamis cite the Prophet’s statement that whoever has him as mawla has ʿAli as mawla as proof of ʿAli’s appointment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r4.anchor: السادسة: في رد الأحاديث التي احتج بها الإمامية في النص على علي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r5.speaker: الإمامية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r5.claim: The Imamis say mawla means one with greater right, so the Prophet’s statement establishes ʿAli’s imamate and obligatory obedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r5.anchor: قالوا: والمولى في اللغة بمعنى أولى فلما قال «فعلي مولاه» بفاء التعقيب علم أن المراد بقوله «مولى» أنه أحق وأولى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r6.speaker: الإمامية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r6.claim: They argue that comparing ʿAli to Aaron implies succession, since Aaron was Moses’ deputy, brother, and prophetic partner.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r6.anchor: قالوا: ومنزلة هارون معروفة، وهو أنه كان مشاركا في النبوة ولم يكن ذلك لعلي،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the Ghadir report is not mass-transmitted and its soundness is disputed; Abu Dawud and Abu Hatim criticize it as contradicted by another prophetic report.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r7.anchor: والجواب عن الحديث الأول: أنه ليس بمتواتر، وقد اختلف في صحته، وقد طعن فيه أبو داود السجستاني وأبو حاتم الرازي،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r8.speaker: أبو داود السجستاني وأبو حاتم الرازي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r8.claim: Abu Dawud and Abu Hatim argue the Ghadir report conflicts with the Prophet’s saying that four tribes are clients only of God and His Messenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#5/r8.anchor: وقد طعن فيه أبو داود السجستاني وأبو حاتم الرازي، واستدلا على بطلانه بأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi replies that even if sound, the Ghadir report proves ʿAli’s merit rather than imamate: mawla can mean wali, as in 66:4.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r1.anchor: جواب ثان: وهو أن الخبر وإن كان صحيحا رواه ثقة عن ثقة فليس فيه ما يدل على إمامته، وإنما على فضيلته،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r2.claim: One reported occasion is a dispute between ʿAli and Usama: after Usama denied being ʿAli’s mawla, the Prophet made the statement.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r2.anchor: جواب ثالث: وهو أن هذا الخبر ورد على سبب، وذلك أن أسامة وعليا اختصما، فقال علي لأسامة: أنت مولاي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r3.claim: Another reported occasion is the slander of ʿAli after his comment about Aisha; the Prophet defended him against hypocrites, whom some Companions identified by their hatred of ʿAli.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r3.anchor: جواب رابع: وهو أن عليا عليه السلام لما قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قصة الإفك في عائشة رضي الله عنها: النساء سواها كثير.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi says the Aaron comparison does not mean succession after the Prophet’s death: Aaron died before Moses, and Joshua succeeded Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r4.anchor: وأما الحديث الثاني فلا خلاف أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يرد بمنزلة هارون من موسى بالخلافة بعده،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r5.claim: The comparison means ʿAli was left in charge of the Prophet’s household during his life and absence, as Aaron deputized for Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#6/r5.anchor: وإنما أراد أني استخلفتك على أهلي في حياتي وغيبوبتي عن أهلي، كما كان هارون خليفة موسى على قومه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r1.claim: During Tabuk the Prophet left Ali in Medina; after hypocrites alleged dislike, he told Ali the allegation was false and compared his position to Aaron's with Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r1.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما خرج إلى غزوة تبوك استخلف عليا عليه السلام في المدينة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r2.claim: The appointment did not uniquely distinguish Ali: the Prophet left other companions in charge during expeditions, and this report is solitary through Saʿd b. Abi Waqqas.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r2.anchor: فقد شارك عليا في هذه الفضيلة غيره لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم استخلف في كل غزاة غزاها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r3.claim: When sending Muʿadh to Yemen, the Prophet said Abu Bakr and Umar were indispensable to him, like hearing and sight to the head, and called them his ministers on earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r3.anchor: إنهما لا غنى بي عنهما إن منزلتهما مني بمنزلة السمع والبصر من الرأس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r4.claim: A report says the Prophet described Abu Bakr and Umar as being to him like Aaron to Moses; unlike Ali's report, it was stated without a precipitating occasion.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r4.anchor: وهذا الخبر ورد ابتداء، وخبر علي ورد على سبب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r5.claim: Because Abu Bakr's and Umar's report was initiated without a specific occasion while Ali's answered one, the author concludes Abu Bakr has the stronger claim to the imamate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r5.anchor: فوجب أن يكون أبو بكر أولى منه بالإمامة، والله أعلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r6.claim: One route to establish an imam is explicit designation; the Prophet indicated Abu Bakr, who in turn designated Umar.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r6.anchor: أحدها: النص، وقد تقدم الخلاف فيه، وقال فيه أيضا الحنابلة وجماعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r7.claim: A predecessor may designate a group and leave the choice among them; Umar did so, and the companions selected Uthman.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r7.anchor: وهو الطريق الثاني ويكون التخيير إليهم في تعيين واحد منهم كما فعل الصحابة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r8.claim: A third route is agreement of the people empowered to bind and loose in the imam's city; if no successor exists, their accepted choice binds Muslims elsewhere unless the imam openly manifests corruption.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#7/r8.anchor: الطريق الثالث: إجماع أهل الحل والعقد وذلك أن الجماعة في مصر من أمصار المسلمين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r1.speaker: رسول الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r1.claim: The Prophet says sincerity to God, adherence to the community, and counsel to rulers keep rancor from a believer's heart, and the Muslims' call encompasses those behind them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r1.anchor: ثلاث لا يغل عليهن قلب مؤمن إخلاص العمل لله ولزوم الجماعة ومناصحة ولاة الأمر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r2.claim: One qualified member of the people of authority can conclude the imamate, against those who require a group; Umar's pledge of Abu Bakr was accepted by the companions, and contracts need no minimum number.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r2.anchor: فإن عقدها واحد من أهل الحل والعقد فذلك ثابت ويلزم الغير فعله، خلافا لبعض الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r3.speaker: أبو المعالي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r3.claim: Abu al-Maʿali says an imamate concluded by one person's pledge is binding and cannot be revoked absent a change or event; he calls this consensus.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r3.anchor: من انعقدت له الإمامة بعقد واحد فقد لزمت، ولا يجوز خلعه من غير حدث وتغير أمر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r4.claim: Some count seizure by a qualified contender as a fourth route to the imamate, even without consultation or prior choice, once people pledge to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r4.anchor: فإن تغلب من له أهلية الإمامة وأخذها بالقهر والغلبة فقد قيل إن ذلك يكون طريقا رابعا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r5.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله التستري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r5.claim: Asked about a ruler who overcomes the country, Sahl al-Tustari says to obey him, pay what he claims as his due, refrain from denouncing or fleeing him, and keep entrusted religious secrets.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r5.anchor: سئل سهل بن عبد الله التستري: ما يجب علينا لمن غلب على بلادنا وهو إمام؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r6.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r6.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mandad says a qualified person who seizes authority without consultation or choice has a completed pledge once people give allegiance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r6.anchor: وقال ابن خويز منداد: ولو وثب على الأمر من يصلح له من غير مشورة ولا اختيار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r7.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r7.claim: Some of the author's colleagues say witnesses are not required for the imamate contract because no decisive revealed proof establishes that requirement.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r7.anchor: قال بعض أصحابنا: إنه لا يفتقر إلى الشهود لأن الشهادة لا تثبت إلا بسمع قاطع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r8.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r8.claim: Others require witnesses to prevent secret competing claims and ensuing disorder, and consider two witnesses sufficient.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r8.anchor: ومنهم من قال: يفتقر إلى شهود فمن قال بهذا احتج بأن قال: لو لم تعقد فيه الشهادة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r9.speaker: الجبائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r9.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi requires four witnesses, a contracting party, and the candidate, using Umar's six-person council as evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r9.anchor: خلافا للجبائي حيث قال باعتبار أربعة شهود وعاقد ومعقود له لأن عمر حيث جعلها شورى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r10.claim: The author rejects al-Jubbaʾi's extra requirements: both sides accept two witnesses, while the additional number has no supporting proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r10.anchor: لا خلاف بيننا وبينه أن شهادة الاثنين معتبرة، وما زاد مختلف فيه ولم يدل عليه الدليل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r11.claim: The imam has eleven conditions; the first is descent from Quraysh, whose supporting report continues in the next segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#8/r11.anchor: الحادية عشرة: في شرائط الإمام وهي أحد عشر: الأول: أن يكون من صميم قريش

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r1.claim: The first condition is Qurayshi descent, supported by the report that leaders are from Quraysh; the author notes disagreement over it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r1.anchor: " الأئمة من قريش " وقد اختلف في هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r2.claim: The imam must be fit to judge Muslims and be an independent jurist who can address cases without needing another's legal opinion; this is agreed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r2.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون ممن يصلح أن يكون قاضيا من قضاة المسلمين مجتهدا لا يحتاج

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r3.claim: He needs sound judgment and practical expertise in war, armies, frontier defense, protecting the community, restraining wrongdoing, and recovering victims' rights.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r3.anchor: أن يكون ذا خبرة ورأي حصيف بأمر الحرب وتدبير الجيوش وسد الثغور

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r4.claim: He must not be too tenderhearted to impose penalties or afraid to execute severe punishments; the companions' consensus and the imam's judicial and supervisory duties support these qualifications.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r4.anchor: أن يكون ممن لا تلحقه رقة في إقامة الحدود ولا فزع من ضرب الرقاب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r5.claim: The imam must be free and Muslim; the author says the requirements of freedom and Islam are clear.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r5.anchor: أن يكون حرا ولا خفاء باشتراط حرية الإمام وإسلامه وهو السادس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r6.claim: The imam must be male and physically sound; women cannot hold the imamate, although jurists differ on women's eligibility to judge cases in which their testimony is admissible.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r6.anchor: أن يكون ذكرا، سليم الأعضاء وهو الثامن. وأجمعوا على أن المرأة لا يجوز أن تكون إماما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r7.claim: The imam must be an adult and sane, with no disagreement on these requirements.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r7.anchor: أن يكون بالغا عاقلا ولا خلاف في ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r8.claim: The imam must be just, and the community agrees a sinful person cannot initially be appointed; he should be foremost in knowledge, as the leaders' report and God's choosing Talut for knowledge and bodily strength indicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r8.anchor: أن يكون عدلا لأنه لا خلاف بين الأمة أنه لا يجوز أن تعقد الإمامة لفاسق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r9.claim: A report says the imams are the community's intercessors, so people should consider whom they choose for intercession.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r10.claim: God's choosing Talut means selecting him and indicates lineage as a condition; the imam need not be infallible, know the unseen, be the best horseman or bravest, or belong only to Banu Hashim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r10.anchor: معناه اختاره وهذا يدل على شرط النسب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r11.claim: A less excellent candidate may be appointed when choosing the superior risks civil strife or disables the public functions for which the imam is installed; Umar's council supplies precedent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r11.anchor: يجوز نصب المفضول مع وجود الفاضل خوف الفتنة وألا يستقيم أمر الأمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r12.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r12.claim: The majority say an imam who becomes manifestly sinful after appointment loses office, because sin disables the duties for which the imamate exists.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r12.anchor: فقال الجمهور: إنه تنفسخ إمامته ويخلع بالفسق الظاهر المعلوم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r13.speaker: آخرون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r13.claim: Others say removal is permitted only for unbelief, abandoning prayer or its call, or abandoning a rule of the law; the supporting hadith begins in the next segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#9/r13.anchor: وقال آخرون: لا ينخلع إلا بالكفر أو بترك إقامة الصلاة أو الترك إلى دعائها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r1.claim: The report of ʿUbada forbids disputing authority except upon clear unbelief for which there is proof from God; Muslim transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r1.anchor: إلا أن تروا كفرا بواحا عندكم من الله فيه برهان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r2.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r2.claim: A report from ʿAwf b. Malik says rulers are not to be opposed so long as they establish prayer; Muslim transmits it.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r3.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r3.claim: Umm Salama reports that one who inwardly dislikes and rejects wrongdoing by rulers is safe, while one who approves and follows is culpable; the Prophet says not to fight rulers while they pray, and Muslim transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r3.anchor: وعن أم سلمة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r4.claim: An imam must resign if he finds a defect in himself that affects his fitness for office.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r4.anchor: ويجب عليه أن يخلع نفسه إذا وجد في نفسه نقصا يؤثر في الإمامة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r5.claim: Jurists disagree whether an unimpaired imam may resign; the author says he may, citing Abu Bakr's request to be released, the companions' refusal, and the analogy of an agent or judge who can resign.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r5.anchor: فلو لم يكن له أن يفعل ذلك لأنكرت الصحابة ذلك عليه ولقالت له: ليس لك أن تقول هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r6.claim: Once the imamate is validly concluded by the council or one member, everyone must pledge obedience and uphold God's Book and the Prophet's Sunna.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r6.anchor: وجب على الناس كافة مبايعته على السمع والطاعة، وإقامة كتاب الله وسنة رسوله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r7.claim: An abstainer with an excuse is excused, while an unexcused person may be compelled so the Muslims do not divide.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r7.anchor: ومن تأبى عن البيعة لعذر عذر، ومن تأبى لغير عذر جبر وقهر لئلا تفترق كلمة المسلمين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r8.claim: If two caliphs receive pledges, the first remains caliph and the second is to be killed; the author says literal killing is clearer, though some understand it as removal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#10/r8.anchor: وإذا بويع لخليفتين فالخليفة الأول وقتل الآخر واختلف في قتله هل هو محسوس أو معنى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r1.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r1.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri reports the Prophet's instruction to kill the later of two pledged caliphs; Muslim transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r1.anchor: إذا بويع لخليفتين فاقتلوا الآخر منهما " رواه أبو سعيد الخدري

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r2.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r2.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allah b. ʿAmr says one who pledges hand and heart must obey if able, but a rival claimant is to be struck down; Muslim transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r2.anchor: ومن بايع إماما فأعطاه صفقة يده وثمرة قلبه فليطعه إن استطاع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r3.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r3.claim: A report from ʿArfaja says to strike a rival claimant with the sword, whoever he may be.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r4.claim: Having two imams causes hypocrisy, opposition, schism, and loss of blessings; distant regions such as al-Andalus and Khurasan may be an exception discussed later.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r4.anchor: وهذا أدل دليل على منع إقامة إمامين ولأن ذلك يؤدي إلى النفاق والمخالفة والشقاق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r5.claim: A revolt against an imam known for justice must be fought; if the imam is sinful and the rebel appears just, people should wait to assess him or agree collectively to remove the first imam, since rebels may revert after gaining power.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r5.anchor: لو خرج خارجي على إمام معروف العدالة وجب على الناس جهاده فإن كان الإمام فاسقا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r6.claim: Installing two or three imams at one time and in one city is unanimously forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r6.anchor: فأما إقامة إمامين أو ثلاثة في عصر واحد وبلد واحد فلا يجوز إجماعا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r7.speaker: أبو المعالي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r7.claim: Abu al-Maʿali says his colleagues bar two imams at opposite ends of the world; he personally finds a pair in one contiguous region forbidden by consensus while distant realms remain an open possibility.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r7.anchor: قال الإمام أبو المعالي: ذهب أصحابنا إلى منع عقد الإمامة لشخصين في طرفي العالم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r8.speaker: الأستاذ أبو إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r8.claim: Abu Ishaq permits two imams in extremely distant regions so people's rights and legal judgments are not left unattended.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r8.anchor: وكان الأستاذ أبو إسحاق يجوز ذلك في إقليمين متباعدين غاية التباعد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r9.speaker: الكرامية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r9.claim: The Karramiyya permit two imams without qualification, arguing that each governs his own region and that two prophets could coexist; they take Ali and Muʿawiya to be two imams.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r9.anchor: وذهبت الكرامية إلى جواز نصب إمامين من غير تفصيل ويلزمهم إجازة ذلك في بلد واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r10.speaker: الكرامية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r10.claim: The Karramiyya argue that a pair of rulers each manages his own region and that two prophets coexisting would not invalidate prophethood, so two imams need not invalidate imamate.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r10.anchor: وإذا كان اثنين في بلدين أو ناحيتين كان كل واحد منهما أقوم بما في يديه وأضبط لما يليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r11.claim: The author's reply is that reason might allow two imams, but revealed law forbids it; the proof is introduced at the end of this segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#11/r11.anchor: والجواب أن ذلك جائز لولا منع الشرع منه لقوله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r1.claim: The command to kill the later of two pledged caliphs and the community's consensus forbid dual imamate; Muʿawiya claimed only delegated rule over Syria, and no one in their era claimed that both were imams.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r2.claim: Even if reason does not rule out two imams and no other text forbids them, consensus is decisive evidence that they are prohibited.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r2.anchor: أقوى السمع الإجماع، وقد وجد على المنع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r3.claim: The angels' question does not imply independent knowledge of the unseen: hearing khalifa, they inferred that some descendants might corrupt because a successor should reform; God clarified that some would not, then taught Adam the names and disclosed His hidden knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r3.anchor: لما سمعوا لفظ خليفة فهموا أن في بني آدم من يفسد إذ الخليفة المقصود منه الإصلاح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r4.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r4.claim: Thaʿlab says the angels had seen jinn corrupt and shed blood on earth before Adam; God sent Satan with an angelic host to kill them and drive them to seas and mountains, so they asked whether the human successor would be like the jinn.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd and others say God informed the angels that Adam's descendants would corrupt and shed blood, so they expressed astonishment at appointing one who would disobey despite God's favor, or at the disobedience itself, or magnified both matters.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وغيره: إن الله تعالى أعلمهم أن الخليفة سيكون من ذريته قوم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r6.claim: Qatada says God had told the angels that creatures on earth would corrupt and shed blood; they asked whether this khalifa was the one foretold or another. Al-Qurtubi calls this a good view and also praises inference from the wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: كان الله أعلمهم أنه إذا جعل في الأرض خلقا أفسدوا وسفكوا الدماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r7.claim: The wording may be expanded elliptically: God announced a khalifa who would do these acts, and the angels asked whether this was the foretold one; both explanations are persuasive, and the first draws scholarly inference from the wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#12/r7.anchor: والقول الأول أيضا حسن جدا لأن فيه استخراج العلم واستنباطه من مقتضى الألفاظ

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r1.claim: A report established in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere has God ask the angels how they left His servants; this is interpreted as rebuke for their question about corruption and disclosure of what God already knew.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r1.anchor: على ما ثبت في صحيح مسلم وغيره إنما هو على جهة التوبيخ لمن قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r2.claim: The relative pronoun man is the first object of jaʿala and fiha stands in for the second; yufsidu agrees with man in form, though a non-Qur'anic plural yufsidoon may agree by meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r2.anchor: في موضع نصب على المفعول بتجعل والمفعول الثاني يقوم مقامه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r3.claim: The Qur'anic phrasing uses singular agreement by form, while Arabic also allows plural agreement by meaning, as illustrated by clauses about listeners.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r3.anchor: ويجوز في غير القرآن يفسدون على المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r4.claim: Yasfiku coordinates with yufsidu and can follow either agreement pattern.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r5.speaker: أسيد عن الأعرج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r5.claim: Asid transmits al-Aʿraj's reading yasfaka with accusative, treating it as a response to the question with waw; a line of poetry illustrates the construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r5.anchor: وروى أسيد عن الأعرج أنه قرأ «ويسفك الدماء» بالنصب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r6.claim: Safk means pouring or spilling; Ibn Faris and al-Jawhari say it can describe pouring tears as well as blood, while safak means a slanderer or one capable of speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r6.anchor: والسفك: الصب. سفكت الدم أسفكه سفكا: صببته، وكذلك الدمع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r7.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r7.claim: Al-Mahdawi says safk is used only for blood, though it may also mean scattering speech, as in the expression safaka al-kalam.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r7.anchor: قال المهدوي: ولا يستعمل السفك إلا في الدم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r8.claim: The singular dam has a deleted final letter, said to be ya; its original form appears in the poetic dual al-damiyan, showing that the noun was not originally only two letters.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#13/r8.anchor: وواحد الدماء دم، محذوف اللام. وقيل: أصله دمي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r1.claim: The angels' tasbih means declaring God exalted above what does not suit His attributes; in Arabic it is magnifying Him by declaring Him free of evil, as al-Aʿsha's line uses subhan for disavowal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r1.anchor: والتسبيح في كلامهم التنزيه من السوء على وجه التعظيم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r2.speaker: طلحة بن عبيد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r2.claim: Talha b. ʿUbayd Allah asked the Prophet what subhan Allah means; the Prophet explained it as declaring God free of every evil.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r2.anchor: وروى طلحة بن عبيد الله قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r3.claim: Tasbih derives from sabh, movement or going; one who glorifies God proceeds in declaring Him free of evil, linked to the long daytime sabh in 73:7.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r3.anchor: وهو مشتق من السبح وهو الجري والذهاب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r4.claim: The construction nahnu was discussed earlier; its nuns cannot be assimilated because that would bring two vowelless consonants together.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز إدغام النون لئلا يلتقي ساكنان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
