QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas interpret the angels' tasbih as prayer, citing the description of Jonah as one of the tasbih-makers in 37:143.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r5.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود وابن عباس: تسبيحهم صلاتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r6.speaker: المفضل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r6.claim: Al-Mufaddal says the angels' tasbih is raising the voice in remembrance, supported by Jarir's line about pilgrims glorifying and proclaiming God's greatness.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r7.claim: Qatada takes tasbih in its ordinary linguistic sense, saying subhan Allah; al-Qurtubi calls this correct and cites the Prophet's report that subhan Allah wa bi-hamdih is among God's chosen words.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة: تسبيحهم: سبحان الله على عرفه في اللغة، وهو الصحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r8.speaker: أبو ذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r8.claim: Abu Dharr reports that the Prophet was asked which speech is best and replied that it is what God chose for His angels or servants: subhan Allah wa bi-hamdih; Muslim transmits it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r8.anchor: ما اصطفى الله لملائكته أو لعباده سبحان الله وبحمده

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r9.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن قرط
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r9.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman b. Qurt reports that on the night of the Night Journey the Prophet heard glorification in the highest heavens: subhan al-ʿAli al-Aʿla; al-Bayhaqi reports it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r9.anchor: وعن عبد الرحمن بن قرط: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة أسري به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r10.claim: Bi-hamdika may mean that the angels join praise to tasbih; al-hamd means praise.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r10.anchor: أي وبحمدك نخلط التسبيح بالحمد ونصله به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r11.claim: Alternatively, bi-hamdika is a parenthetical acknowledgment: the angels say they glorify and sanctify, while affirming that God is praised for guiding them to this worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r11.anchor: اعتراضا بين الكلامين كأنهم قالوا: ونحن نسبح ونقدس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r12.claim: Mujahid, Abu Salih, and others say taqdis means magnifying God and purifying His mention of what heretics attribute to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r12.anchor: ونطهر ذكرك عما لا يليق بك مما نسبك إليه الملحدون قاله مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r13.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak and others interpret taqdis as purifying themselves for God in pursuit of His pleasure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r13.anchor: وقال الضحاك وغيره: المعنى نطهر أنفسنا لك ابتغاء مرضاتك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r14.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r14.claim: A group including Qatada says taqdis means prayer. Ibn ʿAtiyya calls this weak, but al-Qurtubi says it is sound because prayer includes magnification, sanctification, and tasbih.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#14/r14.anchor: وقال قوم منهم قتادة: { ونقدس لك } معناه نصلي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r1.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r1.claim: ʿAisha reports that the Prophet said in bowing and prostration, subbuh quddus, Lord of the angels and the Spirit; Muslim transmits it.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r2.claim: Across its forms, quds means purification: the Holy Land is purified, al-Malik al-Quddus is the Pure, and the sacred valley is purified; Bayt al-Maqdis names a place of purification from sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r2.anchor: وبناء «قدس» كيفما تصرف فإن معناه التطهير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r3.claim: The term qudus is associated with purity; the term for a bucket used in ablution and qādus derive from the same idea of washing and purification.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r3.anchor: وبيت المقدس سمي به لأنه المكان الذي يتقدس فيه من الذنوب أي يتطهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r4.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r4.claim: The Prophet said a community is not purified if the weak person's right is not taken from the strong; Ibn Majah transmits it, meaning may God not purify it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r4.anchor: لا قدست أمة لا يؤخذ لضعيفها من قويها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r5.claim: The poet's phrase thawb al-muqaddas means a purified garment; prayer purifies a servant from sins and is entered in the worshipper's best state because it is the best deed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r5.anchor: أي المطهر. فالصلاة طهرة للعبد من الذنوب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r6.claim: Aʿlam may be a future verb or an adjective meaning knowing, as in Allahu akbar meaning great; in the first reading ma is its accusative object, in the second it is genitive by annexation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r6.anchor: فيه تأويلان قيل: إنه فعل مستقبل. وقيل: إنه اسم بمعنى فاعل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says aʿlam cannot take nunation here by grammarians' agreement; Sibawayh and al-Khalil do not nunate an indefinite proper name on the afʿal pattern, while al-Akhfash does.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ولا يصح فيه الصرف بإجماع من النحاة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r8.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r8.claim: Al-Mahdawi allows an assumed tanwin on aʿlam if it means ʿalim, with ma then accusative, analogous to the construction hajjaj bayt Allah.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r8.anchor: قال المهدوي: يجوز أن تقدر التنوين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r9.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r9.claim: Al-Jawhari explains that hajjaj bayt Allah is genitive by annexation for women who made pilgrimage, but accusative if no pilgrimage occurred and tanwin is intended.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r9.anchor: قال الجوهري: ونسوة حواج بيت الله، بالإضافة إذا كن قد حججن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Iblis grew arrogant after being honored as heaven's treasurer, assumed his rank made him superior, and scorned Adam's disobedience; the angels did not know Iblis's contrary inner state.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r10.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: كان إبليس لعنه الله قد أعجب ودخله الكبر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r11.claim: Qatada says God's hidden knowledge was that among those to be created on earth would be prophets, virtuous people, and the obedient.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة لما قالت الملائكة: { أتجعل فيها } وقد علم الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r12.claim: The phrase may encompass everything that was, is, and will be.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:30#15/r12.anchor: قلت: ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون مما كان ومما يكون

QASHANI:2:30/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30/r1.claim: The time reference points to eternity; God's saying casts His will to create Adam into sacred angelic and spiritual beings.
QASHANI:2:30/r1.anchor: إذ: إشارة إلى السرمد الذي هو من الأزل إلى الأبد

QASHANI:2:30/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30/r2.claim: Every created event first has a form in the spirit world of prior decree, then the heart-world of the Preserved Tablet, then the soul-world, Tablet of Effacement and Affirmation or lowest heaven.
QASHANI:2:30/r2.anchor: كل ما يحدث في عالم الكون له صورة قبل التكوين في عالم الروح

QASHANI:2:30/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30/r3.claim: Human speech and action similarly exist first in spirit and deeper unseen levels, then the self's lower unseen level, before appearing on the limbs.
QASHANI:2:30/r3.anchor: فإن كل ما يظهر على جوارحك التي هي عالم كونك وشهادتك

QASHANI:2:30/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30/r4.claim: Making is broader than origination or formation, so God says 'making' rather than 'creating'; the human combines the two worlds.
QASHANI:2:30/r4.anchor: والجعل أعم من الإبداع والتكوين، فلم يقل (خالق) لأن الإنسان

QASHANI:2:30/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30/r5.claim: The human vicegerent takes on God's traits, executes His command, governs creation, orders its affairs, and calls people to obedience.

QASHANI:2:30#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30#2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30#2/r1.claim: The angels' objection and claim to precedence reflect their inability to see divine attributes manifest uniquely in the human composite encompassing both worlds.
QASHANI:2:30#2/r1.anchor: هو احتجابهم عن ظهور معنى الإلهية والأوصاف الربانية فيه

QASHANI:2:30#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30#2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30#2/r2.claim: Corruption and bloodshed signify beastly lust and predatory anger, powers necessary when spirit is joined to body; angels know their own purity and these lower acts.
QASHANI:2:30#2/r2.anchor: الأفعال البهيمية التي هي الإفساد في الأرض، والسبعية

QASHANI:2:30#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30#2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30#2/r3.claim: Each angelic rank knows what is below and within itself but not above; they see the soul as evil-bearing intermediary between luminous spirit and dark body.
QASHANI:2:30#2/r3.anchor: كل طبقة من الملائكة المقدسة تطلع على ما تحتها وما في أنفسها

QASHANI:2:30#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30#2/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30#2/r4.claim: The angels do not know that human comprehensiveness attracts divine light, the secret of God's statement that He knows what they do not.
QASHANI:2:30#2/r4.anchor: ولا تعلم أن الجمعية الإنسانية جالبة للنور الإلهي

QASHANI:2:30#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30#2/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30#2/r5.claim: Glorification denies partner, incapacity, and defect; sanctification also denies attachment, passivity, contingency, multiplicity, and potentiality, so every sanctified being glorifies but not vice versa.
QASHANI:2:30#2/r5.anchor: والفرق بين التسبيح والتقديس، أن التسبيح: هو التنزيه

QASHANI:2:30#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:30#2/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:30#2/r6.claim: The nearest angels, pure spirits, are sanctifiers because they are un-veiled, overcome lower realms with light, act on others, and possess all perfections actually; other angels glorify.
QASHANI:2:30#2/r6.anchor: الملائكة المقربون الذين هم الأرواح المجردة بتجردهم وعدم احتجابهم عن نور ربهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r1.claim: The verse recounts Adam's creation and God's honoring of him, a general favor to all humanity and the third general blessing in this passage.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية دالة على كيفية خلقة آدم عليه السلام وعلى كيفية تعظيم الله تعالى إياه

RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r2.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r2.claim: One view treats إذ as an extra particle customary in Arabic; Razi rejects it because the Qur'an contains nothing without meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r2.anchor: المسألة الأولى : في إذ قولان : أحدهما : أنه صلة زائدة إلا أن العرب يعتادون التكلم بها

RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r3.claim: Razi's preferred analysis makes إذ accusative through an implied اذكر: remember that your Lord said this to the angels; the omission is clear from context.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r3.anchor: وهو الحق أنه ليس في القرآن ما لا معنى له وهو نصب بإضمار اذكر

RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r4.claim: Other passages state اذكر explicitly, and the Qur'an functions as one discourse, so their explicit wording can suffice here; they may have preceded this sura.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r4.anchor: كقوله : { واذكر أخا عاد إذ أنذر قومه بالأحقاف } ( الأحقاف : 21 )

RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r5.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r5.claim: Al-Kashshaf also allows إذ to be governed by قالوا.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r5.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ويجوز أن ينتصب ( إذ ) بقالوا

RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r6.claim: The word ملك derives from a root meaning message: ألكني إليه means send me to him, and المألكة or الألوكة means a message.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r6.anchor: الملك أصله من الرسالة ، يقال ألكني إليه أي أرسلني إليه والمألكة والألوكة الرسالة

RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r7.claim: The original form ملأكة lost its hamza, whose vowel shifted to the preceding letter for ease because the word was frequent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r7.anchor: وأصله الهمزة من ( ملأكة ) حذفت الهمزة وألقيت حركتها على ما قبلها طلبا للخفة

RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r8.claim: Al-Kashshaf derives الملائك as the plural of the original ملأك, like شمائل from شمأل, with feminine plural تاء.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146#2/r8.anchor: الملائك جمع ملأك على الأصل كالشمائل في جمع شمأل وإلحاق التاء لتأنيث الجمع

RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r1.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r1.claim: Those who put angels before prophets cite 2:285's order of belief and the Prophet's instruction to begin with what God began with.
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r1.anchor: قدم ذكر الإيمان بالملائكة على ذكر الإيمان بالرسل في قوله : { والمؤمنون كل ءامن بالله وملئكته وكتبه ورسله }

RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r2.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r2.claim: They also argue angels precede prophets because angels mediate revelation and the law to the messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r2.anchor: الملك واسطة بين الله وبين الرسول في تبليغ الوحي والشريعة فكان مقدما على الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r3.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r3.claim: Others put prophethood first because reason alone cannot establish angels; revelation, grounded in knowledge of prophethood, is the route to affirming them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r3.anchor: لا طريق لنا إلى معرفة وجود الملائكة بالعقل بل بالسمع ، فكان الكلام في النبوات أصلا

RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r4.claim: Razi reconciles the sequence: angels precede prophets in rank and nobility, but follow them in our reasoning because we establish angels through inquiry.
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r4.anchor: الملك قبل النبي بالشرف والعلية وبعده في عقولنا وأذهاننا بحسب وصولنا إليها بأفكارنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r5.claim: Rationalists agree that angels ennoble the upper world, just as humans ennoble the lower world.
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r5.anchor: لا خلاف بين العقلاء في أن شرف الرتبة للعالم العلوي هو وجود الملائكة فيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r6.speaker: أكثر المسلمين
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r6.claim: Most Muslims hold that angels are subtle airy bodies, able to take different forms, and dwelling in the heavens.
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r6.anchor: مسكنها السموات ، وهذا قول أكثر المسلمين

RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r7.speaker: طوائف من عبدة الأوثان
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r7.claim: Some idol worshippers identify angels with the actual planetary natures they deem auspicious or inauspicious: auspicious planets are mercy angels and inauspicious ones punishment angels.
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r7.anchor: قول طوائف من عبدة الأوثان وهو أن الملائكة هي الحقيقة في هذه الكواكب الموصوفة بالإسعاد والأنحاس

RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r8.speaker: معظم المجوس والثنوية
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r8.claim: Most Magians and dualists posit two eternal, transparent, choosing substances, Light and Darkness, opposite in nature and action; Light is good and beneficial, Darkness its contrary.
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r8.anchor: قول معظم المجوس والثنوية وهو أن هذا العالم مركب من أصلين أزليين وهما النور والظلمة

RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r9.speaker: معظم المجوس والثنوية
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r9.claim: In their account, Light continually generates angels as friends without sexual reproduction, like wisdom from a wise person; Darkness similarly generates devils as enemies.
RAZI-FULL:v2p147/r9.anchor: جوهر النور لم يزل يولد الأولياء وهم الملائكة لا على سبيل التناكح بل على سبيل تولد الحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r1.speaker: طوائف من النصارى
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r1.claim: Some Christians identify angels with disembodied rational souls: purified, good souls are angels, while evil, clouded souls are devils.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r1.anchor: قول طوائف من النصارى وهو أن الملائكة في الحقيقة هي الأنفس الناطقة

RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r2.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r2.claim: Philosophers describe angels as self-subsisting, nonspatial substances distinct from human souls and greater in power and knowledge, as the Sun is to its light.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r2.anchor: قول الفلاسفة : وهي أنها جواهر قائمة بأنفسها وليست بمتحيزة البتة

RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r3.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r3.claim: They divide angels into celestial governors, related to spheres as human souls to bodies, and proximate angels absorbed in knowing, loving, and obeying God; some add good or evil angels governing the lower world.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r3.anchor: منها ما هي بالنسبة إلى أجرام الأفلاك والكواكب

RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r4.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r4.claim: Philosophers agree on celestial governors and angels devoted to God, while some also posit terrestrial angels governing the lower world, good as angels and evil as devils.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r4.anchor: ومنهم من أثبت أنواعا أخر من الملائكة وهي الملائكة الأرضية المدبرة لأحوال هذا العالم السفلي

RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r5.speaker: الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r5.claim: Philosophers affirm rational proofs of angels' existence; Razi says he has deep, subtle discussions of their arguments, while other people offer merely persuasive proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r5.anchor: أما الفلاسفة فقد اتفقوا على أن في العقل دلائل تدل على وجود الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r6.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r6.claim: One proof divides living beings into mortal rational humans, mortal nonrational beasts, and rational immortal angels; if wisdom creates the lower and middle ranks, it should create the highest too.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r6.anchor: القسمة العقلية تقتضي وجود أقسام ثلاثة فإن الحي إما أن يكون ناطقا وميتا معا

RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r7.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r7.claim: Another proof says the celestial world is nobler and life, intellect, and speech nobler than their opposites, so it is implausible that these exist only in the dark lower world.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r7.anchor: الفطرة تشهد بأن عالم السموات أشرف من هذا العالم السفلي وتشهد بأن الحياة والعقل والنطق أشرف

RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r8.speaker: أصحاب المجاهدات وأصحاب الحاجات والضرورات
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r8.claim: A third proof invokes mystics' witnessing and unveiling, remarkable guidance for rare treatments and antidotes, and true dreams; it persuades hearers and is certain to those who experience it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r8.anchor: أصحاب المجاهدات أثبتوها من جهة المشاهدة والمكاشفة ، وأصحاب الحاجات والضرورات أثبتوها

RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r9.speaker: الأنبياء عليهم السلام
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r9.claim: Razi says all prophets agree on the existence of angels, a matter of consensus among them, established by transmitted reports.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148/r9.anchor: فلا نزاع البتة بين الأنبياء عليهم السلام في إثبات الملائكة ، بل ذلك كالأمر المجمع عليه

RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r1.speaker: عليه الصلاة والسلام
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r1.claim: A Prophetic report says the heavens groan, rightly so, for every space the size of a foot contains an angel prostrating or bowing; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r1.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط ما فيها موضع قدم إلا وفيه ملك

RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r2.claim: A report gives successive tenfold ratios from humans and jinn through land, bird, and sea animals to earthly angels and the angels of each heaven, up to the angels of the Throne's pavilion; even all those angels are a drop beside those circling the Throne.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r2.anchor: وروي أن بني آدم عشر الجن ، والجن وبنو آدم عشر حيوانات البر ، وهؤلاء كلهم عشر الطيور

RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r3.claim: The report describes 600,000 Throne pavilions, angels in every footspace worshipping, and numberless ranks whose species, lifespans, and worship only God knows.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r3.anchor: من سرادقات / العرش التي عددها ستمائة ألف ، طول كل سرادق وعرضه وسمكه

RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r4.claim: In a report Razi saw in an admonition book, the Prophet at the Ascension met angels moving like a marketplace; Gabriel did not know their destinations and had never seen the same angel twice.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r4.anchor: رأيت في بعض كتب التذكير أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام حين عرج به رأى ملائكة في موضع بمنزلة سوق

RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r5.speaker: ملك
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r5.claim: In that report, an angel could not say how long he had existed, only that God had created a star every 400,000 years and that many such stars had appeared since his creation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p148#2/r5.anchor: وقيل له مذ كم خلقت ؟ فقال لا أدري غير أن الله تعالى يخلق كوكبا في كل أربعمائة ألف سنة

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r1.claim: Razi classifies angels as bearers of the Throne, those surrounding it, and senior angels including Gabriel and Michael.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r1.anchor: فأحدها : حملة العرش وهو قوله : { ويحمل عرش ربك فوقهم يومئذ ثمانية }

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r2.claim: Gabriel conveys revelation to prophets, as in the description of the Trustworthy Spirit bringing revelation to Muhammad's heart.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r2.anchor: أنه صاحب الوحي إلى الأنبياء قال تعالى : { نزل به الروح الامين * على قلبك }

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r3.claim: Gabriel is named before other angels; because he brings knowledge and Michael provides sustenance, spiritual nourishment makes Gabriel superior.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r3.anchor: ذكره قبل سائر الملائكة في القرآن { قل من كان عدوا لجبريل }

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r4.claim: Gabriel is named alongside God as the believers' protector, and is called the Spirit of Holiness in the address concerning Jesus.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r4.anchor: جعله ثاني نفسه { فإن الله هو مولاه وجبريل وصالح المؤمنين }

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r5.claim: Gabriel supports God's allies and defeats enemies with a thousand marked angels.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r5.anchor: ينصر أولياء الله ويقهر أعداءه مع ألف من الملائكة مسومين

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r6.claim: The Qur'an praises Gabriel as a noble messenger, powerful, well-positioned near the Throne, obeyed, and trustworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r6.anchor: أنه تعالى مدحه بصفات ست في قوله : { إنه لقول رسول كريم * ذى قوة عند ذى العرش مكين

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r7.claim: Gabriel's mission and honor lie in mediating between God and all prophets, who are thus his community and the noblest of God's servants.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r7.anchor: فجميع الأنبياء والرسل أمته وكرمه على ربه أنه جعله واسطة بينه وبين أشرف عباده وهم الأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r8.claim: Gabriel's strength is shown by lifting the cities of Lot's people to heaven and overturning them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r8.anchor: وقوته أنه رفع مدائن قوم لوط إلى السماء وقلبها

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r9.claim: Gabriel is obeyed as the angels' leader and exemplar; his trustworthiness is also affirmed by the verse about the Trustworthy Spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r9.anchor: وكونه مطاعا أنه إمام الملائكة ومقتداهم ، وأما كونه أمينا فهو قوله : { نزل به الروح الأمين

RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r10.claim: Razi says reports establish Israfil and Azrael; Azrael is the Angel of Death, while the plural messengers who take souls may be a group led by him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p149/r10.anchor: ومن جملة أكابر الملائكة إسرافيل وعزرائيل صلوات الله عليهما وقد ثبت وجودهما بالأخبار

RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r1.claim: The Qur'an's plural messengers taking souls can mean subordinate angels assigned to death under the Angel of Death.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r1.anchor: ذلك يدل على وجود ملائكة موكلين بقبض الأرواح ويجوز أن يكون ملك الموت رئيس جماعة

RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r2.claim: Reports identify Israfil as the angel who blows the Trumpet, associated with the Qur'anic account of the blasts and resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r2.anchor: فقد دلت الأخبار على أنه صاحب الصور على ما قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r3.claim: Razi lists angels of Paradise, angels of Hell led by Malik and collectively called the zabaniyah, guardian angels, and recorders of deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r3.anchor: رابعها : ملائكة الجنة قال تعالى : { والملائكة يدخلون عليهم من كل باب

RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r4.claim: Other angels manage the affairs of the world; Razi connects them with the angels ranged in ranks, those scattering, and those apportioning commands.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r4.anchor: الموكلون بأحوال هذا العالم وهم المرادون

RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says angels besides the guardians record leaves falling from trees; in a desert, a person who feels movement should call on God's servants for help.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس قال : إن لله ملائكة سوى الحفظة يكتبون ما يسقط من ورق الأشجار

RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r6.claim: Angels are God's messengers, as stated in 35:1; the verse saying God chooses messengers from angels does not mean only some angels are messengers, since من is explanatory.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r6.anchor: أن الملائكة رسل الله ، قال تعالى : { جاعل الملائكة رسلا }

RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r7.claim: Razi reads من in 22:75 as explanatory rather than partitive, answering the objection that only some angels are messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r7.anchor: وجوابه أن من للتبيين لا للتبعيض

RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r8.claim: Angels' nearness to God cannot mean nearness in place or direction; it means nearness in rank and honor.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150/r8.anchor: وثانيها : قربهم من الله تعالى ، وذلك يمتنع أن يكون بالمكان والجهة فلم يبق إلا أن يكون

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r1.claim: Angels are honored, do not disdain worship, and glorify God day and night without tiring.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r1.anchor: ومن عنده لا يستكبرون عن عبادته

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r2.claim: Their words, supported elsewhere, show constant worship that God does not deny.

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r3.claim: They hasten to obey God out of reverence, as in their unanimous prostration.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r3.anchor: الثاني : مبادرتهم إلى امتثال أمر الله تعظيما له وهو قوله : { فسجد الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r4.claim: They do nothing except by God's revelation and command.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r4.anchor: أنهم لا يفعلون شيئا إلا بوحيه وأمره وهو قوله : / { لا يسبقونه بالقول

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r5.claim: Eight bearers carry the Throne and Kursi; the smaller Kursi exceeds all seven heavens, displaying their strength.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r5.anchor: حملة العرش وهم ثمانية يحملون العرش والكرسي ثم إن الكرسي الذي هو أصغر من العرش أعظم من جملة السموات السبع

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r6.claim: The Throne's height is beyond conception and its ascent takes fifty thousand years, yet angels descend in an instant.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r6.anchor: أن علو العرش شيء لا يحيط به الوهم ويدل عليه قوله

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r7.claim: A single trumpet blast makes those in heaven and earth swoon, and the next revives them, showing immense power.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r7.anchor: فصاحب الصور يبلغ في القوة إلى حيث أن بنفخة واحدة منه يصعق من في السموات والأرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r8.claim: Gabriel's strength let him uproot the mountains and settlements of Lot's people at once.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r8.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام بلغ في قوته إلى أن قلع جبال آل لوط وبلادهم دفعة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r9.claim: Despite abundant worship and never slipping, angels remain fearful and apprehensive of God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r9.anchor: مع كثرة عباداتهم وعدم إقدامهم على الزلات البتة يكونون خائفين وجلين

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r10.speaker: التفسير
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r10.claim: A tafsir report says the heavens hear revelation like a chain striking stone, become frightened, then ask what God said and answer that He said the truth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r10.anchor: روي في التفسير أن الله تعالى إذا تكلم بالوحي سمعه أهل السموات مثل صوت السلسلة على الصفوان

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet chose servant prophethood after Gabriel signaled humility when an angel offered kingship or servanthood.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بناحية ومعه جبريل إذ انشق أفق السماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r12.claim: Al-Bayhaqi's report from Ibn Abbas describes Israfil standing with lowered gaze and consulting the Preserved Tablet when commanded.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r12.anchor: روى البيهقي في ( شعب الإيمان ) عن ابن عباس قال بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بناحية

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r13.claim: The report assigns Gabriel winds and armies, Michael vegetation, and the Angel of Death the taking of souls; Gabriel says he feared the Hour.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r13.anchor: على أي شيء أنت قال على الرياح والجنود قلت على أي شيء ميكائيل قال على النبات

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r14.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r14.claim: Ali describes angels in varied worship postures, glorifying tirelessly without sleep, lapse, bodily fatigue, or forgetfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r14.anchor: قال في بعض خطبه : ثم فتق ما بين السموات العلى فملأهن

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r15.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r15.claim: Ali says angels serve as trustees of revelation and messengers, execute God's decrees, guard people, and keep Paradise's gates.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r15.anchor: ومنهم أمناء على وحيه وألسنة إلى رسله ومختلفون بقضائه وأمره ومنهم الحفظة لعباده

RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r16.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r16.claim: Ali says angels neither imagine God bodily nor assign Him creaturely qualities, places, or likenesses.
RAZI-FULL:v2p150#2/r16.anchor: لا يتوهمون ربهم بالتصوير ولا يجرون عليه صفات المصنوعين ولا يحدونه بالأماكن ولا يشيرون إليه بالنظائر

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that God addressed angels who fought with Iblis, after their forces expelled corrupting jinn from earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r1.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس أنه سبحانه وتعالى إنما قال هذا القول للملائكة الذين كانوا محاربين مع إبليس

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r2.speaker: الأكثرون من الصحابة والتابعين
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r2.claim: Most Companions and Successors say God addressed all angels: the unqualified term denotes them all, and restriction is contrary to the default.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r2.anchor: وقال الأكثرون من الصحابة والتابعين أنه تعالى قال ذلك لجماعة الملائكة من غير تخصيص

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r3.claim: جاعل derives from جعل, which takes two objects; في الأرض and خليفة are the two objects, meaning to make a successor on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r3.anchor: جاعل من جعل الذي له مفعولان دخل على المبتدأ والخبر

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r4.claim: The earth most naturally means all the earth from east to west.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r4.anchor: الظاهر أن الأرض التي في الآية جميع الأرض من المشرق إلى المغرب

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r5.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet says earth was spread from Mecca, where angels first circled the House; that place is the earth in the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r5.anchor: وروى عبد الرحمن بن سابط عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : دحيت الأرض من مكة

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r6.claim: Razi judges the whole-earth interpretation closer to the apparent wording than the Mecca report.

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r7.claim: A khalifa succeeds another and takes that one's place; Razi illustrates this with verses about successors on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r7.anchor: الخليفة من يخلف غيره ويقوم مقامه قال الله تعالى : { ثم جعلناكم

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r8.claim: One view takes the successor to be Adam, with his descendants, rather than Adam himself, intended by the prediction of corruption.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r8.anchor: أحدهما : أنه آدم عليه السلام . وقوله : { أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها } المراد ذريته

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r9.claim: One explanation, reported from Ibn Abbas, is that Adam succeeded the jinn removed from earth before his arrival.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r9.anchor: الذين تقدموه . يروى ذلك عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والسدي
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r10.claim: Another view, attributed to Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, and al-Suddi, makes Adam God's deputy judging accountable creatures; 38:26 supports it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r10.anchor: إنما سماه الله خليفة لأنه يخلف الله في الحكم بين المكلفين من خلقه وهو المروي عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس والسدي

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r11.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says the successor is Adam's descendants, who follow one another, supported by the verse about successors on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r11.anchor: قول الحسن ويؤكده قوله : { وهو الذى جعلكم خلائف الارض }

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r12.claim: خليفة may be singular or plural and apply to male or female.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r12.anchor: والخليفة اسم يصلح للواحد والجمع كما يصلح للذكر والأنثى

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r13.claim: A variant reading has خليقة with qaf.

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r14.claim: God told the angels because He knew they would ask about the secret, and it benefited them to hear the answer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r14.anchor: علم أنهم إذا اطلعوا على ذلك السر أوردوا عليه ذلك السؤال فكانت المصلحة تقتضي إحاطتهم بذلك الجواب

RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152/r15.claim: The announcement also teaches people to consult one another.

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r1.speaker: الجمهور الأعظم من علماء الدين
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r1.claim: Most religious scholars hold that every angel is protected from every sin.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r1.anchor: الجمهور الأعظم من علماء الدين اتفقوا على عصمة كل الملائكة عن جميع الذنوب

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r2.speaker: الحشوية
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r2.claim: The Hashwiyya dissent from universal angelic immunity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r2.anchor: ومن الحشوية من خالف في ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r3.claim: Although 66:6 concerns Hell's keepers, 16:50 is general: angels do everything commanded, including avoiding prohibitions, since refraining is commanded too.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r3.anchor: إلا أن هذه الآية مختصة بملائكة النار فإذا أردنا الدلالة العامة تمسكنا بقوله تعالى : {

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r4.claim: The command statement is universal because each commanded act allows exception, which removes what otherwise falls within the statement.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r4.anchor: لا شيء من المأمورات إلا ويصح الاستثناء منه والاستثناء يخرج من الكلام ما لولاه لدخل

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r5.claim: Their status as honored servants who do not speak ahead of God and act by His command clears them of sin.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r5.anchor: بل عباد مكرمون * لا يسبقونه بالقول وهم بأمره يعملون

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r6.claim: Angels could not rightly criticize human sin if they themselves sinned.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r6.anchor: أنه تعالى حكى عنهم أنهم طعنوا في البشر بالمعصية ولو كانوا من العصاة لما حسن منهم ذلك الطعن

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r7.claim: Uninterrupted glorification day and night is incompatible with committing sin.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r7.anchor: أنه تعالى حكى عنهم أنهم يسبحون الليل والنهار لا يفترون ومن كان كذلك امتنع صدور المعصية منه

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r8.speaker: المخالف
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r8.claim: An opponent says the question is an objection to God and therefore a grave sin.

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r9.speaker: المخالف
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r9.claim: An opponent says accusing humans of corruption and killing is backbiting, a major sin.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r9.anchor: أنهم طعنوا في بني آدم بالفساد والقتل وذلك غيبة والغيبة من كبائر الذنوب

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r10.speaker: المخالف
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r10.claim: An opponent says the angels' self-praise and claim of exclusive glorification resemble conceit and backbiting.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r10.anchor: وثالثها : أنهم بعد أن طعنوا في بني آدم مدحوا أنفسهم بقولهم : { ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك }

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r11.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r11.claim: The Prophet lists self-admiration among three ruinous traits, used against angelic self-praise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r11.anchor: قال عليه السلام . ( ثلاث مهلكات ، وذكر فيها إعجاب المرء بنفسه

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r12.speaker: المخالف
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r12.claim: The opponent also cites the prohibition on declaring oneself pure in 53:32.

RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r13.speaker: المخالف
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r13.claim: An opponent says the angels' confession that they know only what God taught resembles an apology and implies a prior offense.
RAZI-FULL:v2p152#2/r13.anchor: أن قولهم لا علم لنا إلا ما علمتنا يشبه الاعتذار فلولا تقدم الذنب

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r1.speaker: المخالفون
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r1.claim: One Harut and Marut version says a woman demanded idol worship; lust overcame them after they refused, and she rose to their heavenly place as Venus, which they linked to mocking Adam's descendants.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r1.anchor: قالا وما هي ؟ قالت : تسجدان لهم الصنم ، فقالا : لا نشرك بالله

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r2.speaker: المخالفون
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r2.claim: Another version says an earthly woman became Venus after the angels drank wine, committed adultery and murder, worshipped an idol, and learned the Great Name enabling ascent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r2.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى أن الزهرة كانت فاجرة من أهل الأرض وإنما واقعاها بعد أن شربا الخمر وقتلا النفس

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r3.speaker: المخالفون
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r3.claim: The tale says the angels chose immediate punishment, were hung upside down in a Babylonian well until Judgment, and teach sorcery there.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r3.anchor: اختارا عذاب الدنيا فجعلهما ببابل منكوسين في بئر إلى

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r4.speaker: المخالفون
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r4.claim: A third objection says Iblis was a close angel, then disobeyed and disbelieved, proving angels can sin.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r4.anchor: الشبهة الثالثة : أن إبليس كان من الملائكة المقربين

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r5.speaker: المخالفون
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r5.claim: A fourth objection infers angels are punished because 74:31 calls them keepers of Hell and 2:39 describes its eternal inhabitants.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r5.anchor: وما جعلنا أصحاب النار إلا ملئكة

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r6.claim: Razi says the angels did not mean to alert God to something overlooked, which would be unbelief, or to censure His act; he gives other readings.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r6.anchor: فنقول إنه ليس غرضهم من ذلك السؤال تنبيه الله على شيء كان غافلا عنه

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r7.claim: Their question may express amazement that God grants blessings to corrupt beings, magnifying His perfect knowledge and wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r7.anchor: كأنه يتعجب من كمال حكمته وعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r8.claim: The Mu'tazilite answer is that the angels sought to reconcile God's wisdom with enabling creatures He knows will corrupt and murder.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r8.anchor: وهذا جواب المعتزلة قالوا : وهذا يدل على أن الملائكة لم يجوزوا صدور القبيح

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r9.claim: The Mu'tazilite answer says God cannot do evil; its support is that the angels assign corruption to creatures, not the Creator.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r9.anchor: وهذا جواب المعتزلة قالوا : وهذا يدل على أن الملائكة لم يجوزوا صدور القبيح من الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r10.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r10.claim: Their gloss clears God's essence of bodily attributes and His acts of blame and foolishness.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r10.anchor: والثاني : أنهم قالوا : { ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك } لأن التسبيح تنزيه ذاته عن صفة الأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r11.speaker: الحكماء
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r11.claim: Philosophers say evil necessarily accompanies worldly good, but good outweighs evil; abandoning much good to avoid little evil would be worse.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r11.anchor: والحكمة تقتضي إيجاد ما هذا شأنه لا تركه وهذا جواب الحكماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r12.speaker: الحكماء
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r12.claim: On this account, good from the lower world's composition exceeds its evils, so wisdom requires creating it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r12.anchor: والحكمة تقتضي إيجاد ما هذا شأنه لا تركه وهذا جواب الحكماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r13.claim: Their question may express reverence: a devoted servant dislikes having servants who disobey the master.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r13.anchor: أن سؤالهم كان على وجه المبالغة في إعظام الله تعالى فإن العبد المخلص

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r14.claim: They may ask for earth, or part of it, for themselves if beneficial; God chose heaven for angels and earth for people, for their religious good.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r14.anchor: مسألة منهم / أن يجعل الأرض أو بعضها لهم إن كان ذلك صلاحا فكأنهم قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r15.claim: Another possibility is that they sought the wisdom for creating beings who would corrupt and kill.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r15.anchor: أنهم طلبوا الحكمة التي لأجلها خلقهم مع هذا الفساد والقتل

RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r16.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r16.claim: Al-Qaffal reads their words as a prediction that God will place a successor on earth, rather than a question.
RAZI-FULL:v2p154/r16.anchor: قال القفال يحتمل أن الله تعالى لما أخبرهم أنه يجعل فى الأرض خليفة

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r1.speaker: جرير
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r1.claim: Jarir's verse beginning فألستم خير من ركب المطايا shows an interrogative form can make an affirmative assertion.

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r2.claim: On al-Qaffal's reading, God knows humanity's hidden virtues and reasons for creating them, beyond their outward corruption.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r2.anchor: فأنتم علمتم ظاهرهم وهو الفساد والقتل وما علمتم باطنهم وأنا أعلم ظاهرهم وباطنهم

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r3.claim: The angels did not backbite: those posing the problem had to mention its difficulty, corruption and killing, not worship and monotheism.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r3.anchor: من أراد إيراد السؤال وجب أن يتعرض لمحل الإشكال

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r4.claim: Self-praise is not always forbidden, since 93:11 says to speak of God's blessing.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r4.anchor: مدح النفس غير ممنوع منه مطلقا لقولاه : { وأما بنعمة ربك فحدث }

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r5.claim: Alternatively, they affirmed God's divinity and wisdom to show they sought details rather than attacking Him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r5.anchor: ليس المراد مدح النفس ، بل المراد بيان أن هذا السؤال ما أوردناه

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r6.claim: Razi accepts that not asking was preferable; the angels apologize for leaving the preferable, not for sin.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r6.anchor: نحن نسلم أن الأولى للملائكة أن لا يوردوا ذلك السؤال ، فلما تركوا هذا الأولى كان ذلك الاعتذار اعتذارا من ترك الأولى

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r7.claim: Though 21:27 says angels do not speak ahead of God, general statements may be specified, so their question could be authorized.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r7.anchor: إذا كانوا مأذونين في هذا السؤال فكيف اعتذروا عنه ؟ قلنا العام قد يتطرق إليه التخصيص

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r8.claim: Scholars disagree whether angels inferred corruption by conjecture or knew it certainly.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r8.anchor: اختلف العلماء فيه ، فمنهم من قال : إنهم ذكروا ذلك ظنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Kalbi are cited for conjecture by analogy with the jinn who lived on earth before Adam.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r9.anchor: الأول : وهو مروي عن ابن عباس والكلبي أنهم قاسوه / على حال الجن

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r10.claim: Another conjecture was that the four humors produce appetite and anger, leading to corruption and bloodshed.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r10.anchor: عرفوا خلقته وعرفوا أنه مركب من هذه الأخلاط الأربعة فلا بد وأن تتركب فيه الشهوة والغضب

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r11.claim: Ibn Masud and a group of Companions are cited for the view that angels knew with certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r11.anchor: وهو مروي عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r12.claim: One certainty report says God told angels the successor's descendants would corrupt, envy, and kill.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r12.anchor: قالوا ربنا وما يكون ذلك الخليفة ؟ قال يكون له ذرية يفسدون في الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r13.claim: Another says God had told them a great earthly creation would corrupt and shed blood.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r13.anchor: أنه تعالى كان قد أعلم الملائكة أنه إذا كان في الأرض خلق عظيم أفسدوا فيها وسفكوا الدماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd says angels learned sin would arise when they asked whom Hell was for and were told it was for disobedient creatures.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r14.anchor: قال ابن زيد لما خلق الله تعالى النار خافت الملائكة خوفا شديدا

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r15.speaker: الملائكة
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r15.claim: They may have read the Preserved Tablet, where events through the Resurrection had been written.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r15.anchor: لما كتب القلم في اللوح ما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة فلعلهم طالعوا اللوح فعرفوا ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r16.claim: A khalifa as God's deputy judges people; because judges are needed for disputes, announcing a successor implied future conflict.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r16.anchor: معنى الخليفة من يكون نائبا لله تعالى في الحكم والقضاء

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r17.claim: Razi rejects conjecture as the basis: accusing others without assurance of truth conflicts with angelic infallibility.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r17.anchor: والقول بأنه كان هذا الأخبار عن مجرد الظن باطل لأنه قدح في الغير بما لا يأمن أن يكون كاذبا فيه

RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r18.claim: These additional stories are isolated reports and cannot outweigh the proofs already given.
RAZI-FULL:v2p155/r18.anchor: أما الوجه السادس : هو الأخبار التي ذكروها فهي من باب أخبار الآحاد فلا تعارض الدلائل

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r1.claim: Razi rejects the Harut and Marut tale: saying they would not sin if tested accuses God of lying or ignorance; even the Hashwiyya concede pre-descent immunity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r1.anchor: أنهم ذكروا في القصة أن الله تعالى قال لهما لو ابتليتكما بما ابتليت به بني آدم لعصيتماني

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r2.claim: Choosing worldly or later punishment is incoherent: repentance should have been offered, as it is even to lifelong polytheists and prophet-persecutors.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r2.anchor: كان الأولى أن يخيرا بين التوبة وبين العذاب والله تعالى خير بينهما من أشرك به طول عمره

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r3.claim: The tale contradicts itself by having punished angels teach and promote sorcery.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r3.anchor: في القصة أنهما يعلمان السحر حال كونهما معذبين ويدعوان إليه وهما معاقبان على المعصية

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r4.claim: The adulterous woman becoming a luminous star and being honored by God's oath is absurd; Razi points to 81:15–16 and defers sorcery to 2:102.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r4.anchor: المرأة الفاجرة كيف يعقل أنها لما فجرت صعدت إلى السماء وجعلها الله تعالى كوكبا مضيئا

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r5.claim: Razi says he will establish that Iblis was not an angel.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r5.anchor: وأما الشبهة الثالثة : فسنتكلم في بيان أن إبليس ما كان من الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r6.claim: In 74:31, أصحاب النار means Hell's keepers, controllers, and administrators, not angels being punished.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r6.anchor: يريد به خزنة النار والمتصرفين فيها والمدبرين لأمرها

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r7.claim: The wording of 2:39 does not itself prove angels are punished in Hell; that is known from other evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r7.anchor: لا يدل أيضا على كونهم معذبين بالنار بمجرد هذه الآية بل إنما عرف ذلك بدليل آخر

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r8.speaker: جمهور الفلاسفة وكثير من أهل الجبر
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r8.claim: Most philosophers and many determinists say angels are pure good with no capacity for evil.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r8.anchor: فقال جمهور الفلاسفة وكثير من أهل الجبر : إنهم خيرات محض ولا قدرة لهم البتة

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r9.speaker: جمهور المعتزلة وكثير من الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r9.claim: Most Mu'tazilites and many jurists say angels can do both good and evil.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r9.anchor: وقال جمهور المعتزلة وكثير من الفقهاء : إنهم قادرون على الأمرين

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r10.speaker: جمهور المعتزلة وكثير من الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r10.claim: The question must be sin or leaving what is preferable, either of which implies capacity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r10.anchor: أن قولهم : { أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها } إما أن يكون معصية أو ترك الأولى

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r11.speaker: جمهور المعتزلة وكثير من الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r11.claim: They argue 21:29 threatens an angel who claims divinity and 7:206 praises angels for not being arrogant, implying capacity for evil.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r11.anchor: قوله تعالى : { ومن يقل منهم إنى إلاه من دونه فذالك نجزيه جهنم }

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r12.speaker: جمهور المعتزلة وكثير من الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r12.claim: They argue angels merit praise for good only if able to refrain; compelled agents or those unable to desist are not praiseworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r12.anchor: لو لم يكونوا قادرين على ترك الخيرات لما كانوا ممدوحين بفعلها لأن الملجأ إلى الشيء ومن لا يقدر على ترك الشيء لا يكون ممدوحا

RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r13.claim: Razi replies that Mu'tazilites deem divine reward obligatory, making God's omission impossible, yet praise Him for granting it; inability to omit does not preclude praise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p157/r13.anchor: فيكون الله تعالى فاعلا للثواب والعوض واجب وتركه محال مع أنه تعالى ممدوح على فعل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r1.claim: The wāw in ‘and we glorify’ is circumstantial, like saying, ‘Would you favor someone while I am more deserving of favor?’
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r1.anchor: الواو في { ونحن } للحال كما تقول أتحسن إلى فلان وأنا أحق بالإحسان

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r2.claim: Tasbih and taqdis mean distancing God from what is evil or unfitting.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r2.anchor: والتسبيح تبعيد الله تعالى من السوء وكذا التقديس

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r3.claim: The terms are associated with swimming in water and traversing land, respectively, in the sense of going through and far away.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r3.anchor: من سبح في الماء وقدس في الأرض إذا ذهب فيها وأبعد

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r4.claim: Distance from evil is tasbih; distance from good is a curse (laʿn).
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r4.anchor: إن أريد به التبعيد عن السوء فهو التسبيح وإن أريد به التبعيد عن الخيرات فهو اللعن

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r5.claim: In essence, God is beyond possibility: denying possibility entails denying multiplicity, corporeality, accidents, opposites, and peers, affirming absolute unity and necessary existence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r5.anchor: أما في الذات فأن لا تكون محلا للإمكان فإن منع السوء وإمكانه هو العدم

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r6.claim: In attributes, God is free of ignorance and change, encompasses all knowables, and is able to do all that can be done.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r6.anchor: وأما في الصفات فأن يكون منزها عن الجهل فيكون محيطا بكل المعلومات

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r7.claim: In acts, God neither seeks benefit nor avoids harm nor gains or loses perfection; he is independent of all existents and nonexistents and sovereign over their creation and annihilation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r7.anchor: وأما في الأفعال فأن لا تكون أفعاله لجلب المنافع ودفع المضار وأن لا يستكمل بشيء منها

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r8.speaker: أهل التذكير
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r8.claim: Ahl al-tadhkir say tasbih in the Qur’an can mean transcendence: God has no peer, administers the heavens and worlds, is above wrong descriptions, self-sufficient and sovereign, all-knowing, and without consort or child.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r8.anchor:
قال أهل التذكير :
التسبيح جاء تارة في القرآن بمعنى / التنزيه وأخرى بمعنى التعجب

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r9.speaker: أهل التذكير
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r9.claim: Ahl al-tadhkir also take tasbih as expressing wonder: at subduing powerful animals for humans, creating without fatigue, teaching without a human teacher, and forgiving long sin after brief repentance.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r9.anchor: أما التعجب فكذلك ( ا ) أنا الذي سخرت البهائم القوية للبشر الضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r10.speaker: أهل التذكير
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r10.claim: They urge tasbih for divine favor and relief, including seeking God’s pleasure and praising him morning and evening.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158/r10.anchor: ثم يقول إن أردت رضوان الله فسبح ، وسبحوه بكرة وأصيلا

RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r1.claim: The homily lists tasbih by throne-bearing angels, the close and other angels, prophets, Companions, insects, animals, atoms, and all things in the heavens and earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r1.anchor: لأن لي من يسبحني ، ومنهم حملة العرش

RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r2.claim: God needs no creatures’ tasbih; because nonliving things do not need its reward, God gives their reward to the human who serves him, showing that the whole world can be put at the servant’s service.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r2.anchor: أنا الغني عن تسبيح هذه الأشياء ، وهذه الأشياء ليست من الأحياء

RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r3.claim: Remembering God benefits and purifies the servant, not God; the homily likens the command to a loan that God, though rich, repays tenfold.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r3.anchor: والنكتة الأخرى أذكرني بالعبودية لتنتفع به لا أنا

RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r4.claim: God needs no army, but promises to help the servant who helps him, although heaven and earth are already his armies.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r4.anchor: كن معينا لي وإن كنت غنيا عن إعانتك

RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r5.claim: God needs no remembrance because all already remember him, yet remembers the servant who remembers him; he needs no service, since he is king and all creation prostrates, but brief service earns lasting rest.
RAZI-FULL:v2p158#2/r5.anchor: ولا حاجة بي إلى ذكرك لأن الكل يذكروني

RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf treats ‘with your praise’ as a circumstantial phrase: we glorify you while praising you and clothed in your praise.
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) بحمدك في موضع الحال

RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r2.claim: One explanation is that glorifying God with praise recognizes that his praise and majesty make him deserving of glorification.
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r2.anchor: الأول : أنا إذا سبحناك فنحمدك سبحانك

RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r3.claim: A second explanation is that people can glorify God only through his enabling grace, as David’s example illustrates.
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r3.anchor: الثاني : أنا نسبحك بحمدك فإنه لولا إنعامك علينا

RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r4.speaker: داود
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r4.claim: David says he cannot thank God, since he can reach gratitude for a blessing only through another blessing; God says recognizing this dependence is gratitude.
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r4.anchor: قال داود عليه السلام : يا رب كيف أقدر أن أشكرك

RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r5.claim: Abu Dharr asks which utterance God loves most; the Prophet answers that it is what God chose for his angels, ‘Glory and praise be to God’; al-Razi says Muslim recorded it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r5.anchor: ما اصطفاه الله لملائكته : سبحان الله وبحمد رواه مسلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr recounts that a hypocrite rebuffed a Muslim who reminded him to pray; ʿUmar struck him, and the Prophet told ʿUmar his anger was honor and his approval judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r6.anchor: وروى سعيد بن جبير قال : ( كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r7.speaker: جبريل
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r7.claim: Gabriel tells the Prophet that angels in the first, second, and third heavens remain prostrating, standing, and bowing, praising God as Lord of dominion, might, and life.
RAZI-FULL:v2p159/r7.anchor: فأتاه جبريل فقال : يا نبي الله سألك عمر عن صلاة أهل السماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Masʿud interpret ‘we glorify’ as ‘we pray,’ taking tasbih to mean prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r1.anchor: أي نصلي والتسبيح هو الصلاة ، وهو قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r2.claim: Taqdis means purification, as in the expression ‘the Holy Land.’

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r3.claim: One interpretation addresses God: we declare him purified, describing him with the loftiness and might that befit him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r3.anchor: أحدها : نطهرك أي نصفك بما يليق بك من العلو والعزة

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r4.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r4.claim: Mujahid says the angels purify themselves of sins and errors in pursuit of God’s pleasure.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r4.anchor: قول مجاهد نطهر أنفسنا من ذنوبنا وخطايانا ابتغاء لمرضاتك

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r5.claim: Abu Muslim says they purify their deeds of sin so the deeds are sincerely for God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r5.anchor: قول أبي مسلم نطهر أفعالنا من ذنوبنا حتى تكون خالصة لك

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r6.claim: Another interpretation is purifying the heart of attention to anything besides God until it is absorbed in the lights of knowing him.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r6.anchor: نطهر قلوبنا عن الالتفات إلى غيرك حتى تصير مستغرقة في أنوار معرفتك

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r7.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r7.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that the angels attribute their glorification and purification to themselves; if God did those deeds, there would be no merit in them over bloodshed.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r7.anchor: قالت المعتزلة هذه الآية تدل على العدل من وجوه : أحدها : قولهم : { ونحن نسبح

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r8.claim: They argue that if God caused corruption and killing, his answer should have been that he owns creation and does as he wills.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r8.anchor: لو كان الفساد والقتل فعلا لله تعالى لكان يجب أن يكون الجواب أن يقول إني مالك أفعل ما أشاء

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r9.claim: They argue that God’s answer disavows corruption and murder, which would be impossible if those acts were his own.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r9.anchor: وثالثها : أن قوله : { أعلم ما لا تعلمون } يقتضي التبري من الفساد

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r10.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r10.claim: They ask how God can be praised as transcendent if every indecency, ugliness, injustice, oppression, and corruption is created by his making and will.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r10.anchor: إذا كان لا فاحشة ولا قبح ولا جور ولا ظلم ولا فساد إلا بصنعه وخلقه ومشيئته

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r11.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r11.claim: They argue that if God created people for disbelief, his answer should have admitted he created them to corrupt and kill; its refusal supports the Muʿtazilite doctrine of justice.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r11.anchor: لو كان خالقا للكفر لكان خلقهم لذلك الكفر فكان ينبغي أن يكون الجواب نعم خلقهم ليفسدوا وليقتلوا

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r12.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r12.claim: They argue that if corruption and killing were God’s acts, they would be like colors and bodies, which are not ordinarily met with wonder.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r12.anchor: وسادسها : لو كان الفساد والقتل ، من فعل الله تعالى لكان ذلك جاريا

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r13.claim: Al-Razi says the Muʿtazilite objections are answered by the arguments about motive and knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r13.anchor: والجواب عن هذه الوجوه المعارضة بمسألة الداعي والعلم

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r14.claim: The answer may mean that, despite corruption and killing, God knows there will also be many righteous and devout people among humanity.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r14.anchor: لا تتعجبوا من أن يكون فيهم من يفسد ويقتل فإني أعلم مع هذا بأن فيهم جمعا من الصالحين والمتقين

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r15.claim: If the angels were grieving, the answer reassures them that there are many devout people whom God will not disappoint.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r15.anchor: لا تغتموا بسبب وجود المفسدين فإني أعلم أيضا أن فيهم جمعا من المتقين

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r16.claim: If the angels ask for the wisdom, God gives the general point; revealing the full detail might itself be harmful.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r16.anchor: وثالثها : أنه طلب الحكمة فجوابه أن مصلحتكم فيه أن تعرفوا وجه الحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r17.claim: If they are asking to remain in heaven rather than have a human vicegerent on earth, God says their welfare lies in being in heaven, not on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r17.anchor: أنه التماس لأن يتركهم في الأرض وجوابه إني أعلم أن مصلحتكم أن تكونوا في السماء لا في الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r18.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r18.claim: God may be revealing that Iblis is among the angels, with envy, pride, and hypocrisy in his heart.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r18.anchor: وهو أن معكم إبليس وأن في قلبه حسدا وكبرا و نفاقا

RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r19.claim: Their self-praise may itself amount to glorifying themselves; later humans will instead humble themselves by confessing wrong and asking mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v2p160/r19.anchor: فإنكم لما وصفتم أنفسكم بهذه المدائح فقد استعظمتم أنفسكم فكأنكم أنتم بهذا الكلام في تسبيح أنفسكم

QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r5.claim: The Adam narrative says clay was gathered from every region and left to ferment for forty mornings; the angels wondered what its destiny would be, then marveled at his fashioned form.
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r5.anchor: أمر حتى سل من كل بقعة طينة ثم أمر بأن يخمر طينه أربعين صباحا

QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r6.claim: God's announcement about Adam disclosed a secret and divided the angels' conjectures, despite their wonder at the artistry and wisdom of his form.
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r6.anchor: فحين قال : { إني جاعل في الأرض } ترجمت الظنون

QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r7.claim: Among created things, Adam alone receives this explicit announcement; its wording would resemble consultation from a creature, but here it honors and singles him out.
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r7.anchor: خلق الجنان بما فيها ، والعرش بما هو عليه من انتظام الأجزاء

QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r8.claim: He cites an unnamed poet saying that among the many beauties seen, the speaker's choice fell upon the beloved, illustrating Adam's special selection.

QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r9.claim: The angels' question is inquiry, not objection to God's decree; Qushayri prefers the reading that preserves their immunity from sin.
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r9.anchor: فإن حمل الخطاب على ما يوجب تنزيه الملائكة أولى لأنهم معصومون

RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says the preposition bi in the angels' tasbīḥ requires grammatical analysis to determine what it attaches to.
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r1.anchor: وكذلك البحث عن قوله : ﴿ ونحن نسبح بحمدك ﴾ [ البقرة : 30 ] فإنه يجب البحث عن هذه الباء

RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r2.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r2.claim: An unnamed view nests all knowledge in four books, Qur'anic sciences in the Fātiḥa, and the Fātiḥa's sciences in the bāʾ of the basmala.
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r2.anchor: قيل : كل العلوم مندرج في الكتب الأربعة وعلومها في القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī says the aim of knowledge is to bring the servant to God; the basmala's bāʾ denotes attachment and thus expresses that aim.
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r3.anchor: لأن المقصود من كل العلوم وصول العبد إلى الرب وهذا الباء باء الإلصاق

RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r4.claim: Min is declinable because its ending changes under different governing factors, as shown by min ibnika versus min al-rajuli.
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r4.anchor: ههنا اختلف آخر هذه الكلمة باختلاف العوامل فإنه لا معنى للعامل إلا الأمر الدال

RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r5.claim: Min has four uses: indicating an origin, a part, an explanation, or an augmentative function.
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r5.anchor: كلمة من وردت على وجوه أربعة : ابتداء الغاية والتبعيض والتبيين والزيادة

RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r6.speaker: المبرد
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad holds that min originally marks the beginning of an extent, with its other uses derived from that sense.
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r6.anchor: قال المبرد : الأصل هو ابتداء الغاية والبواقي مفرعة عليه

RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r7.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r7.claim: Others hold that the partitive use is primary and that min's other uses derive from it.
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون : الأصل هو التبعيض والبواقي مفرعة عليه

RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r10.claim: He also asks why the formula of seeking refuge says min Satan rather than ʿan Satan.
RAZI-FULL:v1p88/r10.anchor: فلم جاءت الاستعاذة بلفظ من فقال { أعوذ بالله من الشيطان } ولم يقل عن الشيطان

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r1.claim: Khalīfah can mean successor or deputy; khalīfat rasūl Allāh, successor or steward of God’s Messenger, was shortened to khalīfah and anglicized as caliph.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r1.anchor: a word that can also mean “successor” or“deputy,” hence khalīfat

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r2.claim: Here and in 6:165, khalīfah suggests universal human inheritance and responsibility: all people are, in their inner reality, God’s vicegerents.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r2.anchor: In some verses, such as here and 6:165, khalīfah appears to denote a universal human inheritance and responsibility, since all human beings are in their inner reality the khalīfah of God.

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r3.claim: In other passages khalīfah means successor, as in 7:69 for successors after Noah’s people; related references include 7:74, 10:14, 10:73, 27:62, and 35:39.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r3.anchor: In others, the sense of “successor” comes to the fore (e.g., 7:69, which refers to vicegerents

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r4.claim: Some commentators derive khalīfah from khalafa, to come after: humans follow other creatures and summarize all grades of being in the human state.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r4.anchor: some commentators say that khalīfah comes from khalafa (“to come after”) and means that human beings come after all creatures and all grades of being are summarized in the human state.

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r5.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s report identifies Iblīs as al-Ḥārith, a custodian of Paradise and member of the angelic tribe al-ḥinn, created from smokeless fire unlike the angels created from light.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r5.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said that Iblīs was a member of a tribe of angels called al-ḥinn

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r6.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r6.claim: In the same report, jinn first inhabited earth and shed blood; God sent Iblīs with the al-ḥinn against them, driving them to islands and mountain edges, and Iblīs grew proud of the victory.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r6.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said that Iblīs was a member of a tribe of angels called al-ḥinn
