STUDYQURAN:2:30/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r7.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r7.claim: The report says Adam’s clay body remained lifeless for forty years; Iblīs entered and taunted it, threatening to destroy or defy Adam if either gained power over the other.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r7.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said that Iblīs was a member of a tribe of angels called al-ḥinn

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r8.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r8.claim: In the account, God commands only the angels accompanying Iblīs to prostrate; Iblīs refuses, claiming superiority by age and greatness and contrasting his fire with Adam’s clay.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r8.anchor: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to have said that Iblīs was a member of a tribe of angels called al-ḥinn

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r9.claim: The Quran’s other indication of this order of creation is 15:26–27: human beings were made from molded clay and jinn earlier from scorching fire.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r9.anchor: The only other indication in the Quran of such an order of creation is found in 15:26–27

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r10.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r10.claim: Many commentators accept that jinn inhabited earth before human beings.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r10.anchor: That jinn inhabited the earth before human beings is accepted by many commentators.

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r11.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r11.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers that God addressed all the angels, rather than only those who fought alongside Iblīs.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r11.anchor: al-Rāzī prefers the opinion that God spoke to all the angels, not only those who warred alongside Iblīs.

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r12.claim: The specific story details that Iblīs was an angelic-tribe member are unreliable popular narratives; Ibn ʿAbbās would have known 18:50 identifies Iblīs as a jinn.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r12.anchor: since an authority such as Ibn ʿAbbās would have known that the Quran in 18:50 identifies Iblīs as a jinn, not an angel.

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r13.claim: Prior jinn violence offers one possible explanation for the angels’ question about placing a corrupt, blood-shedding being on earth.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r13.anchor: It does, however, provide one possible explanation for the angels’ question, Wilt Thou place therein . . . , namely, that they had previous experience with the blood and corruption of the earth’s previous inhabitants.

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r14.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r14.claim: Many commentators read the angels’ apparently audacious question as wonder at God’s Wisdom, not doubt or concern; they are not alarmed.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r14.anchor: many commentators explain the angels’ apparently audacious question as an expression of wonder on their part, rather than doubt or concern (R). They marvel at God’s Wisdom

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r15.claim: The usual theological view is that angels cannot disobey or rebel.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r15.anchor: It is thought that disobedience or any brand of rebelliousness is impossible for angels

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r16.speaker: Muʿtazilites
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r16.claim: Al-Rāzī notes the Muʿtazilite view that angels can be disobedient.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r16.anchor: the Muʿtazilites believed that angels could be disobedient.

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r17.speaker: Z
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r17.claim: An alternate rendering is We glorify Thee while praising Thee.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r17.anchor: Hymn Thy praise and call Thee Holy can also be read, “We glorify Thee while praising Thee” (Z)

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r18.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r18.claim: The phrase generally means that good will come from humanity despite inevitable bloodshed and corruption, but only God knows what that good is.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r18.anchor: I know what you know not is generally understood to mean that, despite the inevitability of bloodletting and corruption, good things will come of the creation of human beings, but only God knows what they are (R).

STUDYQURAN:2:30/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r19.claim: As noted in 2:11–12, corruption can also mean degradation of the natural environment.
STUDYQURAN:2:30/r19.anchor: As mentioned in 2:11–12c, such corruption can also refer to the degradation of the natural environment.

TAB-FULL:v1p466/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r1.speaker: بعض المنسوبين إلى العلم بلغات العرب من أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r1.claim: A Basran language scholar says the opening means And your Lord said, treating idh as an extra particle with no meaning; he adduces poems by al-Aswad b. Yaʿfur and ʿAbd Manāf al-Hudhalī.
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r1.anchor: وقال ربك، وأن إذ من الحروف الزوائد، وأن معناها الحذف. واعتل لقوله الذي وصفنا عنه في ذلك ببيت الأسود بن يعفر

TAB-FULL:v1p466/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r2.claim: Tabari rejects deleting idh: it can function conditionally and indicate an unspecified time, so a particle that gives the sentence meaning cannot be declared superfluous.
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r2.anchor: وذلك أن «إذ» حرف يأتي بمعنى الجزاء، ويدل على مجهول من الوقت، وغير جائز إبطال حرف كان دليلا على معنى

TAB-FULL:v1p466/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r3.claim: In al-Aswad b. Yaʿfur's line, fa-idhā points to the present situation and the preceding life; removing idh would destroy the poem's sense.
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r3.anchor: أراد بقوله: فإذا الذي نحن فيه، وما مضى من عيشنا. وأشار بقوله ذلك إلى ما تقدم وصفه

TAB-FULL:v1p466/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r4.claim: In ʿAbd Manāf b. Rabīʿ's line, idhā introduces a condition whose consequence is omitted but understood; removing it would break the meaning.
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r4.anchor: لو أسقط منه إذا بطل معنى الكلام؛ لأن معناه: حتى إذا أسلكوهم في قتائدة سلكوا شلا

TAB-FULL:v1p466/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r5.claim: Arabic also omits recoverable words after expressions such as wherever, before and after, and if a brother honors you; the surviving wording still signals what is omitted.
TAB-FULL:v1p466/r5.anchor: وكما تقول العرب: أتيتك من قبل ومن بعد؛ تريد: من قبل ذلك ومن بعد ذلك.

TAB-FULL:v1p469/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p469/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p469/r1.claim: A further poem beginning fa-idhā wa-dhālika provides another parallel for the meaningful use of idhā in al-Aswad b. Yaʿfur's line.
TAB-FULL:v1p469/r1.anchor: فإذا وذلك لا يضرك ضره … في يوم أسأل نائلا أو أنكد

TAB-FULL:v1p469/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p469/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p469/r2.claim: Tabari links this clause to the preceding rebuke: the audience is implicitly told to remember God's favors in creating them and the earth, and to remember His act toward their father Adam.
TAB-FULL:v1p469/r2.anchor: ثم عطف بقوله: {وإذ قال ربك للملائكة} [البقرة: 30] على المعنى المقتضى بقوله: {كيف تكفرون بالله}

TAB-FULL:v1p471/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p471/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p471/r1.claim: In the cited poem, wa-lā mutadārik has no preceding overt verb to coordinate with; it is governed by the implied sense of the earlier negated phrase.
TAB-FULL:v1p471/r1.anchor: فقال: ولا متدارك، ولم يتقدمه فعل بلفظه يعطف عليه، ولا حرف معرب إعرابه

TAB-FULL:v1p471/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p471/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p471/r2.claim: The poem means I am not seeing; mutadārik is coordinated with the syntactic position of tarā as if the omitted laisa and bi- were expressed.
TAB-FULL:v1p471/r2.anchor: لأن قوله: أجدك لن ترى بثعيلبات بمعنى: أجدك لست براء، فرد متداركا على موضع ترى

TAB-FULL:v1p471/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p471/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p471/r3.claim: Likewise, idh in this verse attaches to the implied command to remember in the preceding clause, coordinating by its meaning rather than an overt matching form.
TAB-FULL:v1p471/r3.anchor: لما سلف قبله تذكير الله المخاطبين به ما سلف

TAB-FULL:v1p472/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r1.claim: Malāʾika is the plural of malak; its singular is more commonly unhamzated, with the hamza's vowel transferred to the previously silent lām, while the plural restores the hamza.
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r1.anchor: فإذا جمعوا واحدهم ردوا الجمع إلى الأصل وهمزوا، فقالوا: ملائكة.

TAB-FULL:v1p472/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r2.claim: Arabic often alternates between a hamzated root form and an unhamzated derived form, as in raʾaytu beside narā, tarā, and yarā.
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r2.anchor: فتترك الهمز في الكلمة التي هي مهموزة فيجري كلامهم بترك همزها في حال، وبهمزها في أخرى

TAB-FULL:v1p472/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r3.claim: Malak may also be pronounced maʾlak by metathesis, like the paired forms jabadh/jadhab and shaʾmal/shamʾal.
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r3.anchor: وقد يقال في واحدهم: مألك، فيكون ذلك مثل قولهم: جبذ وجذب، وشأمل وشمأل

TAB-FULL:v1p472/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r4.claim: If the singular were maʾlak, its expected plural would be mālik, which Tabari does not recall hearing; the attested plurals are malāʾik and malāʾika.
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r4.anchor: غير أن الذي يجب إذا سمي واحدهم مألك، أن يجمع إذ جمع على ذلك: مالك، ولست أحفظ جمعهم كذلك سماعا

TAB-FULL:v1p472/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r5.claim: The root meaning of malāʾak is a message or dispatch; ʿAdī b. Zayd uses it for a message sent to al-Nuʿmān.
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r5.anchor: وأصل الملأك: الرسالة، كما قال عدي بن زيد العبادي

TAB-FULL:v1p472/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r6.claim: The form malāʾak derives from laʾaka ilayhi, to send a message; maʾlak derives from alaka ilayhi, also to send or dispatch one.
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r6.anchor: فمن قال: ملأكا، فهو مفعل من لأك إليه يلأك: إذا أرسل إليه رسالة ملأكة. ومن قال: مألكا

TAB-FULL:v1p472/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r7.speaker: أمية بن أبي الصلت
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r7.claim: Umayya b. Abī al-Ṣalt uses the plural malāʾik in poetry for the angels.
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r7.anchor: قال أمية بن أبي الصلت في جمعهم كذلك: [البحر الوافر]

TAB-FULL:v1p472/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r8.speaker: لبيد بن ربيعة
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r8.claim: Labīd b. Rabīʿa uses alūk for a message sent by a mother with her boy.
TAB-FULL:v1p472/r8.anchor: كما قال لبيد بن ربيعة: [البحر الرمل]

TAB-FULL:v1p475/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p475/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p475/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says malāʾika is the plural of malak; the singular without hamza is more common in Arabic, with the hamza dropped and the formerly still lām vowelled.
TAB-FULL:v1p475/r1.anchor: فسميت الملائكة ملائكة بالرسالة، لأنها رسل الله

TAB-FULL:v1p475/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p475/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p475/r2.claim: He connects the name malāʾika to risāla, since angels carry God’s messages between Him and prophets and servants to whom they are sent; the cited line uses aliknī for delivering a message.
TAB-FULL:v1p475/r2.anchor: ألكني إليها عمرك الله يا فتى … بآية ما جاءت إلينا تهاديا يعني بذلك: أبلغها رسالتي

TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada understand إني جاعل as I am doing or making, rather than specifically creating.
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، وأبي بكر يعني الهذلي، عن الحسن، وقتادة، قالوا

TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r2.speaker: أبو روق
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r2.claim: Abu Rawq reports a general rule that every occurrence of jaʿala in the Qur’an means created.
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي روق، قال: «كل شيء في القرآن جعل فهو خلق»

TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that God will install a successor in the earth and make a replacement there, which he says best accords with Hasan and Qatada’s interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r3.anchor: والصواب في تأويل قوله: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} [البقرة: 30] أي مستخلف في الأرض

TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r4.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the earth was spread from Mecca, angels first circumambulated the House, and it was the earth meant here; surviving prophets and their followers later worshipped there, with several prophets’ graves between Zamzam and the Black Stone and Station.
TAB-FULL:v1p475#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن سابط، أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

TAB-FULL:v1p477/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī derives khalīfa as a faʿīla form from someone succeeding another in an affair and taking his place after him.
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r1.anchor: قولك: خلف فلان فلانا في هذا الأمر إذا قام مقامه فيه بعده

TAB-FULL:v1p477/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r2.claim: He links the sense to 10:14: God made a later people successors in the earth after their predecessors, replacing them.
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r2.anchor: ثم جعلناكم خلائف في الأرض من بعدهم لننظر كيف تعملون} [يونس: 14] يعني بذلك: أنه أبدلكم في الأرض

TAB-FULL:v1p477/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r3.claim: The supreme ruler is called khalīfa because he succeeds the previous ruler and takes his place in governing.
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r3.anchor: ومن ذلك قيل للسلطان الأعظم: خليفة، لأنه خلف الذي كان قبله، فقام بالأمر مقامه

TAB-FULL:v1p477/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq takes khalīfa to mean an inhabitant and cultivator unlike the angels; al-Ṭabarī rejects this as the meaning, despite God saying the figure would inhabit the earth.
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r4.anchor: وليس الذي قال ابن إسحاق في معنى الخليفة بتأويلها، وإن كان الله جل ثناؤه إنما أخبر

TAB-FULL:v1p477/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that jinn first inhabited earth and shed blood; God sent Iblis with angels to defeat and expel them, then placed Adam there as their successor.
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال

TAB-FULL:v1p477/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r6.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas says angels were created Wednesday, jinn Thursday, and Adam Friday; when some jinn disbelieved, angels fought them, producing bloodshed and corruption on earth.
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r6.anchor: حدثنا إسحاق، قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع بن أنس

TAB-FULL:v1p477/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r7.speaker: الحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r7.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri is credited with reading khalīfa as successive generations: Adam’s descendants replace their father and each generation succeeds the one before it.
TAB-FULL:v1p477/r7.anchor: وهذا قول حكي عن الحسن البصري

TAB-FULL:v1p479/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p479/r1.speaker: ابن سابط
TAB-FULL:v1p479/r1.claim: Ibn Sābit says the angels’ description of those who corrupt and shed blood refers to Adam’s children.
TAB-FULL:v1p479/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب، عن ابن سابط: في قوله

TAB-FULL:v1p479/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p479/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p479/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd reports that God planned to create a creature and make a khalīfa in an earth then without creatures, apart from the angels.
TAB-FULL:v1p479/r2.anchor: حدثني يونس، قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب، قال: قال ابن زيد

TAB-FULL:v1p479/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p479/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p479/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Ibn Zayd’s statement could mean generational succession, as in Hasan’s view, or that God would appoint a khalīfa to judge among creatures by His judgment.
TAB-FULL:v1p479/r3.anchor: وهذا القول يحتمل ما حكي عن الحسن، ويحتمل أن يكون أراد ابن زيد أن الله أخبر الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v1p480/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r1.speaker: السدي، عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وأصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r1.claim: In a report through al-Suddi from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and Companions, God says the khalīfa will have descendants who corrupt, envy one another and kill one another.
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r1.anchor: عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس، من أصحاب النبي

TAB-FULL:v1p480/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r2.claim: On this report’s reading, the khalīfa is Adam and those who succeed him in obeying God and judging His creatures justly; corruption and unjust bloodshed belong to their descendants, not these deputies.
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r2.anchor: فكان تأويل الآية على هذه الرواية التي ذكرناها عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس: إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة مني

TAB-FULL:v1p480/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r3.claim: This reading agrees with Hasan’s view in separating the khalīfa from the corrupt, but differs because it makes Adam God’s appointed deputy while Hasan means generations succeeding one another and assigns corruption to the khalīfa.
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r3.anchor: وهذا التأويل وإن كان مخالفا في معنى الخليفة ما حكي عن الحسن من وجه، فموافق له من وجه

TAB-FULL:v1p480/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the inference that the angels explicitly blamed God’s khalīfa: they said only one would corrupt, so God could have told them the khalīfa’s descendants would do so, as the Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas report says.
TAB-FULL:v1p480/r4.anchor: بل قالت: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها} [البقرة: 30] وغير منكر أن يكون ربها أعلمها أنه يكون لخليفته ذلك ذرية

TAB-FULL:v1p482/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p482/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p482/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī asks how angels could know before Adam and his descendants existed that the khalīfa’s people would corrupt and shed blood: did they know the unseen, or merely conjecture and speak without knowledge?
TAB-FULL:v1p482/r1.anchor: أعلمت الغيب فقالت ذلك، أم قالت ما قالت من ذلك ظنا

TAB-FULL:v1p482/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p482/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p482/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas’s account says Iblis was a fire-born angelic being called al-Hinn, named al-Harith and a keeper of Paradise; jinn first corrupted earth, and Iblis’s angelic force defeated them, prompting the angels’ question, while God knew Iblis’s hidden pride.
TAB-FULL:v1p482/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال

TAB-FULL:v1p482/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p482/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p482/r3.claim: The same account says God had Adam’s soil raised and formed him from sticky clay; his body lay for forty nights, and Iblis struck it, entered and exited it, before the spirit entered through Adam’s head.
TAB-FULL:v1p482/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس، قال

TAB-FULL:v1p485/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p485/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p485/r1.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s report, Adam’s haste is linked to human impatience; he praises God at a sneeze, Iblis refuses prostration from pride and is expelled, then Adam names things, while the angels disclaim unseen knowledge and God exposes Iblis’s concealed pride.
TAB-FULL:v1p485/r1.anchor: وهذه الرواية عن ابن عباس تنبئ عن أن قول الله جل ثناؤه

TAB-FULL:v1p485/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p485/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p485/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reads the address as directed to a particular angelic faction, Iblis’s companions who fought the jinn, to test them, expose their limited knowledge, and show that honor comes without bodily strength.
TAB-FULL:v1p485/r2.anchor: وأن الذين قيل لهم ذلك من الملائكة كانوا قبيلة إبليس خاصة، الذين قاتلوا معه جن الأرض قبل خلق آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p485/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p485/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p485/r3.claim: He calls the angels’ question a lapse and conjecture about the unseen; they were shown their error, repented and disclaimed unseen knowledge, while God exposed Iblis’s hidden arrogance.
TAB-FULL:v1p485/r3.anchor: ويصرح بأن قيلهم لربهم: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء} [البقرة: 30] كانت هفوة منهم ورجما بالغيب

TAB-FULL:v1p487/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p487/r1.speaker: السدي عن أبي مالك وأبي صالح وابن عباس وابن مسعود وأصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p487/r1.claim: Al-Suddi’s report from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and Companions says Iblis ruled a heaven, grew proud, and angels were told the khalīfa’s descendants would corrupt, envy and kill; their question followed. The account then tells how angels collected multicolored clay despite earth’s pleas, explaining human diversity, and Adam was formed from it.
TAB-FULL:v1p487/r1.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود

TAB-FULL:v1p488/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p488/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p488/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī continues the al-Suddi account: Iblis calls Adam hollow and vows to destroy him; when the spirit reaches Adam, he sees fruit, hungers and rushes toward it before the spirit reaches his feet, illustrating human haste.
TAB-FULL:v1p488/r1.anchor: فقال للملائكة: لا ترهبوا من هذا، فإن ربكم صمد وهذا أجوف، لئن سلطت عليه لأهلكن

TAB-FULL:v1p488/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p488/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p488/r2.claim: The account continues: angels prostrate except proud Iblis, who is expelled; Adam names the creatures, the angels acknowledge they know only what God taught, and God reveals the pride Iblis concealed.
TAB-FULL:v1p488/r2.anchor: فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون إلا إبليس أبى أن يكون مع الساجدين أي استكبر وكان من الكافرين

TAB-FULL:v1p488/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p488/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p488/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says this report’s opening differs from the earlier Ibn Abbas account, while its ending agrees in the angels’ admission of ignorance and disclosure of Iblis’s pride.
TAB-FULL:v1p488/r3.anchor: فهذا الخبر أوله مخالف معناه معنى الرواية التي رويت عن ابن عباس من رواية الضحاك

TAB-FULL:v1p490/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī argues that if God had already told angels the descendants would corrupt and shed blood, they could not be reproached for repeating that fact or challenged to name what God had hidden.
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r1.anchor: وهذا إذا تدبره ذو الفهم، علم أن أوله يفسد آخره، وأن آخره يبطل معنى أوله

TAB-FULL:v1p490/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r2.claim: He suspects a transmitter misreported the account; a plausible original reading is that angels inferred too much from God’s statement about corrupt descendants and were challenged to prove what they presumed to know.
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r2.anchor: وأخشى أن يكون بعض نقلة هذا الخبر هو الذي غلط على من رواه عنه من الصحابة

TAB-FULL:v1p490/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r3.claim: On this reconstruction, angels generalized from some descendants’ corruption to all of them; God had concealed that many would obey, reform the earth, preserve blood and attain honor.
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r3.anchor: من طاعتهم ربهم وإصلاحهم في أرضه وحقن الدماء ورفعه منزلتهم وكرامتهم عليه

TAB-FULL:v1p490/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explicitly says this is his description of how the report may be interpreted, not the interpretation he chooses for the verse itself.
TAB-FULL:v1p490/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكرناه هو صفة منا لتأويل الخبر لا القول الذي نختاره في تأويل الآية

TAB-FULL:v1p491/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r1.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن سابط
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r1.claim: Abd al-Rahman b. Sabit takes the angels’ description of the corrupt blood-shedders to mean human beings.
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r1.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن سابط، قوله: " {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء} [البقرة: 30] ، قال: يعنون الناس "

TAB-FULL:v1p491/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r2.claim: Qatada reports that God sought the angels’ counsel about Adam; they knew bloodshed and earthly corruption were especially hateful to God, while Adam’s line would also include prophets, messengers, righteous people and people of Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: قوله: " {وإذ قال ربك للملائكة إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} [البقرة: 30] ، فاستخار الملائكة في خلق آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p491/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r3.claim: Al-Tabari reads this Qatada account as the angels speaking from conjecture, not certain prior knowledge; God counters that Adam’s progeny will include prophets and people devoted to obedience.
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r3.anchor: وهذا الخبر عن قتادة، يدل على أن قتادة كان يرى أن الملائكة قالت ما قالت من قولها

TAB-FULL:v1p491/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the angels thought none would be more honored or knowledgeable than them; Adam’s creation tested them, as all creation is tested, and heaven and earth were commanded to obey.
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r4.anchor: أن ابن عباس كان يقول: إن الله لما أخذ في خلق آدم قالت الملائكة: ما الله خالق خلقا أكرم عليه منا، ولا أعلم منا

TAB-FULL:v1p491/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r5.claim: In another report, Qatada says God had informed the angels that earthly creatures would corrupt and shed blood, which explains their question.
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: في قوله: " {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها} [البقرة: 30] ، قال: كان الله أعلمهم إذا كان في الأرض خلق أفسدوا فيها

TAB-FULL:v1p491/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r6.speaker: الحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r6.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri is among the interpreters who share Qatada’s view that God had already informed the angels of the coming corruption and bloodshed.
TAB-FULL:v1p491/r6.anchor: وبمثل قول قتادة قال جماعة من أهل التأويل، منهم الحسن البصري

TAB-FULL:v1p493/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p493/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p493/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada report that God told the angels he would act, gave them some knowledge but withheld other knowledge, and they asked on the basis of what they had been taught, knowing bloodshed was a grave sin.
TAB-FULL:v1p493/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، وأبي بكر، عن الحسن، وقتادة، قالا: " قال الله لملائكته: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} [البقرة: 30] قال لهم إني فاعل

TAB-FULL:v1p493/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p493/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p493/r2.claim: The angels privately claimed that no creation would surpass them in knowledge or honor; God tested that boast by teaching Adam the names and challenging them to name them.
TAB-FULL:v1p493/r2.anchor: فلما أخذ في خلق آدم، همست الملائكة فيما بينها، فقالوا: ليخلق ربنا ما شاء أن يخلق

TAB-FULL:v1p493/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p493/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p493/r4.claim: Adam names every thing shown to him, including peoples; the angels’ public concern was human corruption, while their concealed claim was that they were better and more knowledgeable.
TAB-FULL:v1p493/r4.anchor: قال: أما ما أبدوا فقولهم: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء} [البقرة: 30] وأما ما كتموا

TAB-FULL:v1p495/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p495/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p495/r1.claim: Al-Rabi b. Anas says angels were created Wednesday, jinn Thursday and Adam Friday; after some jinn rebelled, angels fought them on earth, causing the bloodshed and corruption behind their question.
TAB-FULL:v1p495/r1.anchor: عن الربيع بن أنس: " في قوله: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} [البقرة: 30] الآية. قال: إن الله خلق الملائكة يوم الأربعاء وخلق الجن يوم الخميس، وخلق آدم يوم الجمعة

TAB-FULL:v1p495/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p495/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p495/r2.claim: Al-Rabi reports that the angels privately boasted of superior knowledge and honor; God taught Adam the names to show his superiority, exposing their public words and hidden claim.
TAB-FULL:v1p495/r2.anchor: وحدثت عن عمار بن الحسن، قال: أخبرنا عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع، بمثله: " {ثم عرضهم على الملائكة فقال أنبئوني بأسماء هؤلاء

TAB-FULL:v1p495/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p495/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p495/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd relates that angels, afraid of hell, wondered whether they might disobey; God announced a human population of corruption, Adam’s knowledge proved his superiority, and Iblis refused to yield, citing fire versus clay.
TAB-FULL:v1p495/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد بما حدثني به، يونس بن عبد الأعلى قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب، قال: قال ابن زيد: " لما خلق الله النار

TAB-FULL:v1p497/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p497/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v1p497/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains khalifa as a nonangelic inhabitant who settles and cultivates the earth; Adam’s creation was a test, and God had disclosed that his descendants would sin and shed blood.
TAB-FULL:v1p497/r1.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق بما حدثنا به ابن حميد، قال: حدثنا سلمة بن الفضل، عن محمد بن إسحاق

TAB-FULL:v1p497/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p497/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v1p497/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Adam was formed from earth and God’s hands for honor, lay forty years before ensoulment and became pottery-like without fire; he sneezed at ensoulment, angels prostrated, but proud, envious Iblis refused.
TAB-FULL:v1p497/r2.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: فيقال والله أعلم: خلق الله آدم ثم وضعه ينظر إليه أربعين عاما

TAB-FULL:v1p498/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the angels spoke on the basis of what God had informed them would happen among Adam’s descendants.
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: " إنما تكلموا بما أعلمهم أنه كائن من خلق آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p498/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r2.claim: One view says God allowed the angels to ask after telling them what Adam’s descendants would do; astonished, they asked how creatures could disobey their creator, and God said it would happen even among some who seemed obedient.
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إنما قالت الملائكة ما قالت: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء} [البقرة: 30] لأن الله أذن لها

TAB-FULL:v1p498/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r3.claim: Some Arab grammarians say the question was not a protest against God but a request to learn; the angels mentioned their own glorification because they disliked disobedience after the jinn had disobeyed.
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r3.anchor: وقال بعض أهل العربية: قول الملائكة: {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها} [البقرة: 30] على غير وجه الإنكار منهم على ربهم

TAB-FULL:v1p498/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r4.claim: Another view takes the angels’ words as a request for guidance about what they did not know, equivalent to asking God to inform them, not as a rebuke.
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: ذلك من الملائكة على وجه الاسترشاد عما لم يعلموا من ذلك

TAB-FULL:v1p498/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the angels asked God to inform them whether he would put such corrupt beings on earth and leave his deputies among them; their question was inquiry, not denial, though they abhorred disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r5.anchor: وأولى هذه التأويلات بقول الله جل ثناؤه

TAB-FULL:v1p498/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r6.claim: Al-Tabari rejects the claim that God authorized a question of astonishment after disclosure: neither the verse’s apparent wording nor a conclusive report supports it, so it cannot ground the Qur’an’s interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r6.anchor: فدعوى لا دلالة عليها في ظاهر التنزيل ولا خبر بها

TAB-FULL:v1p498/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r7.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وقتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r7.claim: Al-Tabari says it is compatible with reports from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud, via al-Suddi and supported by Qatada, that God disclosed Adam’s descendants’ corruption and the angels asked to learn more.
TAB-FULL:v1p498/r7.anchor: ما روي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود من القول الذي رواه السدي ووافقهما عليه قتادة

TAB-FULL:v1p500/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r1.claim: If God had disclosed the future corruption, Al-Tabari says the angels could be asking whether it would in fact occur and asking God to make them earth’s deputies so that no one would disobey.
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r1.anchor: ذلك منهم؟ ومسألتهم ربهم أن يجعلهم الخلفاء في الأرض حتى لا يعصوه

TAB-FULL:v1p500/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r2.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس والربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas and also followed by al-Rabi b. Anas, says angels knew of the jinn who had lived on earth before Adam and asked whether later creatures would act like them; their question was inquiry, not certainty.
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r2.anchor: ما رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس وتابعه عليه الربيع بن أنس من أن الملائكة قالت ذلك لما كان عندها من علم سكان الأرض قبل آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p500/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r3.claim: Al-Tabari does not call the prior-jinn account or Ibn Zayd’s astonishment account impossible, but sets both aside because no sufficiently authoritative report establishes them.
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r3.anchor: وإنما تركنا القول بالذي رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس ووافقه عليه الربيع بن أنس وبالذي قاله ابن زيد في تأويل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v1p500/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the angels’ question as amazement that God would create beings who disobey their creator, rather than as knowledge that this would certainly occur.
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r4.anchor: وغير خطأ أيضا ما قاله ابن زيد من أن يكون قيل الملائكة ما قالت من ذلك على وجه التعجب

TAB-FULL:v1p500/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r5.claim: Al-Tabari says knowledge of past events is reliable only through transmission that rules out collusion, lying, error and forgetfulness; the cited reports do not meet that standard, so the text-supported interpretation is preferable.
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r5.anchor: والخبر عما مضى وما قد سلف، لا يدرك علم صحته إلا بمجيئه مجيئا يمتنع منه التشاغب والتواطؤ

TAB-FULL:v1p500/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r6.claim: Al-Tabari explains that the verse omits God’s disclosure that the khalifa’s descendants would corrupt; the angels’ question implies it, as a poet’s phrase implies the omitted command to leave him alone.
TAB-FULL:v1p500/r6.anchor: فلا تدفنوني إن دفني محرم … عليكم ولكن خامري أم عامر

TAB-FULL:v1p503/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r1.claim: Al-Tabari glosses tasbih with praise as magnifying God through praise and gratitude; he also defines its root sense as declaring God free of attributes unworthy of him.
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r1.anchor: وأصل التسبيح لله عند العرب التنزيه له من إضافة ما ليس من صفاته إليه والتبرئة له من ذلك

TAB-FULL:v1p503/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r2.claim: In Arab usage, remembrance and prayer can be called tasbih; the report also records the angels’ repeated phrase of glorification with praise.
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r2.anchor: ما اصطفى الله لملائكته: سبحان ربي وبحمده، سبحان ربي وبحمده

TAB-FULL:v1p503/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r3.claim: Said b. Jubayr reports an episode in which Umar asks about the angels’ prayer; Gabriel says the lowest heaven’s angels prostrate, the second’s bow, and the third’s stand until the Resurrection, each reciting praises.
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي، فمر رجل من المسلمين على رجل من المنافقين

TAB-FULL:v1p503/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r4.speaker: أبو ذر
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r4.claim: Abu Dharr reports that when asked which words God loves most, the Prophet named the words God chose for the angels: repeated glorification of the Lord with praise.
TAB-FULL:v1p503/r4.anchor: عن أبي ذر: " أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عاده، أو أن أبا ذر عاد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقال: يا رسول الله بأبي أنت

TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari says tasbih fundamentally declares God free of attributes that do not belong to him; al-Asha’s verse means, reproachfully, ‘Glory be to God against alqama’s boasting.’
TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r1.anchor: أقول لما جاءني فخره … سبحان من علقمة الفاخر

TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وأصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi reports from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud and some Companions that the angels’ phrase means they pray to God.
TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود

TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.claim: Qatada takes tasbih here in its familiar, literal sense of glorification.
TAB-FULL:v1p503#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قوله: {ونحن نسبح بحمدك} [البقرة: 30] قال التسبيح التسبيح "

TAB-FULL:v1p505/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r1.claim: Al-Tabari defines taqdis as purification and magnification: subbuh denotes declaring God free of defects, quddus his purity and exaltation, and holy land is purified land.
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r1.anchor: فإن معنى قوله ذلك راجع إلى المعنى الذي ذكرناه من التطهير؛ من أجل أن صلاتها لربها تعظيم

TAB-FULL:v1p505/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r2.claim: The angels’ tasbih clears God of what polytheists attribute to him and includes prayer; taqdis ascribes purity to him, free from what disbelievers allege.
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r2.anchor: فإن معنى قوله ذلك راجع إلى المعنى الذي ذكرناه من التطهير؛ من أجل أن صلاتها لربها تعظيم

TAB-FULL:v1p505/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r3.claim: Qatada says the angels’ taqdis means prayer.
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: في قوله: " {ونقدس لك} [البقرة: 30] قال: التقديس: الصلاة "

TAB-FULL:v1p505/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r4.claim: Abu Salih interprets taqdis as magnifying and glorifying God.
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r4.anchor: عن أبي صالح: في قوله: " {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} [البقرة: 30] قال: نعظمك ونمجدك "

TAB-FULL:v1p505/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r5.claim: Mujahid says taqdis means to magnify and exalt God.
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد: في قول الله: " {ونقدس لك} [البقرة: 30] قال: نعظمك ونكبرك "

TAB-FULL:v1p505/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq paraphrases the angels’ words as a promise not to disobey or do anything God dislikes.
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r6.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} [البقرة: 30] لا نعصي ولا نأتي شيئا تكرهه "

TAB-FULL:v1p505/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك: " في قوله: {ونقدس لك} [البقرة: 30] قال: التقديس: التطهير "

TAB-FULL:v1p505/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r8.claim: Al-Tabari reconciles prayer and glorification with purification: prayer magnifies God and cleanses him of the false attributions made by disbelievers.
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r8.anchor: فإن معنى قوله ذلك راجع إلى المعنى الذي ذكرناه من التطهير؛ من أجل أن صلاتها لربها تعظيم

TAB-FULL:v1p505/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r9.claim: Al-Tabari says ونقدسك could replace ونقدس لك with no change in meaning; both transitive constructions are idiomatic, as Qur’anic usage also shows.
TAB-FULL:v1p505/r9.anchor: ولو قال مكان: {ونقدس لك} [البقرة: 30] : ونقدسك، كان فصيحا من الكلام، وذلك أن العرب تقول: فلان يسبح الله ويقدسه

TAB-FULL:v1p508/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God knew that Iblis's heart concealed arrogance and self-delusion unknown to the angels.

TAB-FULL:v1p508/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود، وأصحاب النبي
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r2.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Ibn Masud and other Companions the gloss that God's knowledge concerned Iblis's affair.
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r2.anchor: عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس، من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} [البقرة: 30] يعني من شأن إبليس

TAB-FULL:v1p508/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r3.claim: Mujahid says God knew Iblis's disobedience and that He created him for it.
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} [البقرة: 30] قال: علم من إبليس المعصية وخلقه لها

TAB-FULL:v1p508/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r4.claim: Mujahid also says God knew Iblis concealed pride and would refuse to prostrate to Adam.
TAB-FULL:v1p508/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: في قوله: " {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} [البقرة: 30] قال: علم من إبليس كتمانه الكبر أن لا يسجد لآدم

TAB-FULL:v1p510/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r1.claim: Mujahid once glosses the phrase as God's knowledge of Iblis's created-for disobedience, and once as referring to Adam.
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: " في قوله: {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} [البقرة: 30] قال: علم من إبليس المعصية وخلقه لها. وقال مرة آدم

TAB-FULL:v1p510/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r2.claim: Mujahid says God knew Iblis's disobedience and created him for it, while knowing Adam's obedience and creating him for it.
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r2.anchor: عبد الوهاب بن مجاهد يحدث عن أبيه: " في قوله: {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} [البقرة: 30] قال: علم من إبليس المعصية وخلقه لها

TAB-FULL:v1p510/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq reads the phrase as God's knowledge of what was among them, which He had not disclosed to the angels: disobedience, corruption, and bloodshed.
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق: " {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} [البقرة: 30] أي فيكم ومنكم ولم يبدها لهم

TAB-FULL:v1p510/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r4.claim: Qatada says God knew that Adam's descendants would include prophets, messengers, righteous people, and inhabitants of Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} [البقرة: 30] فكان في علم الله أنه سيكون من ذلك الخليفة أنبياء ورسل

TAB-FULL:v1p510/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r5.claim: Al-Tabari explains that the angels wondered at a creation that would sin and implied that they themselves glorified, prayed to, and obeyed God.
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r5.anchor: فإنا نعظمك ونصلي لك ونطيعك ولا نعصيك

TAB-FULL:v1p510/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r6.claim: God's answer points to Iblis's hidden arrogance, unknown to the angels, and reproaches their universal claim about themselves when some among them would disobey.
TAB-FULL:v1p510/r6.anchor: وعلى قيلهم ذلك ووصفهم أنفسهم بالعموم من الوصف عوتبوا

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r1.claim: The angels made their prayer a means to God; He burned thousands of them for an hour, and they admitted their incapacity.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : إن الملائكة جعلوا دعاءهم وسيلة إلى الله ، فأمر الله النار فأحرقت منهم

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r2.claim: When the angels boasted of their deeds, glorification, and sanctification, God struck them with ignorance until they confessed they had no knowledge.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : لما باهوا بأعمالهم وتسبيحهم وتقديسهم ضربهم كلهم بالجهل حتى قالوا : لا علم لنا

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r3.claim: Their inability to grasp what was decreed taught them their shortfall before the realities of the Real.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : عجزهم عن درك المكتوبات عرفهم بذلك قصورهم عن حقائق الحق

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r4.claim: Pride in one's work and abundant worship makes ignorance one's home; the angels' boast led them to confess ignorance.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : من استكبر بعمله واستكثر بطاعته كان الجهل وطنه ، ألا تراهم لما

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r5.claim: Whoever says “I” contests divine power; the angels' boastful claim to glorify God also objected to lordship, despite being a setting for divine instruction.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r5.anchor: قال الواسطي : من قال أنا فقد نازع القدرة ، قالت الملائكة : نحن نسبح بحمدك

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r6.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r6.claim: God formed the vicegerent according to prior knowledge, composed his form, clothed him in signs of divine attributes so he might know God, and held his breaths in reserve until their manifestation.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r6.anchor: قال الواسطي في قوله : ﴿ إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة ﴾ خلقه بعلمه السابق ودبره بالتركيب

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r7.speaker: بعض العراقيين
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r7.claim: Vicegerency requires seeing things through the divine essence in separation and connection, though neither is ever truly detached from God; temporal beings cannot unite with the pre-eternal.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعض العراقيين : شروط الخلافة رؤيته بذاته الأشياء فصلا ووصلا ، إذ الفصل والوصل

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r8.claim: Knowledge of God is more complete than spiritual exertion.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أعلمهم أن العلم بالله أتم من المجاهدات

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r9.claim: The angels reproached and belittled Adam without recognizing his unique creation, so God ordered them to prostrate to him.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : عيروا آدم واستصغروه ولم يعرفوا خصائص الصنع فيه فأمروا بالسجود له

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r10.speaker: بعض البغداديين
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r10.claim: God adorned Adam with special gifts and manifested attributes of pre-eternity; bowing to him became nearness to God, while pride toward him brought distance.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r10.anchor: وقال بعض البغداديين : حلاه بخصائص الخلع وأظهر عليه صفات القدم ، فصار الخضوع له قربة إلى الحق

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r11.claim: God addressed the angels to expose their reliance on their own actions, worship, and purification, not to seek their counsel; He then returned them to their proper station by ordering prostration to Adam.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r11.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ﴿ إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة ﴾ خاطب الملائكة لا للمشورة ولكن لاستخراج

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r12.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r12.claim: God exposed the angels' hidden self-regard and displayed generosity: prior care is not undone by offenses, and honoring them for their deeds would have concealed that grace.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r12.anchor: قال الواسطي في قوله ﴿ إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة ﴾ أظهر عليهم ما أضمروه

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r13.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r13.claim: After the angels boasted of praise and sanctification, God taught Adam the names, making them recognize their own shortfall and confess ignorance.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r13.anchor: ولما قالوا ﴿ ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك ﴾ علم آدم الأسماء كلها فرجعوا إلى رؤية التقصير

SULAMI:v1p54#2/r14.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r14.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r14.claim: Glorification and sanctification do not themselves bring one near to God; nearness comes through pre-eternal grace, which sins cannot diminish.
SULAMI:v1p54#2/r14.anchor: إن التسبيح والتقديس لا يقربان منك إنما يقرب منك سبق عناية الأزل وهو لا تقدح فيه الجنايات والعصيان

SULAMI:v1p56/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p56/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان المغربي
SULAMI:v1p56/r1.claim: The angels' claim to praise and sanctify God exemplifies how creaturely claims lead to ignorance.
SULAMI:v1p56/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان المغربي : ما بلاء الخلق إلا الدعاوى ، ألا ترى أن الملائكة قالوا

TUSTARI:2:30/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30/r1.claim: Before Adam's creation, God announced to the angels that He would install him as a vicegerent on earth.
TUSTARI:2:30/r1.anchor: إن الله تعالى قبل أن يخلق آدم عليه السلام قال للملائكة

TUSTARI:2:30/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30/r2.claim: Adam was made from clay of divine might and from the light of Muhammad.
TUSTARI:2:30/r2.anchor: وخلق آدم عليه السلام من طين العزة من نور محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

TUSTARI:2:30/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30/r3.claim: God warned Adam that his commanding soul was his fiercest enemy and exposed its thoughts and desires to teach constant need and refuge: ask for aid in obedience, protection from sin, gratitude for blessing, and patience in affliction.
TUSTARI:2:30/r3.anchor: وأعلمه أن نفسه الأمارة بالسوء أعدى عدو له

TUSTARI:2:30/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30/r4.claim: The heart must not settle into even the slightest whisper of the lower soul; it must turn back to its Lord.
TUSTARI:2:30/r4.anchor: ولا يساكن قلبه أدنى وسوسة لها دون الرجوع عنها إلى ربه

TUSTARI:2:30/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30/r5.claim: The soul is still when commanded and active at prohibition; Adam was to restrain its motion and move from stillness, with no escape from sin except God's protection and no obedience except by His aid.
TUSTARI:2:30/r5.anchor: وجعل طبعها في الأمر ساكنا، وفي النهي متحركا

TUSTARI:2:30/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30/r6.claim: Adam was allowed to eat freely in Paradise but forbidden the tree; seeing it, he wished for permanence despite knowing his term was fixed, and Satan exploited that inward wish by promising the tree of immortality.
TUSTARI:2:30/r6.anchor: فأتاه إبليس من قبل مساكنة قلبه بوسوسة نفسه في ذلك، فقال: هل أدلك على شجرة الخلد

TUSTARI:2:30/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30/r7.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30/r7.claim: God allowed the enemy's whisper to reach Adam in accordance with prior knowledge, decree, and just judgment.
TUSTARI:2:30/r7.anchor: وألحق الله عز وجل به وسوسة العدو لسابق علمه فيه، وبلوغ تقديره وحكمه العادل عليه

TUSTARI:2:30#2/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r1.claim: Following an unnamed Successor's twofold distinction of forgetfulness, Sahl reads Adam's as leaving the covenant; God left persistent sinners in punishment just as they had been left without His protection.
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r1.anchor: يعني ترك العهد، ومثله في تنزيل السجدة

TUSTARI:2:30#2/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r2.speaker: بعض التابعين
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r2.claim: The other sense is losing a memory, illustrated by Moses and the fish and Moses' request to al-Khidr; the Prophet is promised preservation from forgetting.
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r2.anchor: والوجه الآخر النسيان هو الذي لا يحفظ فيذهب من ذكره

TUSTARI:2:30#2/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r3.claim: Adam's thought was an impulse of innate appetite, not reflective consideration; had it been contemplation, it would have become worship.
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r3.anchor: ولم تكن فكرته اعتبارا، فكانت تكون عبادة

TUSTARI:2:30#2/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r4.claim: Before creation God decreed that a heart settled on anything besides Him would face Satan's whisper through desire, while the person could instead return in refuge; Adam's deed became a lesson in his descendants through the Last Day.
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r4.anchor: وهذا حكم الله تعالى به قبل خلق السماوات والأرض أنه لا يرى بقلبه عنده شيئا، وهو غيره مساكنا إياه، إلا سلط عليه إبليس

TUSTARI:2:30#2/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r5.claim: Eating was not the real point: God meant that Adam should not let his aspiration settle on anything other than Him.
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r5.anchor: ولم يرد الله معاني الأكل في الحقيقة، وإنما أراد معاني مساكنة الهمة

TUSTARI:2:30#2/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r6.claim: Anyone who claims what is not theirs and settles inwardly on its desire risks divine abandonment, unless God mercies them by protecting them from self-management and aiding them against Satan and the ego.
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r6.anchor: وكذلك من ادعى ما ليس له، وساكنه قلبه ناظرا إلى هوى نفسه فيه

TUSTARI:2:30#2/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r7.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r7.claim: Paradise's people are protected from the self-management of worldly life; Adam was not protected from planning for permanence, so appetite and desire overpowered knowledge, reason, clarity, and the heart's light by prior decree.
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r7.anchor: فأهل الجنة معصومون فيها من التدبير الذي كانوا به في دار الدنيا، فآدم صلوات الله عليه

TUSTARI:2:30#2/r8.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r8.claim: The Prophet is quoted as saying that desire and appetite overcome knowledge and reason, explaining Adam's susceptibility to temptation.
TUSTARI:2:30#2/r8.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TUSTARI:2:30#3/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:30#3/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:30#3/r1.claim: The angels mean that they purify themselves by uttering what God graciously inspired them to say.
TUSTARI:2:30#3/r1.anchor: أي نطهر أنفسنا بقولنا ما ألهمتنا تفضلا منك علينا

AKHFASH:v1p62/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p62/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p62/r1.claim: The angels were not objecting to God; they asked in order to learn, or expressed aversion to disobedience because the jinn had disobeyed earlier.
AKHFASH:v1p62/r1.anchor: لم يكن ذلك انكارا منهم على ربهم، انما سألوا ليعلموا

AKHFASH:v1p62/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p62/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p62/r2.claim: All remembrance and prayer may be called tasbīḥ; سبح بالحمد means make your glorification accompanied by praise of God.
AKHFASH:v1p62/r2.anchor: فذلك لان الذكر كله تسبيح وصلاة

AKHFASH:v1p62/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p62/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p62/r3.claim: The question is framed as an acknowledgment, like the poet's rhetorical ألستم خير من ركب المطايا, meaning that they are indeed so.
AKHFASH:v1p62/r3.anchor: جاء على وجه الاقرار كما قال الشاعر

TABRISI:2:30/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30/r1.claim: قول introduces quoted speech; رب means master or lord, applies to a house or horse, and with the definite article is reserved for God.
TABRISI:2:30/r1.anchor: القول موضوع في كلام العرب للحكاية نحو قولك قال زيد خرج عمرو والرب السيد

TABRISI:2:30/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30/r2.claim: رب is traced to ربيته, managing someone's affairs; a rabbani scholar manages the community's affairs.
TABRISI:2:30/r2.anchor: وأصله من ربيته إذا قمت بأمره ومنه قيل للعالم رباني لأنه يقوم بأمر الأمة

TABRISI:2:30/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r3.speaker: أكثر العلماء والخليل
TABRISI:2:30/r3.claim: Most scholars derive angels from الألوكة, “message”; al-Khalil defines ألوك as message and gives the related form مألكة.
TABRISI:2:30/r3.anchor: فذهب أكثر العلماء إلى أنه من الألوكة وهي الرسالة وقال الخليل الألوك الرسالة

TABRISI:2:30/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r4.speaker: غيره
TABRISI:2:30/r4.claim: Another etymology says a message is called ألوكة because it is chewed in the mouth, like a horse chewing its bridle.
TABRISI:2:30/r4.anchor: وقال غيره إنما سميت الرسالة ألوكا لأنها تولك في الفم أي تمضغ والفرس تألك اللجام

TABRISI:2:30/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r5.speaker: عدي بن زيد
TABRISI:2:30/r5.claim: Adi ibn Zayd's مألكا in his poem witnesses the message derivation.
TABRISI:2:30/r5.anchor: قال عدي بن زيد: أبلغا النعمان عني مألكا

TABRISI:2:30/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r6.speaker: لبيد
TABRISI:2:30/r6.claim: Labid's ألوك in his poem witnesses the message derivation.
TABRISI:2:30/r6.anchor: وقال لبيد: وغلام أرسلته أمه بألوك

TABRISI:2:30/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r7.speaker: الهذلي
TABRISI:2:30/r7.claim: The Hudhali poet's ألكني in his verse is another witness to the message derivation.
TABRISI:2:30/r7.anchor: وقال الهذلي: ألكني إليها وخير الرسو

TABRISI:2:30/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30/r8.claim: On the message derivation, ملائكة is a reversed plural of ملأك meaning messenger; a poem attests the hamzated form.
TABRISI:2:30/r8.anchor: فالملائكة على هذا وزنها مفاعلة مقلوبة جمع ملأك في معنى مالك قال الشاعر

TABRISI:2:30/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30/r9.claim: Some Arabs keep the hamza, but most shift its vowel to the lām and drop it, saying ملك.
TABRISI:2:30/r9.anchor: ومن العرب من يستعمله مهموزا والجمهور منهم على إلقاء حركة الهمزة على اللام وحذفها

TABRISI:2:30/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:2:30/r10.claim: Abu Ubayda derives the word from لأك, “to send”; ملأك and ملائكة are then unaltered forms with an extra initial mīm.
TABRISI:2:30/r10.anchor: وذهب أبو عبيدة إلى أن أصله من لأك إذا أرسل فملأك على هذا القول مفعل

TABRISI:2:30/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r11.speaker: ابن كيسان
TABRISI:2:30/r11.claim: Ibn Kaysan derives it from الملك: ملأك is فعال like شمأل, ملائكة is فعائلة, the mīm is original, and hamza added.
TABRISI:2:30/r11.anchor: وذهب ابن كيسان إلى أنه من الملك وأن وزن ملأك فعال مثل شمأل وملائكة فعائلة

TABRISI:2:30/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30/r12.claim: Though “angel” originally meant messenger, it became the established label for God's nonhuman messengers, as “heaven” came to name the familiar skies.
TABRISI:2:30/r12.anchor: وإن كان أصله الرسالة فقد صار صفة غالبة على صنف من رسل الله غير البشر

TABRISI:2:30/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r13.speaker: أصحابنا
TABRISI:2:30/r13.claim: The author's companions say not all angels are messengers, citing 22:75; if all were messengers all would be selected, so ملك is generic rather than derived from message.
TABRISI:2:30/r13.anchor: وقال أصحابنا رضي الله عنهم إن جميع الملائكة ليسوا برسل الله بدلالة قوله تعالى

TABRISI:2:30/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30/r14.claim: جعل, خلق, فعل, and إحداث are related, but جعل can assign a state without creating; فعل and إحداث mean bringing into existence.
TABRISI:2:30/r14.anchor: والجعل والخلق والفعل والإحداث نظائر إلا أن الجعل قد يتعلق بالشيء لا على سبيل الإيجاد

TABRISI:2:30/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30/r15.claim: خليفة and إمام overlap in use but differ: a khalifa succeeds a predecessor, while an imam leads and is to be followed and obeyed.
TABRISI:2:30/r15.anchor: والخليفة والإمام واحد في الاستعمال إلا أن بينهما فرقا فالخليفة استخلف في الأمر

TABRISI:2:30/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30/r16.claim: سفك means pouring out blood; grammarians disagree whether دم follows فعل or فعِل.
TABRISI:2:30/r16.anchor: والسفك صب الدم والدم قد اختلف في وزنه فقال بعضهم دمي على وزن فعل

TABRISI:2:30#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r1.claim: A poem supports دم on فعل; another derives it as فعِل and explains the restored, vowelled yāʾ in its dual as evidence of its original form.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r1.anchor: فلو أنا على حجر ذبحنا جرى الدميان بالخبر اليقين

TABRISI:2:30#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r2.claim: Tasbih is declaring God free of evil and unworthy attributes; السبوح deserves glorification and القدوس purification and sanctification.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r2.anchor: والتسبيح التنزيه لله تعالى عن السوء وعما لا يليق به والسبوح المستحق للتنزيه والتعظيم

TABRISI:2:30#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r3.claim: تقديس means purification, opposed to defilement; القدس can also mean a vessel for washing.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r3.anchor: والتقديس التطهير ونقيضه التنجيس والقدس السطل الذي يتطهر منه

TABRISI:2:30#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:30#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh reports a pronunciation with fatḥa in سبوح قدوس; ḍamma is more common, while fatḥa is more analogical.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r4.anchor: وقد حكى سيبويه أن منهم من يقول سبوح قدوس بالفتح والضم أكثر في الكلام والفتح أقيس

TABRISI:2:30#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:30#2/r5.claim: سبحان means God's release from every evil and His sanctification; Sibawayh treats it as a fixed proper name, and poets use tanwin by necessity.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r5.anchor: قال سيبويه: سبحان الله معناه براءة الله من كل سوء وتنزيه الله

TABRISI:2:30#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r6.claim: سبحان derives from السبح, going or flowing; this supreme religious glorification is reserved for God, as worship is the highest gratitude due only to Him.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r6.anchor: وهو مشتق من السبح الذي هو الذهاب ولا يجوز أن يسبح غير الله وإن كان منزها

TABRISI:2:30#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:2:30#2/r7.claim: Abu Ubayda calls إذ extra; al-Zajjaj and others reject this because a particle that adds sound meaning cannot be discarded.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة إذ ههنا زائدة وأنكر الزجاج وغيره عليه هذا القول

TABRISI:2:30#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:30#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes إذ as a time marker: after mentioning creation, the verse means “at the time when your Lord said.”
TABRISI:2:30#2/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج: ومعناه الوقت ولما ذكر الله تعالى خلق الناس وغيرهم فكأنه قال

TABRISI:2:30#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r9.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:2:30#2/r9.claim: Ali ibn Isa supplies the omitted command اذكر, making إذ its accusative object.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r9.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى تقديره اذكر إذ قال ربك للملائكة فموضع إذ نصب على إضمار فعل

TABRISI:2:30#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r10.claim: إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة is the object clause of قال; the angels' speech is the object clause of قالوا.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r10.anchor: وإني جاعل في الأرض خليفة جملة في موضع نصب بقال

TABRISI:2:30#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r11.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:30#2/r11.claim: The waw of ونحن is circumstantial, also called the waw of interruption, resumption, or inception; the implied relation is إذ نحن.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r11.anchor: والواو في قوله ونحن واو الحال وتسمى واو القطع وواو الاستئناف وواو الابتداء

TABRISI:2:30#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r12.claim: The circumstantial phrase is governed by أتجعل فيها من يفسد; باء in بحمدك attaches to نسبح and لام in لك to نقدس.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r12.anchor: والعامل في الحال ههنا أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها وهذه حالنا والباء في بحمدك تتعلق بنسبح

TABRISI:2:30#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r13.claim: ما is a relative pronoun with an omitted object pronoun understood as لا تعلمونه; the clause is the accusative object of أعلم.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r13.anchor: وما موصولة وصلته لا تعلمون والعائد ضمير المفعول حذف لطول الكلام أي لا تعلمونه

TABRISI:2:30#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r14.claim: God announces to the angels that He will create Adam as a successor on earth; the address may be to all angels or to those settled on earth after the jinn, per Ibn Abbas.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r14.anchor: قيل إنه خطاب لجميع الملائكة وقيل خطاب لمن أسكنه الأرض بعد الجان من الملائكة عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:30#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r15.claim: The khalifa is Adam, God's deputy on earth who judges justly; Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud say God informed the angels that some descendants would corrupt.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r15.anchor: أراد بالخليفة آدم ع فهو خليفة الله في أرضه يحكم بالحق إلا أنه تعالى كان أعلم ملائكته

TABRISI:2:30#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#2/r16.claim: Another view calls Adam and his descendants successors to the angels who had inhabited earth before them.
TABRISI:2:30#2/r16.anchor: وقيل إنما سمى الله تعالى آدم خليفة لأنه جعل آدم وذريته خلفاء للملائكة

TABRISI:2:30#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:30#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that jinn lived on earth, corrupted it and shed blood, were destroyed, and were replaced by Adam and his descendants.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r1.anchor: والظاهر أنها الأرض المعروفة وهو الصحيح

TABRISI:2:30#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
TABRISI:2:30#3/r2.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri takes خليفة as Adam's descendants, who succeed one another and Adam in upholding justice and cultivating earth.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r2.anchor: والظاهر أنها الأرض المعروفة وهو الصحيح

TABRISI:2:30#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#3/r3.claim: A view takes الأرض as Mecca, citing its being the first land spread and a report about prophets' graves there; the author prefers the apparent, known earth.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r3.anchor: والظاهر أنها الأرض المعروفة وهو الصحيح

TABRISI:2:30#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r4.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:30#3/r4.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that the earth was spread out from Mecca, which is why it is called the Mother of Towns.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r4.anchor: والظاهر أنها الأرض المعروفة وهو الصحيح

TABRISI:2:30#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#3/r5.claim: A report places Noah, Hud, Salih, and Shuʿayb's graves between Zamzam and the Corner and Station.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r5.anchor: وروي أن قبر نوح وهود وصالح وشعيب بين زمزم والركن والمقام

TABRISI:2:30#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r6.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
TABRISI:2:30#3/r6.claim: Many commentators say angels expelled corrupt jinn from earth and asked whether God would place there beings like those former corrupters.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r6.anchor: كما فعل بنو الجان قاسوا بالشاهد على الغائب وهو قول كثير من المفسرين

TABRISI:2:30#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#3/r7.claim: A second view takes the angels' question as a request to understand the plan's wisdom, not an objection or claim of foreknowledge.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r7.anchor: وثانيها: أن الملائكة إنما قالت ذلك على سبيل الاستفهام وعلى وجه الاستخبار والاستعلام عن وجه المصلحة

TABRISI:2:30#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
TABRISI:2:30#3/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masud report that God told angels about future sinful descendants; He disclosed the unseen and events later confirmed His report.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r8.anchor: على ما روي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود والغرض في إعلامه إياهم يقينا على وجه علمه بالغيب

TABRISI:2:30#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#3/r9.claim: Another explanation says the announcement taught Adam he was created for earthly life, not Paradise; the angels sought the wisdom of that arrangement.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r9.anchor: وقيل ليعلم آدم أنه خلق للأرض لا للجنة فقالت الملائكة أتجعل فيها من يفعل كذا وكذا

TABRISI:2:30#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#3/r10.claim: This reading requires ellipsis: God knows future corruption and hidden interests, the angels implicitly compare their obedience with humans, and His reply supplies what they do not know.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r10.anchor: وهذا الوجه يقتضي أن يكون في أول الكلام حذف ويكون التقدير إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة وإني عالم

TABRISI:2:30#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#3/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#3/r11.claim: Such concise ellipsis is Qur'anic eloquence when the remaining wording signals what was omitted; the segment introduces al-Shanfara's poem as evidence.
TABRISI:2:30#3/r11.anchor: ومثل هذه الحذوف العجيبة والاختصارات البديعة كثيرة في القرآن والحذف معدود في أنواع الفصاحة

TABRISI:2:30#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r1.claim: The angels mean Adam's descendants who are neither prophets nor protected from sin, not Adam himself or other prophets and protected people.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r1.anchor: وإنما أرادت الملائكة بقولهم أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ولد آدم الذين ليسوا بأنبياء ولا معصومين

TABRISI:2:30#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r2.claim: Al-Shanfara's poem omits “do not bury me, but leave me to be eaten by the hyena”; the intended continuation is recoverable.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r2.anchor: ولا تقبروني إن قبري محرم عليكم ولكن خامري أم عامر

TABRISI:2:30#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r3.claim: Abu Dawud's poem omits “if you disapprove, leave”; the omitted clause follows from the conditional context.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r3.anchor: إن من شيمتي لبذل تردي دون عرضي فإن رضيت فكوني

TABRISI:2:30#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r4.claim: Antara's curse on a camel omits the wish that its milk dry up, explaining its inability to bear young and increased strength for travel.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r4.anchor: هل تبلغني دارها شدنية لعنت بمحروم الشراب مصرم

TABRISI:2:30#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:2:30#4/r5.claim: Mujahid says praising God is tasbih because praise exalts Him and recognizes He deserves glorification.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r5.anchor: وهذا تنزيه له واعتراف بأنه أهل لأن ينزه ويعظم ويثنى عليه عن مجاهد

TABRISI:2:30#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r6.claim: The angels' praise is compared with the wording about angels praising their Lord in 42:5.

TABRISI:2:30#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
TABRISI:2:30#4/r7.claim: A second explanation takes tasbih as prayer, as in 37:143 where Jonah is called one of the worshippers.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r7.anchor: أي من المصلين عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود

TABRISI:2:30#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r8.speaker: المفضل
TABRISI:2:30#4/r8.claim: Al-Mufaddal says it means raising one's voice in God's remembrance; Jarir's verse about pilgrims' loud praise illustrates the sense.

TABRISI:2:30#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r9.claim: One explanation is declaring God free of deficient attributes and unworthy things; on this reading the lām is extra.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r9.anchor: أي ننزهك عما لا يليق بك من صفات النقص ولا نضيف إليك القبائح فاللام على هذا زائدة

TABRISI:2:30#4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r10.claim: Other explanations take the phrase as praying for God's sake or purifying oneself from sins.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r10.anchor: وقيل نقدس لك أي نصلي لأجلك وقيل نطهر أنفسنا من الخطايا والمعاصي

TABRISI:2:30#4/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
TABRISI:2:30#4/r11.claim: One view is that God knows Satan's concealed pride, vanity, and disobedience when ordered to prostrate to Adam.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r11.anchor: وقيل أراد ما أضمره إبليس من الكبر والعجب والمعصية لما أمره الله سبحانه بالسجود لآدم عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود

TABRISI:2:30#4/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r12.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:30#4/r12.claim: Qatada says God knows which prophets and righteous people will descend from Adam.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r12.anchor: وقيل أراد أعلم من في ذرية آدم من الأنبياء والصالحين عن قتادة

TABRISI:2:30#4/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r13.claim: A further view takes the words to mean God's exclusive knowledge of how to manage people's interests.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r13.anchor: وقيل أراد به ما اختص الله تعالى بعلمه من تدبير المصالح

TABRISI:2:30#4/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r14.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:2:30#4/r14.claim: Abu Abdillah reports that angels asked to be khalifa because they obey unlike others; after learning they had overstepped, they sought forgiveness at the Throne, and God directed Adam to build an earthly refuge for sinners.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r14.anchor: وروي عن أبي عبد الله قال إن الملائكة سألت الله تعالى أن يجعل الخليفة منهم وقالوا نحن نقدسك ونطيعك ولا نعصيك

TABRISI:2:30#4/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r15.claim: God knows the interests better and does what is most fitting; the reply implies He does not perform evil, since otherwise it would have no force.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r15.anchor: وهذا يدل على أنه تعالى لا يفعل القبيح لأنه لو كان يحسن منه كل شيء لم يكن لهذا الكلام معنى

TABRISI:2:30#4/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:30#4/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:30#4/r16.claim: After recalling life, earth and its contents, and heaven as blessings, the passage turns to Adam's special excellence and returns to the argument of 2:28–29.
TABRISI:2:30#4/r16.anchor: أن الله تعالى ذكر أول النعم له علينا وهي نعمة الحياة ثم ذكر بعده إنعامه علينا بخلق الأرض وما فيها وبخلق السماء

THALABI:v1p175/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p175/r1.claim: Thaʿlabī explains malak as formed by dropping the hamza for ease and frequent use.
THALABI:v1p175/r1.anchor: ثم حذف الهمزة للخفة وكثير استعماله فقيل: ملك

THALABI:v1p175/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r2.speaker: النضر بن شميل
THALABI:v1p175/r2.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl says Arabs neither derive a verb from malak nor inflect it; its origin is beyond their knowledge.
THALABI:v1p175/r2.anchor: إن العرب لا تشتق فعله ولا تصرفه، وهو مما فات علمه

THALABI:v1p175/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p175/r3.claim: Khalifa means a replacement for those before, succeeding them after they depart.

THALABI:v1p175/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p175/r4.claim: A khalifa is one entrusted to carry out an order on behalf of the one who commands.
THALABI:v1p175/r4.anchor: فالخليفة من يتولى إمضاء الأمر عن الآمر

THALABI:v1p175/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r5.speaker: زيد بن علي
THALABI:v1p175/r5.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAli read khalifa with qaf as khalīqa.

THALABI:v1p175/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r6.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v1p175/r6.claim: Exegetes recount that jinn first worshipped on earth, then envy and aggression led them to fight and corrupt it.
THALABI:v1p175/r6.anchor: قال المفسرون: وذلك أن الله تعالى خلق السماء والأرض

THALABI:v1p175/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r7.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v1p175/r7.claim: An angelic force called jinn, led by Iblis, expelled the earlier jinn to mountains and sea islands and took over earth.
THALABI:v1p175/r7.anchor: يقال لهم: الجن، رأسهم عدو الله إبليس وهم خزان الجنان

THALABI:v1p175/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r8.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v1p175/r8.claim: God gave Iblis dominion over earth, the lowest heaven, and the gardens’ storehouses; he worshipped across earth, heaven, and paradise, then grew proud and resented removal when a successor was announced.
THALABI:v1p175/r8.anchor: وأعطى الله إبليس ملك الأرض وملك سماء الدنيا وخزانة الجنان، فكان يعبد الله تارة في الأرض،

THALABI:v1p175/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r9.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v1p175/r9.claim: The angels disliked the appointment because they worshipped less than the others and removal from their post was severe.
THALABI:v1p175/r9.anchor: لأنهم كانوا أهون في الملائكة عبادة، ولأن العزل شديد.

THALABI:v1p175/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p175/r10.claim: They explain corruption as sins and bloodshed as spilling blood without right.

THALABI:v1p175/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r11.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v1p175/r11.claim: Al-Suddi says God told the angels that the successor would have descendants who corrupt, envy, and kill one another, explaining how they knew the unseen.
THALABI:v1p175/r11.anchor: قال السدي: لما قال الله لهم ذلك، قالوا: وما يكون من ذلك الخليفة؟

THALABI:v1p175/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p175/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p175/r12.claim: The question is introduced with an implied fa, effectively meaning “so they said”; Thaʿlabī cites poetry for this omission.
THALABI:v1p175/r12.anchor: قالوا عند ذلك: أتجعل فيها ومعناه: فقالوا، فحذف فاء التنسيق.

THALABI:v1p176/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p176/r1.claim: The continuation of the quoted poem concludes the example for omitting the connective fa; its gloss is “so I was their neighbor.”
THALABI:v1p176/r1.anchor: كنت لهم من النصارى جارا أي فكنت لهم

THALABI:v1p176/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v1p176/r2.claim: Most exegetes say the angels inferred human corruption by analogy with the earlier jinn, reasoning from the witnessed to the unseen.
THALABI:v1p176/r2.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين: أرادوا كما فعل بنو الجان قاسوا بالشاهد على الغائب

THALABI:v1p176/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r3.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
THALABI:v1p176/r3.claim: Some grammarians supply an omitted alternative: will God appoint one who does not corrupt or shed blood? They compare the ellipsis in 39:9.
THALABI:v1p176/r3.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني: فيه إضمار واختصار معناه: أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها

THALABI:v1p176/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r4.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
THALABI:v1p176/r4.claim: Al-Hasan ibn al-Faḍl selects the interpretation that supplies the unstated contrast with people who do not corrupt or shed blood.

THALABI:v1p176/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r5.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p176/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says the angels utter “Glory and praise belong to God”; this is the creatures’ prayer and glorification, through which they receive provision.
THALABI:v1p176/r5.anchor: قال الحسن: يقولون: سبحان الله وبحمده، وهو صلاة الخلق

THALABI:v1p176/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
