THALABI:v1p176/r6.speaker: أبو ذر
THALABI:v1p176/r6.claim: Abu Dharr reports that the Prophet named the words God chose for His angels as the best speech.
THALABI:v1p176/r6.anchor: الحديث المروي عن أبي ذر إنه قال لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي الكلام أفضل؟

THALABI:v1p176/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p176/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes tasbih as prayer commanded by God; prayer is called subha.
THALABI:v1p176/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه: ونحن نصلي لك بأمرك، والتسبيح يكون بمعنى التنزيه

THALABI:v1p176/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p176/r8.claim: On the prayer interpretation, the angels pray and recite the Opening of the Book in their prayer.
THALABI:v1p176/r8.anchor: وقيل: معناه: نصلي، ونقرأ فيها فاتحة الكتاب.

THALABI:v1p176/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p176/r9.claim: Nuqaddisu means declaring God transcendent; on one analysis the lām is merely connective.

THALABI:v1p176/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p176/r10.claim: Alternatively, the lām marks purpose: the angels purify their hearts of associating partners with God and their bodies of disobedience for His sake.
THALABI:v1p176/r10.anchor: وقيل: هي لام الأجل، أي ونطهر لأجلك قلوبنا من الشرك بك

THALABI:v1p176/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r11.speaker: بعض العلماء
THALABI:v1p176/r11.claim: Some scholars reorder the sense as “we glorify and sanctify You by Your praise”: otherwise the angels seem to boast of their deeds, whereas this credits every act of worship to God.
THALABI:v1p176/r11.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: في الآية تقديم وتأخير مجازها: ونحن نسبح

THALABI:v1p176/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p176/r12.claim: God knows the benefit in appointing a successor on earth, so the angels should not object to His judgment and governance.
THALABI:v1p176/r12.anchor: إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون من استخلافي في الأرض ووجه المصلحة فيه، فلا تعترضوا

THALABI:v1p176/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p176/r13.claim: One reported explanation is that among those appointed on earth will be prophets, saints, scholars, and righteous people.
THALABI:v1p176/r13.anchor: وقيل: أراد أني أعلم أن في من استخلفه في الأرض: أنبياء وأولياء

THALABI:v1p176/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p176/r14.claim: Another explanation is that God knows humans will sin and that He will forgive them.
THALABI:v1p176/r14.anchor: وقيل: أني أعلم إنهم يذنبون وأغفر لهم.

THALABI:v1p176/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p176/r15.speaker: بعض الحكماء
THALABI:v1p176/r15.claim: A sage argues that Adam was destined to leave paradise before entering it: the earthly successor was announced first, and Adam’s later departure after sin shows divine decree.
THALABI:v1p176/r15.anchor: قال بعض الحكماء: إن الله تعالى أخرج [أدم] من الجنة قبل أن يدخله فيها .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p306/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p306/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p306/r1.claim: Grammarians classify idh and idha as time particles: idh is for the past and idha for the future.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p306/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p306/r2.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p306/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad says idh paired with a future-form verb gives it past meaning, as in ‘when he plotted’ (8:30).
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p306/r2.anchor: قال المبرد: إذا جاء (إذ) مع المستقبل كان معناه المضي نحو قوله: {وإذ يمكر}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r1.claim: The account says God had given Iblis dominion over earth, the lower heaven, and the gardens’ treasuries; he worshipped in these places, grew proud, and God disclosed his arrogance before announcing a successor on earth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r1.anchor: كان الله تعالى قد أعطى إبليس ملك الأرض وملك السماء الدنيا وخزانة الجنان، وكان يعبد الله عز وجل تارة في الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r2.claim: God’s informing the angels is glad tidings about Adam’s honored status, following the practice of announcing prophets before their creation and mission; it is not consultation, which is impossible for the omniscient God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r2.anchor: الله تعالى الملائكة بهذا يكون على جهة البشارة لهم بمكان آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r3.claim: Al-Farra says a coordinating fa is omitted before the angels’ speech, as in a poem where ‘I was a neighbor to them’ means ‘so I was a neighbor to them.’
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r3.anchor: قال الفراء (¬1): أراد: فقالوا فحذف فاء النسق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r4.claim: One report says ten thousand angels asked the question and God sent a fire that burned them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r4.anchor: فروي أن الذين قالوا هذا عشرة آلاف من الملائكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r5.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r5.claim: Some explain an omitted alternative: ‘Will You place one who corrupts and sheds blood, or one who does not?’ Like 39:9 and Abu Dhuʾayb’s ‘is her suitor rightly guided or astray?’, the angels ask to learn, not to object; God had not disclosed Adam’s descendants’ conduct.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r5.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني: فيه إضمار واختصار، معناه: أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r6.speaker: أبو ذؤيب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r6.claim: Abu Dhuʾayb’s verse supplies the ellipsis ‘rightly guided or astray’ as evidence for an omitted alternative in a question.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r6.anchor: وكقول أبي ذؤيب: عصيت إليها القلب إني لأمرها ... مطيع فما أدري أرشد طلابها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r7.claim: Another explanation is that the angels wondered whether the successor would be from the jinn, whose predecessors corrupted the earth, or from the angels, who glorify God; God did not reveal that Adam’s descendants would include both obedient and disobedient people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p323/r7.anchor: وقيل: لما قال الله: {إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة} أشكل على الملائكة أن الخليفة ممن يكون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r1.claim: Naqdis means to purify and declare God free of any unbefitting deficiency; taqdis and quds mean purification, and bayt al-maqdis is the purified house.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r1.anchor: و (التقديس): التطهير، والقدس: الطهارة، والبيت المقدس: المطهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj connects qudus, ‘bucket,’ with purification because one cleanses oneself using it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: ومن هذا قيل للسطل: قدس، لأنه يتقدس منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r3.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r3.claim: Another etymology says qiddas means silver beads because they are white and pure; a poetic line compares tears to a broken string of qiddas.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r3.anchor: قال غيره (¬7): والقداس هو (¬8) الجمان (¬9) من فضة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r4.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi says the angels declare God free of evil and refuse to attribute evil to Him; the lām is not purposive but functions like that in 27:72. He also analyzes al-muqaddas as either a verbal noun or a place, with bayt al-maqdis a place of purification cleansed of idols, as in 2:125.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: معنى نقدس لك: ننزهك عن السوء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq reads the lām as purposive: the angels purify themselves for God, cleansing their hearts of idolatry and bodies of disobedience; bayt al-maqdis is the purified house or place where one is purified of sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p331/r5.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: معنى: (نقدس لك) أي نطهر أنفسنا لك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says what God knew included Iblis’s concealed resolve to disobey and his pride.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the phrase refers to what Iblis’s affair would ultimately become.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r2.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: {ما لا تعلمون} مما يؤول إليه أمر إبليس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r3.claim: Qatada says God knew Adam’s descendants would include people who obey Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة (¬1): {أعلم ما لا تعلمون} أنه يكون في أولاد آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God tests those thought obedient and they may become disobedient, while those thought disobedient may become obedient.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: معناه أبتلي من تظنون أنه مطيع فيؤديه الابتلاء إلى المعصية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r5.claim: Another view is that God meant Adam’s superiority, the angels’ commanded prostration, and Adam’s advantage through knowledge of the names; the angels had assumed none would be more honored than they.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r5.anchor: وقيل: {إني أعلم ما لا تعلمون} من تفضيل آدم عليكم، وما أتعبدكم به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r6.claim: Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir pronounce the first-person yāʾ with fatḥa before an open hamza, as in innī aʿlam and innī arā; Abu Amr also does so before a kasra hamza, and Nafi adds cases before a ḍamma hamza.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r6.anchor: وفتح أبو عمرو وابن كثير (الياء) في قوله: {إني أعلم} [البقرة: 30]، {إني أرى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r7.claim: Those who open the yāʾ argue that its vowel is original, parallel to the addressee’s kaf; fatḥa is tolerated on yāʾ, as declension and forms with a preceding vowelless consonant show.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r7.anchor: أن هذه (الياء) أصلها الحركة، لأنها بإزاء الكاف للمخاطب، فكما فتحت الكاف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r8.claim: Those who leave the yāʾ vowelless argue that fatḥa, like the other vowels, is disliked with yāʾ; Arabic can suppress it even when grammar would otherwise require it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p333/r8.anchor: من أسكن هذه (الياءات) فحجته أن الفتحة مع

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#2/r1.claim: The introductory idh is extra; the sense is simply, “Your Lord said to the angels,” with its omission explained in al-Mushkil.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#2/r1.anchor: أراد: وقال ربك للملائكة، و"إذ" تزاد والمعنى إلقاؤها

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#2/r2.speaker: أهل النظر من أصحاب اللغة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#2/r2.claim: Linguists infer that God had told the angels the successor's descendants would corrupt and shed blood; the angels' question presupposes this information, and the account is abbreviated.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45#2/r2.anchor: يرى أهل النظر من أصحاب اللغة: أن الله جل وعز قال: إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r1.claim: Quddūs follows the faʿūl pattern and derives from quds, meaning purity.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r1.anchor: وهو حرف مبني على "فعول"؛ من "القدس" وهو: الطهارة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r3.claim: In the angels' statement, nuqaddisu laka means that they ascribe purity to God.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r3.anchor: {ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك} (4) ؛ أي: ننسبك إلى الطهارة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r4.claim: Nuqaddisuka and nuqaddisu laka, like nusabbihu laka and nusabbihuka, have the same meaning.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r4.anchor: و"نقدسك ونقدس لك" و"نسبح لك ونسبحك" بمعنى واحد.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r5.speaker: أهل النظر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r5.claim: The people of speculation identify Ḥaẓīrat al-Quds as Paradise, a place purified from worldly impurities such as excrement, urine, and menstruation.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p8#2/r5.anchor: حظيرة القدس - فيما قاله أهل النظر - هي: الجنة. لأنها موضع الطهارة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad to recall and tell them when his Lord spoke to the angels.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r1.anchor: واذكر لهم يا محمد إذ قال ربك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r2.claim: The khalīfa is Adam, successor to the angels who had inhabited the earth after the jinn; the story recalls the beginning of human creation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r2.anchor: جعله خليفة عن الملائكة الذين كانوا سكان الأرض بعد الجن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r3.claim: The angels anticipated human corruption by analogy with the jinn, reasoning from the known to the unseen.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r3.anchor: كما فعل بنو الجان، قاسوا [الشاهد] على الغائب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r4.claim: The angels declare God free of every evil and say, Glory and praise belong to God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r4.anchor: نبرئك من كل سوء، ونقول: سبحان الله وبحمده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r5.claim: They declare God transcendent above whatever is unbefitting Him.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r6.claim: What God knew and the angels did not was Iblis’s concealed resolve to disobey.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r6.anchor: من إضمار إبليس العزم على المعصية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r7.claim: The angels privately concluded that their Lord would create no creature more knowledgeable than they were.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r7.anchor: لن يخلق ربنا خلقا هو أعلم منا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r8.claim: God favored Adam over the angels through knowledge and taught him the names of every thing, down to ordinary utensils.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:30/r8.anchor: وعلمه اسم كل شيء حتى القصعة

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r1.claim: From 2:28 onward, the passage counters disbelief and ingratitude with proofs and blessings; 2:30–35 then presents stewardship, knowledge, angelic prostration, and the Garden.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r1.anchor: 30-35. âyetlerde hilâfet, ilim, meleklerin secdesi ve cennet nimetleri sıralanmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r2.claim: Although 4:1 and 39:6 later describe Adam's creation and human reproduction, this passage concerns capacities, responsibilities, authority, and blessings bestowed on humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r2.anchor: Burada anlatılan insanın yaratılması değil, Allah tarafından ona verilen özellikler, sorumluluklar, yetki ve nimetlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r3.claim: Khilāfa means succeeding another, representing that person, or exercising that person's authority.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r3.anchor: Sözlükte hilâfet, “bir kimsenin diğerinin yerini alması, onu temsil etmesi, onun salâhiyetlerini kullanması” mânasına gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r4.claim: One possible referent is earlier conscious beings who lived on earth, whom Adam and humanity succeeded.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r4.anchor: daha önce yeryüzünde yaşamış şuurlu varlıkların halifesidir; onların yerine gelmiş, onların yerini almıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r5.claim: The commentary prefers that Adam and humanity are God's stewards: the angels' question, God's test, and Adam's knowledge and capacities show his fitness for that role.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r5.anchor: buradaki hilâfetin Allah ile ilgili olduğunu, Âdem’in ve insanoğlunun yeryüzünde Allah’ın halifesi olacaklarını göstermektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r6.claim: The promise to establish a community as stewards is conditioned on faith and righteous conduct, supporting the interpretation of stewardship as service under God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r6.anchor: Bir ümmeti yeryüzünde halife kılmak, onlara “hilâfet yetkisi vermek”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r7.claim: Human stewardship is limited to human nature and capacities; no creature can represent God, take God's place, or exercise God's authority.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r7.anchor: İnsan dahil hiçbir varlığın Allah Teâlâ’yı temsil etmesi, O’nun yerini alarak tasarrufta bulunması mümkün değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r8.claim: Adam and his descendants exercise stewardship by living on God's earth in accordance with God's will and instructions.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r8.anchor: Âdem’in ve neslinin halifeliği, Allah’ın mülkü bulunan yeryüzünde O’nun iradesine uygun yaşamak ve tâlimatı doğrultusunda tasarrufta bulunmaktan ibarettir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r9.claim: The verses about humanity's creation to worship God and its creation as steward express one truth; worldly blessings are allotted to serve that purpose.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r9.anchor: İnsanların Allah’a kul olsunlar diye yaratıldıklarını ifade eden âyetle (Zâriyât 51/56) halifeler olarak yaratıldıklarını ifade eden âyetler aynı gerçeği anlatmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r10.claim: People must recognize their opportunities and blessings as God's property, entrusted for a purpose and condition, and use them according to God's will and approval.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r10.anchor: İnsanoğlu kendisine verilen imkân ve nimetlerin Allah’ın mülkü olduğunu, bir amaca ve şarta bağlı olarak kendisine emanet edildiğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r11.claim: Unlike angels, humans have the nature and capacity to fulfill stewardship, provided they do not corrupt their innate disposition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r11.anchor: Meleklerden farklı olarak insanoğlu bu hilâfeti gerçekleştirecek fıtratta ve kabiliyette yaratılmış olup fıtratını bozmadığı takdirde bu vazifesini başarabilecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r12.claim: Through the account of the angels, God also informs humanity about this responsibility and instills awareness of it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r12.anchor: Allah Teâlâ meleklerin şahsında bunu insanoğluna da bildirip şuuruna yerleştirmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r13.claim: General stewardship is not exclusive to Adam; other verses explicitly extend this capacity and authority to all people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r13.anchor: buradaki hilâfet (genel hilâfet), yalnızca Âdem’e mahsus değildir; birçok âyet

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r14.claim: Political caliphate is a concept and institution that arose after the Prophet from practical need; the Qur'an does not use the term for it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r14.anchor: Özel (siyasî) hilâfet, Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de bu isimle bulunmayan, Hz. Peygamber’den sonra ihtiyacın ortaya çıkardığı bir kavram ve kurumdur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r15.claim: The Qur'anic term for those who perform the political function of caliphate is ulu al-amr.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r15.anchor: Siyasî anlamda hilâfet fonksiyonunu üslenenler için Kur’an’da kullanılan tabir “ülü’l-emr”dir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r16.claim: A hadith says caliphate lasts thirty years after the Prophet and is followed by oppressive rule; if authentic, it is the first use of caliphate as an office in Islamic sources, though its authenticity is questioned.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r16.anchor: “Hilâfet benden sonra otuz yıldır, daha sonra ısırıcı saltanat yönetimi olacaktır” meâlindeki hadiste

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r17.claim: Abu Bakr was called the Messenger of God's caliph because he succeeded him as head of state; Umar was called the caliph's caliph, after which the shorter title caliph prevailed, alongside titles such as commander of the faithful and imam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r17.anchor: Hz. Ebû Bekir, devlet başkanlığı bakımından Resûlullah’ın yerini aldığı için (bu sebeple) kendisine “Resûlullah’ın halifesi” denilmiş, Hz. Ömer’den “Resûlullah’ın halifesinin halifesi” diye söz edilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r18.claim: Political organization is needed to fulfill duties assigned to the community as a whole; individuals conditionally transfer their supra-individual authority and responsibility to a worthy person.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r18.anchor: ferdin halifeliği yanında ümmetin halifeliğini de hayata geçirebilmek için siyasî teşkilâtlanmaya ihtiyaç hâsıl olmuş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r19.claim: The pledge of obedience to a caliph is conditional on the caliph following God's commands and prohibitions and the religious rules governing the office.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r19.anchor: Halifeye verilen itaat sözü (biat), onun Allah’ın emir ve yasaklarına (hukuka, göreviyle ilgili dinî hükümlere) uygun davranması şartına bağlıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r20.speaker: Melekler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r20.claim: The angels, created earlier in the malakut realm and unlike humans, expected themselves to govern earth and enact the divine will stated plainly in a book binding on every believer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r20.anchor: Asıl vatanları olan melekût âleminde daha önce yaratılmış ve insandan farklı özelliklerle donatılmış bulunan melekler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r21.speaker: Melekler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r21.claim: The angels considered an earth-born human deficient and prone to corruption, and therefore unfit for stewardship; God disclosed his contrary will and its rationale.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r21.anchor: topraktan yaratılacak insanın bu kaynağa bağlı özellikleri dolayısıyla eksikleri olacağı, fesat çıkarmaya müsait bulunacağı için hilâfete lâyık olmadığını zannetmişlerdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r22.claim: Human knowledge of angels is chiefly revelation-based because people cannot know beings of the unseen and malakut through ordinary means; interpretations drawn by human reasoning and analogy differ.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r22.anchor: Meleklerin varlıkları ve özellikleriyle ilgili bilgiler büyük ölçüde vahye dayanmakla beraber akıl, keşif ve tecrübe yoluyla da meleklerin varlıklarının

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r23.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r23.claim: Some maintain that reason, spiritual unveiling, and experience can establish the existence of angels and some of their attributes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r23.anchor: akıl, keşif ve tecrübe yoluyla da meleklerin varlıklarının ve bazı özelliklerinin bilinebileceği ileri sürülmüştür

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r24.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r24.claim: An a fortiori argument says that if mortal conscious beings exist, immortal ones can also exist, and intelligent beings in the lower world make such beings in the nobler heavens all the more plausible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r24.anchor: Akıl ve şuur sahibi (nâtık) ölümlü varlıklar yaratılmış bulunduğuna göre bunların, dünya durdukça ölümsüz olanlarının da yaratılmış olması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r25.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r25.claim: Accounts from spiritually trained people, people aided by angels in helplessness caused by distress or illness, and people who see angels in dreams are cited as personal experiences.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r25.anchor: Özel ruhî temrinler yapan ve eğitim gören kimselerin, sıkıntı ve hastalıktan çaresiz kalıp meleklerin yardımlarından istifade edenlerin ve melekleri rüyada görenlerin nakilleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r26.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r26.claim: Such accounts provide subjective certainty to the experiencers but do not bind those who hear them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r26.anchor: kendileri için sübjektif anlamda kesin delildir, bunları duyanlar için ise bağlayıcı değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r27.speaker: Müslüman âlimlerin çoğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r27.claim: Most Muslim scholars describe angels as subtle, shape-shifting beings whose primary abode is the transcendent heavens and who multiply through continual creation rather than reproduction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r27.anchor: Müslüman âlimlerin çoğuna göre melekler, latîf (madde yoğunluğu olmayan, görüşü engellemeyen), çeşitli şekillere girebilen ve asıl yerleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r28.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r28.claim: Angels have high rank, nearness to God, and great powers bestowed by him; they are set to act according to divine command and will and never depart from it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r28.anchor: Allah nezdinde yüce değerleri ve yakınlıkları, O’nun bahşettiği büyük güçleri vardır, ilâhî emir ve iradeye göre davranmak ve asla bunun dışına çıkmamak üzere programlanmışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r29.speaker: Bazı filozoflar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r29.claim: Some philosophers regard angels as beings of intellect, analogous to the human intellect.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r29.anchor: Bazı filozoflara göre ise melekler insandaki akıl türünden varlıklardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r30.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r30.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r30.claim: One class of angels bears the Throne.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r30.anchor: Kur’an’daki açıklamalara göre melekleri, özellik ve vazifeleri bakımından şu sınıflara ayırmak mümkündür: 1. Arşı taşıyanlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r31.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r31.claim: Another class surrounds the Throne and glorifies God.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r32.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r32.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r32.claim: Gabriel, also called Jibril and the Holy Spirit, is tasked with bringing revelation to the prophets.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r32.anchor: Cibrîl ve Rûhulkudüs isimleriyle de anılan bu melek peygamberlere vahiy getirmekle görevlendirilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r33.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r33.claim: The Qur'an describes Gabriel as noble, powerful, honored, respected, and trustworthy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r33.anchor: Tekvîr sûresinin 20. âyetinde onun belli başlı sıfatları şöyle sıralanmıştır: “Gerçekten değerli, güçlü ve Arş’ın sahibi katında itibarlı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r34.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r34.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r34.claim: Michael is assigned to regulate natural events; the Qur'an mentions him with Gabriel and says God is an enemy to their enemies.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r34.anchor: Mîkâil, tabiat olaylarını dengelemek ile görevli melektir. Cebrâil’le birlikte adı Kur’an’da anılmış ve bunlara düşman olana Allah’ın düşman olacağı bildirilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r35.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r35.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r35.claim: The Qur'an mentions the trumpet to be blown at the beginning of the resurrection and revival.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r35.anchor: Kıyamet ve yeniden diriliş başlarken üflenecek olan sûr, Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de zikredilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r36.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r36.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r36.claim: Hadith reports identify Israfil as the angel assigned to blow the trumpet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r36.anchor: Bu sûra üflemekle görevlendirilmiş meleğin İsrâfil olduğu da hadislerde bildirilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r37.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r37.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r37.claim: The Qur'an mentions both an angel of death and angels charged with taking people's lives.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r37.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de hem ölüm meleğinden (Secde 32/11) hem de vefat ettirme görevini yüklenmiş meleklerden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r38.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r38.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r38.claim: Although the name does not occur in sahih hadith, other Islamic literature calls the angel of death Azrail.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r38.anchor: Sahih hadislerde bu isim geçmemekle beraber diğer İslâmî literatürde ölüm meleği Azrâil olarak anılır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r39.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r39.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r39.claim: Because many angels are assigned to take lives, Azrail may be their chief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r39.anchor: Bu işle görevlendirilen melek sayısı çok olduğuna göre Azrâil’in bunların reisi olması ihtimali vardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r40.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r40.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r40.claim: Many angels are in Paradise to serve believers who enter it; their leader is called Ridvan.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r40.anchor: Cennette çok sayıda meleğin bulunduğu ve buraya girme mutluluğuna erişmiş müminlere hizmet edecekleri ifade buyurulmuştur (Ra‘d 13/23). Bu meleklerin başkanına “Rıdvan” denir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r41.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r41.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r41.claim: Hell has angels who perform duties toward those suffering punishment; they are called zabani, and their leader is Malik.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r41.anchor: Burada da azap çekenlerle ilgili vazifelerini yerine getiren melekler vardır (Müddessir 74/31). Bunların cins ismi “zebâni”dir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r42.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r42.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r42.claim: Guardian angels accompany people, watch over and protect them, wish them well, and inspire good things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r42.anchor: Bunlar insanların yanlarında bulunmakta, onları gözetme, koruma, iyiliklerini isteme, onlara iyi şeyleri ilham etme gibi vazifeler yapmaktadırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r43.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r43.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r43.claim: Recording angels remain near people and write down all their deeds.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r43.anchor: Bunlar da insanların yakınlarında bulunmakta ve yapıp ettikleri her şeyi yazmaktadırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r44.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r44.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r44.claim: Angels assigned to the material realm are present throughout the physical cosmos and ensure God's laws are carried out there.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r44.anchor: Bunlar maddî kâinatta olup biten her şeyin içinde bulunmakta ve Allah’ın kanunlarının yerine gelmesini sağlamaktadırlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r45.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r45.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r45.claim: One proposed explanation is that the angels learned about human wrongdoing from the Preserved Tablet, where future events are recorded.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r46.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r46.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r46.claim: Another proposal is that similar beings had earlier been created and sent to earth, and the angels learned by observing them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r46.anchor: daha önce yaratılıp yeryüzüne gönderilmiş benzer varlıklar olabileceği ve bunlara bakarak bilgi sahibi oldukları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r47.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r47.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r47.claim: A further explanation is that the angels inferred human conduct by analogy with jinn or predatory animals.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r47.anchor: cinlere veya yırtıcı hayvanlara kıyas ettikleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r48.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r48.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r48.claim: The commentary finds two explanations more reasonable, closer to reality, and more consistent with the narrative style.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r48.anchor: Biz şu iki ihtimali ve yorumu akla ve vâkıaya daha yakın ve hadisenin anlatılış üslûbuna daha yatkın buluyoruz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r49.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r49.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r49.claim: The angels may have stated their opinion after God first introduced the human he would create and announced his appointment as steward.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r49.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın yaratacağı insanı onlara önce tanıtması, sonra da onu yeryüzüne halife yapacağını bildirmesi üzerine –bu bilgiye dayanarak– kanaatlerini açıklamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r50.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r50.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r50.claim: Alternatively, the angels may have witnessed Adam's creation and inferred from his material and spiritual traits that he could do both good and evil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:30/r50.anchor: Âdem’in yaratılışını müşahede etmişler, onun maddî ve mânevî özelliklerini görüp bilmişler ve bu özellikleri taşıyan bir varlığın hem iyi hem kötü işler yapabileceğini

NAHHAS:v1p206/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
NAHHAS:v1p206/r9.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says «إذ» is a temporal adverb and is not an extra word.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r9.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة إذ اسم وهو ظرف زمان ليس مما يزاد

NAHHAS:v1p206/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p206/r10.claim: Abū Isḥāq connects the mention of human and other creation to an implied beginning: their creation began when the Lord spoke to the angels.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r10.anchor: ذكر الله عز وجل خلق الناس وغيرهم فالتقدير ابتدأ خلقهم إذ قال ربك

NAHHAS:v1p206/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r11.claim: «الملائكة» is genitive after the lām; the group is grammatically feminine.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r11.anchor: ( للملائكة ) خفض باللام والهاء لتأنيث الجماعة

NAHHAS:v1p206/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r12.claim: The yāʾ in «إني» is accusative and «جاعل» is the predicate of «إن»; the original «إنني» loses a nūn where two meet.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r12.anchor: ( إني جاعل في الأرض ) الياء في موضع نصب جاعل خبر أن والأصل إنني

NAHHAS:v1p206/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r13.claim: «الأرض» is genitive after «في», while «خليفة» is accusative after «جاعل».
NAHHAS:v1p206/r13.anchor: في الأرض خفض بفي ( خليفة ) نصب بجاعل

NAHHAS:v1p206/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r14.claim: «خليفة» is the object of «جاعل»; its tanwīn cannot be omitted with the intervening phrase, though it could if the object immediately followed.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r14.anchor: ( خليفة ) نصب بجاعل ولا يجوز حذف التنوين للفصل

NAHHAS:v1p206/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r15.claim: «خليفة» may be active: one who succeeds the angels or other predecessors in the earth, as also related.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r15.anchor: خليفة يكون بمعنى فاعل أي يخلف من كان قبله من الملائكة

NAHHAS:v1p206/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r16.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r16.claim: Alternatively «خليفة» may be passive, one who is succeeded.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r16.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون خليفة بمعنى مفعول أي يخلف كما يقال ذبيحة بمعنى مفعولة

NAHHAS:v1p206/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r18.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r18.claim: «من يفسد» is accusative as the first object of «تجعل»; «فيها» supplies the second object's position on the singular wording.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r18.anchor: ( فيها من يفسد ) في موضع نصب بتجعل والمفعول الثاني يقوم مقامه فيها يفسد على اللفظ

NAHHAS:v1p206/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r19.claim: Outside the Qurʾānic wording, the plural «يفسدون» is possible by sense.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r19.anchor: ويجوز في غير القرآن يفسدون على المعنى

NAHHAS:v1p206/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r20.speaker: الأعرج
NAHHAS:v1p206/r20.claim: Al-Aʿraj is reported to read «ويسفك الدماء» with «الدماء» in the accusative as the answer to the question introduced by wāw.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r20.anchor: وروي عن الأعرج ( ويسفك الدماء ) بالنصب يجعله جواب الاستفهام بالواو

NAHHAS:v1p206/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r21.claim: The singular of «الدماء» is «دم»; no noun has only two letters without an omitted letter, here a yāʾ retained in poetic usage.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r21.anchor: وواحد الدماء دم ولا يكون اسم على حرفين إلا وقد حذف منه والمحذوف منه ياء

NAHHAS:v1p206/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r22.speaker: الشاعر
NAHHAS:v1p206/r22.claim: An unnamed poet's «الدميان» shows the original yāʾ in the dual form of «دم».
NAHHAS:v1p206/r22.anchor: قال الشاعر ( فلو أنا على حجر ذبحنا … جرى الدميان بالخبر اليقين )

NAHHAS:v1p206/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r23.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r23.claim: The nūn cannot be assimilated into the following nūn because the result would put two quiescent consonants together.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r23.anchor: ( ونحن نسبح بحمدك ) لا يجوز إدغام النون في النون لئلا يلتقي ساكنان

NAHHAS:v1p206/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r24.speaker: من حرك الياء
NAHHAS:v1p206/r24.claim: Those who vocalize the yāʾ in «إني» avoid leaving a one-letter noun without a vowel.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r24.anchor: من حرك الياء فقال إني اعلم ما كره أن يكون اسم على حرف واحد ساكنا

NAHHAS:v1p206/r25.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r25.speaker: من أسكنها
NAHHAS:v1p206/r25.claim: Those who leave the yāʾ quiescent say it has joined to what precedes it.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r25.anchor: ومن أسكنها قال قد اتصلت بما قبلها

NAHHAS:v1p206/r26.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r26.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r26.claim: «أعلم» can be a present verb or a participle meaning “knowing,” as «الله أكبر» can mean “God is great.”
NAHHAS:v1p206/r26.anchor: اعلم فعل مستقبل ويجوز أن يكون اسما بمعنى فاعل كما يقال الله أكبر بمعنى كبير

BURHAN:v1p139/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p139/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p139/r2.claim: The inventory records where parallel Qur'anic phrases include or omit letters and vary in form, including this opening with waw in Baqarah, al-Hijr, and Sad.
BURHAN:v1p139/r2.anchor: ﴿ وإذ قال ربك للملائكة ﴾ بواو فى البقرة والحجر وص

BURHAN:v3p459/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p459/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p459/r2.claim: The angels' wording pairs corruption with glorification and bloodshed with sanctification: glorification supports reform, while sanctification protects blood; the latter is nobler.
BURHAN:v3p459/r2.anchor: فقابل الإفساد بالتسبيح والحمد وسفك الدماء بالتقديس

BURHAN:v3p459/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p459/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p459/r3.claim: The four terms form earthly and heavenly pairs, with the soul positioned between them; corruption and sanctification are the far ends, and the middle terms bridge earth and heaven.
BURHAN:v3p459/r3.anchor: وهذا شكل مربع من أرضى وهو الإفساد وسفك الدماء وسمائي وهو التسبيح والتقديس

BURHAN:v3p459/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p459/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p459/r4.claim: Al-Zarkashi calls this analysis profound and says it opens further insights into Qur'anic passages, including the Throne Verse.
BURHAN:v3p459/r4.anchor: وهذا القدر الذي ذكره هذا الحبر مرمى عظيم يوصل إلى أمور غير متجاسر عليها

BURHAN:v1p261/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p261/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p261/r2.claim: The Ottoman order of Baqarah, Ali Imran, al-Nisa, then al-Ma'idah is especially well arranged; Ibn Masud's codex put al-Nisa before Ali Imran, and surah order was chosen by scholarly judgment, not divinely prescribed.
BURHAN:v1p261/r2.anchor: وهذا الترتيب بين هذه السور الأربع المدنيات البقرة وآل عمران والنساء والمائدة من أحسن الترتيب

BURHAN:v1p261/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p261/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p261/r3.claim: The Qur'an was not collected as a codex during the Prophet's life while revelation continued; Abu Bakr and the Companions compiled it after his death, then Uthman copied and dispatched codices.
BURHAN:v1p261/r3.anchor: فلهذا تأخرت كتابته إلى أن كمل نزول القرآن بموته صلى الله عليه وسلم فكتب أبو بكر والصحابة بعده

BURHAN:v3p266/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p266/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p266/r6.claim: Delaying the person praised or blamed can emphasize the intended focus: نعم الرجل زيد is stronger than placing Zayd first.
BURHAN:v3p266/r6.anchor: ومن هذا أن تأخر المقصود بالمدح والذم أولى من تقدمه

ITQAN:v3p243#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p243#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p243#3/r1.claim: Tadmin has four senses: using a word for another whose meaning it contains; implying a meaning without naming it; linking post-rhyme wording to the rhyme; and embedding another's speech to reinforce meaning or structure.
ITQAN:v3p243#3/r1.anchor: يطلق على أشياء أحدهما إيقاع لفظ موقع غيره لتضمنه معناه وهو نوع من المجاز

ITQAN:v3p243#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p243#3/r2.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v3p243#3/r2.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isba says he found Qur'anic examples only in two places, each incorporating a passage from the Torah or Gospel: “life for life” and “Muhammad is God's messenger.”
ITQAN:v3p243#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن أبي الإصبع ولم أظفر في القرآن بشيء منه إلا في موضعين تضمنا فصلين من التوراة والأنجيل

ITQAN:v3p243#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p243#3/r3.speaker: ابن النقيب
ITQAN:v3p243#3/r3.claim: Ibn al-Naqib and others broaden the examples to include creatures' reported speech, such as the angels, hypocrites, Jews, and Christians, and foreign-language material.
ITQAN:v3p243#3/r3.anchor: ومثله ابن النقيب وغيره بإيداع حكايات المخلوقين في القرآن

ITQAN:v1p250#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r1.claim: “Major” idgham has a moving first letter in the pair, whether the letters are identical, alike in articulation, or near in articulation or quality; several explanations are given for its name.
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r1.anchor: فالكبير ما كان أول الحرفين فيه متحركا سواء كانا مثلين أم جنسين أم متقاربين وسمي كبيرا لكثرة وقوعه

ITQAN:v1p250#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r2.claim: Among the ten imams, Abu Amr ibn al-Ala is especially associated with major idgham; it is also reported from al-Hasan al-Basri, al-A'mash, Ibn Muhaysin, and others.
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r2.anchor: والمشهور بنسبته إليه من الإئمة العشرة هو أبو عمرو بن العلاء وورد عن جماعة خارج العشرة كالحسن البصري والأعمش

ITQAN:v1p250#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r3.claim: Its purpose is ease of pronunciation, though many prominent works on readings do not mention it.
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r3.anchor: ووجهه طلب التخفيف وكثير من المصنفين في القراءات لم يذكروه البتة كأبي عبيد

ITQAN:v1p250#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r4.claim: Mutamathilain share articulation and quality; mutajanisain share articulation but differ in quality; mutaqaribain are close in articulation or quality.
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r4.anchor: ونعني بالمتماثلين ما اتفقا مخرجا وصفة والمتجانسين ما اتفقا مخرجا واختلفا صفة وبالمتقاربين ما تقاربا مخرجا أو صفة

ITQAN:v1p250#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r5.claim: Idgham among identical letters occurs across seventeen letters; the verse's “we glorify You” is one example, as are other cited letter pairs.
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r5.anchor: فأما المدغم من المتماثلين فوقع في سبعة عشر حرفا وهي الباء والتاء والثاء والحاء والراء

ITQAN:v1p250#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r6.claim: The conditions include matching in writing and usually meeting across two words; exceptions include مناسككم and ما سلككم, while pronoun tāʾ, a doubled first letter, and tanwin prevent idgham.
ITQAN:v1p250#2/r6.anchor: وشرطه أن يلتقي المثلان خطا فلا يدغم

ITQAN:v2p525/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p525/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p525/r1.claim: The third category is wāw of circumstance, which enters a nominal clause, as in the angels' “while we glorify You.”
ITQAN:v2p525/r1.anchor: ثالثها واو الحال الداخلة على الجملة الاسمية نحو

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r1.claim: Zuhayr’s horses and pack animals do not denote literal mounts; the image says youthful desire has departed, like a journey’s purpose fulfilled and its animals unloaded.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r1.anchor: وليس ألا انك أردت أن الصبا قد ترك واهمل وفقد نزاع النفس اليه وبطل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r2.claim: One may read the horses as youthful impulses and powers, but this is strained and should not be imposed on every image.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r2.anchor: وقد يجىء وإن كان كالتكلف أن تقول إن الأفراس عبارة عن دواعي النفوس وشهواتها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r3.claim: Farazdaq’s mount in ignorance means that he often hurried into falsehood and ignorance; an elaborate allegory would miss the immediate sense.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r3.anchor: وذلك أن المعنى على قولك لطالما سعيت في الباطل وقديما كنت في الإسراع إلى الجهل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r4.claim: In ‘loose reins,’ take the equestrian image as a mental picture transferred to a person; interpreting the reins as restraint is needless overreading.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r4.anchor: وكذا قولهم هو مرخى العنان وملقى الزمام لا وجه لأن تتوقع إلا وأن تجرى العنان عليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r5.claim: The image works by abstracting the horse’s condition in the mind and then imagining a person according to that condition.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p36/r5.anchor: على انتزاع الشبه من الفرس في حال ما يرخى عنانه وإن ينظر إلى الصورة التي توجد من حاله تلك في العقل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p301/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p301/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p301/r1.claim: Al-Mutanabbi’s point is that noble qualities are intrinsically noble: neither a person’s bodily sex nor a name’s grammatical gender adds or removes their merit.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p301/r1.anchor: وذلك أن الصفات الشريفة شريفة بأنفسها وليس شرفها من حيث الموصوف وكيف والأوصاف سبب التفاضل بين الموصوفات

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p301/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p301/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p301/r2.claim: The reading that a virtuous woman is ‘a man in meaning’ is rejected: it conflicts with the moon example and makes the couplet self-contradictory.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p301/r2.anchor: لا أن يقال إن المعنى أن المرأة إذا كانت في كمال الرجل من حيث العقل والفضل وسائر الخلال الممدوحة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r1.claim: The first poet reverses the analogy: a spear’s shaking resembles an animal’s tremor in appearance, but does not arise from an animal’s pain or fear.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r1.anchor: أن كون حركات الرمح في ظاهر حركة المرتعد لا يوجب أن يكون ذلك من ألم عارض وكأنه عكس القضية

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r2.speaker: ابن المعتز
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r2.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz gives the sword’s trembling the same actual cause as trembling in an animal.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r2.anchor: وأما ابن المعتز فحقق كونها في السيف على حقيقة العلة التي لها تكون في الحيوان فاعرفه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r3.claim: Al-Buhturi makes the spears’ thrusting look like stumbling and treats it as an action with a cause, paralleling Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s sword image.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r3.anchor: جعل فعل الطاعن بالرماح تعثرا منها كما جعل ابن المعتز تحريكه للسيف وهزه له ارتعادا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r4.claim: These poets feign that the source of a comparison is actually present, then invent a cause for it: a sky-earth marriage, a buried beloved in clouds, or a released fasting fetter.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r4.anchor: كل واحد من هؤلاء خدع نفسه عن التشبيه وغالطها واوهم أن الذي جرى العرف بان يؤخذ منه الشبه قد حضر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r5.claim: Snow as camphor and cloud-rain as tears are familiar comparisons; the crescent as a broken fetter is novel, though a broken bracelet supplies a parallel image.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p251/r5.anchor: والفرق بين بيت السرى وبيتي الطائيين أن تشبيه الثلج بالكافور معتاد عامي جار على الألسن

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r1.claim: Fronting the person or topic before its predicate alerts the listener to whom the report concerns; it does not claim that the action belongs exclusively to them.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r1.anchor: من تنبيه السامع لقصدهم بالحديث من قبل ذكر الحديث ليحقق الأمر ويؤكده

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r2.speaker: صاحب الكتاب
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r2.claim: Sibawayh explains that fronting an object and resuming it with a pronoun first calls attention to it, then predicates the action of it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r2.anchor: فقال : وإنما قلت عبد الله فنبهته له ، ثم بنيت عليه الفعل ورفعته بالابتداء

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r3.claim: An ungoverned noun signals that a predication about it is intended; the listener is prepared for the report, which therefore lands more firmly and with less doubt.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r3.anchor: لا يؤتى بالاسم معرى من العوامل إلا لحديث قد نوي إسناده إليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r4.claim: He cites the fronted topic in the statement about adopted deities as a clear Qur'anic instance of drawing attention before the predicate.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r4.anchor: واتخذوا من دونه آلهة لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r5.claim: He also cites the wording about people arriving professing faith as another clear instance of mentioning the topic before its report.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p111/r5.anchor: وإذا جاؤوكم قالوا آمنا وقد دخلوا بالكفر وهم قد خرجوا به

TAB-FULL:v1p527/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r2.claim: God's disclosure of unseen matters to Muhammad, inaccessible except by revelation, establishes his prophethood before the Jews and shows his message comes from God.
TAB-FULL:v1p527/r2.anchor: احتج فيها لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم على من كان بين ظهرانيه من يهود بني إسرائيل بإطلاعه إياه من علوم الغيب

BURHAN:v1p155/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p155/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p155/r5.claim: The context identifies the unnamed vicegerent in God's announcement to the angels as Adam.

BURHAN:v4p400/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p400/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p400/r4.claim: Ma is declarative or relative before laysa, lam, or la, and after illa, as in the cited examples.
BURHAN:v4p400/r4.anchor: إذا جاءت قبل ليس أو لم أو لا أو بعد إلا فإنها تكون خبرية

BURHAN:v4p207/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p207/r6.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v4p207/r6.claim: Some treat إذ in the creation account as extra; another analysis takes it to mean قد.

BURHAN:v2p342/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p342/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v2p342/r1.claim: Two interpretations of the angels' question ask whether God will put them there or the speakers there, or whether their situation will change.
BURHAN:v2p342/r1.anchor: وقيل المعنى اتجعلهم فيها أم تجعلنا وقيل المعنى تجعلهم وحالنا هذه أم يتغير

BURHAN:v3p91/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p91/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p91/r6.claim: God’s answer to the angels’ question about corruption presupposes wisdom and interests known to Him; otherwise neither their question about His wisdom nor this answer would make sense.

BURHAN:v2p387/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p387/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p387/r9.claim: A statement may be emphatically confirmed even when its audience has no doubt, as in God's declaration إني جاعل, strengthened by inna and the active participle.
BURHAN:v2p387/r9.anchor: قصد تحقيق المخبر به كقوله تعالى إني جاعل فأكد بإن وبإسم الفاعل مع أنهم ليسوا بشاكين في الخبر

BURHAN:v4p434/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p434/r7.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v4p434/r7.claim: Kufan grammarians posit a waw of ṣarf that shifts the verb to subjunctive; the cited instance is the accusative reading of ويسفك.
BURHAN:v4p434/r7.anchor: ولها قسم آخر عند الكوفيين تسمى واو الصرف ومعناها إن الفعل كان يقتضي إعرابا فصرفته الواو عنه إلى النصب

BURHAN:v2p337/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p337/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p337/r7.claim: The angels’ question is apparently a request for guidance, with its phrasing shaped by etiquette; another view takes it as wonder.
BURHAN:v2p337/r7.anchor: والظاهر أنهم استفهموا مسترشدين وإنما فرق بين العبارتين أدبا وقيل هي هنا للتعجب

BURHAN:v2p339/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p339/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p339/r10.claim: The angels' أتجعل فيها question is not a request for information because God had already announced that He would place a vicegerent on earth.
BURHAN:v2p339/r10.anchor: وقوله ﴿ أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ﴾ 7 وهم لم يستفهموا لان الله قال ﴿ إني جاعل في الأرض خليفة ﴾

BURHAN:v2p339/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p339/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BURHAN:v2p339/r11.claim: Abū ʿUbayda likens the angels' question to someone striking a servant while saying, “Will you do this?”; another view calls it wonder, which the source weakens.
BURHAN:v2p339/r11.anchor: وشبهة أبو عبيدة ( 8 ) بقوله الرجل لغلامه وهو يضربه الست الفاعل كذا

BURHAN:v2p339/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p339/r12.speaker: النحاس
BURHAN:v2p339/r12.claim: Al-Naḥḥās prefers the explanation attributed to Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās: the angels asked whether the vicegerent would have descendants who corrupt and kill one another.
BURHAN:v2p339/r12.anchor: وقال النحاس الأولى ما قاله ابن مسعود وابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ولا مخالف لهما

ITQAN:v4p384/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p384/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p384/r4.claim: The intended first human and his spouse are Adam and Hawwa; her name is written long because she was created from a living person.
ITQAN:v4p384/r4.anchor: هو آدم وزوجه حواء بالمد لأنها خلقت من حي

ITQAN:v2p339#7/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p339#7/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p339#7/r15.claim: To sanctify for God means to purify.

ITQAN:v1p252/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p252/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p252/r2.claim: Qāf assimilates into kāf after a vowel and also in one word before mīm; kāf assimilates into qāf after a vowel, except when its preceding letter is still.
ITQAN:v1p252/r2.anchor: والقاف في الكاف إذا ما تحرك ما

ITQAN:v3p215/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p215/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p215/r4.claim: Interrogation can seek guidance, as in the angels’ question about placing a corrupter on earth.
ITQAN:v3p215/r4.anchor: التاسع عشر الاسترشاد نحو ﴿ أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p143/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p143/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p143/r4.claim: Ḥamd can mean acting at God’s command, as in the angels’ declaration and the response to the call on the Day of Resurrection.
DAMGHANI:v1p143/r4.anchor: الحمد بمعنى الأمر قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

DAMGHANI:v1p162/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p162/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p162/r2.claim: خليفة can mean a replacement for those who came before, here replacing the jinn.
DAMGHANI:v1p162/r2.anchor: الثاني : الخليفة البدل ممن مضى قوله سبحانه

MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r5.claim: He groups the cited examples as surplus letters in speech whose dropping yields the intended construction.
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r5.anchor: ومن مجاز ما يزاد فى الكلام من حروف الزوائد، قال الله: «إن الله لا يستحيي أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f1.claim: Al-Baqara opens the Adam story at its earliest event: before Adam is created, God tells the angels He will appoint a vicegerent on earth.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f1.anchor: تبدأ هذه القصة في البقرة من أقدم حدث فيها حين أبلغ الرب ملائكته بقراره في أن يجعل في الأرض خليفة وذلك قبل خلق آدم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f2.claim: The angels question the appointment because of corruption and bloodshed; God cuts off their fears and conjectures by asserting His unlimited knowledge.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f2.anchor: وفيها ذكر مراجعة الملائكة لربهم في هذا القرار مُبدينَ عدم رغبتهم في هذا الاستخلاف لأسباب ذكروها. فقطع عليهم تَخَوُّفَهم وظنونهم بعلمه الذي لا يُحَدُّ

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f6.claim: Appointment as God's vicegerent is itself an honor, since the one entrusted with vicegerency must hold an elevated status.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f6.anchor: فهذا تكريم، إذا المستخلف ذو منزلة رفيعة ولا شك

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f9.claim: The story establishes God's comprehensive knowledge, denies the angels knowledge except what He teaches them, and gives Adam knowledge fit for the vicegerency.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f9.anchor: نفي العلم عن الملائكة إلا ما عَلَّمهم إياه ربُّ العزة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f10.claim: Successful vicegerency requires authority to administer its domain and proven capacity; God gave humanity the earth, Adam's test showed his fitness, and the chooser knows the unseen.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f10.anchor: أن يكون للخليفة حَقُّ التصرف والتدبير فيما استُخلِفَ فيه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f11.claim: The verse before the story summarizes both Adam's narrative and the two requirements of vicegerency: the earth is given to people and God knows everything.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f11.anchor: أنَّ الآية التي وقعت في مقدمة القصة أجملت قصة آدم من ناحية، وأجملت ركني الاستخلاف المذكور فيها من ناحية أخرى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f2.claim: Although the appointment has not yet occurred, جاعل presents it as settled and inevitable through the active participle.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r3/f2.anchor: فهو لم يجعله بعد ولكن ذكره بصيغة اسم الفاعل للدلالة على أن الأمر حاصل لا محالة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r1.claim: The account in al-Baqara begins at the earliest point in Adam's story, a point not narrated elsewhere in the Quran and the starting point for Quranic narratives.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r1.anchor: لم تُذكر هذه النقطة في أي مكان آخر في القرآن وهي أول نقطة نبدأ فيها القصص القرآني

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r2.claim: Al-Baqara's account centers on Adam's honor and the knowledge he bears; teaching Adam extends to his descendants' succession, which entails both the right and the ability to act, with ability established through knowledge.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r2.anchor: وهل هو قادر على القيام بالمهمة أو لا (أثبت القدرة بالعلم)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r3.claim: A righteous, God-fearing, faithful human is more honored by God than the angels; God honored humanity through knowledge and intellect.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r3.anchor: الإنسان الصالح التقي المؤمن أكرم عند الله تعالى من الملائكة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r4.claim: Al-A'raf presents Adam's story as a rebuke for human ingratitude, unlike al-Baqara's focus on honor; its opening recalls God's provision and says people give little thanks.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r4.anchor: أما في سورة الأعراف فورود قصة آدم ليست من باب التكريم (قليلاً ما تشكرون) عتاب من الله تعالى على قلة شكرهم

NASHR:v2p236/r21.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r21.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p236/r21.claim: The two Medinan readers, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr open the yāʾ in إني أعلم at both occurrences.
NASHR:v2p236/r21.anchor: إني أعلم الموضعان فتحهما المدنيان، وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r1.claim: Some commentators proposed that God informed the angels of human traits or showed them the Preserved Tablet; Ibn ʿĀshūr says his explanation makes this speculation unnecessary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r1.anchor: وفي هذا ما يغنيك عما تكلف له بعض المفسرين من وجه اطلاع الملائكة على صفات الإنسان قبل بدوها منه من توقيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r2.claim: Some commentators analogized to an earlier nation that had vanished; Ibn ʿĀshūr says his prior explanation removes the need for this proposal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r2.anchor: له بعض المفسرين من وجه اطلاع الملائكة على صفات الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r3.claim: Some commentators analogized to predatory beasts that lived on earth before Adam, as in Genesis; Ibn ʿĀshūr likewise treats this as unnecessary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r3.anchor: له بعض المفسرين من وجه اطلاع الملائكة على صفات الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r4.claim: The angels judged what humanity could do by its potential, not by acts already committed or by examining individuals; this does not mean every human, unlike Adam, would corrupt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r4.anchor: لأنه حكم عليهم قبل صدور الأفعال منهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r5.claim: The imperfect verbs indicate recurring occurrences of corruption and bloodshed, not behavior continuously displayed by humanity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r5.anchor: لأن المضارع يدل على التجدد والحدوث دون الدوام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r6.claim: The angels knew that God's purpose in creating the earth was its order and reform, learned through revelation, the nature of vicegerency, or signs of God's care and intent that it endure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r6.anchor: وهم علموا مراد الله ذلك من تلقيهم عنه سبحانه أو من مقتضى حقيقة الخلافة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r8.claim: This is not forbidden backbiting: the angels speak in a pre-legal realm, for public advice can justify mentioning faults, the subject is an unnamed class, and no harm of backbiting arose here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p403/r8.anchor: ولا يرد هنا أن هذا القول غيبة وهم منزهون عنها لأن ذلك العالم ليس عالم تكليف ولأنه لا غيبة في مشورة ونحوها

IBNHIBBAN:6186/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6186/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNHIBBAN:6186/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that after Adam descended, angels questioned humanity’s corruption; God tested Hārūt and Mārūt on earth, where a woman’s demands led them to shirk, drunkenness, sex, and murder before they chose worldly punishment.
IBNHIBBAN:6186/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر، أنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «إن آدم لما أهبط إلى الأرض قالت الملائكة: أي رب {أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء

IBNHIBBAN:6186/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:6186/r2.speaker: أبو حاتم
IBNHIBBAN:6186/r2.claim: Abū Ḥātim clarifies that the woman called al-Zuhara was a human woman of that time, not the celestial planet Venus.
IBNHIBBAN:6186/r2.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: «الزهرة هذه امرأة كانت في ذلك الزمان، لا أنها الزهرة التي هي في السماء التي هي من الخنس»

MUSNAD-AHMAD:6178/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:6178/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:6178/r1.claim: The Prophet recounts that angels questioned human corruption, so Harut and Marut were sent down; a woman drew them into idolatry, murder, wine, and sex, after which they chose worldly over afterlife punishment.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:6178/r1.anchor: سمع نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: " إن آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أهبطه الله تعالى إلى الأرض

BURHAN:v3p342/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p342/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p342/r10.claim: تضمين can also mean inserting another speaker's words into one's discourse to reinforce meaning or shape composition; Zarkashi calls this ibdaʿ.
BURHAN:v3p342/r10.anchor: ويطلق التضمين أيضا على إدراج كلام الغير في أثناء الكلام لتأكيد المعنى أو لترتيب النظم ويسمى الإبداع
